#1
Premise of the story: Person reincarnates in Anime Japan and makes use of tropes because why the fuck not.

Also, the multicross elements is "inspired" from different works because author doesn't know enough of each source material and is too lazy to read em.

Chapter 1

The sky was gloomy like it was about to rain, and the park was devoid of people.

She had gone here to clear her mind instead of attending the club. She didn't want to meet Makoto-kun or Kaede yet. She can't stand the current atmosphere of the club, their dynamic getting stifled with an unsaid tension. Everything feels forced, and it hurts to see her valued friendships getting turned into that.

Which is why she, Yuki Yanai, walked on the deserted park to clear her mind from everything.


Spoiler

She alone walked in the park that day. The place was popular for many during spring because of the blooming Sakura trees, but for the fall season, there was not much reason for people to come to this place.

It also made it harder for other people to look for her. No one would suspect her being here for now. Perhaps Makoto-kun and Kaede would be worried where she went, and this way they wouldn't find her. And it's not like there's not much to do in the club for today either. She checked.

She hoped they'd be fine with her being selfish for now.

"Perhaps confessing that day was a mistake…" she muttered.

She knew that when she took the chance, things wouldn't be the same. She knew her feelings about Makoto-kun despite the way they might act towards each other and the thought that they could become more made her heart soar. For all his personality flaws, the boy had become someone that she trusts.

But it was obvious that she wasn't the only one feeling that way. Her valued friend, Kaede, was undoubtedly feeling the same way. She had seen the looks the girl gave him. It took a while to acknowledge it, but they were both pining for the same person.

And now the three of them, who simply enjoyed each other's presence in the club, out of desire to turn things into something much more - things had become complicated.

The thought made her chuckle ruefully, and as if sensing her mood the weather turned gloomier. It looked like it was about to rain, with the wind rustling the nearby trees and bringing the humid scent of rainfall with it. She supposed that she had to bring out her umbrella soon, especially with the sound of crackers being chewed—

…Crackers being chewed?

She blinked and turned to the noise, and there she saw that this whole time, there had been somebody sitting on a bench near from where she was. She realized that the person sitting there wore a uniform from the same school as her, and the person simply lounged on the bench while eating snacks as if without a care in the world.

A familiar memory tickled the back of her mind. She recognized this person - this was somebody from her class, albeit someone she never talked to.

"That person… Basa-kun, right…?"

The munching stopped, and his eyes turned to her as if acknowledging her for the first time.

"Hm?" he titled his head curiously. "Hold on, aren't you that girl from my class?"

Yuki found herself unable to speak for a moment. She was never the closest to her classmates, and while she would maintain a polite relationship with them, she never really focused on them. This person however was someone she never interacted with and had stuck to her mind - and for good reason at that.


Spoiler

Basa-kun was known for being a delinquent. Putting aside his tanned and fit appearance that was so reminiscent of gyaru fashion, there were plenty of rumors popping up around him and most of them weren't good to hear. She never was someone to believe such baseless rumors, especially with her falling victim to jealous bullies during middle school, but this was an exception.

Then there was also that odd tendency to arrive in class soaked with something. It was a strange quirk that was almost comical with how often it happens. He just seems to be unlucky when around any liquid in general.

Nevertheless, her classmate was plenty strange. She was also positive that he was someone that Yuki didn't want to interact with no matter what. And right now she was left alone in this deserted park with such a person.

Something must have appeared on her face as he gave her a raised brow.

"Hey, what's with that expression? Oh, I get it - it's because you're thinking that I'm a thug, aren't you? That's rude." Yuki blinked in surprise at his statement, making him roll his eyes. "I'll have you know that this tanned skin is entirely natural and not because I'm some gyaru-o character. I'd say you're stereotyping… but I guess that's already given for anime bullshit."

…What?

Before she could process what he said, she was interrupted with him shoving the food in his mouth and speaking to her once more.

"So, what are you doing here in this lonely park? Don't you have people to talk to? Maybe things to monologue about? Problems to drama on?" he quipped with his mouth full of food.

His mocking tone, even if she didn't understand his words, made her eyes narrow at him. "I believe that is none of your business." she responded harshly.

"Hm… hold on, the sky is gloomy, and you're alone. You must have come here monologuing about some problem or something. If I remember, you have a club right? That's right, only three members - you, a boy, and another girl. I'm guessing a love triangle, or maybe even mutual affections?" Yuki stiffened at his words as he swallowed his snack and rubbed his chin in thought. "And it was just the school festival recently. Something must have happened to cause some drama there."

Then, his eyes widened as he put his fist in his palm in realization.

"Oh, you two must have confessed in the festival and things must have been awkward or something! I think that's an appropriate drama." he turned to her. "So, am I right? That's what happened, isn't it?"

Yuki's throat was dry, and she looked at the person in front of her with no small amount of shock and even a little bit of fear. She took a slight step back.

"H-How…?" she asked, voice slightly hoarse.

He somehow rolled his eyes. Rolled his eyes at that. "It's predictable. It's a given that there's gonna be drama in that school every week no matter what happens." he shook his head in dismay. "Seriously, for people with unrealistically high empathy you drama characters can be dumb. This is why I prefer shounen, things are more simple there even when things get rowdy or cheesy."

Yuki was speechless, her confusion completely overwhelming her.

"What…? What are you even saying!? I don't understand!"

What was this person saying? Is he right in the head, or was he just messing with her? Why is he talking about fiction genres and characters? How was he, a stranger, able to know her entire situation like it was nothing!?

Then, before she could voice out all of those, all those grind to a halt when she felt something in the world change. Like everything just went still, followed by a complete feeling of dread that suffused within her and struck her to her core.

And it was coming from somewhere.

She turned to the direction of the source of the feeling… and what she saw there was nothing short of an image brought forth by a terrible nightmare.

Right there was a monster in parody of a woman, with only the top half being a naked beauty that would've ensnared anyone like a deadly siren on the sea and the bottom half being a monstrous spider-like body with a terribly horrifying mouth on where its private parts are supposed to be.

"Oh~? Prey within my territory~? It's been a while since I had my last human!" the monster said sensually.

Yuki's eyes were wide and bloodshot, taking in the unbelieving sight in front of her. This… this wasn't real, right? Monsters aren't real, right? She was losing her mind right now, right? Of course, of course. At first she meets someone who talks as if real life was fiction and now she was looking at a monster - of course she was losing her mind!

She desperately turned to the other person with her, about to shout to her classmate or maybe even babble incoherently, she didn't really know—

—Only to be met with the sight of him with an expression of slight surprise while looking at the monster.

"That's strange, it shouldn't be appearing right now." he said.

Something shattered inside her with how calmly he said that.

And as the monster pounced at them, Yuki screamed as loudly as she could.

Tropes. The DNA of the Story.

Tropes are an idea that recur in any narrative media. It is ever-present, a concept that appears again and again in the same or altered form. Because in the depths of the human psyche which governs creativity, whence all stories come forth, are also governed in the same pattern-liking that our brains operate on. Thus, it follows that stories would have repeating elements as well.

In other words, for something to be a story, then there has to be tropes. And for there to be tropes, then there has to be a story. Two concepts that cannot be separated, as one defines the other intrinsically.

So, what exactly does all that mean?

Well, it means that if I have to live in a world that operates on a narrative, then it is logical that a world like that would also have tropes to follow.

Because the simple fact is that I, Basa-kun, was reincarnated… into something that can only be described as an "Anime world".

And all the implications that come with it.

My hand stopped the stray demon as it went for an overhead swipe with its spider-like appendages when it pounced. There was a squawk of surprise when I did so, but I ignored it in favor of focusing on the monster right in front of me.

My muscles barely even strained in effort blocking that attack so this stray demon must be one of the weaker ones. Relatively weak that is - the demon hit like a truck, but my shounen training from hell has paid dividends in allowing me to do shit like this. Still, it could've been worse and if it was this weak then it makes things easier for me.

The most curious thing however was that it appeared when the heroine was around. It just wasn't supposed to do that since they're entirely different genres. Did I mistake the type of genre the heroine belonged to, then? Or was it my presence that changed things?

Curious. Very curious.

The bewitching woman that made the top-half of the demon's body looked at me in puzzlement. "Hm~? A prey fighting back?" she said in surprise. "That's strange, you feel like a normal human but how—?"

Oh, it's monologuing. Chance.

I threw a water balloon I procured specifically for this situation towards its large lower mouth, and it closed reflexively in surprise from my sudden action. The balloon managed to get in though, and I heard it audibly popping as the sharp teeth maw shredded it.

Spreading the holy water inside the balloon inside the stray demon and splashing some on me as well.

I frowned as I felt my uniform get soaked. Ugh, trust my character quirk appearing in inconvenient times.

"—GYAAAAAAAH!!! WHAT DID YOU DO!?!?" my attention returned to the stray demon as it shouted in pain, its body losing strength at swallowing incredibly concentrated holy water. "I'M, I'M BURNING…!"

I kept a close eye as the miracle liquid worked its magic and purified the stray demon from the inside. It tried to weakly reach for me with its hands but I simply batted it away. In no time the demon lurched, before its monstrous form eventually turned to ash.

And just like that a potential problem in this park is solved. Seriously, out of all places it could hide in it chose somewhere nearby a drama school. Not like the two genres would interact, but as an exception I might get swept with whatever shenanigans if I just happened to be near.

I let out a satisfied exhale. "Well, that settles that."

I turned around and went to leave—

"W-Wait!"

Oh, right. I knew I was forgetting something.

I glanced back to the heroine, who was looking at me with confusion and fear in her eyes. Understandable, since a few minutes earlier she was living in an entirely different world than the one she found herself now. How should I deal with this…?

"Right, right." what was her name again? "Yuki… was it? Please don't tell anyone what happened here. Well, even if you do it's not like anyone will believe you, but I'd appreciate it if you don't do it. Doing that will be more trouble than it's worth. Trust me." I said to her. "Just forget about this whole thing and move on with your life."

Alright, warning given. I'm sure she'll still be snooping around, but at least I reminded her of the fact of how it might affect her if she just thoughtlessly tried to spread things. After saying my piece the heroine didn't say anything so I took that as a chance to leave, walking away and leaving her alone in her thoughts.

The genre she stays in will prevent her from seeing more, so things are effectively over.

…

…Aah, I just totally set up a flag didn't I?

Yuki watched as her enigmatic classmate left, her mind awhirl with thoughts about what had just happened.

Monsters, people getting strong enough to fight those monsters - it seemed something out of fiction, like one of those low-brow light novels Makoto-kun reads. And if that person's statements were to be believed, then fictional logic operated in real life as well.

She didn't know what to do with all this. He had a point when saying that no one would believe her if she told other people - the only thing that would accomplish was tear her reputation to shreds, or in the worst case scenario, treat her like she was insane.

That meant that she couldn't say anything about it to others. But she doesn't want to let things lie like that either. She wants to know what happened, out of her own concern for her safety and peace of mind.

And if she wanted to make sense of what had happened, the logical conclusion was to investigate things itself from the source.

"Basa-kun… just who is that person?"

Somehow, her previous problems were much smaller than she thought.

Was supposed to finish this earlier but I suddenly got sick and it fucked me over real bad. Anyway, here it goes.

And since I saw a quite reasonable post requesting to say the source material; today's inspired anime include references to DxD and Fate.

Edit: Changed the names of DxD Expies because it's gonna get confusing down the line.
Chapter 2

A whole day had gone by since the incident, and not once was Yuki able to sleep with what she witnessed yesterday never leaving her mind. She had tried to follow her enigmatic classmate yesterday only to fail when she realized she was no longer anywhere in the area, leaving her to dwell helplessly on the revelations thrown at her.

As much as she wanted to stay home in case monsters that she thought didn't exist would eat her, she knew that if she wanted an explanation she had no choice but to attend school. And that was exactly what she did - she came to class early, slightly paranoid of her surroundings, before arriving in her classroom like usual.

Yuki's classmates all arrived slightly later. They talked about mundane things, clueless of the monsters lurking around them. It was surreal to see people acting this way now that she knew better. She ignored the unreasonable anger and envy of them continuing to live life that way, and crushed the temptation to just tell the truth to her classmates about what she saw yesterday.

That would be nothing but foolishness since no one will believe her.

Then, minutes before homeroom would start, he arrived.

The sliding door opened to reveal Basa-kun whose uniform was completely soaked as usual. No one commented on it and he was entirely ignored, with people not wanting to associate themselves with a known delinquent. He then wordlessly walked to his seat before sitting down on it.

Yuki discreetly stared at her classmate. She should've questioned it further, but why does he always get wet? Such a thing isn't normal. Even if a person can be said as "unlucky", there has to be some sort of limit to it. But no - her classmate seems to be getting doused with liquids around him in general.

Then there are the more stranger qualities about him. This high school is unforgiving with delinquency as it is an elite school in their prefecture. What's more, she can recall one or two times when he visibly isn't listening to class. Despite that, he remained in the school.

She suspects there's some sort of foul play involved. Hypnosis, perhaps…? With what she saw yesterday, it was definitely something possible.

But then if that was the case, why didn't he use it on her when she saw the monster—?

"Yuki~! Good morning!"

Her train of thought was interrupted with a familiar voice, and she stopped looking at Basa-kun and turned to see the one who greeted her. There she saw a familiar girl with a sunny disposition which she had come to associate with a valued friend.


Spoiler

"Good morning, Kaede." she greeted back.

Kaede looked at her, then to the direction that she was looking at. Her brows furrowed. "Um… were you looking at Basa-kun just now…? Should I be worried?"

Yuki kept her expression still and dismissed her worries with a shake of her head. "Don't worry, Kaede. It's nothing." she paused. "I was just wondering why he's always wet whenever he arrives in class."

"Is that so…? I mean, I guess it's strange…" she trails off, but she could tell from her expression that she was unconvinced. Nevertheless, she didn't push. "Still, Yuki! Why didn't you go to our club yesterday!? Me and Makoto-kun were worried about you when you didn't show up, you know!"

She winced. "I'm sorry, but there was an emergency and I wasn't able to tell you…" she was lying, but it's not like she could tell the truth, could she? "Did something happen at the club that I missed? I had to leave in a hurry yesterday."

"Well there wasn't any request for us, so it was just free time. It was boring though, so I tried asking Makoto-kun some things. Did you know that he—"

She listened to Kaede's stories half-heartedly as she described what she and Makoto-kun had been up to yesterday. It wasn't her focus though, with her mind fixated on a certain classmate that she'll interrogate later on to know the truth of what happened yesterday.

Because she's going to get her answers.

One way or another.

I wasn't oblivious to the fact that a certain heroine had been eyeing me the moment I arrived in class.

Just as expected, even after warning her, she would be stubborn about it and would probably be hunting me down to ask me later. Not like it's going to be a problem - school is getting boring nowadays, and this has been the most interesting thing up to date.

Still, I can't help but think of the heroine as a source of curiosity, ever since yesterday.

Because the thing is, as I have commented, the heroine wasn't supposed to be at that park and meet the monster.

There are rules to this world. For a world with its inhabitants living out a story, something needs to control it slightly so that it wouldn't devolve into chaos. A story's setting needs to be coherent - and that wouldn't work if everything is a mish mash of different ideas born from different stories. That's just one example as there are plenty more reasons, but nevertheless it shows there is a need for control.

And one of the main rules of this world is this: stories of different genres generally don't interact with one another.

Drama-centered stories generally wouldn't interact with shounen-centered ones. These stories have conflicting nature and could be found metaphorically - or literally - in different worlds. Drama stories are mostly found in the mundane, while shounen stories can be found in fantastical and action-oriented settings mostly hidden from the public eye. The characters themselves would be different as well, with drama characters being more complicated and have more depth than shounen characters in general.

Of course there are exceptions to this rule. Multi-genre stories are one of them. Then there are also backstories, but that's a different beast entirely.

Still, that goes back to the heroine. She, a drama character, had no business in being in a place where a shounen antagonist is located. I'd given it some thought, thinking that it may be my influence, but I was pretty sure that even if I wasn't there the stray demon would still notice and eat her. Then I thought that it was a case of me mistaking the genre she belonged to, thinking she belonged to a school drama instead of something along the lines of "mundane girl encounters the supernatural and becomes a magical girl" type of story.

In that case, that would make me the teacher type of character that would guide her in the supernatural. I dismissed that as well, because I was pretty sure that I was still a side character in the eyes of the world. My "side character quirk" after living in a relatively simple shounen setting is still present. I also ran some tests; some simple mind scanning spells along with spiritual meditation showed my baseline mind and soul is still the same, and self-divination showed our fates being untangled. At no point did I become a teacher type of character - which is great news, because being that type of character usually carried plenty of death flags that it could stab them.

…Though I guess I can leave out the ponderings for later. The staring was getting a bit unnerving, so I stood up and went to the rooftop when it was lunch.

Predictably, there was no one around despite it being a popular place for many stories. And since the flag I planted yesterday dictates that she must be around, I called for the heroine.

"I know you're there. You've been pretty much staring at me the whole morning, so if you've got something to say then here's your chance."

There was a moment of silence, then the door to the rooftop opened to reveal the girl herself.

I gave her a raised brow. "Did anyone see you coming here? Because if they see a heroine like you meeting a delinquent like me, there's gonna be plenty of misunderstandings."

And wasn't that a source of frustration to me for quite some time. It's not my fault I look straight out of an NTR doujin manga!

The heroine blushed a bit as she understood the implication, before shaking her head and giving me a glare. "No, no one saw me go up here. I made sure of that."

She can say that, but with how bullshit the world is, you can never be too sure. I hummed, trying to decide in my mind the appropriate spell in my repertoire for this situation, before choosing and discreetly casting a spell that detects nearby lifeforms that I stole from those magi that I encountered a while back.

"Well, I guess you're telling the truth, heroine." I commented when the spell brought back a negative.

"Can you stop calling me that? I have a name. It's Yuki Yanai." she growled.

"Sure. Yanai, then." I acquiesced, shrugging. "So, what brings you here and what do you want with dear ol' me?"

She took a deep breath. "What do I want? What I want… is an explanation."

I hummed at that. "Explanation about what?"

"Please don't play dumb with me." she said with eyes narrowed. "I want an explanation of everything! The monster that tried to eat me, you fighting that monster - and you acting like, like the world is some sort of story!"

"Did that happen? I don't think that happened. Are you sure you're not just becoming crazy?"

"You just called me a 'heroine' not a second ago!"

"Oh yeah - uh, I mean no I didn't do that."

"You…!"

I watched as the heroine visibly exhaled to calm herself down, before glaring straight at me. Wow, that's a really scary glare. If those could kill then I'd be dead plenty of times over you know?

"You are being difficult." she started after a while. "Fine, be that way. But know this - I won't stop trying to find the truth out of you. And if you won't give me what I want… well, I know that you said that no one would believe me, but that wouldn't stop me from spreading the truth through different means."

…Say what?

I gave her a confused face. "What are you talking about?"

"You want to keep a low profile, don't you?" she pointed out. "Something that prevents you from putting things out in the open. For someone who has access to supernatural powers, especially for a delinquent like you—"

"Oi, I'm not a delinquent."

"—Then the fact that you're not using your powers recklessly and have to hide it means that you want to keep yourself hidden. And if you're not going to tell the truth of what happened yesterday to me… then I'll do everything in my power to make sure that you won't be able to stay hidden no matter what."

I raised an eyebrow at that. "Everything in your power? Power as what? A highschool student?"

"No." her glare hardened. "My power as the daughter of the Yanai Family, which has a seat in the National Diet along with a considerable influence on the Japanese Conglomerate."

I hummed at that.

Of course, of course. Rich daughter of a powerful family… She must be the modern princess type of heroine. Should've expected this sort of thing really, but she certainly doesn't act like a typical ojou-sama though. I guess with how subdued she is and with the way she doesn't consciously show off her wealth, she must be the rich and lonely sort of type.

Still, isn't this a bit too reckless? She should know that I have the advantage here. I'm the one with the powers, and she doesn't know what I could do to her. Not like I'll hurt her though, but she doesn't know that. So why would she try to threaten me even knowing that fact? And with me less than a few meters in front of her even. Isn't this kind of threat better done without it being face to face?

Drama characters are hyperempathetic and have greater mental acuity than any other genres, and that combo somehow leads to overthinking and misunderstandings which is the source of conflict in their stories. What they do not do is to make rash, reckless decisions that could potentially end their lives. No, that sort of thing belongs to shounen.

So why do this at all?

My eyes tracked her form, and I noticed something strange. I walked towards the heroine, who stiffened at my movement but still maintained her glare at me, before stopping right in front of her and forcing her to look up to me as I towered over her from our sheer height difference.

Then I swiped the cleverly hidden object underneath her uniform's blazer, making her squawk.

"So," I mused as I held the object with my hands. "You're recording this with your phone, huh?"

"G-Give, give that back!" she shouted, trying to swipe it but I kept it out of reach and put a hand on her shoulder. The heroine tried to struggle, but a firm hand made her unable to throw my grip off.

"Hm, and by the looks of it, it's going to upload the recording automatically somewhere. I guess this is insurance if I was going to hurt you? Or rather, were you hoping for me to do that? And the whole threat was just bait for me to make me reveal myself. Smart." I frowned. "Still a bit reckless, but at least there's some thought put into it."

The heroine stopped struggling, and adopted a despaired expression. For a moment she didn't speak as she looked down… then she weakfully whispered something that barely caught with my ears. "...It's also in case you used hypnosis too."

"Oh, that's a good point. I guess assuming hypnosis exists is logical when you witness the supernatural. If I hypnotized you and made you forget, then you'd still remember what happened because of the recording… Good reasoning, but I generally don't mindwipe if I can help it. It's a lot harder than it sounds." I commented.

The heroine didn't reply, but she did look up and give me another glare. Though this one was less assured and more of putting up a front, judging by the slight shaking of her figure.

"S-So, you've got me cornered, good for you. What are you going to do now?" she clenched her fists. "Hypnotize me? Silence me? K-Kill me?"

I raised a brow, deleting the recording on the phone. I then gave the phone back to her, the heroine taking it with surprise, and took a few steps back from her personal space.

"You want answers right?" I shrugged. "Sure, I'll tell you."

She paused at that, and what I had said seemed to have broken something in the heroine as she looked at me like I was some sort of metafictional anomaly. "...Pardon?"

"I said I'll tell you." I repeated.

"Y-You will? Just like that!?"

"Yes." I rolled my eyes. "Should I say it again? Yeah, I'll explain it to you."

A familiar expression came to her face, and I realized it was the same face she made when she was overwhelmed with the sheer confusion of what happened yesterday. "...W-Why? I just threatened you, didn't I? You're just going to let me go?"

"Are you complaining about that?" I chuckled. "And no, you didn't threaten me. At all. At no point was I in any danger in this situation - You're gonna need something more if you want to threaten me."

The heroine looks like she wants to say more, but nothing seemingly came out as words failed her.

I shook my head. "Anyway, if you're serious about wanting to know more then meet me after your club hours. I'll give you the full explanation after that. So for now…" I gestured for her to go away. "Shoo shoo. Go bother someone else."

The heroine bit her lip, looking at me doubtfully for a few moments… then ultimately nodded her head. She then turned around and left the rooftop - and thankfully, no witnesses around to see her as she did so.

I waited for her to be truly gone before I relaxed.

Then, I brought out my trusty notepad and pen.


Spoiler

I smiled as I finished penning my notes.

"This was a very productive day."

Meanwhile, as those events occurred, there was also something happening in another school that was previously an all-girl high school. In this certain place, a mansion-like building situated within the outskirts of the school grounds acted as the base of operations of a certain club.

Inside it was a blonde male student. He was someone who could be described as bewitchingly handsome, with a disarming smile on his face that would certainly capture the hearts of many women. He walked inside the mansion's halls, until he stopped at a certain door and knocked on it gently.

"Come in." an elegant voice said from the inside.

He did so, slipping inside the room and closing the door behind him. There, he was met with a red-haired female student who sat behind a table, in a room that looked like her office.

If the blonde was described as incredibly handsome, then the red-haired woman can only then be described as sinfully beautiful. A perfect body that - man or woman - would lust over, along with a face that would give any model a run for their money. She was a beauty beyond compare.

The blonde bowed respectfully at her. "Buchou, I've come bearing reports."

"Oh?" she let out a smile. "Let's hear it then, Kiba."

And now that she had converted a human into a devil, she welcomed him to her club.

…And now, he was sitting here, instead of a dark-skinned blonde who kept calling her names and being generally mean towards her. She can't help but feel guilty thinking that - she didn't regret converting Ryuusei-kun into a devil, but it's making her feel bummed that the human she converted was not the one she was targeting.

That Basa-kun! Why can't he just join!? Now she can't help but not treat this supposed joyous occasion the respect it deserves since she keeps comparing him to her newest recruit!

Not showing a hint to her inner troubles, she directed a gentle smile at the boy. "Anyway, we're all demons here in this club Ryuusei-kun. You were pretty much dying when I found your body, and the only way to heal from that injury was to revive you as a demon.

The reminder of his near-death experience dampened his expression, and his brows furrowed in anger. "...Yeah, I remember being stabbed by that fallen angel." his eyes then widened as his gaze snapped towards her. "Can I ask what happened to Aisha!? She was with me that time! Is she safe!?"

She nodded. "She is unharmed. I managed to fight off the fallen angel and remove his influence from her. She was hypnotized by the angel and dispelling it effectively removed her memories of the entire event. The girl should be at home right now."

That seemed to remove his worries as he visibly deflated in relief. "I see, that's good… I was worried that things went bad." his mouth curled into a sharp glower. "That fallen angel, I'll never forgive what he did to her…!"

Then, he paused, before looking at them with a hesitant expression. "Um… wait, so if you're demons, does that mean you guys are bad? I'm pretty sure that's how it goes…"

Rias shook her head with an amused smile. "Don't worry, Ryuusei-kun. We may be demons, but we're not like that. We may be predisposed to sin but it doesn't mean that we're evil." she explained. "For all intents and purposes you can think of us as humans with extra appendages, but with an affinity for magic."

She started to explain to Ryuusei-kun about demons.

The words came easily to her with her explaining the same thing to Yuki-san yesterday. Now that she mentioned that, 'practice for exposition'... she remembered Basa-kun saying something along those lines. He definitely knew what was going to happen with how he phrased his words. And that led to her thinking of the implications of such a thing.

Basa-kun was a strange person - discounting the fact that he was a human magus, there's the fact that he believed that the world worked like it was a story. She dismissed him at first when she was younger, thinking that it was just some weird personality thing… but then his predictions never seemed to fail, and at some point they even started making sense.

Which brings Rias to her current point. Basa-kun always rejected her invitations because, in his own words, 'didn't want to fulfill that role' and never expanding further. Rias knew that she could be an idiot at times but she wasn't that oblivious. With how he called her a heroine plenty of times in the past, she knew that the 'role' would be a protagonist.

And now, there was a stranger coming to her life that could be that.

"Huh…" Ryuusei-kun muttered after her explanation. "I never thought demons would also live similarly to humans. I figured that they'd be similar to how that fallen angel acted."

"If I may ask," Kiba interjected from the side, giving him a questioning look. "What caused the fallen angel to attack you in the first place? We can't seem to understand why he did that."

The boy frowned. "I don't know, he kept spouting stuff about me being some chosen descendant or something, but I was honestly so focused on running away with Aisha at that time."

"I see. Now that you mentioned it, I can definitely tell that there's something inherently odd about you. I never quite noticed it but it's there…" Kiba trailed off.

A wordless noise on the sofa made everyone turn to Koneko who was lounging there, eating cookies. "Hn, he smells odd. Virile, like prime meat… but also strong. Strange."

Akeno put a finger on her chin in thought. "Hm, Ryuusei-kun, are you a descendant of some hero perhaps? It must be something in your blood that was mixed in."

"Um… I don't think so? Mom and Dad never really told me about anything like that…"

Rias struggled to keep her face neutral.

Chosen descendant!? Hidden power!? This person is definitely the protagonist! Basa-kun definitely knew that this was going to happen!

Again, normally someone like this joining her club would make her feel overjoyed, but on this occasion… she didn't know how to feel.

"Isn't this great, Rias?" Akeno suddenly said cheerfully. "With Ryuusei-kun with us, there's a chance that you can finally achieve your dream of becoming the President of hell!"

Rias' face immediately reddened and turned to her friend, breaking her graceful act. "Akeno! You can't just say that!"

"Oh, he'll know eventually anyway. At least this way you won't dally around like you did the rest of us." the raven-haired girl said dismissively.

"I wasn't dallying around! And that's not the point!" She can't just say embarrassing things like that out loud!

Ryuusei-kun tilted his head in confusion. "Um… president of hell? What are you guys talking about?"

Kiba let out a chuckle as he shook his head. "The entirety of Hell is governed by a president. Buchou here is ambitious enough to try pining herself as one - so that she could change hell and turn it into a better place."

"I-I don't know what you're talking about."

"Buchou's childhood dream." Koneko piped up from the side, nodding her head sagely.

"No it's not!" Rias denied loudly.

Akeno nodded as well. "She truly is the goodest demon."

"Shut up, Akeno! I'm the most devious damn demon around! No one can be more crafty and cunning than I!"

"Yes, yes." her three club members said in unison.

Rias can't help but cover her face, head steaming from her club members saying such embarrassing things. Great, she wanted to show their newest member a dignified leader and now he'll think of her as a childish woman! Everything is ruined!

"Wait, really!? That's pretty cool, Rias-san!" Ryuusei-kun shouted spiritedly. "Don't worry, there is no shame in such things! I'll support you in your dream as much as I can! I understand your woes… for I too, have a childhood dream that I want to achieve!"

Rias' eyes widened. "Ryuusei-kun…"

"That's right! Nothing can stop us from living our lifelong goals!" he stood up and pumped his fist in determination. "You'll be the president of hell… while I'll have a harem of beauties!"

—What the hell was this guy saying!?

Her club's reaction was mixed at his declaration, with Koneko looking at him like a weirdo, Kiba palming his face, and Akeno giggling uncontrollably. Rias, meanwhile, just gave him a smile that twitched dangerously. "I-Is that so…"

This… this is the protagonist?

Hold on, wouldn't her being a heroine like what Basa-kun called her mean that she'll be paired with him!? Does that mean that she'll fall in love with this guy!?

That Basa-kun, was this seriously the guy he was thinking of as the protagonist!? If so, please reconsider! She doesn't want to be part of this person's 'harem'! That sounds like a nightmare scenario no matter how differently it's framed!

Stupid Basa-kun! Baka-kun! He should've just taken up her offer instead, that idiot!

There will be retribution for this! Just you wait!

Chapter 5

Today had been enlightening, she reflected.

The morning sun shone bright as Yuki walked alongside Basa-kun. Her enigmatic classmate was humming a tune as they did so, filling the silence between them on their little walk.

They had just finished eating breakfast inside Basa-kun's apartment prepared by his own neighbor, Aoki Yumiko. Yuki was forced to dine with them as well, as the mature woman didn't seem to take no for an answer and partly because she also didn't eat breakfast yet in her haste to show Basa-kun what she found.

It was… surprisingly pleasant, all things considered. The woman acted motherly and friendly, but not overbearingly so. Aoki-san seemed to treat her like her own child and acted as if she wanted to spoil her. She also fussed with Basa-kun and she saw a new sight of him being acting reserved. The whole atmosphere felt like they were a family eating breakfast in their household.

Yuki wasn't familiar with the experience, with her own mother acting strict and raising her as someone worthy of their family name. It was something new to her, but she didn't really mind the whole thing.

Though the breakfast was mostly spoiled by the fact that Basa-kun somehow slept with the woman. And worse, Aoki-san seems to be very vocal about the fact - It seemed that the woman got it into her head that she and Basa-kun were lovers and thus started to directly reference how… competent he was in that department, out of some twisted desire to make him more appealing in her eyes.

Her face was entirely red during that time. It was honestly jarring how such a sweet-looking woman can start spouting degeneracy with a motherly smile on her face, as if she was a proud mom that was boasting about her son. And the things she said… she couldn't believe it either.

"The adult genre exists.'' That was her enigmatic classmate's explanation after they had left the apartment. The implications sent her mind reeling at what such a statement left, and the images in her mind left by Aoki-san's statements left her flustered. She couldn't look at Basa-kun for a while after that.

Nevertheless, that wasn't important.

Because right now, the two of them walked towards not to their school as their destination, but rather to the place where the suspected base of operation of those who caused the recent disappearances around town.

Basa-kun decided to deal with it because there was still enough time before school started, and that the place was close enough for him to just get there with a slight detour. Yuki decided to accompany him, partly out of curiosity and out of desire to help.

Yuki frowned.

…His words about her still repeat in her mind. About herself and her issues.

She knew she wasn't a perfect person - she might project herself as someone like so on the outside, but there had been many nights where she broke down crying when stress got to her, especially during her childhood. Nevertheless, she wasn't keen on reflecting on her own insecurities as well, choosing to forgo it into dealing with other matters. She wasn't strong enough to face them, that much she knew.

So for Basa-kun to just recognize it and bluntly say it like that, and for it to be right as well… and for him to say that it was normal to have issues as characters for drama stories…

She didn't know how to feel.

Her musings were interrupted however with Basa-kun stopping. She blinked, turning to him with a perplexed expression, before she suddenly realized where they were.

They were finally at their destination, the abandoned church.

"Alright, we're here." Basa-kun started, eyes scouring the place with a thoughtful gaze. "Hm, looks as ominous as I thought." his eyes narrowed. "Strange though… There certainly is a dense miasma of corrupted energies going around, but this is too much. Older too."

She couldn't sense energies like her enigmatic classmate somehow could, nor could she understand the rest of what he said, but Yuki found that she agrees with the statement. Looking at the place… there was as if some sort of wrongness in it that made her skin crawl.

"Remind me again, what did your research say about this place?" Basa-kun asked.

"Not much. Plenty of people said that it's hunted though because of the disappearances. But we know now that it's because of the fallen angels."

"Hm." Basa-kun hummed at her statement.

The two of them entered the abandoned church. It was rather small and humble compared to Buddhist temples, as Christianity wasn't practiced much in Japan than other religions, but she could tell that in the past the church would've been of high make. Marble floors that once were polished and stained glass windows that had long since faded showed hints of the church's old glory.

And all that was left now is a dusty old church with graffiti sprayed upon the almost brittle walls, along with the occasional flora that had overgrown from the outside soil. The inside was also slightly wet and humid due to the fact that it had rained the night before and the debilitated roof had many holes in it.

"What are we going to do now?" she asked.

Basa-kun didn't answer for a moment, then he spoke. "How about you take a look at it?"

She looked at him questioningly. "What do you mean?"

"Try to investigate. We're thinking that this is the base of operation for our kidnapping suspects; is there anything to find here that can support that?"

Yuki frowned. Was this a test? She supposes that she could entertain him.

She looked around the place, examining anything for clues. On a cursory glance this place is as abandoned as it gets - untouched and forgotten by time, only desecrated by the occasional vandalism. However, there were a few things that one could spot with a sharp eye that could prove that assumption wrong. Small litters, indicating evidence of recent activity. And while it could be argued that the liters could be blown by the wind, maybe even thrown by a past vandal, or anything like that…

She spots something and she finds herself walking towards it before bending down to pick it up.

Between her fingers was a cigarette butt thrown away.

"Someone was here." she concluded.

The cigarette butt she held was in pristine condition, with the whites of its filter paper still visible and not unlike the other litters which were in various degrees of decomposition, although there was a slight smudge of dirt on it. Interestingly it wasn't wet like the others and was completely dry despite the fact that it had rained yesterday. This must've meant that whoever threw this away only did so a few hours before.

It was also squashed flat, meaning it was stepped on. And since it was dry the floor must have been dry as well when the cigarette was thrown away. Yuki looked down on the floor where the cigarette butt was and saw a slight smidge of soil and dirt on the floor that was hard to see if one wouldn't specifically look for it. However, the floor's dust and debris should've been washed away especially with such heavy rain yesterday; at no point the dirt should've remained when the surrounding marble was clear of it.

And since the litter was stepped on by a shoe, it must have trodden on wet soil, like the one outside the church.

"Footprints." she muttered, realizing what exactly she was looking at. "These are footprints."

She looked around and also saw some smidge of dirt near her. These must have been other footprints as well, implying the presence of more people. Yuki looked ahead and tried to follow where they went - from the entrance they walked across the hall.

"And it all leads to…" she turned to the church altar, where a lectern long gone would have to be placed. She frowned however, when she realized there wasn't exactly anything there. "...Nowhere, I suppose. That's strange, why did it suddenly cut off?"

No, that was strange, there must be something. She doesn't see anything though, there wasn't anything there. But… she had a feeling that was wrong, somehow. Shouldn't there be at least something?

Her thoughts spiraled, and for a moment it felt like she had a terrible migraine. There was something there, but there wasn't - two repelling ideas clashing within her mind and replacing each other ad nauseam. What was—?

"You can stop looking at that."

Yuki turned to look at Basa-kun, who was writing something on a notebook. Before she could question what he was writing however, he pocketed it and approached the altar as well. "Don't worry, you're correct in your assessment. That's the place."

Her brows furrowed. "What do you mean? There's nothing here." …Or was there?

He seemed to notice her confusion. "Yeah, it's a bit nauseating to deal with. Hold on."

Kneeling on his knees, he then started to tinker with… something. Yuki couldn't understand what he was doing, but she could hear him muttering about 'arrays' and 'scriptures'. She tried to follow but the conflicting thoughts in her head were distracting enough for her to have a hard time doing so.

Then suddenly it disappeared and clarity fell upon her. Yuki felt something pressing on her mind go away, and she realized that there was something in the altar that she didn't see earlier - a square cut hole on the ground, with stairs leading somewhere further down.

Basa-kun stood up, grabbed a handkerchief from his pocket, and wrote something there. After doing so he extended the cloth to her.

"Here, take it." he offered.

Yuki took the cloth but her attention was focused on what was ahead of her.

There was a hidden entrance.

"It's cliché for bases to have hidden entrances. Well, not really hidden, since a hidden entrance almost always gets revealed either way, but these fallen angels seem to not be trying very hard. " Basa-kun explained. "They're not even hiding evidence of their presence or the memetic bounded field they put on the entrance. I guess they were arrogant enough to think that it's enough."

"Memetic bounded field?" Yuki muttered as she tried to shake her head clear.

"Magic thing that affects your mind in a specific area. Plants ideas in your head like how it hid that entrance." he clarified. "I modified it and put it on the handkerchief. If you hold that then no one would notice you."

Then, he walked towards the stairs and went down.

Yuki followed wordlessly behind him as they descended the stairs, their footsteps echoing in the stairwell that was only partially lit sunlight that passed through the church. Much to her consternation though, Yuki couldn't help but feel nervous as they went down the steps, no matter how much she tried to bury the feeling.

But, when they finally arrived at the end of the stairwell and were met by an expansive basement, the nervous feeling was quickly smothered with shock with what she saw.

There were people. People that were blindfolded, gagged, and kneeling with their hands tied behind their backs. Immediately, Yuki had recognized them as those who were stated as missing in the police reports. They were placed on the far corner of the basement away from sight, unmoving, and quiet. She suspected that magic was involved to make it that way.

And near them were a group of people; two men and two women. The basement had simple furniture like a table and chair, seemingly brought from the outside and just placed here. They seemed to just be lounging around, doing nothing in particular and just chatting with each other. Although one of the males were smoking and one female was reading a book.

Yet all of those observations remain on the sideline because of one thing - these people have folded black feathered wings on their backs.

Fallen angels.

She stiffened when she felt a hand suddenly grip her shoulder, but relaxed when she realized that it was just Basa-kun. She turned to face him and was met with an even stare. "Calm down. They haven't noticed us."

Yuki nodded her head and took a deep breath to calm herself. Her hands clutched the cloth in her hands tightly.

"What's going to happen next?" she asked after.

"Just observe them, find out what's going on and what they're doing, and see what's the best move forward while taking care of the consequences of involving ourselves." he explained idly. "Ideally we should leave without interfering at all and things will be fine without doing anything."

She nodded, then turned to watch the fallen angels as they chatted.

"—Hey, how long are we going to wait inside this dump of a church? I want to go back and sleep on a proper bed already." one of the male fallen angels grunted.

"Go complain to those old men then. See if you can get anything." the smoking one replied.

"I probably could. It's not like they can do anything to us with them looking so feeble like that."

"Don't." the female angel reading a book interrupted, not even looking up from its pages. "You'd probably get killed and I don't want to have anything to do with it. Did you hear what happened to one of our agents here when he disobeyed orders?"

The smoking angel raised a brow. "This I didn't hear. I suppose you mean the one monitoring the descendant of the chosen hero?"

"Yes. Apparently he fucked around and tried to kill the mortal. Not a problem really, but you'd think that he would've read between the lines and realized that the old men were thinking of using the mortal as an asset." she replied. "Then there's also the fact that the dumbass failed to kill the mortal because of some intervention with the demon here. They were really angry about that, so they ripped his wings off and force-fed it to him before executing him."

The other male angel scoffed. "That just means he's weak then. He gets what he deserves."

The smoking angel puffed his cigarette. "And what, you're different? Fear the old men who survived the War of Heaven, newbie. A hundred year old neophyte like you shouldn't get a big head with the freedom from the heavenly host, and just because you were grouped in with us because of your skills it doesn't mean that you're some sort of genius."

"Tch." the male angel clicked his tongue before standing up and approaching the kidnapped people. "At least let me entertain myself. This whole assignment has been tedious." he grabbed the face of one of the females there, inspecting her thoughtfully. "Couldn't I at least play with this one? She doesn't look too bad."

This time the smoking angel scoffed. "What, can't get your game outside? Should be easy picking some girl up."

"The hell is that supposed to mean!?"

"Enough." their bickering stopped when the last female fallen angel spoke, her stern voice echoing throughout the basement. "Those mortals will remain untouched. We cannot afford to mess up the ritual."

The male angel removed his hands from the female, before moving back to his seat. "Yeah, yeah." he grumbled.

Yuki scowled as she heard all of this.

"...Disgusting." she muttered. "How can they do this?"

"Some people are just evil." that was Basa-kun's reply. "Simple evil exists, since without it there can be no clear good. Without such a thing, there is no conflict in stories-to-be. Nothing to move its plot forward."

Bitterness filled up inside her at those words, making her grit her teeth. His words on how everything works like a story remains doubtful in her ears, no matter how much things are pointed out to her that proves it so. Yet if his words really were to be believed… if the world really does work like that…

"Isn't that unfair? That we experience problems just because there has to be this 'conflict'?"

Basa-kun gave her a glance. She didn't know what was going on his mind as he did so, but there was something behind those eyes.

Then he shrugged.

"Someone has to be entertained after all." he idly answered.

What… What does that mean? What was he implying?

Yuki opened her mouth, about to ask more questions, but before she could do so she was interrupted by a hum from Basa-kun, who was looking thoughtfully at the fallen angels.

"I guess intervening them would be the best choice. They're clearly trying to go out of their way to harm innocents even when there are other ways to accomplish the task… I'd probably need to change their mind about their approach for that."

Yuki looked at him in surprise. "You're going to intervene? How? What are we going to do?"

Basa-kun started walking towards the fallen angels.

"Just stay there and let me deal with it."

"Just stay there and let me deal with it." I told the heroine as I approached the fallen.

Man, that girl really is something else. Aside from the initial nervousness, she didn't even hesitate in accompanying me into the lair of these fallen angels. I never said a thing when she started following me after we finished breakfast with Aoki-san. I was expecting hesitation or maybe even her backing out in fear - but no, it doesn't seem that way.

Curiously, the heroine was getting more and more interesting by the day. Who knew that she would stumble upon a memetic bounded field on her own? I noticed it as soon as we went inside the church but she actually managed to focus on it after following the evidence. That's something that even those ridiculously effective shounen top detectives will miss, no matter how much evidence pointed towards its existence - trust me, I've checked.

And with her being able to follow me and interact fully with other people of different genres, something that I've never seen anyone do was icing on the cake. Even Rias, who I've known for years now, hasn't interacted with Aoki-san despite being close by. The two had never met despite being aware of the other's existence as my neighbor/past classmate because they never seem to cross each other's paths by coincidence, no matter how contrived the reason. Yet, somehow this heroine never had any problems with that.

It pretty much led me to a single conclusion. Something that I was suspecting for a while now.

It's not a matter of this girl somehow changing genres but rather, the genre divide didn't work for this heroine. An abnormality like that is so utterly unique in this world that I only know of one person like that.

Me.

Very curious, very curious indeed. Why was the girl a similar existence to me, I wonder? And why now? Why did she spontaneously get that ability? And the possibility she brings - does that mean there are even more people who suddenly gained the ability like her? The implications, people, there are just so many!

But I digress. There are fallen angels that need dealing with.

I left the memetic bounded field that I gave the heroine. Naturally as I walked away from her I also left its area of effect, making my appearance go not unnoticed. The fallen suddenly jolted from their seats as they felt my presence appear almost out of nowhere.

There's a lot of them, and I'd like to deal with this as cleanly as possible so… I guess I'll go with one of my usual approaches.

"Hey, what's up my dudes?" they turned to me in surprise and I raised a hand in greeting. "Fancy seeing you here. Nice weather we're having. Did you get a haircut?"

There was a beat of silence.

"What the—" the smoking fallen angel said in surprise, his cigarette falling from his hand. "Who the hell are you!?"

"A human…?" the female fallen with the book muttered, before rounding to the shocked male beside her. "Hey, I thought you got the bounded field running!?"

"I did! No human shouldn't have been able to get here!"

"Well clearly not since we're seeing one right now!"

"It's not my fault!" he defended.

"What is the meaning of this!? Why is there a mortal here!?" the leader female fallen snarled at her followers.

"Blame the newbie. He must have messed things up somehow."

"Wha— Say that to my face again, you nicotine addict!"

"You fucked things up."

"You…!"

I sighed loudly, the sound of it cut through the din, and I raised my arms placatingly at the bickering fallen angels who suddenly stopped bickering to look at me.

"Now, now, let's all calm down." I said in a calming tone. "No need to get so worked up."

"YOU'RE THE LAST ONE WE WANT TO HEAR THAT FROM!" they all shouted.

How to deal with shounen characters with the least amount of effort exerted. Let's run that through, shall we?

First, in the event that you are in a position where you can take out the characters by surprise, and that they know nothing about you, first lower their guard by applying rules of shounen comedy. Say something ridiculous or wacky, one that will catch them off guard, before following with a dialogue that follows the forced structure of Japanese Manzai Comedy.

"You! Mortal!" the ill-tempered male fallen shouted at me while pointing rather aggressively. "How did you get here!?"

"Eh? What do you mean? I just walked inside the church." I answered cluelessly.

"That's fine but you shouldn't have passed the bounded field!"

"Eh? Blonde and filled? The hell are you talking about?"

The male fallen paused in hesitation. "...You didn't pass through anything strange? Nothing at all?"

"Dunno. I was walking around and when I tripped I somehow got into these stairs. Then I went down and I got here and saw you guys."

"Are you telling me that mortal literally stumbled in here?" the other female fallen said in disbelief.

"I gotta say though." I continued. "You guys have pretty cool costumes. Those are some really realistic wings. Are you cosplayers? Did I stumble on a secret cosplay rendezvous or something?" I made a show to look at the kidnapped people. "...Or maybe something kinkier? I don't judge."

There was silence.

The smoking fallen angel, who had dropped his cigarette in surprise at my appearance, shook his head and approached me. "Well, whatever. This was unexpected… but ultimately harmless. Oi, newbie. You go and fix the bounded field." he started walking towards me. "I'll just quickly deal with this mortal."

Second step.

"An unfortunate fate you found yourself, mortal. To think you'll literally stumble your way to death." the fallen said. "Nonetheless, I—"

My leg lashed out with a kick strong enough to displace air that hit his side, the sheer force of the hit making him bend around on my leg like a wet noodle, before launching his body to the side where it smashed on the wall with an audible crash.

The other fallen looked at their comrade who was now fully unconscious.

"Eh?" the book-reading fallen uttered, her book falling out of her hands from shock.

As the scene is focused on comedy, these characters have their guards down and are vulnerable for attacks. And so, if one of the characters reaches your range, either by you moving or them approaching you… use the opportunity to take them out immediately to create a mood whiplash that breaks the hell out of the tone of the scene.

"You…! Who the hell are you!?" one of them stepped back cautiously,

I smiled, and the fallen bristled.

"What are you talking about? I'm just an ordinary guy."

Third step.

Take the initiative. Gain control of the flow of the battle. Right now, the mood whiplash created a contrast in the scene, and my smiling self had turned intimidating. The fear factor makes these characters unable to act for a moment as they hesitate on what to do. They would be sweating slightly, mind racing as they stare at my form, that if this scenario were to be in some manga then…

ゴゴゴゴゴゴゴ

Yeah, like that.

However, these people are fallen angels. Their pride would be clashing with their sense of danger. Least of all, they don't want to acknowledge the fact that a mortal like me would be able to make them feel fear. And it wouldn't do good for a fight scene where the person currently in the spotlight cannot show off, therefore…

"Damn mortal…! You think you can play around with us like that!?"

"Kill him!"

Two of the fallen angels flapped their wings, launching themselves at me with a great burst of speed. Shimmering light appeared on their hands which solidified into spears; raising them up, they aimed to stab me with their weapons.

Naturally, I didn't let them.

Their movements were polished, having lived for a millenia or longer and thus experienced in the arts of war. Yet for all their grace and martial ability they were still slow enough that I had to wait for them to reach me first before using that opportunity to meet their attacks.

I settled myself into a stance, then just before their spears would've skewered me—I moved.

Between my fingers, I caught the head of the spear stabbing to my face and made it stop completely. In that same movement, I also leaned my body to the side by stepping one leg back to avoid the other spear stabbing me in the heart. It's not a practical way to defend myself from the attack, but the thing is that doesn't matter.

Which leads to the final step.

Show-off the difference in power. Make a show of how you completely outclass them when the spotlight is pointed right towards you. A brazen act like that emphasizes just how much I outlevel them, upstaging them completely and turning them into mooks.

Then, in the spirit of every action anime where a character tries to show off, these mooks will then say—

"What!? (Nani!?)"

In that moment of melodramatic shock, I used that window of opportunity to attack them. They didn't register me moving in a burst of speed and lashing out my fists towards their bodies. With combined knowledge of martial arts and applying magecraft, my fists dug into their guts and ignored their innate angel durabilities, spittle coughed out their mouths as I hit their knockout button and made their eyes roll up.

Their bodies fell to the ground as it lost strength. They didn't stand back up.

I let out a breath.

And that, kids, is how you do a curbstomp.

I turned to the last female fallen angel, the one who hadn't attacked me, and I found her dropping to the ground from losing the strength of her legs as she openly stared at me with fear in her eyes.

"Don't do anything stupid now.." I told her. "I'm going to ask you some questions, and if you answer I'll leave you alone."

"A-Ah…" she stammered.

Before I could do anything though, I heard hurried footsteps coming right beside me. I turned around to see that it was the heroine. With wide eyes she looked at me, to the fallen angels, then back to me again.

"What the heck was that!?" she almost shrieked.

I raised a brow. "What are you so surprised about? I'm sure you know I'm not exactly normal."

She hesitated at that. "No, but those movements… that wasn't magic now, was it?"

"Well I guess it's pretty unbelievable when seeing it for the first time. Yeah, that was martial arts. It's not magic, but there are moments where it gets just as ridiculous that it might as well be one." the amount of 'styles' I saw born out of nebulous logic… seriously, there's so much. I shook my head. "Anyway, time to find out more about this whole thing. Hey, you."

"Y-Yes!" the female fallen angel answered fearfully.

"Tell us what's the deal with this kidnapping thing."

The fallen angel did just that, squealing out their plans for us to hear.

It appeared that they were kidnapping these people as a sacrifice.to power some ritual in order to open a gateway to hell. They were apparently sent here and were ordered by their higher ups. The magic circle was to act as an alternative pathway in order for them to allow clandestine operations after allying with some demon noble scion in hell as they plotted stuff, yada yada.

"Then our boss would arrive in this town so that he would get rid of the demon this city and—"

"Yeah, it's fine. You can stop now." I said, stopping her.

The heroine frowned. "Rid of the demon in this city? Does that mean they want to fight Satanichia-san? She's involved with this?"

"She usually involves herself with the supernatural, so yes, she'll be involved. Especially when demons are in the picture." I answered. "Well, I guess that answers that. Get those people out here by the way, I'll just be hypnotizing these people so that they'll think they completed the ritual. Probably heal them too so they wouldn't notice anything wrong."

The heroine nodded her head in agreement, heading towards the kidnapped people and doing just that. However, she stopped.

"Wait." she called out. "There are some people missing here."

"Ah, right." I frowned and glanced around the basement. "About that… that's different."

It was something that I noticed when we arrived at the church that I started to think that there was more to this than I thought.

If one were to observe this place closely and take note of whatever details you can find, it's easy to see that there was something strange in the place and that it wasn't just a simple base of operations for these fallen angels.

This basement's moss-ridden walls exhibited wear and tear that indicated that this place had been around for a long time. This place looked ancient, looking similar enough to the ruins of a dungeon - and for a person sensitive enough to the supernatural, they can feel the corrupted energies suffused on its bricks being far older than expected.

This basement, whatever it is, predated the church that was built above it. In fact, it was probable that the church was built here because of this place. Something to stave off whatever was in here; a place that was enough to attract fallen angels due to how much corruptive energies it exudes.

Then there was also the fact that the heroine missed in her investigations and something that I included in my own. It's true that there are mysterious disappearances in this place, but the truth was it was already happening even before the fallen angels - albeit in a far spaced out manner. In a manner of years, at most.

I had suspicions on what dwells in this basement.

Turning to the heroine who looked confused at my reply to her, I spoke. "Grit your teeth."

My finger snapped, and a burst of mana spilled out around me that unwound the hidden seal in the local space. The dispelling magic worked its way around, then eventually reached a crack in the seal that was spilling corrupted energy that seeped out to the materium, widening it, then eventually making it disappear.

Then the world cracked and revealed something despicable.


Spoiler

It was hard to look at, yet the best it could be described as is a formless mesh of false flesh with three eyes and a grinning pseudo-mouth. In a way, it looked like a woman and maybe even a nun wearing a veil, but only if it was viewed in the right angle and with darkness surrounding it. It was a parody of a human being, like a predator mimicking something so that it may attract its prey.

And from its appearance a terrible suffocating pressure pressed upon the area. The mere sight of it invoked a feeling of revulsion, terror, and helplessness rolled into one, and it seemed like whatever this thing is, it was meant to be feared. Because that's what it essentially was; fear made manifest.

A horror monster.

I stared at the eldritch monster calmly.

"Let's get this over with."
