Sorry again for the long wait. The finals term happened in a single week then exams the week after that, and then after that we worked on thesis defense. It was hell.

Anyhow, here goes the next chapter.

Chapter 6

I hate horror monsters.

Now that statement may come off as unexpected. I, Basa-kun, have explored every genre of this world thoroughly that there are so many things about it that don't bother me anymore - so why would I be scared of horror monsters? Shouldn't there be more things to be scared of, like in a normal action setting perhaps?

But the thing is, I'm not scared of horror. And that's not a statement of denial to assuage my pride or anything. Because, let me reiterate, I am not scared of horror monsters.

I hate it.

See, monsters are the staple of the horror genre - stories that were meant to spook people by making characters live out terrifying experiences. Something that they might survive but more than likely would not.

And in a ridiculous anime world like this, where the people are given certain roles from the moment they're born out of their mother's womb, what else perfectly encapsulates the unfairness and cruelty of the world giving such a grim fate towards its denizens just for a story? What else shows just how little your free will is in this world and what it means to live here?

Fate leads the unwilling, and drags along the reluctant. That is to say not all fates are bad; some live peaceful, if not outright just happier lives. But such a fate is a privilege that can be decided essentially by how lucky you are. And some aren't just that fortunate.

Which is why I hate horror monsters. I hate what they are - and especially, what they represent.

But, I digress.

"—Ah!"

From the sudden appearance of the monster, the heroine let out a choked gasp. The first time of getting exposed to a horror monster was a memorable one. I myself had a similar reaction when I first encountered one and only got used to the instilled fear by repeated exposure to recognize that the feeling was false. And also the fact that I've encountered things worse than it was helping tremendously.

Impressively, the heroine seemed to have the resilience to withstand its terrifying presence and not get overwhelmed with the sudden sensation of fear - she grit her teeth and shook in place, but her legs didn't lose strength and she remained standing.

In contrast, the fallen angel shrieked in fear and was staring at the monster with wide fearful eyes. Her body, still on the floor, was paralyzed even as she shook in place.

"W-What, what is that?" the heroine stuttered out in fear.

I glanced back at the monster. "It's a creature from the horror genre. Likely the source of the corruption in this church." I answered. "I should've realized that if there was a place that it'll be at, it would be here. It was probably 'hibernating' inside the damaged seal in this basement after a recent victim and which made it ignore the fallen angels when they arrived."

In short, this church had been the setting for two different plots. The genre divide probably worked to give some string of coincidences so that the fallen angels wouldn't meet this monster - and it would probably continue for other different plots that could involve this church.

As for what exactly this monster was, I do not know exactly. I do have an idea of what exactly the situation is though with the environment around me painting it out. It was probably a spirit captured in the older times and its seal had been damaged at some point, perhaps due to an unfortunate accident or just because of time. That caused the corrupted energy to leak out, causing the land to become cursed, and is mitigated by the building of this church above it.

Judging by the current state of this church it seems to have failed. What's more, the monster had taken it into account in its hunt for victims. Since it kind of looks like a nun, it was probably hunting around any poor soul around here looking like that, making them let their guard down and allow them to approach. Of course, this leads to a reveal that they're not really looking at something human.

Then, they'll get killed. Or perhaps escape. But the mere fact that this monster wasn't defeated even in such a long time meant that this will continue again and again, taking the lives of victims subjected to the tragic fate of a horror character.

I frowned. Not for long.

The monster turned its eyes to me, being the nearest one after being suddenly forced into wakefulness. I could sense malice from its deformed face and the terrible pressure multiplied as it focused its attention on me.

—I may have said to the heroine that sometimes the best thing to do is to leave things alone in the plot, but this is one of the exceptions. Horror stories rarely end with things getting better - they usually end in some tragedy with lives lost, or worse, show that the monster is alive in some way.

What's more, the scope of the story is usually small and is limited to the monster and its victims. That means that if I were to get rid of the monster, then it wouldn't be like the case of intervening with large plots where the effects of my actions could potentially make things worse further down the line.

Therefore, there's no reason that these things shouldn't be purged without hesitation.

The monster's face stretched inhumanly, its mouth grinning with a creepy smile as its three eyes set itself on my form. I wasn't making my mana circuits open nor was exuding any particular energy so to it, I was just prey - a normal human that can be subjected to its torture and malice. It then started to lumber toward me.

And I walked towards it in kind.

"Wait, Basa-kun!" the heroine shouted out, voice cracking slightly. "What are you—"

I raised up a hand.

Holy Evocation. Purification Spiritual Breathing. Essence Destruction. Flames of Exorcism. Sealing Arts: Hakai. Supernatural Nullification. Burning Star of Annihilation. Ravage Ectoplast. Bladeless Spiritual Cutting. All of that, and many more.

The various spells, magics, skills, abilities and martial arts that I thought would be appropriate - I brought it all up and integrated them together in a flawless combination. I focused it all on the tip of my pointing finger, and the digit suddenly lit up like a bright star as the concentrated energies turned into a unified whole.

The monster paused for a brief moment as it registered that I was no normal prey, but it was too late.

I touched it with my finger.

There was a moment of silence, both infinite and instant in length in time as if reality had lagged slightly trying to parse the different systems I strung up together, then space warped at the point I had touched the monster as all the abilities I brought up worked together in tandem.

Then a large chunk of the monster's upper body exploded in a shower of gore, and everything took on a lighter atmosphere as the terrifying receded almost instantaneously.

Sighing, I wiped away the blood that had stained my face. I was completely in the blast zone of the gore, and now I'm covered in blood, viscera, and whatever else fluids that thing has. "...I was sure Flames of Exorcism and Burning Star would've boiled the blood off this time." I muttered, tone clipped, before blinking when the blood staining me felt boiling hot and it was actually hissing. "Hm. Not enough heat to completely vaporize then. Or maybe unique to the physiology of the monster? I guess I'll find out."

I turned back towards the heroine. "Alright, we're done here. You can… Hm?"

The heroine had a silly expression with her mouth wide open, as if unable to believe what she just saw. Beside her, the fallen angel was sprawled on the floor, mouth foaming and completely catatonic.

"Y-You… t-that…" the heroine tried to speak.

I raised a brow. "You good?"

She inhaled sharply and tried to visibly calm herself down. "...Forgive me, these past few minutes have been… trying."

I stare at her for a few seconds. "You know, there's no need to act tough. It's okay to feel bothered by what you saw."

She opened her mouth, about to say something, but she stopped and grit her teeth. "I'm fine." she insisted.

Okay, then.

I shrugged. "Well if you're going to be like that, you can go gather those kidnapped people above while I deal with everything here. I'll clean up the mess and clear the memories of the fallen angels."

After saying my piece, I glanced back at the monster's body and examined it closely. The horror monster was the type that was incorporeal judging by the flesh and gore was dispersing into wisps. My guess would be that it's some type of curse made manifest, kinda like that particular supernatural action setting that I encountered once.

Anyways, the body's mine now. I could study it or maybe make use of it as material, as horror monsters are magical creatures in their own right. Still, I should probably get moving before the corpse disappears completely.

Activating a spell, I touched the floor and summoned a glowing magic circle filled with formulae which surrounded the corpse which then started to ascend slowly, passing through it and sending it to my subspace where it will be preserved completely. I stood back up and waited for the whole process to shortly finish.

"..."

I turned to the heroine, who was still standing there, unmoving. "...Are you just going to stay there? I thought you'd have wanted to help those kidnapped as fast as possible?"

"...It won't move."

"What?"

The heroine glanced to the side. "I can't… I can't move my legs."

I gave her a flat look for a few seconds, before palming my face with a sigh.

"See, this is why I told you to not act tough. I'll go help the people who were kidnapped while you recover." I walked towards the humans near the corner of the basement. "I swear, you better not have peed yourself while you're at it. I'm not going near you and make my quirk act if you did."

"Wha—!? I-I did not!"

After cleaning up the basement and the strategic use of hypnotism to deal with the loose ends, we now have the police managing to rescue a bunch of kidnapped people from an abandoned church who they found sedated in a hidden basement. This will definitely be on the news tonight as many would be disturbed by a serial kidnapper present in the neighborhood, unknowing of the fact that they were now safe from a far worse evil.

Alongside that, the fallen angels would also think that they successfully completed the ritual that needed human sacrifices in order to activate a portal to hell instead of me just powering it open. It took a bit of my magical reserves, but I believe it is needed so that whatever plot they belong to will move forward. No chance of it being led straight to me, of course. I made sure of it.

All that accomplished in around a single hour after breakfast on our way to school. It was a productive start to the day all things considered, and there's still about a couple of hours left before class starts. Plenty of time for us to not be late.

As we walked, the heroine was completely silent. Her expression was that of being filled with thought, absorbing everything that had happened in the past hour, because while she may have an idea of the supernatural and all the other things beyond her setting - this was the first time she was exposed to it in full.

I stopped on my tracks, prompting the heroine to look up from her pondering and do so as well.

"If we go further from here we'll have other students seeing us," I explained before she could voice out her question. "So unless you want to have some rumors about you hanging out with someone like me, then we'll have to separate here. You go past this street while I go there."

She blinked. "Ah, yes. Of course."

The heroine walked forward a bit, but her legs stopped moving after a few steps.

"...Is it always like this?" she suddenly asked.

I gave her a curious look. "What do you mean?"

She turned around, staring at me straight in the eye. "I'm asking if this is normally how it goes for you. You deal with these kinds of things everyday, is that correct?"

"Yeah?" I answered with a raised brow.

For a second she seemed unsure, but it was quickly smothered in but a moment when she took a deep breath.

"Please teach me magic." she implored. "I want to help."

My brows furrowed.

"...Didn't I tell you to not let your issues dictate you? You don't have to feel responsible for risking your life to help others when you have your own life to live."

She shook her head. "N-No. I'm not…" she paused. "I… perhaps I still feel the need to hold myself responsible to help others, but it's not the reason I'm asking so right now. No, I'm doing so because I think it's the right thing to do."

She gave me a determined look; the certainty held in her gaze made it so that it wouldn't be too out of place on many shounen protagonists.

"I want to help you in your mission of dealing with these different… plots. And I want to learn magic so I may assist you."

I stared at her in silence.

She uneasily fidgeted in place as her request remained unanswered.

"O-Or am I being a hindrance? I certainly have been bothering you these past couple days, aren't I? My presence would have slowed your plans somewhat." she sighed. "I-If that's the case, I understand. You can erase my memories so that you could go back to doing your—"

I raised a hand, making her stop.

Then I grinned.

"Sure." I answered.

The heroine paused. "Eh?"

I brought my hand down. "You want to help? Sure. I'll teach you some magic too." I shrugged. "I'll warn you that I'm a strict teacher though. So you better prepare yourself."

She blinked in surprise, before shaking it off and nodding. "Y-Yes. Thank you."

I shook my head. "No. If anything, I should be thanking you." I said to her. "Let's meet at my apartment again if you want to start learning."

Walking past the stunned heroine, I waved a hand as I went on my way.

"Looking forward to working with you, Yuki."

The broad back of the young man who had defeated beings of myths and horror not even a few hours prior had retreated, eventually disappearing once he crossed the street.

…He finally called me by my name.

That was what Yuki had thought as she watched her enigmatic classmate walk away, slightly surprised that he actually chose to do so after all the times he had kept called her 'heroine'.

And the way he grinned victoriously earlier, as if he was waiting for her to say all that…

According to Basa-kun, reality works like a story. That meant that to him, perhaps, she was nothing but a heroine and never will be anything else. A simple character without any true depth.

Was that her passing some sort of test? Was that his way of telling Yuki that he acknowledges her? That to him, she wasn't just some character acting on a narrative?

Basa-kun acted aloof and uninterested around everyone in general. Her classmates thought of it as him being arrogant, but if one were to see reality his way, then there was a divide between others and him that kept him from ever relating to them. Only two people - that being his neighbor Aoki-san and his old classmate Rias - seemed to have been the exception. And even in the short time she had met them she knew that they were undoubtedly people he cherished.

It was flattering, she supposed, for her to be acknowledged by him.

Perhaps the Yuki of yesterday wouldn't say that at any point but seeing what he had done this morning had changed her impression of him tremendously. She had thought of him as a thug with supernatural powers, but it was clear that Basa-kun was helping others as much as he could. He was, quite literally, an unnoticed hero.

Just how long had he been dealing with things like this? What she saw earlier - it was surreal. She still felt shivers recalling that monster underneath the Church, and yet Basa-kun treated it as an ordinary thing.

And chances are with him, it probably was.

It was humbling to see all that. Days before, her life was consumed by problems that could be boiled down to simple misunderstandings, and then you have Basa-kun fighting demons or something.

So she wanted to help. Just so to lessen the burden that a person like him must have. The ever-present need to feel responsible for others was still there, lurking in the back of her mind, but she had learned to steadily ignore it now that Basa-kun had pointed it out.

She was doing this because it is the right thing to do… and maybe because she was curious and was slightly excited to learn magic. But mostly the first part.

"Still, I suppose I should prepare myself for it." she muttered, resuming her walk.

As she pondered just how to do all that, however, she failed to notice someone in front of the school gate who seemed to have waited for her.

"Yuki-san!"

Yuki jerked slightly at her name being called, and turned her attention to someone she had avoided in the past few days. The aloof and stoic boy with black and messy hair that was part of her club, along with the bubbly Kaede.

"M-Makoto-kun…" she said in surprise. "What are you doing here?"

Spoiler: Literally most generic anime boy

Her clubmate raised a hand in greeting and approached her, giving her a slight smile. "Good morning, Yuki-san. I was just waiting for something to arrive - you know, about the request we received yesterday?"

She tilted her head. "Was there? I don't quite recall any request like that."

"A-Ah, it must have been the day before then." he corrected, averting his eyes as he did so. "You… weren't there."

Yuki slowly nodded. That was when she had met Basa-kun when she encountered the stray demon.

They descended into slight silence. The air between them was uncertain, with what had happened in the festival, and now she didn't really know how to deal with it. It was as if there was a wall separating between them now.

Though she noticed that it wasn't as oppressive as it was before. A change on her part. She wondered if it was because of the literal oppressive presence she had felt an hour ago.

And more than that, she was starting to wonder… was it really that big of a deal in the first place? Sure it was awkward, but it's a natural consequence of being uncertain. One that could be solved by clear communication. And yet… she never thought of that.

Was this what Basa-kun had meant with drama characters being dumb and creating their own drama?

"I see." she finally said after a while of silence, shelving the epiphany for later. "I hope you can complete the request then." she paused. "...By the way, is it alright for us to talk later at the club, Makoto-kun?"

He blinked in surprise. "Ah, we will? I-I mean, sure. Let's talk."

Yuki smiled. It's about time they deal with the tension between them anyway.

"Great. I'll see you and Kaede there."


"Home sweet home." I muttered as I closed the door behind me. After the fiasco during the morning it had been a full day of monitoring the city and other places I tagged, along with studying the horror monster corpse inside my subspace while half-heartedly listening to class. A bit of an uneventful day, all things considered.

That is, if you didn't count the events this morning. Now that is something that I'm getting excited about.

Exterminating horror monsters was good and all, and whatever was happening to Rias' plot remained untouched. But that wasn't what I was excited about; it was what happened after, with the heroine firmly requesting to involve herself to my cause.

There was a choice for her to want to have a normal life, choosing to stay within the confines of her genre despite exhibiting the ability to bypass it. It would be deadly, considering she might stumble upon action settings again like when we first met, and she'd be defenseless. But despite the risks there was always a chance for her to choose so.

However, she didn't choose it. Instead she chose to do what she thought was right. She wanted to assist me, helping me in my quest to not let plots devolve into disasters. That meant plenty of opportunities; opportunities for lessened workload due to someone helping me, opportunities for another mind to serve as a second opinion…

Opportunities for study of another being capable of ignoring this world's very nature.

My lips quirked up into a smile, the giddiness I felt earlier returning back to me. The road to true understanding was a long one, but with her presence it would be shortened quite a bit. The notebook I carried and the notes filling its pages just from this morning's observations can testify to that.

Still, with that done and the heroine coming to learn some magic, it'll have to be after school club hours before I could actually do anything. Plus I already drafted a lesson plan for the heroine to learn during school hours, so there wasn't really anything for me to do now.

Whenever in times like these I usually visited Aoki-san and hang out with her, maybe have some fun ravishing her sexy milf body until she and I were satisfied, but she won't be back in a few hours after returning to work.

That meant I was left with free time with nothing to do… which really just meant shenanigans coming inbound. Because that's how this world works.

So, I found myself completely unsurprised when stomps from further in the living room alerted me of another presence in the apartment.

"Basaaaaa!!!"

And before I knew it, I was face to face with an angry redhead demon girl.

"Hello, Rias." I greeted flatly.

"You!" she shouted, pointing her finger straight at my face. "You have some explaining to do, mister!"

I sighed.

This is going to be troublesome.

Chapter 7

I stared flatly as the redhead in front of me started to rant about something or another.

"—I know that you know what's happening! I should've known when you were acting all mysterious and smug that you were expecting something to happen!" she pointed at me aggressively. "Well, guess what, I know that you know it too!"

"The hell are you on about?" I deadpanned.

"Stop playing dumb!"

"No, really, I have no idea what you're saying."

She puffed her cheeks. "I'm talking about Ryuusei-kun! You knew about what would happen to him, right! And you must have summoned me somehow so that I could defend him from the fallen angel!"

My eyes widened, slightly shocked—

"Hah! See! I knew it was you!" she said in smug satisfaction after noticing my reaction. "There's no way you'll deny it now!"

"Ah, well. I was just slightly surprised that you'd noticed it. I didn't think that you would. At all." I put a hand on her shoulder and patted it, making her blink. "Good job for that, I suppose." I congratulated.

"...W-Why are you acting like that's a great achievement for me? Did you really think I wouldn't notice?" she said indignantly. "What do you think I am, an idiot!?"

I put my hand down. "Anyway, what were you talking about again?"

"Don't ignore the question! You totally think I am, don't you!"

The redhead then sighed, slumping down in a depressed manner, and my flat stare aimed at her form remained unchanging as she started to groan pitifully.

"Mouu, Basa-kun… can you please just tell me what I'm going to do now? You know what's going to happen, don't you? I need your help!" she pleaded.

"What happened to not believing that this world runs on narrative rules?" I said, raising a brow. "I distinctly remember you denying that multiple times. Why change that now?"

"That was then, this is now!" she said in complete conviction and shamelessness.

I scratched my head and sighed. "...Yeah yeah, go tell me what's happening then."

The redhead then started to explain to me what was happening in her club. Since Rias was familiar with anime tropes - with her guilty pleasure being reading trashy light novels and watching bad anime - she had it correct that she was a heroine in the protagonist's story of becoming special in the supernatural world. And now, she came to me because she doesn't want to fall in love with the protagonist.

"—So you see, I'm trying to find a way to deal with it." she fretted, biting the nail of her thumb as she started pacing in the middle of her explanation, before whipping her head around to face me with hope burning in her eyes. "But you must know something about that, right!? I mean, you're the leading expert here!"

I stared at her.

"Nah, I think it's over for you."

My words visually stabbed itself to her heart, making her back away clutching her chest. "E-Eh?"

"You'll be part of his harem no matter what you do. Try to resist and you'll eventually warm up to him, try to go along without meaning it and it'll lead to the same result." my words uppercutted her this time. "All roads lead to defeat. You'll be riding on his dick before you even notice it." a punch to the gut.

She slumped on the floor, weakly bringing a hand up in surrender. "N-No… no more…!"

I brought a hand to my chin, slightly pondering on how to voice out my thoughts, before shrugging.

Rias clenched her fists. Yosh! She was feeling pumped up!

"Just watch me, Basa-kun." she whispered. "It doesn't matter even if you think it's not possible. I'll change whatever plot is coming to me and make it better!"

"Because… I'm going to be the protagonist of my own story!"

I looked up, suddenly feeling disturbed.

"Damn, even the ceiling." I grumbled as I tried to check how much I needed to fix from Rias' earlier mess. "And she chewed through all the wards too. She really went ahead and threw all her might from that attack, huh?"

Well, I guess I was a bit too mean and blunt to her earlier, but still.

...Hold on. I paused and considered what just happened.

I just suddenly looked up like I felt something happening from some sixth sense. The senseTM​ itself didn't activate though, but it certainly looked like it did... And that's just what really matters in the end, isn't it?

Sighing, I scratched the back of my head.

"I guess I need to prepare for something happening again…"

Chapter 8

It was noon in the city. Things were going according to schedule.

The view of the target was clear, as he chose a good spot for his mission to be carried out beforehand - the residential building remained in full view despite being a few kilometers away from it, while from their standpoint, he was covered and protected by other buildings for cover. Plenty of escape routes too in case things go wrong; he didn't think he'd need them, but it never hurts to be too careful.

His coat fluttered against the winds as he stood on top of the building as he held the highly advanced binoculars up to his eyes. He tracked his target, who wore a jacket with its hood up to cover his face, entering the residential building. To an outsider the man looked nothing special whatsoever, getting easily lost in a crowd, maybe even giving off the impression of a pathetic unemployed shut-in. Yet he knew that the person had intentionally crafted the cover for himself.

This was the person who was responsible for the murders downtown. The victims were killed in what looked like a ritualistic manner, leading local news outlets to pick up some interest in it, especially with people still rapt in the recent news of people returning from a mass kidnapping incident. Conspiracy theorists assert ridiculous statements that it was creatures of horror or demons. The police, however, had thought it had been the work of a serial killer. But in truth… it was far, far worse.

He had investigated the crime scene himself. The right amount of paperwork from his field of work and a few applications of the newly developed memory altering devices let him grant access. And once there, he had undoubtedly confirmed the suspicions that he had held - it was no ritualistic murder, but rather, the victims' lives were used as fuel. A fuel for attaining power.

For the person who had been responsible for the incident… was nothing else but a "warlock". A person who wields a great weapon in his hands, capable of hurting great many people. A person who will eventually have descendants in the future which will obtain a great amount of power. A person who was chosen as a contestant for some strange death game that will alter the course of their future.

Spoiler: Edgy boi

A person like him.

"My lord." a soft but firm voice called him from behind, making him put down the binoculars and turn around.

Flowing white hair like snow, and a form that can only be described as beautiful. She was dressed in strange garbs, her robes embedded with an aesthetic that resembled futuristic design which held no functionality, yet he wasn't fooled by it as it disguised a large amount of circuitry embedded underneath its covers. On her hip was a device resembling a gun but functioned as more - a "wand", a tool of great destruction used by warriors of the future.


Spoiler

She was what was called a witch. A being of great destruction in the future, called in the present to participate in a secret war of their future descendants for some wish-granting device which would alter the future she belonged to. It was all very complicated, but it remains that she must follow his orders, as her warlock.

"What is it?" he asked.

"The preparations are finished, as you had ordered." she answered, neutral face bearing no emotion, yet he could still feel a hint of disapproval through their cerebral bond.

"Is that so?" he turned back to the building. "Very well."

There was a slight silence as he waited for his target to reach the position.

"...Should it really come to this?" the witch spoke up once more after a while. "Surely, there must be some other alternative we can do?"

"You should know by now finding solutions where everyone lives is naive." he muttered, tone cold. "Every action we hesitate to do will lead to more deaths. The target is an expert at escaping authorities of countless nations, and now he has the power of a witch with him. This is the best time, his most vulnerable time, that we can utilize to end him. Enough to ensure that he won't be using the Sangraal for whatever wish his future descendants want."

"But does that warrant killing all these people!?" she shouted, composure finally broken. "Ensuring the enemy is defeated, I understand, but if it means that all these bystanders are killed—!"

"Astra." he called her name sharply. "You are a soldier. Act like it, and follow your orders."

His interruption made her close her mouth. His steady gaze clashed against her own mutinous glare… which eventually ended with the witch gritting her teeth and looked away sharply. No further protestations came forth from her. The turbulent anger, disappointment, and betrayal he keenly felt through their bond however showed her own feelings on the matter.

He didn't care what she felt, only that she gave him results.

He returned to using the binoculars once more, and he watched as the target reached his own room in the residential building as the door opened. He watched the almost imperceptible relaxing of his shoulders from a human's unconscious reflex of letting their guard down in a perceived safe place. He watched as the person walked up to the window of his room and looked into the city below.

And he watched, as he clicked the detonator on his hand, as the man died from the fiery explosion.

The primed bombs which were installed throughout the various weak points in the buildings where he wouldn't think of looking all exploded at once, causing a loud booming noise that could be heard even from where they are, kilometers away from the place.

And to add further fuel to the fire the entire place collapsed, burying the man and others who unfortunately got caught up into them, and turning what was once a residential building into a graveyard of concrete and tempered steel.

He confirmed his kill. There were no signs of his own witch coming out anywhere - and if there was a time that it should've revealed itself, it would be now. A few more moments of nothing appearing had led him assured that the witch had gone back to its own timeline after the warlock was killed.

He brought down the binoculars.

"We're done here." he muttered, turning around and walking away as he did so.

"...As you command." the witch answered quietly, the hollowness in her voice reaching his ears.

He tried to ignore it. They had done the world some good. The death of a few hundred civilians wouldn't compare to the countless lives of those from the future. The monster responsible for killing many had disappeared, along with his own monstrous descendants that would bring misery to many others in the future.

And it didn't matter if he became a monster on his own to do it.

I watched as the super-duper edgy-wedgy protagonist walked away from the building roof, coat fluttering coolly against the wind, with his heroine trailing right behind him from kilometers away. Waiting for a moment I made sure that they were completely gone out of range.

"Alright, they're gone." I called out.

Surrounding me were the concrete rubble which the residential building had turned to. It was a scene of morbid destruction, but if one were to look closely, things were "miraculously" contained without hitting any nearby buildings or pedestrians. It also happened that the place was entirely quiet and lacking any screams from a disaster like this - and while that can be explained by a sobering realization that all people within the building are dead, there are also no hints of dead bodies around.

And that's because there is no one around to actually die. We arranged things for the residential building, with the help of the right paperwork and use of hypnosis, so that the residents would have to leave for some "renovations". As of now, the families and other tenants in this place were somewhere else, probably slightly annoyed at the suddenness of them being kicked out, before immediately turning grateful at their fortune of not getting caught in the destruction.

Well, all of them except for one.

"Graaagh!" there was a shout followed by a rumbling from nearby.

I glanced to the side when the rubble then exploded, revealing a person underneath. It was obviously the serial killer that the edgy protagonist was trying to kill. He was the only one not given the notice for the renovation and would've been the only one present from the bomb's explosion.

He was fated to die today - I checked with my countless divination magic. But our intervention to evacuate the other residents made the outcomes unclear. I thought we'd be fortunate enough for him to get killed but it doesn't look like that's the case.

The person standing in front of me barely resembled a person - his body parts were in tatters, showing the horrifying butchery a person would turn into if they were bombed by an explosive, but instead of actual gore he was instead leaking black ichor instead of blood and held various circuitry in his insides instead of organs. The black ichor moved like it had a mind of its own as it tried to cover his various bits in an effort to keep the person alive.

That's probably what the whole serial killing was about. He harvested those victims for body modification. I did notice some organs missing on the bodies here and there. That was probably the unique ability of his witch.

"What the hell is happening!?" the serial killer shouted in rage, voice twisted and distorted from his tattered lungs and as monstrous as his form as the black ichor started to envelop him more and more. "Witch! Tell me what—!" he looked around. "Witch, where the fuck are you! Show yourself, can't you see I'm fucking injured!"

The man kept shouting, yet no matter how much he called the witch won't arrive. My fault, actually. I blocked them. Teehee.

He growled when no witch appeared. "Useless, useless!" he glanced around. "...No matter, I can recover from this, I've recovered from worse! I only need to,,,!" he spotted me, who was just standing to the side of the rubble.

Then, he grinned malevolently at me. It didn't look good. I mean, he didn't have a face after all.

"A chance!" he started running at me. "Stay still, and let me consume you—!"

Perhaps if he were a bit more calm, he would've noticed the fact that there was something wrong with seeing a person just standing in the middle of the rubble without a scratch. He would've also noticed that I was unreacting despite his monstrous form as any normal person would've run away from terror. And perhaps, most importantly, if he were to notice all that and use his cybernetic augmentations…

He would've noticed that I wasn't alone.

"—Grk!" the serial killer flinched. He stopped in place suddenly, and he looked down.

There was a blade stabbed through his chest.

The serial killer then quickly died as the katana swerved and cut his entire torso diagonally. More black ichor spilled, but this time there was no saving him. The circuits inside his body sparked… and the serial killer died.

Yuki swung her sword to the side, flicking off the ichor from the blade, before sheathing it back to her scabbard. She looked a little bit green.

I gave her a scrutinizing look. "You alright?"

"I…" she shook her head and looked away. "No, I'm not. But I was doing the world a favor by getting rid of him." she grit her teeth. "I'll get over this."

It was her first time taking a life after all. I made sure to warn her of this particular mission and was about to do it myself, but she volunteered, saying that she ought to get used to it. A bit of a morbid reason, all things considered, but a necessary one in this line of work.

Still, who knows what's going on in that drama character mind of hers. Best she be monitored.

"Is that so?"

"Yes." she answered, taking one last look at the corpse before approaching me. "The next thing is cleaning up, then?"

I took her unsaid offer to change the subject, glancing around the destruction surrounding us. "No need, I already took care of that. All we need to do is to leave a fake body in place of this one." and boy am I skilled in making fake bodies. It's a skill I didn't think I'd learn and be good at. "Good job on your part, by the way. You're getting skilled with your sword."

She frowned. "Am I? I just caught him by surprise." she brought something out of her pocket, revealing the handkerchief with the memetic bounded field to disguise her presence. She looked at it thoughtfully. "This handkerchief just made him not notice me until it was too late."

"No, I definitely saw improvement. You target your sword unconsciously on the more vulnerable parts to make a cleaner kill. That's a sign of you getting more synchronized with your weapon." my correction surprised her. "And you did great utilizing that handkerchief with you. I gave you that as a test; you have much more tools at your disposal since you can cross settings, so it wouldn't do good depending on one power like your spirit weapon. You passed splendidly."

The heroine blinked at that. Perhaps unconsciously her usual calm facade softened briefly into a hidden smile, showing a hint of lifted spirits in response to my praise, although returning to her composed and regal expression. "I see." she muttered.

"It's yours now, by the way." I gestured to the cloth on her hand. "Let's see… as another test, try to modify the bounded field so it can be switched on and off. I should've taught you the necessary knowledge to do that already. Try to accomplish it before we arrive at school before I tell you how; I'll just deal with the body shortly."

Yuki nodded and wasted no time doing so, concentrating every bit of effort on her task. Ever the honor student I suppose, but I guess her desire to focus on other things instead of what she did earlier was also a factor.

I turned around and went to the body to start cleaning up, and things went smoothly after that. We left before the authorities with various news reporters on their tow managed to arrive, with the news certainly reporting of the miraculous incident that happened today.

Of course I'll be monitoring the investigation and make sure they do the usual "gas leaks" or "structural failure" excuse that they always seem to do.

Anyhow… mission success.

In the end, the heroine successfully was able to add a switch array to her handkerchief and we managed to arrive back at the school before lunch was finished. I managed to grab something to eat and for my efforts I was rewarded by me accidentally spilling juice on myself.

The school day proceeded as normal. I paid half-attention to the school teachers as they continued discussing topics that I already know by heart, and I went ahead and used my free time to do more productive things in the back of my head.

Like for example: did you know that there is a brain-centered martial art which lets me have eidetic memory? I can remember things from first glance, making me do stuff like reading books in my own mind. Of course, it's supposed to be some dangerous forbidden art or whatever that makes your brain explode from the sheer information, but that's fixed by my multiple minds from thought partitions.

Then there's also the fact that I can access my subspace mentally, allowing me to perform experiments and tests on the various stuff I hoarded inside. I did have my own lab and testing site in my apartment which has its own sets of tools and machinery for occasions like that, but it's a huge time saver for me.

And judging my new haul, the body of this "warlock" is certainly interesting. It's riddled with many machinery and circuitry that would make a modern engineer's mind boggle. I've seen future tech before from other settings though, so I'm recognizing some components here and there. I could probably work out their functions and how to fabricate them before the day ends if things go to schedule.

So while some of my thought processes devote themselves into doing that, the others were more focused on the surroundings and, out of boredom, I found myself looking at the heroine.

Again, just staring at her reminded me of how much she looked like the textbook heroine. Cold beauty, sitting by a window, and holding a book like a diligent student - this girl is the Yamato Nadeshiko cliché in many school settings. I've seen many girls that look like her and act like her, with only slight variations like the same product from different brands in an effort to make them unique.

And now, she was occasionally talking to people who were seated near her. A second heroine, the bubbly genki girl which contrasts with the frigid ice queen, and a boy who looked out of place - the silent, thoughtful loner that is the place of insertion for the average japanese reader.

Oddly they looked less awkward than they were before. There are some hints of it still, but visibly less than what I'd expect from drama characters like them. Maybe they made up or whatever. Clearly something was up though, especially when you consider the occasional worried glances from their friend group of supporting characters led by, most likely, the foil to the loner protagonist.


Spoiler

Perhaps the effects of the heroine's ability to cross genre boundaries are already manifesting. I'd say I was interested in finding out more privacy be damned, but I respect the choices that she makes as someone unbound by plot. It would be hypocritical for me to do so when I had done the same.

The only thing I can do is to advise her not to create any detrimental changes - something that she probably knew after our work first hand.

I paused, then considered that statement in my head. The thought that I've been deliberating ever since I met the heroine returned, and just like that time, I still didn't have a full picture of what was happening.

Me taking the mentor role was something I wasn't unaware of. Yet, no matter how much I tested for any signs, I remained as a different character in the eyes of the world; fate remained untangled, and there weren't any changes in my mind that focused on the heroine. The background character role I also decided to embody was mutually exclusive in being a mentor-like figure, and so there would be signs if that changed. Yet there was none of that, leading me to my current working hypothesis.

That I was acting like a mentor… without the tropes associated with it.

Something I've never seen before since it's impossible, really. I've found that one of the constant rules from my interactions on different plots is that if you act a certain way you'll get a role, and following that you'll also gain the tropes associated with it. Yet this one is an exception.

But then again, the heroine and I aren't bound by a single plot, are we? The lack of it meant that without the plot, tropes also disappear. Which would make sense. Still it has just been a few days or so - maybe the tropes do exist and that I just need to give it time. This is the first time I interacted with someone who has the same abilities as I do after all, so this is literally new territory for me.

The existence of tropes beyond a plot is quite meta. Who knows, though?

Maybe I'm in a story of my own.

As I pondered, time went by and eventually the final subject ended and class was finally dismissed. It was then that I noticed that there was some weird atmosphere within the class, centered on blonde protagonist foil, which meant that there was some sort of drama going on again. I knew it was going to be a headache so I went ahead and packed up my things so I could leave.

When I stepped out of the door though something that I didn't expect (which is a very big deal, at the risk of sounding egotistic), stopped me from walking down the hallway and leaving school.

"Basa-kun." the heroine called out, as she stepped out into the hallway with her friend and the protagonist in tow. The two looked slightly worried as they stood behind her. "Can we have a moment of your time?"

I stared at her in response.

"...Huh?"

As I accepted her invitation from a terrible mixture of confusion and curiosity, I was brought into their little club. Their clubroom was nothing but an unused classroom with the seat and desks arranged to the side, with exception to the ones in the middle of the room. We sat there, with the two girls together on one side, the protagonist on another, and me opposite the protagonist.

I was given tea out of courtesy as we sat down all calmly, but it was clear that the atmosphere was strange. Well, the heroine looked like she didn't care, but it was obvious that the other two weren't sure how to react to this sudden development. The genki girl had this nervous smile on her face she was putting up to be polite, while the protagonist was openly glaring at me in suspicion. There was an undercurrent of fear and tension between the two of them, as if they were expecting me to attack them or something.

"So, Yanai-san." I intoned, tired of whatever was happening. "Mind telling me why you called me here?"

"I would like to know as well." the protagonist piped up. "In the first place, I didn't think you knew Basa-san here. Did something happen?"

Oi, what are you trying to imply? I can tell that he's getting suspicious that I might have done something to the heroine. Too bad, it wasn't me that did anything. It's your damn heroine that went walking headfirst into a stray demon!

The heroine, for her part, simply sipped her tea before answering. "Nothing like whatever you're implying, Makoto-kun. I have interacted with Basa-kun a few times cordially, and I can say with complete confidence that the rumors circling him are all false." she explained.

The protagonist was unconvinced though. "I don't think so. He's clearly a delinquent like what they say he is." his glare intensified. "Is he forcing you to do this or something?"

Oi, I'm right here you know. If I was actually the cliché delinquent then I might've beaten you up for that.

For her part, the heroine seemed to have thought of her answer, sparing me the effort to make my own. "Basa-kun is not a delinquent. He actually acts decently, albeit a bit blunt at times. I don't recall him being violent or anything." Yuki retorted smoothly. "Not unless you saw him acting as one?"

"I…" the protagonist blinked at Yuki's retort. "W-Well, you've seen how he acts in class! He sometimes dozes off in the middle of a lecture!"

"And yet he still passes the tests and requirements even if he doesn't listen or take notes during lecture. I'm pretty sure he actually studies ahead. In fact, I suspect he can reach my level of intellect because our scores are quite near each other."

No, I'm actually smarter than you. Why did you phrase it that way?

The fast response made the protagonist further off-balance. "W-What? N-No, you can't be serious - he colored his hair blonde and tanned his skin! He's a delinquent no matter how you look at it!"

"I thought so too but that's actually his natural appearance, just like how Haya-kun is also a natural blonde." Yuki paused. "Still, I didn't think that you'd resort to judging by how someone looks, Makoto-kun. I thought you of all people wouldn't treat others that way."

You're guilty of the same thing though.

I gave the girl a flat look, and I can't help but notice the way she deliberately didn't meet my eyes to keep her gaze on her two clubmates.

The protagonist, for his part, seemed unable to muster any response to what Yuki had said and his protest stopped. He was still glaring at me though. The genki girl seemed to notice that and she waved her arms in a placating gesture with a nervous smile.

"W-Well, let's calm down, Makoto-kun. I'm sure Yuki is planning something since she wouldn't do this without reason." she gave her friend a hopeful look. "Isn't that right?"

"Yes. I should probably explain why I brought Basa-kun here." the heroine put down her tea cup with a resounding 'clink!', and looked at her clubmates with a serious gaze. "The reason why I invited him here - is for him to act as an impartial judge between the three of us."

"...What?" me, the protagonist, and the genki girl all said so simultaneously.

"We have been talking about this the past few days, aren't we? I asked for us to forget about what happened at the school festival for a while since we're not fulfilling our requests properly, with us acting awkwardly to each other." Yuki said to her clubmates. "We cannot do that indefinitely, so I want us to set things straight today. I want to get rid of the drama between us."

Her statement made the protagonist look to the side. Her genki girl friend meanwhile looked at her with wide eyes, as if in shock at what she had decided on doing.

"Yuki…" she muttered.

"And don't worry, Basa-kun here would keep in confidence of what we'll tell him today." the heroine added, before turning to me. "Isn't that right?"

…Ah, I see now. So that's her aim, huh?

I suppose now that she's aware of how much the drama is causing trouble in her life, it's only natural for her to get rid of it and take the direct approach. Which would explain the reason why she brought me here - as the expert on the subject, she wanted me to help her and give her advice. My presence would also help not letting things devolve into drama during this straightforward approach which she probably doesn't have any confidence to enforce herself. Very logical, I like it.

I gave her an almost imperceptible nod of approval, which only the heroine caught and was relieved by judging on the slight relaxation of her shoulders, and then shrugged to continue my act of being a stranger to them.

"Yeah, I will." I nodded casually, then changed my body language to appear more friendly and displayed a more welcoming aura. The heroine blinked as she must have slightly noticed what I'd done. "So what exactly am I judging?"

For a moment she looked curious, but Yuki stopped herself in favor of looking at her fellow club members for permission. They looked unsure still, since the prospect of an unrelated person knowing their problems was something many people are not comfortable with, but their desire to finally stop whatever was happening in their club as well as the subtle effects I applied on myself made them nod.

With that, Yuki started to explain the situation. All three of them are awkward and embarrassed as she did so, but the heroine forged on despite it. My guess when I met the heroine for the first time was spot on, with her and the genki girl confessing to the protagonist during the school festival and things turning for the worse for the club's general atmosphere.

Still, it got to the point that things became too embarrassing for them.

"Yuki! I don't think Basa-kun needs to know about all that!" the genki girl shouted, completely red-faced. Opposite from my position on the table, the protagonist also stopped glaring at me and opted instead to palming his face in order to hide his own blushing cheeks.

The heroine clicked her mouth shut from her friend's shout. "A-Ah, yes. I suppose so." she stuttered out, embarrassment coloring her face as well. I guess spelling out all the awkward moments, something that a normal person would try to forget with all their might, would be too much to bear.

This was the step in the right direction though. Embarrassment is one of the major reasons why a drama character would result in doing complex and intricate actions. Clear communication, the bane of any drama, requires one to face up against the embarrassment and continue despite it.

"I think I understand enough." I spoke up. "So essentially, as an outsider, you want my view on what to do so you could fix your situation. Is that correct?"

Yuki nodded at that solemnly, although she looked like she was already expecting what I was about to say. Similarly, the genki girl bit her lip and looked down, unsure, and the protagonist tensed in his seat. I eyed all of them consideringly.

"...Well, judging by your reactions, it looks like you guys already know the answer." I gave the protagonist a level glance. "You have to pick between the two of them, casanova."

The protagonist grit his teeth. "Of course you can say that easily." he spat.

I shrugged. "Well, yeah. You guys brought me here for that purpose. Still, easy or hard, the answer remains the same; the more time you refrain from making a choice, the more this strange atmosphere will remain." I glanced to the side. "Although, I'm convinced that it's not entirely your fault that everything is like this. I'm pretty sure that the whole 'confessing at the same time' thing isn't coincidental at all."

The heroine stiffened slightly at that. Ah, so you're the culprit. I'm guessing that the genki girl here was planning to confess and you knew about that, and you were pressured to do the same thing since there's a chance for missing out on the protagonist here.

…Then again, if that was the case, genki girl should've known about her friend's attraction as well. So why would she tell—? You know what, I'm not going to delve deeper. This is just going to give me a headache.

"Anyway, I'm sure that you've been thinking deeply about the topic. You know, searching yourself, thinking about who you really like. Et cetera, et cetera." I paused. "Unless you think you can somehow manage a harem. Can you? I'll be surprised if you're thinking you can."

"Wha—!" he stuttered for a moment, then glared at me. "This isn't the time for jokes!"

I held back my desire to roll my eyes. "Just pick. Everyone here is expecting you too. And while their feelings might be hurt, it's still less worse than letting this drama unfold much more since it risks damaging their own friendships to each other. Isn't that right, ladies?"

The two girls looked at each other at that, before looking away. I could see hints of agreement in their faces though. As expected, these two treated each other as best friends, which contribute to the whole drama.

"So there you have it." I continued as the protagonist's eyes widened as he realized that yes, they were waiting for him to make a choice. "Go ahead and make your decision already."

He glared at me in anger for putting him in such a position but I met his eyes with a level gaze. Perhaps knowing the truth of my words he eventually backed off, looking down with gritted teeth. For a few moments there was silence… then, he forced himself to speak.

"I…" he croaked out, voice barely audible. "I choose Kaede."

The genki girl's eyes widened in surprise at his answer. In contrast, the heroine beside her just let out a smile, one that betrayed her slight disappointment. For a long time, there was a thoughtful silence as nobody spoke up.

"...Congratulations to you two, then." Yuki said softly after a while.

"Yuki…" the genki girl muttered, tone worried.

"Forgive me, Yuki-san." the protagonist whispered.

Yuki shook her head at that. "No, I was prepared for this possibility. I'm glad that this was all over, and that things will go back to normal after this." her smile turned into a more genuine one. "We'll return to being the club that I treasure so much."

Her other two clubmates, hearing what she had said, mirrored her smile. A pretty heartwarming moment all things considered.

Still, I mentally hummed as I considered the heroine. Yuki was hurt, that much was obvious, but I could see that there was a hint of… relief, within her. Like she was glad she wasn't chosen. I'm not too sure of the reason why that's the case, perhaps it was the fact that she was pressured to confess even when she wasn't sure of her own feelings, or maybe some other factor. But I suppose it's good that she wouldn't regret what happened here, even if it was only some part of her that did.

Yuki then turned to me after that. "...Thank you for your assistance, Basa-kun." she said, sincerely grateful.

I shrugged. "No need for thanks. I just pointed out the obvious."

She smiled at my attempt of being humble, aware of how much I helped her beyond that. "Still, without your presence perhaps things wouldn't proceed as smoothly." she refuted. "This entire club is thanking you for that."

"Yeah, Basa-kun! I suppose you're a cool guy after all!" the genki girl added as she looked at me in a new light.

Opposite me from the table the protagonist still looked a little bit angry at my actions, although he did give me a slight grudging nod of respect before looking away. The hell is with this guy? Why are you still angry? I helped fix the goddamn club from your indecision, damn it. You should be kowtowing to me in gratitude.

Rias pouted as she took a walk after being forced out of her room by Sona. It had been a rough couple of days after her talk with Basa-kun, and she had been thinking on what to do.

She first locked herself in her room and consulted the many anime DVDs, light novels and games that she had in order to familiarize herself with her situation. Just as she had suspected, as a heroine she was pretty much destined to be part of the harem that the protagonist, Ryuusei-kun, will form. It's pretty much written since she belongs in a shounen genre, as Basa-kun had confirmed many times.

Her circumstances made her think if she should just let things happen. Things do end up good for the heroine in all shounen stories. She couldn't blame Basa-kun for saying that it's better for things to be that way either, since things end in a good way as well.

Yet the thought of letting things be… she doesn't want it. Is it selfish? Perhaps. But it's not like meddling with things will automatically make things worse. Sure, there is a potential for it, but it could make things better as well. Stupid Basa-kun is just too jaded to even risk it.

But then again… it wasn't like she was the same. She was worse even, since much of her problems currently in her club were because of her inaction and fear of making things worse, rather than something altruistic like saving lives like Basa-kun's.

But now, it's up to her to act.

Rias will make things better. Just as she had promised Basa-kun. She'll make sure of that.

And it was at the moment that her determination crystallized, she felt something that was pressing on her disappear; perhaps a less aware being wouldn't realize, but as a demon attuned to her senses, it was as if a sudden clarity appeared before her. It was as if an already burdened wall shattered after a slight push, giving her a glimpse to the other side for the first time.

—And when she looked up, she saw a pair of futuristic-looking girls battling high above the sky.

…Rias took a deep breath, then turned to look at Basa-kun.

He had been staring at her for a while now. His gaze looked as mysterious as usual, not even showing a hint of what he was thinking - yet it carried that air of knowledge as if he knew everything that was happening around him. She was completely sure that at this moment, he's very much aware of Ryuusei-kun's problem, and is aware of her knowing that too.

And right now, those eyes were watching her, judging her actions. Waiting for her to do something.

She found herself doing one thing in response.

"—Ryuusei-kun."

Her voice suddenly called out, making the boy snap out of his thoughts.

"B-Buchou?" the boy said hesitantly.

Rias stared at him for a few moments… before breaking into a grin.

"I've decided!" she declared, suddenly standing up from her seat. "An underling of mine shouldn't have a problem like you have! I'll help you - You and that childhood friend of yours will be talking again in no time!"

"E-Eh? Help me?" Ryuusei-kun blinked, before shaking his head emphatically. "No, i-it's fine, Buchou! We're just a bit awkward to each other, I don't really think it's that big of a deal—"

"Nonsense! You two are childhood friends right? Something is clearly wrong if you guys are acting like that!" she retorted. "You might have recovered physically from the fallen angel, but it's clear that the damage he incurred is still there! I'm not going to let things remain like that, Ryuusei-kun!"

She slammed her hands on her table, giving the boy a serious and determined look.

"You're a precious underling of mine, Ryuusei-kun! It's my duty to help you, just as you help me! I'm not going to stand by and do nothing while you suffer!"

She's not going to wait for fate, destiny, narrative or whatever to help him. She's not going to be useless and hope that things will be fine! Because…

"Because… how can I be a president worth following if I didn't do that!?" she shouted.

To do anything else would be lying to herself!

She was Rias Satanichia! The one who would be the President of Hell!

That statement seemed to have shocked Ryuusei-kun speechless, but the gratitude and admiration in his eyes were visible. "I-I… Buchou…!"

The rest of her club seemed to be stunned at her declaration as well. Sona in particular just looked confused.

"Satanachia? What's gotten into you?" her bespectacled friend asked, perplexed.

"Just something that I've realized." she said with a frown. "I've been… a really bad leader, for a while now."

She knew she wasn't a decisive person, so seeing her suddenly say this out of nowhere must be strange. That will change now though!

"You know, the same goes for the rest of you as well." she added, addressing the rest of her club. "I know that I've been ignoring much of our problems… but that'll change now." she clenched her fist. "I swear it!"

Akeno, Kiba, and Koneko blinked before looking at one another at that. She could almost hear the wordless conversation between them, and Rias just had to wonder what they were thinking.

Then, as if deciding upon something, they nodded and turned to her with a smile. "Buchou, what are you saying~? You don't really need to say that, you know." Akeno said, her smile much more genuine than her usual teasing ones. "You might be a bit of a slacker, but we know you'll be with us when we need it."

"I chose to follow you out of hell for a reason, Buchou." Kiba followed. "You're not a bad leader in the slightest."

Koneko nodded. She didn't need to say anything, since her serious gaze said enough.

Rias almost found herself tearing up. "You guys…!"

"Ah well, there is one thing…" Akeno suddenly said, adopting a pondering pose. Rias perked up. "I've been requesting for a renovation for the club building, so maybe our good leader Buchou will—"

"No! We will not be having a BDSM dungeon in our club building!" she interrupted. "I doubt you'll even use it!"

"BDSM!?" Ryuusei-kun looked intrigued.

Akeno gave her a teasing grin. "I was actually suggesting an archiving room for our contracts. Kiba's having trouble on where to store it."

Rias paused. Beside her vice president, Kiba chuckled. "It has been getting harder to find space. I'd suggest electronic contracts at first, Demon society's insistence on physical copies make it harder for us."

She sighed. "Fine… we'll be adding that I guess…"

"I want a bigger fridge too. We have another member in our club now." Koneko piped up.

Rias was about to deny that but hesitated. "I mean… I guess it's a bit too small, especially if I'm going to have more members in the future…"

Sona adjusted her glasses. "By the way, I'd like to point out that the damage you incurred in the building and everything else outside is coming from your budget, and not from the student council."

"—Oh lay off me now, would you!" Rias shouted pathetically.

Her club let out various reactions of amusement, with Akeno, Kiba, and Ryuusei chuckling, and Koneko letting out a silent giggle. Sona cracked a smirk.

Rias sighed in exasperation at their teasing, but slowly let out a smile herself. She turned to Basa-kun, who had been silently watching this whole time, and gave him a meaningful glance.

This is what I decided. She tried to convey. I'm not going to let my fear of making things worse stop me from making things better.

For a moment he said nothing, simply watching her and the rest of her friends. For a moment Rias thought that he'd be angry for choosing to change things and risking potential problems, but much to her surprise… he let out a genuine smile himself.

"I see… so that's your answer, huh." he said. "How fitting for a shounen character."

Before she could ask what that means however, he said something that made her pause.

"By the way, this is pretty heartwarming but the way things are going you should get ready." he warned, making the others look at him.

"Ready for what?" Rias asked.

He raised a brow at her, as if she was asking a particularly dumb question. "What else? For the flag you planted, of course."

Rias stiffened. "Eh?"

—Then for the second time in the day, the club office was enveloped in an explosion, and all hell breaks loose.
