#1,077
It's a new semester and I had to adjust with the new schedule so it took a bit to write this. And now, for the continuation!

Chapter 10

Before the explosion that happened within the Rias' club office, a few minutes prior, an unidentified flying object appeared high up in the stratosphere, partially obscured by the clouds.

If an ordinary person were to look up they would have difficulty seeing it, with its white color blending on the clouds surrounding it, but a closer look would reveal that it wasn't a plane or a vehicle but rather a woman. A woman who wielded floating machinery behind her that is far more advanced than anything found in this era, keeping her aloft up high like a pair of wings, and shielding her from the cold despite the surprisingly skimpy outfit that she wore.


Spoiler

"Target location on sight.* the woman muttered, looking down on the school far below her. "Asking permission to proceed."

This woman was a witch, a warrior of great renown in the future, brought into the past to participate in this great game.

The communication module on her ear lit up, and a pompous male voice spoke on the other end. "Do so. Retrieve your device and don't bring any further shame to our family."

The witch winced at her warlock's words. The reminder of her failure cutting her deeply.

A few days ago, a strange event had left her unable to use her wand, as it had been missing. She had fought off another witch and during the exchange… something, which she could not recall due to a noticeable gap in her memories, occurred. And now she was left without it.

The Witch Armament Nexus Device was, in essence, an integral part of her being a witch. It was her weapon in life, outfitted with various augments that the faction she belonged to so that they could have an edge to this tournament. Yet it also wasn't that - it served as a nexus point for the time travel and also provided her the necessary assistance like monitoring time fluctuations in her spiritron body or even providing her information in the current era. Due to that importance, a witch and her wand are made to be inseparable, able to be teleported to her at all times and other backup systems that every faction in the war had agreed to put.

It wouldn't have been a concern… yet for some reason, attempts of making it return to her had been met with failure. The system had said that it detected some foreign energy that prevented the teleportation.

It was easy to conclude that a third witch had interfered with her battle and stole it. However, the implications of it sent her mind reeling. Out there was a witch with the ability to bypass the restriction families had put into the wand, and furthermore, one who had the ability to control memories judging by her inability to remember the event.

This subtlety… perhaps it was the work of the Arcanist class. Or perhaps something different. Nevertheless, she has failed her duty - and she will not do so once more.

"I shall not fail you, ancestor." she said firmly to her warlock.

There was a scoff on the other side of her comm module. "Hmph, we'll see."

Then the line cut off.

With that, the witch dropped down from the sky and approached the school down below. The familiar feeling of the cloaking equipment enveloped herself, preventing people from below in seeing her. She followed the direction of the last known location of the signal that she received from her wand.

From her forays into the primitive digital network, she knew that the school below was previously an all-girl's school in middle school that eventually turned into a normal one a few years ago, yet the majority of the school body remained female. It had students from mostly high income middle families to daughters of rich aristocrats. Perhaps an ancestor from a rival faction attended here, hence the signal, but she couldn't also shake the suspicion of the situation in general.

What was waiting for her was undoubtedly a trap. Someone who had a witch's wand undoubtedly knows how important it is to them. She had lost her primary weapon, and the best move would be to keep it away. And so to announce the location so daringly… there had to be something strange afoot.

She needed to be careful.

Her eyes spotted an isolated building away from the main campus. She locked onto the specific floor and room, her own augments bypassing the walls to peer inside, only to note that the place which resembled an office looked like a bomb went off it. She also noted the many people inside.

Three boys and three girls are present. They all looked like normal students of the school, except the one other boy who wore a different uniform. All of them were people she could ignore except for two exceptions: the same boy in a different uniform looking in her direction - to which she chalked it as coincidence - and finally the girl who sat on the head table, unlike the others who were seated on the sofa.

The girl had red hair. Something in her absent memories stirred up. She didn't know what technology managed to remove her memories, but as a trained soldier filled with augments in her body and mind, it would take more than that to influence it fully.

Her target was decided. It didn't look like they spotted her with her cloaking device… so if what was waiting for her was a trap, then she simply needed to take them from surprise as well.

The flight unit floating behind her keened much like a warplane and let out a twin jet of flames which accelerated her rapidly, then on her one free hand, she retrieved a small projectile that she had with her. One which she threw at the hole inside the room.

"—Eh?" she heard the girl say.

The projectile exploded, enveloping the room in a flash of light accompanied not by an explosion, but rather something else. The witch finally entered the room without landing on the ground, staying aloft with the flight unit on her back.

The red-haired girl coughed as she tried to recover herself. "Wha—" she stood up from the ground. "What happened!?"

Then, when she looked around, the girl's eyes widened in shock at what she beheld. "Huh!?"

This was because despite the explosion being over, the smoke hadn't cleared. In fact, it wasn't moving as if frozen in time - much like the other things and people in the room.

It was time dilation taken to the extreme. The projectile produced a spherical zone spanning the majority of the mansion and outside it where everything, except for selected targets, will remain unmoving as if in stopped time. Right now, the girl was firmly in the witch's territory.

The technology she wielded was considered advanced and dangerous even in the war-torn future she had come from. For the person who could control time in the palm of their hand holds a great power more than explosives or weapons ever could.

She was of the Chronomancer class; a master of time and the most powerful class of witch. And now, this girl and her witch will fear her for getting in her way.

The girl, who was still reeling in shock, turned to her direction and finally noticed her presence. She took a step back. "E-Eh!? You are…!"

The witch frowned. She noted the recognition in her eyes - furthering her suspicion in her involvement from her absent memories.

"Surrender, and return the wand to me." she demanded in a cold tone. She wasn't entirely without mercy. "You will find no assistance from the outside; everything in here is now under my control. Best give up unless you want yourself eliminated."

Saying that, the girl did something she didn't expect, and it was her turn for her eyes to widen.

From the girl's back came out bat-like wings and a tail, making her resemble a devil or some sorts. The witch found herself tensing as the girl went into a defensive stance.

"H-How did you get here!?" the girl shouted. "You shouldn't have remembered me from my hypnosis!"

Her eyes narrowed. Hypnosis? And the girl said she was responsible for it. Along with the strange bio-modifications that she had, she can only come to one conclusion.

This girl was the third witch that stole her wand.

"I see." she didn't know their ploy, but they were now in her territory and it was as good as over. There would be a time to retrieve her wand later; her priority was taking the witch in front of her first. "Then your end comes here."

She raised an arm towards the enemy, making them twitch.

"Chronify." she said softly.

Spacetime visibly warped in her behest as the voice command removed the girl's restriction to the time dilation. The enemy witch would be like the others around her, stopped in time and unable to act upon her. She could eliminate her easily after that.

Much to her surprise however, the enemy witch did something she had never seen before.

The girl's wings and tail straightened as if in alarm. "Eh!? What the—!?" she looked around, then spread her arms to let out some sort of energy that swept around her, stopping her tech from acting upon her.

The witch's eyes narrowed as her system brought back warnings and errors on its calculations. It identified the main source: a foreign energy, one that was identical to the one stopping her wand from teleporting to her.

Troublesome. She didn't have her wand to shoot her either… so it looks like she has to do this the old-fashioned way and use her fists to do the job.

"W-Wait! Don't attack me please! We don't need to fight!" the enemy witch pleaded as she saw her tense. "I'm sorry for taking your wand, but this is a massive misunderstanding! We don't have to—!"

Her flight unit activated, allowing her to accelerate towards the enemy witch with great speeds. She kicked her feet in a horizontal arc, intent on taking their head off, but the witch was able to react quickly and raise their arm to only take a glancing blow and make distance. She brought her foot down and scrutinized her enemy, who swallowed nervously.

There will be no parley. She didn't know what her enemy was thinking, nor did she recognize someone like her from the future, but it was clear she relied on tricks and acting. Her advantage was taken away with her wand gone, and now she found out that the witch was able to rebuff her time dilation tech. In hindsight, it should be obvious that they also have something for that. Nevertheless, she wouldn't be caught in their web any longer.

Now is the time to fight.

I watched as Rias started to fight the sci fi character.

My body remained seated on the sofa, unmoving due to being inside a zone where time is dilated to the point that time is almost stopped. Of course, having made protections against such a thing due to the sheer amount of characters who have the same power, my perception remained the same and I was completely unaffected by it.

Still though I really have no reason to move - so I just chilled on the soft mattress while observing them from my peripheral vision.

It was obvious that something would happen especially with Rias' little stunt with tempting fate earlier. I saw it coming from a mile away - literally, considering I spotted the sci fi witch floating a mile away in the sky just a few minutes ago. I figured that they might have located the wand that Rias stole and followed it to this place.

I witnessed in real time as the woman visibly ignored Rias' club and the glasses demon girl due to the genre divide, perhaps dismissing them as unimportant. There was also a bit of attention to me but it was quickly staved off by my own trait as a side character as her eyes slid off me. In the end that left Rias, who had somehow spontaneously gained the ability to ignore the boundaries of narrative due to reasons I am unsure of, for the sci fi witch to focus on.

Which now left us with this entirely avoidable confrontation. Really, if that redhead bimbo just kept her hands to herself then things wouldn't have devolved into this. Maybe we can even find out things in a more controlled environment.

Still, this was quite interesting to look at.

"I said wait! Can you please just listen to me!?" Rias shouted comically, which was ignored completely by the witch as they continued to attack.

I could see how they were starting to become visibly frustrated with how Rias seemed to deal with her moves though. Despite showing a lot of skin with her skimpy outfit, I can tell that it was actually a distraction and most of her body was actually synthetic and heavily augmented with machine parts. A single punch from this woman would obliterate a normal person - however, demon physiology is a tad tougher than that. The redhead is showing just how superior it is just by showing how effortlessly she dodged and blocked the hits due to their faster reaction time and tougher physiology.

Then there's also the fact that she's from a shounen genre. People who belong there have generally stronger bodies that defy realistic logic, and watching it now really highlights the difference between the two of them.

"Ah!"

An attack slipped by Rias' guard and managed to cuff her on the head. The redhead yelped in pain and kicked back reflexively, hitting the witch on the gut and making her grunt as she was pushed away. Rias cradled her head as she made distance once more.

"Ouch…!" she whined, before turning to the witch in anger. "That hurt, you know!?"

The witch didn't reply, but I could tell she was a bit insulted with how casually Rias was acting from the twitch in her brow. She brought up a hand much like she did earlier when she tried to time stop Rias… before suddenly disappearing.

"Wha—!"

Rias tensed as the witch suddenly appeared behind her without warning, and the forward chop aimed to her neck was dodged by a slight leaning of her head. In that same moment a magic circle appeared in Rias' hand as she called out an attack for the first time.

"Annihilation!" she shouted, unleashing a torrent of demonic power out of the magic circle towards the witch, who simply avoided it with the help of their jetpack. The attack went through the furniture around and outright disintegrated them.

The witch looked at the resulting destruction with her eyes narrowed. "That strange energy again…" she muttered.

"Grr…" Rias growled, her earlier anger returning to the witch once more. "Damn it, I said just please listen to me! I'm telling you that we don't need to fight! You're looking for that thing I took from you, right!? I can just return it to you if you want!"

"All witches will be eliminated." the woman coldly replied.

"Huh? I'm not a witch! I'm a demon! Do I look like I'm wearing a witch hat and carrying a broom—" she stopped and shook her head. "No, look. I understand that you don't have my kind from wherever you're from, but I'm not whatever you're thinking! Look at my wings and tails! That's not normal for you, isn't it!?"

If I let myself move, I would've raised a brow. What exactly was this girl trying to pull?

Is she trying to convince them about the existence of other settings? You're an exception to the rule that divides them, dumbass. That's not gonna work with others. And I'm sure I've also said it to her in passing as well for her to know that.

Lo and behold, the witch just looked at her like she was an idiot. "Your bio-modifications are lifelike, but I'm not going to think that you belong to a race of some primitive religion. Are you delusional?"

"I'm not—! Look I'm really telling the—!" she stopped herself before looking in my direction, probably remembering that no, what she's doing won't work. Then she sighed. "Oh forget it… you're not going to listen to me at all, are you?" she shook her head. "Fine!"

Then in proper shounen fashion, she clenched her fist in front of her and glared at her opponent.

"If you're not going to listen to me… then I'm going to make you!"

With that declaration, Rias seems to stop holding herself back as crackling demonic energy suffused within her form. Her wings unfurled on her back and flapped once to lift her up to get to the floating witch's level. The two clashed midair, and they launched themselves out of the club office and into the courtyard of this mansion.

"Tch!" the witch clicked her tongue as she was caught off guard by the sudden burst of strength from Rias. "That foreign energy is increasing…!"

"Hah! So you can't detect my magic? Let's see if you can deal with it then! Your mechs or my magic - we'll see which one is better!" Rias shouted with a determined grin.

The redhead demon started to attack aggressively, switching the positions from earlier and making the witch be the one on the defensive this time. Their fight in air was filled with twists, barrel rolls, and turns that looked more like a fight between extremely mobile fighter planes than two people slugging each other.

Rias occasionally formed a magic circle to launch countless bursts of demonic energy towards the witch, which was deftly avoided. I could see that the witch was slowly turning overwhelmed though because of her caution towards the demonic magic that Rias has as well as the sudden ramping up of the intensity in their fight.

Rias, by contrast, seemed to enjoy this opportunity to cut loose and show off herself. I considered the situation at hand at why this was the case.

During these moments does a shounen character's best traits take the spotlight. The hotblooded action, one where emotions and tensions run high - it was at these times that a shounen character is in their element. Logic and realism like stamina, endurance, or any physical limitation that a character may have are thrown away in the face of what is dictated by story themes and narrative to showcase a cool scene.

The rule of cool, in simple terms. Rias, right now, is literally empowered by fate to show off cool shit no matter how dumb or implausible. It's a trick that I sometimes use in shounen genres to give myself a boost. Not to say that it doesn't appear in other genres, but for shounen it's very easy to do so.

The witch however doesn't have that benefit. She actually is part of a genre that's more grounded and realistic; that is, she belongs in a seinen genre. Leading to this result of her having a hard time fighting Rias.

"Tsk!" Rias let out a noise of frustration as the witch disappeared out of the way from her attack due to their application of the time technology. "Let's see if you can dodge this then!" she shouted, before launching out a particularly large volley of energy projectiles.

"Useless." the witch intoned.

As expected, like the rest of Rias' attacks, it was avoided once more as the witch disappeared from her place and reappeared slightly out of the way in an instant. When the woman reoriented herself however, she was shocked to see her getting hit in the face by a fist she didn't see coming. "Grkh—!"

Rias grinned from her successful prediction of her enemy's teleport position. "Do you really think I'll let you keep doing that!?" A large magic circle appeared before her. "Annihilation!"

This time, the witch wasn't able to dodge and was directly hit by the beam of demonic energy. The woman grit her teeth as she tried to oppose it, straining her augmented body… but in the end managed to be overwhelmed as the beam enveloped her whole, swiftly followed by a large explosion.

It was only a matter of time that happened. Rias managed to beat her enemy and it looked like the battle had concluded. One might be tempted to say that the witch had no chance of beating Rias the moment fate empowered her to be stronger.

But… that wouldn't be the case.

Rias kept her distance, staying aloft in the air as she watched as black smoke wafted after the explosion high up in the air. She pumped her fist in victory. "Hah! Take that! I won!"

With that statement the flag was raised, and it was swiftly triggered without mercy.

Because as the smoke eventually dispersed… it revealed not the sight of a defeated enemy, but rather nothing at all. Her enemy disappeared without a trace.

"What!? She's not there!?" Rias shouted in shock, before swiftly trying to look for the missing witch in her surroundings. "Where—!?"

A blur appeared in front of her and she wasn't able to react fast enough for the hand that grasped her throat. There, the witch appeared from nowhere, synthetic skin torn to reveal some of her damaged augments underneath. Her cold glare was aimed solely at the girl she held by the throat.

"Foreign energy analyzed… system updated. That foreign energy you exude will no longer disrupt any calculations." the witch stated clinically. "You can no longer prevent my technology."

It is said that growing up is a delicate balance between dreams and the weight of reality.

In what was interpreted as certainty and determination from shounen, it was reflected by seinen as hubris and idiocy. Both are incompatible with one another, viewing life in conflicting lenses; and that nature makes them perfect to cast down the other with the right circumstance.

Rias might have been beating the witch, but from raising that flag statement earlier, she gave the seinen aspect the perfect opportunity to cast her down for her overconfidence. A taste of reality for a naive child, you might say.

This whole time the witch was playing defensive I could tell that she was analyzing the Rias' magic. She was stalling for time this whole fight. Perhaps if Rias quickly tried to defeat her and didn't get swept away by the trope to show off, she might have defeated her enemy. Yet she failed to notice it, and that had cost her.

"Kghh—!"

Rias struggled on the witch's grip, trying to pry it off, yet her efforts were futile. The witch's face remained emotionless as her hand slowly tightened, intent to crack her neck and finish her off. Rias was starting to turn desperate as her windpipe was slowly getting crushed.

From my peripheral vision, I watched them closely.

Then a terrible crack that echoed and Rias slumped on the witch's grip.

A heavy silence fell.

Then, the witch let go and dropped Rias' body down on the ground. She didn't even spare any look or thought towards it - an efficient and merciless killer, through and through. Instead, she turned back to the club office, perhaps trying to pinpoint the last location of the wand.

She floated towards me and narrowed her eyes, looking at my form in confusion. I had her wand with me after all. Yet I wasn't holding it; I put it in my subspace before this woman had even arrived. Her tech might be able to detect the slightest bit of space distortion around me due to how advanced it is, but otherwise she has no idea where the wand could possibly be. Still, that didn't stop her from trying, and she extended her hand towards me.

…Unfortunately for this woman, victory wouldn't be something that she could get easily.

I stared at her.

She halted immediately, gaze snapping to my face to see that my eyes were now looking at her. It's always been said that the eyes are the window of the soul and I'm staring straight at hers; judging it in its entirety.

The witch jumped back.

"H-His eyes, did it just move…?" she muttered in disbelief. "Impossible, he should've been in stopped time!"

I could count a thousand possible ways I could've ended her right then and there. This time dilation thing never worked for me in the first place - I could have stood up at any time, at any moment, and defeated her easily with her being unable to stop me.

But there was no need to… because all I needed was to give a slight assistance. One that would cause the witch to get distracted for a moment.

"Demonic inferno, rise and blaze forth—!"

My lips involuntarily cracked into a smile.

The witch stiffened at the voice and made her turn around. There she saw a familiar redhead, floating through the air with a hand held to her throat and evidently not dead. There were also very complex magical circles and lines that spun around her form as she fed her magic there.

But the most striking of all was the ball of fire above a raised arm. It was a large amount of demonic energy condensed in a single point, making it glow bright like the sun - the power of a celestial star right in Rias' palms.

And she brought that hand forward and aimed it towards the witch.

The witch tensed, but in response she had extended her arm as well - no doubt intending to use her time tech to stop the attack now that she can affect Rias despite the demonic magic.

"Chronify—!"

"It's convenient." I then stood up from my seat. "Anyway, we'll stop our testing for now. Get yourself ready - We're going to have a field experience."

The two girls stood up as well. Rias looked excited by the prospect of an adventure, while Yuki simply gave me a questioning look. "What are we going to do? And where are we going?"

"A new plotline started, one that the system notified which could potentially affect the world itself. And as for where we are going…"

I stared at the information on my phone, or more specifically, the location. It was somewhere familiar, and at no point is it a coincidence why this was the case.

With the way things look right now… it appears that my predictions on who'll get a sudden case of turning meta would be accurate after all.

"We're going to an idol agency." I revealed.

"The one where Aoki-san works at."

Chapter 12

Deep breath…

Take a deep, deep breath.

It was right there. The place was within her sights, and she only needed to walk over there so that it may all start. It was just a sight of it yet her heart was beating wildly at the prospect of going inside. She couldn't move her legs, the hesitation and nervousness inside her warring and overwhelming the paltry resolve she had gathered just so she could bring herself here.

She gazed at the name displayed at the large building, staring at the logo that would be act as the catalyst .. for her journey.

LOVE☆Doll Productions.

A well known talent agency, one filled with big names in the entertainment industry.

What was she thinking, going to this place? Will she even be allowed inside? A lonely, untalented mess like her with nothing except a guitar and a dream? What if they took one look at her and decided to throw her out? What if they laughed at her instead?

She wanted to be an idol, but she didn't know if she had the strength to do it. It was pathetic that a weak-hearted coward like her who couldn't even have a proper conversation with those from her own school was even attempting to do something like this. The odds are so stacked against her that it wasn't even funny.

The Cardboard Box. She wanted to go back to the Cardboard Box! It was safe, it was unjudging, and most importantly - far away from here!


Spoiler

Yet despite The Promised Land calling out for her, beckoning her to get as far away as possible, Hitori Yumemi found herself rooted in the spot.

Was she insane? Perhaps. Maybe being alone for a long time made her mind finally snap. Even as she questioned herself right now, feeling herself burning hot as if sick and her stomach wanting to hurl its contents…. actually, she really felt like vomiting. S-Should she go to the restroom? Does she even deserve to be in the restroom? Will the restroom even accept her?

T-This is bad. Other people were staring at her. Why is that? Oh, she was dry heaving in the middle of the sidewalk with her hands planted on the ground. That's strange—

—She smashed her head on the pavement.

"No!"

No, she shouldn't make a scene right now! That's the last thing she should do!

Look at these poor pedestrians! They're looking at her like she's completely crazy! The next thing will happen is that they'll record her and she'll be viral online! Wait, isn't that just becoming famous like a idol but with extra steps—No, no wait. That's different!

She… she should try to calm herself down. A drink! Yes, she needed to take a drink. A drink sounds good right now to fix her suddenly dry throat. And if she puked right now it would mean she wouldn't puke later right? Right!?

Her hands disappeared into her bag and tried to grab the water bottle she bought on her way here. Her hands were shaking furiously as she did so, and even taking the cap off was difficult as she tried to curb her rising panic.

"—Ah!"

Yet somehow, she failed a task as simple as that. She shouldn't be surprised.

From her nervous clutches she fumbled the cap off, while also somehow managing to make the bottle slip off her hands. She yelped in surprise as it sailed in the air… before hitting another pedestrian walking just past her, dousing them fully.

The pedestrian stopped for a moment, looking down at his wet clothes, and to the bottle that rolled to the sole of his shoes… Before turning around to look straight at her.

She stiffened.

"A-Ah…"

It was over. Everything was so over. She hadn't even gone inside it and everything had gone wrong already.

Out of all the people that she spilled water to, somehow it had to be a delinquent. A gyaru-oh with tanned skin and blonde hair, along with a clearly fit body on a large frame; they looked like the very stereotype of the person she was told to avoid in school at all cost.

And now that type of person is approaching her.

Hitori had to look up as he towered over her from their sheer height difference. She can only whimper as she was left standing in front of the person she had wronged. Her legs were locked in place, like a pathetic deer caught facing a deadly predator.

Mother, father… it appears that your daughter's life will end. If you deem it worthy to spend some money for the funeral, then I beseech you to bury your daughter's body within her precious box. And to also clear away your daughter's browser history. Your daughter will be waiting for you in another world.

And so she stood there, waiting for her life to end—

"You okay there? You seem a bit shaken up."

She blinked.


Spoiler

The gyaru-oh that stood in front of her didn't face her with an angry expression but rather a slightly concerned one. Gazing at his face she noticed that he didn't look as scary as she imagined - he looked rather fair-looking actually - and although he looked like a delinquent, it also wouldn't be too out of place for him being a model that just played with the particular niche of being tall, dark, and handsome.

The man extended his hand, offering the bottle that she spilled at him. Hitori absent-mindedly took it.

"...A-Ah, I'm…" her eyes widened as she suddenly realized what she did and she immediately bowed her head. "I-I'm very sorry! I didn't mean to—!"

"It's fine, no need." he interrupted. There was no anger in his tone, but that just made the guilt and shame within her worse. She made to apologize again but he spoke before she could open her mouth. "By the way, do you mind if I ask you something?"

Hitori straightened. "Y-Yes?" she paused. "I-I meant, um, you can ask! Please ask away!"

He raised a brow from her high-strung reaction, making her cringe from embarrassment. Nevertheless he ignored it and continued to speak again. "Cool. I was just going to ask if you know the directions to a talent agency around this place? It's called… Love doll, or something."

Her eyes widened. He wanted to go to the talent agency too? Could she be right in her earlier thought that the person right in front of her was some kind of model!? Was this person like her, trying out their luck in the entertainment industry!?

…He'd probably have a better chance than her, to be honest. He certainly had the looks for it, as well as the social skill to affably deal with strangers who spilled water at them. Comparing him to her… it was as if she was but a candle in the face of the sun.

Ha… She was really pathetic…

"...Did she just turn monochrome? What's with this girl." he muttered, scrutinizing her face. Why was he…?

She blinked as she realized that she had been standing there in a daze while completely absorbed in her thoughts. Blushing in embarrassment she immediately answered what he had asked. "A-Ah! You want to go to the talent agency!? T-The building is over there!" she pointed on the place she was gathering her courage to step foot on. "Y-You can see their company ."

He looked at her oddly, then shook her head. "...I suppose it is." he said in thought. Then he gave her a polite nod. "Thanks."

With that he turned around, approaching the building and leaving her there.

"U-Um!" she found herself speaking before he could go far.

He glanced back at her once more, and Hitori swallowed her nervousness to say the question on her lips. "E-Excuse me… but are you going to apply yourself there? Like a male idol?" she asked.

"A male idol? Me…?" she expected him to say yes, but for some reason the man gained this sour look on his face as if the thought repulsed him. He then shook his head. "No, I just have some stuff to do there. I'm not applying myself as a talent."

"O-Oh…" she didn't know what to say to that.

He then gave her a curious look. "Why? Was there something?"

She opened her mouth and for a moment, she considered answering his question and telling him of her troubles. About how she was trying to gather her courage to become an idol, but was having such a hard time doing so because she is painfully aware of how pathetic she was. About how she thought that the person right in front of her was trying to apply as well and how she thought about talking with him, out of some effort to stave off the nervousness of going there.

But the fact that telling her dream, venting, and trying to depend on the person she had spilled water to however, stopped her from doing anything more shameful.

Hitori closed her mouth with a grimace. No, she had already inconvenienced this person quite enough. There was no need to do it any further. "N-Nevermind. I apologize for—"

"Let me guess. You have a dream to become an idol right?"

Her eyes widened and she looked at the man in front of her in surprise. "E-Eh?"

"I can tell that you want to be an idol. So, what's the problem? Are you having the jitters? Can't take the first step?" he continued blandly, further surprising her by saying her worries right out of his own mouth.

"H-How…?"

He hummed. "You look like main character material. The awkward, nervous type. An underdog story perhaps?" he gave her a scrutinizing look, before he shrugged. "Anyways, you don't have to worry about failing to be an idol."

She didn't know what he had meant, but with how nervous and desperate she was with trying to gain the slightest courage to set foot in the talent agency, her mind latched on more to the last part of what he had said. "I-I don't have to worry? What do you mean…?"

"It means exactly what I said." he replied. "I'm not really the person to say this but I might as well; just go apply to that talent agency and be an idol. It'll be difficult, but as long as you persevere and continue despite all of it, then things will be fine."

He stared at her straight in the eye, making Hitori stiffen in place as it felt like he was staring at her soul, judging it in its entirety. Then he spoke once more.

"And though you may get weak-hearted from a lot of things… hard work is the one thing that you don't lack. Isn't that the case, pink-haired girl that I don't know?"

…There were many things that she felt from his words. A part of it was confusion regarding the person right in front of her, because he acted as if he was familiar with her despite being a stranger that she didn't know, and the things he said were by itself very confusing and vague.

Yet the other things that she felt, the majority of it, was directed towards herself.

His words struck something within her, a realization within her own being that pierced through the doubt that ate inside. Yes, it was true that she was pathetic compared to others, but she had worked hard for this. Harder than anything else. And that hard work wouldn't betray her now. She only needed to take her first steps… to make it show its results.

It was in the midst of that reflection when she realized that the person she was talking to was already walking away. Her eyes widened and she cupped her hands to the sides of her mouth.

"U-Um…!" she shouted out loud, ignoring the other pedestrians turning their heads at her. She hated attention but that sort of thing didn't matter right now. Hitori bowed deeply in his direction. "T-Thank you very much!"

In response to her gratitude, he just waved a hand without looking back. It was when he disappeared within the sea of bodies who were also walking down the street and Hitori lost her sight of him that she brought her hands down.

"Just who was that person…?" she said in thought, before grimacing as she realized something. "I should've at least asked for his name…"

Just as she said that however, a familiar cheerful voice called out to her.

"Hitori-chaaaaaan!"


Spoiler

She turned around to see a familiar blonde waving to her with a happy smile on her face. She squeaked when the girl ran over to hug her. "N-Nijika-san!"

Too tight…! She was hugging her too tight! Can't breathe!

"You came! I'm really happy that you did!" the girl said happily, seemingly not noticing her sudden lack of air. Then she turned to look at the side. "See!? I told you that she would come!"

A blue-haired girl that was walking beside the blonde came up to them. "I didn't say that she wouldn't though." she said with a cool smile on her face. She then gave Hitori a nod. "Good to see you here, Hitori-chan."


Spoiler

"Ryo-san, help me…!" she tried to let out desperately.

The cool girl blinked and took a closer look at her state of being crushed by Nijika-san… before giving her a thumbs up. Why!? "Looks like you can put up receiving hugs now. Good job." she congratulated. "You can do better than having your face look like it's being strangled though."

It's not 'looking like'—she really was being strangled! In fact, her head feels like it's starting to pop!

Pop!

The stranger's words echoed in her mind, mirroring what Nijika-san had said. It was right - even if she hadn't had the confidence for herself, she could at least have the confidence for the hard work that she put; the sweat and tears they shed just to get to this day.

Her heartbeat quickened, but this time it wasn't out of nervousness, but rather anticipation.

Today was the day they would be idols.

"Yes!" she said. "Let's go!"

I glanced away as the girl that gave me directions met up with her friends.

…Man, that was some Looney Toons shit.

A bit of a rarity to see; in anime world, cartoonish effects usually limit themselves as a popped vein to indicate anger, a comically large hump of bandage to indicate injury, or teleporting gags that don't make sense like someone appearing behind you.
