#1,536
Hadn't wrote much for like two weeks because I had to lock in for exams (I still failed).

Anyway, here's the next chapter about miss super idol. As you know, the characters are all "inspired" from somewhere so her setting and name was based on this horror story… Well, you'll see where it goes.
Chapter 13

After the whole incident with the idols, Yuki found herself standing with Basa-kun and Rias-san at the company building's management section, with Aoki-san having pulled them aside to talk. She brought them in her own personal office so that no one could be around and they could talk freely.

The blue-haired woman had already ensured that the girls were brought into safety with the idol and their person of interest, Terumi Fuuka, bringing the girls to the infirmary for medical attention and to ensure the idol's safety while Aoki-san reported what happened to the authorities. It didn't take long for the director to be apprehended - and judging by the current chaos within the management section as they went towards Aoki-san's office - it looks like the effects of such an upheaval was starting to show.

That the agency was selling their idols for business opportunities being brought into the open will surely cause a massive scandal that some higher ups were trying to mitigate, but not all of them. The company itself is divided into sides between those who are in that business and those who are not. She was well aware of business politics to know that this event started a schism and power struggle which would change the company as a whole - which would hopefully lead to the legitimate side of the business winning. The talent agency would gain a slight mud in their name but they would become better for it.

Of course, the process was immensely helped with her elder sister's attention on the case. She was sure to choose the legitimate side in the power struggle, seeing the opportunities to gain favors and sneak in men of her own in now empty seats. Her sister's interest would've piqued after having seen her message, as any leverage to be used to further their family's power is worthwhile for them… Yet, Yuki also knew that the cause of it was also due to the fact she, for the first time in her life, had decided to involve herself into these sorts of things.

She strayed far away from their family's political side for many years and deciding to ask a favor for her sister for such a scandal would surely make her intrigued. That, along with other important details like how Yuki was supposed to be in school right now and how she managed to get a front seat in such a scandal in the first place.

She knows that she'll be faced with many questions from her elder sister soon but she'll cross that bridge when the time comes.

For now, they had something far more important to deal with.

Aoki-san's office was small, yet the fact that she had a room on her own instead of a simple cubicle indicated she had a higher position within the managerial staff. The office simply consisted of a work desk, a few filing cabinets, and a small sofa on the side. Aoki-san stood in front of her desk, looking at the three of them as she crossed her arms with a frown plastered on her face. The scene they made looked remarkably similar to students being sent into the disciplinarian's office.

"So… Basa-kun, Yuki-chan, Rias-chan." Aoki-san started with a scolding tone. "Do you mind telling me why you three are here? Because I'm pretty sure that all of you are supposed to be at school right now!"

Yuki looked away slightly at the expression of maternal concern on the woman's face, while Rias-san beside her sheepishly chuckled. There was something discomforting about the possibility of making such a nice woman disappointed for some reason, and she found herself unable to look at her eyes properly even knowing they're guiltless of anything wrong.

Basa-kun, meanwhile, remained completely unaffected by her expression. "We're not skipping school, technically. And as for why we're here…" he seems to contemplate what to say, before shrugging in the end. "Well, we're dealing with the supernatural." he said bluntly.

Aoki-san's eyes narrowed at him. "Basa-kun, now is not the time for jokes. If you keep that up then I'll get angry."

"And I'm not joking." he replied simply, before turning to Rias-san. "Hey, show her your wings."

Rias-san blinked in surprise and Yuki did the same. For a moment she thought of questioning him because they just saw a demonstration of Rias-san a few hours prior, before her eyes narrowed when she realized the implication of it. And judging by Rias-san's widened eyes followed by a determined nod, she also had the same thought.

Aoki-san was about to speak again, perhaps to scold Basa-kun some more, but her words died in her throat when Rias-san did what he asked and revealed her demonic appendages. Bat-like wings and tail unfurled at her back, showing itself out to the world… and most especially to Aoki-san, who was now staring at it with shock.

"E-Eh? Where did that…?" the woman muttered.

This was proof. Basa-kun said that as a person in a mundane setting, it's impossible for her to even interact with the supernatural. Yet here she was, looking at Rias-san's wings despite fate itself preventing it from happening just a few hours ago.

As of now, the genre divide no longer affects Aoki-san. The woman had now become like them.

"She turned meta." Yuki muttered, looking at Aoki-san in a new light.

Basa-kun nodded his head. "Yep. That's confirmation that it affects people around me, particularly love interests. The diagnostic and surveillance spells I put on her this breakfast should be able to record any observable change... With the data from it I'll be getting to the bottom of this." Basa-kun said in thought, rubbing his chin in thought. Then he shrugged. "But that can be done later, I guess."

He did say he predicted who's next to gain an ability like theirs. She wasn't surprised that he decided to take the initiative and see what happens to Aoki-san during such a transformation, much like what he had wanted to know with their testing earlier…

She blinked.

W-Wait, did he just say something strange just now? L-Love interests—!?

"—Basa-kun? Do you mind telling me what you're talking about?" her thoughts were interrupted by Aoki-san, who had a perplexed smile on her face. "A-And why did Rias-chan suddenly gain wings and a tail? W-Was that some sort of cosplay…?"

There was a forced quality to her statement. Before any clarification had been done, the blue-haired woman continued to speak, expression looking as if she gained an epiphany.

"O-Oh, I see! So you three came here to show that? Perhaps to try to audition for LOVE☆Doll? I don't quite understand why cosplay, but it's quite impressive! The way it moves is very realistic!" she complimented. "It looks so lifelike! Why, I even thought it's real for a moment!"

"Because it is, Aoki-san." Basa-kun said idly.

The woman giggled. "Oh, you and your jokes again, Basa-kun. I told you that I might get angry, didn't I? Take this seriously please."

"And I already told you earlier that it's not a joke, Aoki-san."

"Now, now, you can't possibly be saying that Rias-chan has wings and a tail, right?" Basa-kun didn't answer. "...R-Right? Basa-kun?"

That was when Rias-san spoke up.

"It's very real! It's not cosplay at all, Aoki-san! Here, look, it's connected to me." Rias-san turned around to show exactly just that. Her wings flapped slightly behind her, visibly connected to her lower back due to her cropped sweater. "I can even move it, see?"

There was a slight silence.

"I-I see! So it's real, huh?" the woman said after a while, a fixed smile present on her lips. "Wow!"

"Yes, I'm actually a demon!" the redhead replied. "And if that's not proof enough…" she willed out a magic circle, one that produced a spark of grayish energy above her palm. "Ta-da! Magic is real! Pretty cool, right?"

Another bout of silence followed her statement. Yuki looked at Aoki-san, and she noticed that the blue-haired woman just stood there with the same smile, unmoving and unreacting.

"...Aoki-san?" she questioned worriedly.

Her body teetered, and Yuki let out a noise of surprise as the woman's body fell down. Thankfully, Basa-kun caught her and let her unconscious body fall on his arms before she could hit the ground and hurt herself.

The three of them stared at the woman who fainted.

"...Maybe I should've been more delicate with the reveal." Rias-san said with a wince.

"No, it's fine. Best get it out of the way and rip off the band-aid fast. It's the best way to go about things." Basa-kun replied as he brought her body in a bridal carry before depositing on the sofa in Aoki-san's office. "I'll get her up to speed with her many questions after. But for now, we should focus on what we came here for."

Yuki nodded. "Terumi Fuuka. We found her."

The woman who would bring about a world-affecting plot as Basa-kun attested. The details he gave were sparse, apparently due to the innate uncertainties of predicting the undetectable narrative fate, but that was the entire reason why they've come here for.

"What did you do when she introduced herself to you? I felt something happen, but I didn't know what." Rias-san asked curiously, recalling what happened earlier.

"Just had to verify something. I blasted her with a fear aura similar to those from horror monsters." Yuki's eyes widened, and Basa-kun's gaze turned to her. "You should be familiar with what it felt like, and you saw her reaction - she didn't even look like she registered it, did she?"

Yuki's mind raced.

That was… that was impossible. The whole experience of being subjected to a horror monster's fear aura was something she would never forget - she can vividly recall the fear that struck her heart and made her more terrified than anything in her life. So to think that someone will experience it and not notice it at all was unfathomable to her. Terumi Fuuka would have to either have something wrong with her mental faculties or be as powerful as Basa-kun to ignore such a thing - neither of which seem plausible, from the short impression she formed on the idol.

Unless… unless there was a reason why Basa-kun used the fear aura of a horror monster specifically. Her eyes narrowed as a thought appeared in her mind.

"...She belongs in the horror genre, doesn't she? The one who is oblivious to the danger." she deduced, recalling the information of character archetypes within each genre written from Basa-kun's notes. "She's a victim type of character."

"Eh!? Like the first one that dies in a horror movie!?" Rias-san said in shock. "Does that mean Fuuka-san is going to die!?"

"I'm sure that you've watched and read enough anime and manga to realize the signs on her person, Rias." Basa-kun commented.

For a moment the redhead looked clueless, before she blinked and gained a thoughtful look.

"Hold on, she's got a fiance, she has that gentle feel to her… Oh, crap. She's got the dreaded braid hairstyle of death!" Rias-san said with a gasp. "T-Those are definitely big red flags! She's going to die!"

"Yep. And her death will be a catalyst to a plot which will likely affect the world at large." Basa-kun added.

Yuki frowned as she considered the information. Such a thing is indeed a major concern as a horror monster might endanger the lives of many people… but there was something she was missing. Especially with how Basa-kun kept phrasing about what will happen.

"...May I ask something, Basa-kun? You stated 'affecting the world', correct?" she asked, suddenly realizing something. "How is that possible considering the presence of the genre divide? Surely an event like this would be isolated and only affect those included on its own plot, barring circumstances where they interact with similar settings. That is what you told us earlier, isn't that right?"

Basa-kun and Rias-san stared at her. The redhead blinked before gaining a look of understanding, then turning her head to Basa-kun with a questioning look. For his part, Basa-kun stared at her blankly for a few seconds… before giving her a smile.

"I was wondering when you'd notice. Yes, that should be the case." he confirmed.

"But…?" Rias-san prompted.

"But," he continued. "This particular situation is special, which is why I made the systems alert me of it given the slightest possibility of it happening. As you said, plotlines remain isolated and wouldn't affect the world at large, no matter how extensive the destruction it can encompass. A person with the power to destroy the world will usually be foiled before they even have a chance to do so, or perhaps they choose not to as the plot demands or is out of character for them. Different settings do not interact - not unless they are similar to one another, that is. And even then, they only interact slightly."

He frowned as his eyes hardened.

"But… in the right circumstance, that technicality is enough to affect the world at large." he explained solemnly.

"What… what do you mean?" Yuki asked, concerned. Beside her, Rias-san also looked similarly worried.

"A setting will interact with a similar setting, and that setting can also interact with other similar settings as well." Yuki stiffened. "Do it enough times, and it will cross boundaries that aren't supposed to be crossed - for example, from a hard supernatural setting it will affect the soft ones, then eventually mundane settings. You essentially had a supernatural setting affect a mundane one albeit indirectly, despite it normally being impossible. You see where this is going, right?"

Yuki's mind raced. Indeed, the existence of such a technicality can lead to such a situation. But this… he can't possibly mean…

"In a very unlikely and unlucky situation, it's completely possible that one plot will set off a cascade of events which will affect other plots, and spread throughout different genres. That is what a 'world-affecting scenario' is. It affects the world at large and shifts the status quo." he continued to explain, with Yuki and Rias looking at him with wide eyes. "From one event, different genres will feel the shocks of that one plotline, with the effects manifesting in a way that is consistent with the plot and themes of the setting. But there still remains the fact that the effects will eventually escalate and turn the world into something different. It's an upheaval of the global scale."

Yuki pursed her lips. "That should be impossible… you told us the genre divide bends fate itself, so how can it overlook a mere technicality like that? What about the plots that will get affected? Surely such a drastic change shouldn't happen."

Basa-kun smiled ruefully. "Shouldn't it? But taking it to its logical extreme, then applying that reasoning would mean that history won't progress. Humanity wouldn't advance." that made Yuki pause. "Different plots and tropes can be found in different ages in history, you know? This world isn't so static to affect only the modern age with its rules, so if the genre divide worked to keep those settings and tropes constant then we'd still be stuck in the middle ages or something. As for the plots affected, you've said it yourself - fate would make it so that the changes fit with the narrative seamlessly." he shook his head. "This is but a natural part of human history; a drastic transition representing a societal change that has been twisted in the eyes of a narrative world. I've said it's a technicality in the rules… but really, it's more of a feature to prevent a static world."

"Settings indirectly affect each other all the time, but mostly minorly. That keeps the world moving." he added. "But sometimes, you get major changes that affect the world - and that is what we're concerned about here."

Yuki was silent at that, unable to think of anything to say in reply. That was when Rias-san spoke up hesitantly.

"...U-Um, Basa-kun, you said that it's a major global change, correct? It doesn't mean that it's something innately harmful, does it?" she asked.

He hummed. "Well, it is a transition. It can potentially affect the lives of many, but it doesn't mean the change is automatically harmful. The greatest world-affecting changes are major turning points in history after all, like the discovery of metal or the start of the industrial age. You could definitely say it turned our lives for the better."

"Then it's not that bad, is it?" the redhead said optimistically. "Maybe the transition would result in something better? Oh, since the plot that will start it is horror, maybe the general public will be aware of the supernatural and people will start using magic?"

Yuki frowned thoughtfully. "That's…"

Rias-san might have a point with that. Just because it will affect the world as a whole, it doesn't mean that it would be bad. Still, it would be something they need to keep track of as it will affect the lives of literally billions of people.

"All plausible guesses, but I'm more on the side of stopping these sorts of things, actually." Basa-kun stated, making both her and Rias-san look at him in surprise.

"What? Why?" the redhead asked.

He smiled. It wasn't a good sort of smile. "Remember the setting of those witches that came from the future? It's included in the notes I gave to you two."

It was. Yuki had read his notes on her way to the talent agency, brushing up on the different settings she had encountered and will encounter within the city itself. Those witches, she recalled, were from the future that is a… dystopian apocalyptic world…

She paled.

"W-W-Wait." Rias-san also looked similarly alarmed. "You can't be saying that…"

"That the modern age will transition into an dystopian apocalyptic setting?" he said. "There's a good chance of it. I mean, it's certainly backed with the many future plotlines that come from a setting like that."

Both of them looked at Basa-kun with horrified expressions.

"So yeah, I'm not taking any chances when I encounter something like this." he continued idly.

"—That's a given!" Rias-san cried out. "What the hell!? The world will fall into an apocalypse!?"

"Probably, yeah. There's a good chance before a world-affecting scenario would affect things and cause nuclear war by proxy or something. And considering it's the actual future and it's already set into stone - I'm just delaying the inevitable." he stated, shrugging. "Then again, time isn't so linear, having branching paths and alternate timelines, but the fact that the most common anime setting after the modern age is an dystopian apocalyptic one… well, the world has to make room for new settings after all."

Yuki closed her eyes shut. "...That's not helping at all, Basa-kun." she gritted out, before shaking her head. "So we have to prevent the world-affecting scenario from happening… And for that to happen, then we have to stop the horror plot from ever occurring. I seem to recall the fact that you have no qualms involving yourself in that genre, correct?"

"Yeah, we just have to stop it ourselves! It'll work out better for everyone!" Rias-san agreed.

He hummed at that. "We certainly could." he said. "But to do that, we have to be around the victim character first."

Basa-kun turned his head to look at the sofa. She and Rias-san followed his gaze, and they witnessed as Aoki-san groaned as she woke up. The blue-haired looked around blearily, before setting her eyes to them.

"Basa-kun…? And Yuki-chan and Rias-chan too… That's strange, I just had this weird dream where I…" her eyes locked onto Rias-san's wings and tail, which still remained out in the open. Yuki watched as Aoki-san's eyes turned wide and manic. "I-It's— It's not a dream!?"

"It really isn't." Basa-kun said, approaching the woman before putting a reassuring hand on her palm. "You've entered a new world now, Aoki-san. I know it's confusing, but I'll answer any of your questions that you'll have. I'm sure that there's plenty swimming in your mind right now."

…And so, with that statement said, the floodgates opened and Aoki-san let out a stream of babble and questions. Yuki watched as the blue-haired woman floundered as she tried to comprehend a world that had overturned her common sense.

That would be a futile effort, she reflected. Because even now she still struggles to make sense of it herself.
An entire general explanation later and they were subjected to an amusing sight, one that put Yuki's thoughts on her previous revelations in the sidelines momentarily.

"B-Basa-kun! I-I can't believe that you've been carrying this burden for so long!" Aoki-san cried out, sobbing as she hugged Basa-kun tightly. "I knew that there were some strange things you get caught up in, but to think you've been protecting us and many others for all this time…!" she hiccuped. "Y-You're such a good and earnest boy!"

"...It's not that big of a deal."

Yuki smiled at the rare scene of Basa-kun who looked uncomfortable at the affection and sympathy given by the woman. He was stiff in her embrace as she tried to comfort Aoki-san by patting her in the back, trying to soothe the woman from her tears. This was one of the many moments around her that he looked awkward and unsure unlike the usual self-assured and indifferent demeanor he exuded.

It was quite satisfying, to say the least. Especially with what he so casually dropped earlier.

"Hehehe… look at him, trying to act all cool." Rias-san whispered beside her while giggling. It looks like she wasn't the only one amused by the sight. "That guy tries to play it off whenever he gets praised, but he gets all shy and embarrassed on the inside~!"

Basa-kun twitched, undoubtedly hearing her words, and leveled a flat look at the redhead who just looked unrepentant. Yuki concealed her own smile.

"Is that so? I did notice that he tries to act rough in the exterior despite his deeds showing otherwise." she said, playing along. "Could it be that? He's a tsundere?"

Rias-san chortled at her comment and Basa-kun violently twitched, aiming a flatter look towards her. "Pfft, t-that's definitely spot on! That guy's a definite tsundere!" the redhead giggled.

Basa-kun let out a sigh. "Don't even compare me to those bipolar misunderstanding machines." he then looked down to Aoki-san, who was oddly quiet while she buried her face on his chest. "And stop it with the teasing. You're reacting way too much." he said flatly.

The blue-haired woman then chuckled, letting go of him and wiping away the slight tears in her eyes. "It's not teasing… I really am glad." Aoki-san said with a smile on her face. It then dimmed slightly as she gained a thoughtful look. "Still… to think things I never thought possible were actually real. I can't believe magic exists…" her thoughtful expression shifted into a disturbed one. "W-Wait, does that mean all sorts of monsters and things are out there too…?"

"You don't have to be afraid, Aoki-san! Even if the world wasn't what you quite thought it was, and that there are dangers you didn't know were actually real - we're here to protect you!" Rias-san vowed. "We're strong, you know?"

Yuki nodded. "Although I'm not quite at the level of being a fighter as Rias-san and Basa-kun, I would say we managed problems satisfactorily. And I doubt there is anything that could make things difficult with Basa-kun's presence."

"I think you're doing great, Yuki-san. You're improving leaps and bounds. You'll probably catch up in no time." the redhead replied to her with a supportive smile. "But yes, I think nothing will go wrong with Basa-kun here. He has been dealing with this for many years now, and I know he's very powerful." she attested.

Aoki-san blinked, turning to Basa-kun as if she couldn't quite comprehend the idea. "R-Really? Are you some sort of special magician, Basa-kun?"

"Just as special as the three of you are. You all have the potential to be as strong as me." he answered. "Most of the strength came from me taking advantage of abilities and phenomena in different settings, after all."

"...Right, you did say the world works like a story too…" Aoki-san said blankly. "That's… still quite unbelievable, to say the least. Are you saying that my life is going according to some plot? I don't quite think I have a lively enough life for it to belong in some anime or manga…" she paused, looking uncertain. "O-or does it? I'm afraid I'm not caught up with that sort of stuff these days…"

"Yes, your life is dictated by some plot. Specifically, you belong in the adult genre." Basa-kun explained. "With our many sexual escapades, it counts as erotic literature."

Aoki-san blinked, before her cheeks reddened. "Ah, I-I see. That… makes sense." the woman squirmed. "I-I suppose with how intense it gets, sometimes it starts to resemble those types of…" she looked away, trailing off.

"Oh wow, so Aoki-san is from that sort of genre then? I didn't know that, but I guess it fits." Rias-san said with a curious tone. "Ero-doujin's, huh… how does that work? Do you go to sex marathons and fuck all day and night? Maybe those exhibitionism plays? Or is it like S&M?"

Aoki-san's blush intensified as her legs squirmed under her. Yuki tried to keep her expression neutral, and tried to not bring up the images of Basa-kun and Aoki-san doing those deeds in her mind.

"...A-All of them." the woman muttered, looking to the side.

She failed. Yuki shut her eyes and tried to fight down the rising blush on her face.

"Damn." Rias-san let out, biting her lip and looking at Basa-kun. "I really need to up my ante so that I can do it with you already."

Basa-kun raised a single brow. "Take me out for dinner first then maybe I'll consider it. It'll take more than a virgin heroine like you to seduce me." he drawled out, making the redhead squawk.

"W-Wha—!? S-So what if I'm a virgin!? I can totally seduce people! I'm a damn demon!" Rias-san then turned to Yuki and invaded her personal space, much to her surprise. "Y-Yuki-san, I look beautiful don't I? You totally would want to have sex with a bombshell like me, right?"

Yuki felt her face turn red at the sight of the redhead displaying herself to her. Unfortunately due to the girl's forward pose, her eyes were unconsciously drawn down on the demon's beautiful face and her luscious lips, then further down to her bountiful figure. Rias-san smirked triumphantly.

"Aha! See, even Yuki-san agrees!"

"I-I didn't say anything!" Yuki shouted, blushing.

Basa-kun had a flat look. "That doesn't count. You're supernaturally beautiful as a demon, and Yuki is a vulnerable closet bisexual who doesn't even realize she's one. There's no seducing to be done at all."

H-Hold on, what outrageous things was this man spouting!?

"W-Wha—! I-I'm not—!" Yuki shut her eyes and tried to regain her composure. She took a deep breath. "...P-Please, can we just move on from this topic? I believe we're trying to reassure Aoki-san from her worries, correct?"

"Very subtle."

She twitched at his statement. "Please don't make me go over there and smack you, Basa-kun."

A sudden laugh interrupted them before things could escalate, and Yuki turned to see that Aoki-san was looking at them with a joyful smile on her face. The worry that was present on her face ever since they explained the current situation was gone, replaced only with clear mirth and happiness.

Yuki relaxed. It appears that their little banter had given her a slight reprieve. Eventually, her laughter died down into slight chuckles.

"T-That was quite a scene… Thank you, you three. That helped a lot." the woman said, giving them a smile. "I-I still have plenty of questions, but I have a feeling that could be better done later. You three said that you came here for something, isn't that right?"

The three of them glanced between one another, then Basa-kun nodded at her.

"...We do. We want to be around Terumi Fuuka." he stated. "That woman carries a death flag with her. Her plot is about to start, meaning she's predicted to die sometime from now."

That made Aoki-san's smile fall immediately, her eyes widening in horror. "W-What!?" she gasped out. "T-Terumi-chan's going to die!? Are you sure!?"

"Yes. A monster will come and kill her." Basa-kun said, making Aoki-san pale. But before she could panic some more, Rias-san quickly went up to speak.

"Don't worry, Aoki-san! As we said, we're here to put a stop to that!" Rias-san assured her. "She isn't going to die. Right, guys?" she asked, turning to them.

Yuki nodded in agreement, then turned to look at Basa-kun. He just stood there with a neutral look.

"She'll be fine." he simply stated. "Your assistance to make us be around her would be appreciated though."

Aoki-san still looked worried, but she nodded, eyes glinting with resolve. "If… If you need my help, then consider it done. So please help Terumi-chan." she said determinedly. "You need to be around her, then? I can arrange something. Fortunately she doesn't have anything in her schedule but she'll be hanging around the building assisting others."

"Assisting others?" Yuki asked.

The woman nodded, slightly losing her worried look in favor of a soft smile. "That girl… she has a bleeding heart and a sense of duty to match that. She isn't supposed to be working right now, but she comes for the sake of her juniors. She even helps out other employees like me." she frowned. "Terumi-chan should be consoling those girls, but… well, she has a tendency to get a bit overbearing. She should be free right now so I'll give her a call."

Aoki-san turned around to her table and used the desk phone, doing just that. They waited after that, and not even a few minutes later the door to Aoki-san's office received a knock from the outside. Aoki-san opened the door and there, they saw Terumi Fuuka standing at the entrance.

"Yumiko-san? You called for me?" she asked with a smile.

"Yes. You've been thrown out by the doctor, right?" the blue-haired woman asked.

Fuuka-san stiffened. "I— I did not get thrown out!" she stuttered.

"Right." Aoki-san said, unconvinced. "And you won't listen to me telling you to go home as well, correct? You're not scheduled for anything today."

"I told you I didn't get…" she looked away. "...Okay, you're right." the idol then sighed. "Please don't ask me to go home. I don't think I can do that with how restless I feel right now… I'll just be worried sick in my apartment if I go back." she frowned. "My kouhai's still don't know what happened, but I know the news will spread sooner or later. I want to be here when that happens."

Aoki-san's gaze softened. "I can understand… would you mind if I ask you for a favor in the meantime then?" she turned around and gestured to the rest of them. Fuuka-san's eyes easily lit up as she recognized them, especially after the incident and their mutual introductions during that. "I'd like you to give a little tour of the place for these three. I invited them but… well, you see how that turned out."

True to her word, Aoki-san secured them an opportunity to be around Terumi Fuuka.

"...I see. So a tour for these three heroes, huh?" Fuuka-san said, before letting out a smile. "Sure, I suppose it wouldn't do good if their only impression of the company is with what happened earlier."

"Thank you. I'd do it myself, but I have a feeling I'd be very busy after this." Aoki-san said in gratitude. Then her gaze turned far-off, as if she was consumed by her thoughts. "...And I think I'd want to have some alone time before all that as well, just to process all this." she added.

"It was a very shocking turn of events." Fuuka-san agreed, misunderstanding what she meant.

"Yes… yes it was." Aoki-san said in a dazed tone.

Basa-kun walked towards the door, with them following right behind him. As he passed by Aoki-san, he grabbed her hand and squeezed it. "We'll see you later, Aoki-san."

The woman blinked, losing her dazed look, then she let out a warm smile and squeezed his hand back. "I will." she said, before letting go and taking a step away. The woman then frowned and gazed at them solemnly. "Be safe. All of you."

Basa-kun simply nodded.

With that, they left Aoki-san's office and closed the door as they left, following Fuuka-san outside. As they did so however, the idol had a curious look aimed at them.

"What was that about?" she asked.

"She's just worried, especially with what happened." Basa-kun stated vaguely. "Anyhow, we were promised a tour?"

Saying that, the woman's eyes brightened and she gave them all a smile. "Sure. Follow me, you three! I'll show you around!"
The LOVE☆Doll talent agency. It's a company that mainly caters to idols.

It's already obvious from their company name since it itself is a pun; LOVE in Japanese would be 'Ai', and with the Japanese's weird pronunciations for english words, the word 'Doll' would have the same phonemes as '-dol'. So if you combine those two things, you get 'idol'. Very creative, I know.

Of course, it also gives it a coincidentally X-rated meaning that clearly doesn't foreshadow anything, wink wonk. But then again that's already been dealt with, especially with the help of the heroine's sister, who the heroine called in the heat of the moment. I have my own ways to deal with the director, but that works too.

Hm, it's a potential plot hook though. I'd expect the sister to get curious sometime later.

But I digress.

Anyway, this talent agency is filled to the brim with a curious cast of characters since lots of settings utilize idols, but in the end it's no amusement park. Lots of production workshops, casting rooms, and even a big stage to perform on which really showed that this talent agency is one of the major ones in the block, but that's it really. Pretty boring, all things considered… Well, for me, that is. Yuki and Rias are curious about an insider view on being an idol and is currently being enlightened by the walking death flag with us.

Then again, I'm acquainted myself with movie sets and similar places from my many involvements in different genres (happens more often that you'd think; there comes at least a point in detective plots that a murder happens there for some reason), but the two girls with me hadn't, so they probably found this whole thing fascinating unlike me.

"—And this place right here is where we practice our dance. I'm sure you must have passed by it on your way to the management office." the idol explained, showing the earlier lobby where I talked with a murder mystery girl that looked similar to the heroine. "As you can see, lots of other idols are here. It'll be a busy few months for many of us, with the upcoming event and all."

"If I may ask, why aren't you practicing with them, Fuuka-san?" the heroine questioned.

The idol paused, before seemingly gaining a thoughtful look as she put a finger on her chin. "Hmm… well, I normally wouldn't say the reason…"

Yuki shook her head. "It's okay if you don't have to answer, Fuuka-san. It was just out of curiosity."

The idol smiled. "It's fine. With what happened earlier, you three are pretty much trusted. Plus I was dropping hints about it to my fans as well so it's not really much of a big deal." she shook her head. "The truth is, I'm planning to graduate as an idol and try a solo career. It'll be a couple months before the event so there's not much point in me participating."

"Right, and you did say that you have a fiance as well, didn't you?" Rias piped up.

"Yep! And we'll be married right after my graduation!" she turned to me with a teasing smile. "So don't get any ideas, mister!"

I raised a brow. "What makes you think I'd have 'ideas'?"

"Hm, aside from the fact that you look like a playboy, act like a playboy, and are surrounded by beautiful girls?" she gained a faux-thoughtful look. "Hmm… maybe it's because you've been staring at me too much."

"I haven't been staring. Are you sure you're not the one that's conscious of my gaze?"

She crossed her arms, giving me a sly, 'I know what you're doing' look. "I'm not flirting with you."

What's with this woman.

I really haven't been staring at her. The other two heroines with me were actually more conspicuous with that, looking alert in case of anything that might endanger the idol. If anything, they should be the ones she should've noticed.

"...Sure." I settled.

The idol gave me a scolding frown. "You know, you shouldn't really be doing that. Yumiko-san wouldn't appreciate it when you flirt with other girls… I know she's a widow, so don't go filling her heart and leaving it empty a second time, alright?" she warned, tone solemn. Then a few seconds later her frown was replaced with a smile. "Anyhow, can I ask my own question?"

Bit of a mood whiplash there, but I waved it off. I shrugged. "Go ahead."

"So, why did you three come here? Are you interested in becoming idols perhaps?" the idol questioned, head tilted curiously. "You all certainly have the looks for it. Yanai-san has a similar fashion to many of my kouhai… and you two, Satanichia-san and Basa-san. Both of you are foreigners, correct?"

"Yep!" Rias said.

I, meanwhile, raised a brow from that.

"Oh?" I said, slightly surprised. "People don't usually notice that about me."

"Well, the name gives it away. And your appearance too." her eyes sharpened as she observed me. "It's easy to think of you as a delinquent, but taking a closer look that's what you naturally look like, right? You didn't dye your hair nor give yourself a tan at all." she then gave me a sympathetic smile. "That must have caused you a bit of trouble. Some of my kouhai have similar problems, you see. I knew one girl who got bullied for having natural blonde hair."

…Alright, that gives a few points in her favor.

As expected of an idol, she knew her fashion. I suppose she could spot the difference between what is cosmetic and what is natural with her experience in work.

"We're not here to apply as idols, Fuuka-san. We're just here to visit Aoki-san's workplace after she invited us here." the heroine answered.

"I see… a shame then." the idol didn't seem to mind the us not joining, and she turned around and continued walking. "Anyway, we should go to the next place I can show you. It's a bit far away actually, but I think you three are going to like it!"

We followed her and the two girls with me continued to chat with her as she led us to the elevator, then we were brought to the topmost floor in the agency building after a short elevator ride. As we continued walking to wherever the idol was trying to lead us, I glanced to the side to see that the heroine was discreetly glancing at me, as if she wanted to say something.

I casted a little spell so that we could speak telepathically - something that I've mimicked in a particular setting which included psychic viral mutants from some island laboratory. It's a handy trick that I'm sure would be something we'll use often to coordinate with each other on the field now that I wouldn't be working alone. Certainly would be much more reliable than using standard comm units.

Yuki stiffened slightly as she felt my magical energy connect to hers, while Rias just sent me a curious look when I did the same to her.

—So, something you want to talk about? I spoke in their minds.

For their part, they didn't even react when they heard my voice as we kept walking and keeping the idol busy as she kept yapping about something or another. Impressively though, the two girls were keeping up with her conversation despite them not having thought-partitioning down yet for multitasking.

…There's no sign of monsters or any sort of danger at all. The heroine said, making her worry known. Will her death really happen today? I know you said it will, but is there a possibility that it changed with our presence?

Possible, but very unlikely. I answered. It would take more than us just talking to her to stop her death. It falls under minimal interaction in most standards.

…But how can we actually stop her death from happening, Basa-kun? You never said anything about that. Rias asked.

I mentally hummed. Tell me what you think. You guys are here to get experience after all.

That made Rias blink. Er… okay? the redhead's face scrunched up in thought. Can't we protect Fuuka-san from danger? Keep her away from suspicious places or stuff like that? That should prevent her death, correct?

I sent them a mental impression of a head shake. No, her role in her own plot is to be the first victim, therefore fate itself will insist her to die. Terumi Fuuka is marked to be killed by a monster in her plot, from this day onwards. Even if we try to, we don't have the time to protect her at all times.

The redhead let out a frown outwardly. I guess that's true…

"—Hm…? Is there something wrong, Satanichia-san?" the idol asked, stopping what she was saying after noticing her expression.

"O-Oh, nothing! I was just, you know…." Rias floundered, before settling on an excuse. "I was just thinking… h-how it feels like to have your own wedding? I-I mean, you did say you will be having your own, Fuuka-san."

The idol blinked, then giggled. "I see. So you want to know about my wedding? I can tell you that arranging it is very hectic." she let out a smile. "I wanted it to be perfect. I have it pictured in my mind, you know? An ethereal, floaty scenery… filled with hanging flowers and decorative balloons. I want it to ensnare me, make my breath catch in my throat as I walk down the aisle…"

Rias took on a fascinated expression as she listened. "Huh…"

In the meantime, the heroine telepathically spoke up once more. …What about getting rid of her death flags? You said something earlier about signs that she'll die, like her hairstyle. What if we changed that about her?

Those are just signs. Curing the symptom doesn't cure the ailment itself, does it? I replied, before I slightly titled my head in consideration. Though if you mean by other signs like her having a fiance or her gentle personality, then destroying her relationships or inducing a personality change could be enough to change her role from a victim character.

I'd rather not do that, thank you. The heroine said flatly.

—What if we just kill the monster then? Rias piped up, acting like she was listening to the idol as she kept talking about her wedding. Shouldn't that get rid of the danger itself?

You're on the right track. I commented.

The heroine frowned thoughtfully. So the monster has to die during her encounter with it. In short, we use Fuuka-san as bait. I don't quite like the way we'd risk her to such a danger… but I suppose at least that way, she won't die.

In a way, yeah. I said idly.

The heroine's eyes narrowed in suspicion at me. …You're not telling us something. She deduced. What are you—

"—Alright, here we are, you three!" the idol suddenly said, interrupting the heroine. She brought us to a set of stairs that is curiously going up. The heroine's eyes widened imperceptibly at the sight, her gaze turning to me, then back to the stairs. "It's just right up here." the idol continued.

Rias seems to have caught Yuki's change in expression. What's wrong? she asked, concerned.

…This is the top floor, isn't it? So why is there another set of stairs? The heroine pointed out, making the redhead's eyes lit up in realization. This isn't something supernatural that affects the building itself, is it?

I don't feel any signs of magic… Rias trailed off. But you're right. It is strange. We should be ready.

I stayed quiet as the two talked, the three of us following the idol from behind.

The four of us went up the stairs, a sense of unease growing in our little group that the idol seemed oblivious to. The heroine and the redhead were tense, bodies poised and alert for anything that might happen. The sense of unease reached a crescendo as we reached the top and was left face to face with a door.

"Alright, this is my favorite place in the building. It's technically supposed to be restricted to other people but… don't just tell anyone we've been here, alright?" she smiled mischievously, bringing a finger up to her lips.

She opened the door, and Yuki and Rias stiffened—

"Ta-da!"

—And we were left with the sight of a clear blue sky.

The two girls beside me blinked.

The idol stepped out of the roof, giggling as a strong breeze made her dress and hair flutter. "So this is the building's roof! I come here when I have free time with others, like eating lunch or after practice. It's very windy here, isn't it?" she said cheerfully.

Seeing as the two girls were still surprised, I took the opportunity to speak up.

"Yeah." I said, taking a look around the place. "Pretty good view too."

I wasn't lying. Relative to the other buildings around this downtown area, this building was the highest and offered a good view of everything below. Additionally on the horizon, further into the bustling city, you could see the sight of taller buildings that offered a great perspective of the local skyline. I certainly wouldn't mind eating my lunch here.

"Right!? This place is the best!"

…It was just the roof. The heroine muttered telepathically. On the outside her face was as neutral as ever, but if one were to look closely then you could spot the smidgen of red on her cheeks. O-Of course, that makes sense…

Pfft. And she was so worked up about it too.

I-It was your fault acting so suspicious! I thought you were trying to surprise us or something! The heroine shouted in my mind, tone embarrassed.

Wait, did I broadcast those thoughts? Didn't mean that. Teehee pero.

This guy… Yuki grumbled. Was I broadcasting still? Whoops.

Oh, it's okay Yuki-san! Nothing wrong with being cautious! Rias consoled with a chuckle, before moving on to chat with the idol and look at the view from high up.

…Right. The heroine fought down her embarrassment, then she turned her gaze to me. Now, Basa-kun. You're being awfully vague earlier, particularly on what I said about Fuuka-san not dying… Was that meant to imply something?

I met her gaze with a raised brow. Are you giving up? This is supposed to be a test, you know?

She let out a mental sigh. Yes. I'm giving up. Please tell us the answer already.

Alright. I shrugged at that. See the thing is, because she's a victim type of character and with us allowing a monster to be around, along with the presence of definite obstacles that try to prevent the birth of a new plotline… I looked up into the sky. …Well, the narrative fate will absolutely try to guarantee her death.

There was a definite pause as I said that.

"What?" / "Eh?" Yuki and Rias said out loud. momentarily forgetting to use their telepathy.

The idol looked at them in puzzlement. "Hm? …Is there something wrong?" she started to walk towards us. "I—"

What happened after that only occured in less than a second, leaving the two unable to react much to my predictions.

The moment she moved towards us, something snaked down from above, almost innocuous as it did so. It was, however, anything but as it was a little rope tied with a noose on the end. It slid itself almost snuggingly and peacefully past through her head before landing on her neck.

"—ggrhkk!"

Then it tightened, lifting the idol up high - the gravity causing her to let out a unfeminine choking sound as her throat was constricted. And even then that sudden movement is fatal enough as I heard a dangerous crack indicating that her neck broke.

And following the rope that carried the idol, looking right above to whatever it was connected to…


Spoiler

…Well, that's something you don't see everyday.

There we could see a very strange monster, floating like a balloon up high - somehow with the same face as the one that's dying on the rope underneath. It sounds very stupid, but its appearance was so uncanny and unnatural that it was enough to be creepy. It also appeared with the terrifying presence like the monster in the church, but curiously this one was a bit weaker.

Still, the mere sight of it made the heroine and the redhead shocked and unsettled, especially with the dangling body it carried.

"Fuuka-san!" Yuki shouted in horror.

"It got her!" Rias cried out. "W-What the hell even is that!?"

Oi, don't just stand there and get caught up in your reactions. Valuable opportunities are wasted from going all 'Nani!?' when you could be beating it up already. Looks like I'd have to beat that out of these two in practice spars.

Not that it isn't understandable since it does look pretty weird, but it looks like I have to deal with this myself.

—So I moved.

The balloon monster was barely able to register the moment I appeared right in front of its face before kicking it with reinforced legs. My foot hit its face and after the initial resistance, my foot tore through it as it popped like a balloon, air rushing out of its surprisingly hollow insides. The monster didn't even have a chance to change the expression on its large stupid face as it died.

That would've been it… but there was something wrong. My sixth senseTM​ was going overdrive.

I was proven right when I felt some cursed energy travel from the monster down to the idol. I reacted quickly, twisting midair and ripping the woman off the noose on her neck as I saw her face slightly tear similar to the wound I inflicted to the monster. I managed to stop it from getting worse by using a burst of mana to drive away the backlash, and the curse whizzed away into nothingness.

A resonance effect, I realized. The monster was clearly connected to the idol since it bore its face. Perhaps it meant something metaphorical, but all it did was to make the monster even weirder.

The whole exchange lasted in like a second or so and I landed on the ground whilst holding the idol in a bridal carry, before laying her down on the floor. With that, I took stock of the woman's injuries.

Her face was bleeding slightly and there wasn't any much damage to her face thanks to me preventing the backlash from the monster. But that didn't really matter as her neck was broken from the noose hoisting her up earlier and that was fatal enough of an injury. Textbook Hangman's fracture. This woman was, in fact, very much dead.

Good thing though that death isn't the end for many things, especially for a world as ridiculous as this.

Her soul would leave her body in about a few seconds or so, going to whatever afterlife system the world needs her to be in, but it was enough time for me to work my magic. A little bullshit healing martial arts to realign her vertebrae and a healing spell to fix the damage, then moving on to the gash on her face. And just like that her body was now completely healed and as good as new.

Then I kickstarted her heart with an isolated lightning spell targeting her cardiac muscles and the woman was alive again.

Rapid footsteps approached behind me, making me turn around to look. It was Yuki and Rias. Looks like they finally regained their composure.

"Basa-kun! What happened to Fuuka-san!? Is she okay!?" Rias shouted in concern, expression fearful much like Yuki who followed beside her.

"She died, but it's fine now. I revived her." I stood up, ignoring their stunned looks and giving them a hard one of my own. "Anyway, look alive you two… It looks like the plot is starting now."

I looked up at the sky.

The two girls blinked, then followed my gaze. Their postures tensed and the two visibly looked at what they saw in shock, but ultimately managed to get a hold of themselves focused.

Yuki let out a deep breath while she summoned her spirit katanas, the sheathed weapons appearing on her hip, and Rias' eyes narrowed in focus as she unfurled her wings and summoned a magic circle that lazily spun on her palms. They stared at the sky with a hard gaze, intent to deal with our current problem.


Spoiler

Because now, similar balloon monsters started floating from high above with faces of many different people. They dotted the sky countlessly, casting a shade on the sun as they blocked it, appearing like a very demented and strange impression of an alien invasion but with… weird balloon heads. I've seen many strange things, but this one is definitely getting in the top ten.

I let out an exhale.

"This world doesn't just run out of surprises, does it." I said flatly.
