Wow, guess who lives? Sorry for the long wait. Things were busy, but at least I'll be able to conclude this little arc now. Was also planning to create a new story that I'll post some time… despite the fact that I still have many unfinished stories waiting in line :V


Chapter 14

As Basa, Yuki, and Rias are currently dealing with the appearance of horror monsters, inside the building a different scenario was happening entirely. The practice and rehearsals of the many idols participating in the upcoming Idol festival was momentarily halted to address something of importance.

The dance studio that the idols were practicing in was very spacious, enough to house a hundred people with enough space for extras, and was complete with a mock stage set which would be similar to the one in the actual event. Almost fifty or more idol groups were inside making the room filled with a colorful cast of girls, and along with the production crew who assisted them, it made even such a spacious place feel crowded.

Aoki Yumiko stood in front of the crowd as their attention was focused on her.

In light of recent events, an impromptu meeting is arranged within the dance studio. Rumors and details of what happened had already spread - undoubtedly, there are some who witnessed the director of their partner company being hauled by the police - and things would devolve the longer things don't get addressed properly. The split of the company's higher ups on how to deal with the situation wasn't helping things either, so as the highest person in charge that is currently not being suckered into the power struggle within the company, she took it upon herself to deal with it.

Her mind was still whirling from the things that she had learned today. Even now she wondered if what Basa-kun had told her earlier were all false. Magic being? Terumi-chan dying? The world working like an anime story? It all seemed far-fetched and outlandish.

Yet despite all that, she kept her confident smile up.

"So," she began cheerily, addressing the crowd - many of their faces familiar as a veteran manager who had personally worked with many idol groups. "I'm sorry for interrupting this practice session so suddenly, but there are… recent events that needed to be addressed."

A girl suddenly spoke up. Yumiko remembered her as a particularly gutsy and impatient girl, having the same air as Rias-chan, but a unique impulsiveness which led to her charm. "Excuse me, Yumiko-san! I heard that a few idols got blackmailed, was that rumor true!?"

The crowd murmured at that. Those who had heard of it looked similarly concerned, but those who didn't hear the news were just shocked at what they heard. Going back to the girl, a member of her group smacked her in the head for her speaking up, making the girl yelp out an 'Ow!'.

She blinked. That… that reminded her of some of the slapstick anime she watched as a teenager— N-No, no. That can wait for another time.

"Well, it looks like many of you have heard it already." she said with a sardonic smile, one which eventually turned into a frown. Here comes the hard part. "Unfortunately… Yes, that rumor is true. The director of a partner company was found blackmailing a few girls. He was caught and is currently being put behind bars as we speak."

The murmurs and hushed talking exploded into full-blown clamor. She quickly clapped her hands, cutting in and gaining their attention before it could snowball into something worse. "I won't say the names of the idols in question to keep them safe, but you should know that they're currently recovering. Thankfully, we managed to intervene before anything drastic happened."

"How long has this been happening!?" one girl shouted.

"We've heard rumors, but for it to be really true…!" she caught another girl mutter.

Yumiko frowned. "I understand that the news is a shock to everyone, but you can rest assured that we are already doing our best investigating what is going on along with the authorities. Everyone involved will be held responsible." she reassured.

Her words weren't as effective as she liked, seeing the faces of the girls, but it was understandable considering the situation. Even she was unsure of what to do considering the state of the management right now.

"Yumiko-san." a girl suddenly spoke up near her, making her look at them. Yumiko realized that she was the lead of the idol group that just finished practicing on the stage before she appeared with her announcement - Sayaka-chan, if she recalled correctly. The girl with straight black hair and cool disposition reminded her of Yuki-chan… along with many other girls here, now that she noticed.

"Y-Yes, Sayaka-chan?" she said, focusing once more on the conversation at hand.

She was quiet for a moment, seemingly in thought. "I have to wonder - I ran into a few people that wanted to visit you, and I can't help but notice that they're sudden appearance was strange." she tilted her head. "Did they have something to do with the incident?"

E-Eh!? H-How…!?

A few people blinked in confusion at her sudden statement. It was, after all, a completely random thing to say. Yet for Yumiko the whole thing was a completely accurate shot in the dark that it left her reeling in surprise. How did she even manage to get to that conclusion!?

"I-I'm not sure what you're talking about?" she said in confusion, trying to cover her surprise. Judging by the slight narrowing of the girls' eyes though, she hadn't quite managed to - and the girl opened her mouth, undoubtedly about to question her some more.

Thankfully, she was saved from an awkward questioning.

"—What is the meaning of this!?"

The door suddenly opened roughly, banging on the walls and almost tearing off its hinges as it swung open. They all looked as another manager, a peer of Yumiko's in terms of seniority, entered the room with an incensed look on his face.

"Aoki! What are you doing stopping the dance practice!? You're disrupting the schedule!" the man shouted.

She frowned. "I thought it prudent to address a concern before it could get worse. It's my responsibility as their manager."

"It's your responsibility to shut your trap and do what you're told!" he retorted angrily. "Now leave and quit putting rubbish on these idol's heads!"

"What are you talking about? An idol group was just blackmailed - by a director, no less! This is no little matter that can be just ignored!" she said back, her voice rising as well.

"Are you seriously believing in that rumor?"

A befuddled look appeared in her face. "What?"

The manager gave her a sneer. "A director of a partner company blackmailing our idols? Don't be stupid. This is why people like you shouldn't be in charge - do you think you can go freely claiming things like that?"

"They were arrested earlier!" And she saw it happen right in front of her!

He scoffed. "So? That person was just a stalker that had been arrested after breaking in. An entirely unrelated incident. As the chief manager, I would've thought that you can manage to differentiate between truth and rumor." he shook his head. "Now leave these idols be. I'm sure you've fed them enough bullshit for them to drown in it."

The girls and staff around her began murmuring once more, confusion and doubt appearing in their expressions once more as the man's words served to muddle the situation in their minds. Yumiko scowled and glared at the manager who simply looked at her with a gleam in his eye; and just like that, she realized that this man was most likely on the side that worked with the arrested director.

"Do you think you can do this?" she asked darkly. In response, he tilted his head questioningly.

"I don't understand what you're talking about, but I was sent by the higher ups to fix anything that might make the situation more complicated as it is." he mirrored her glare. "Expect some words from them after your little stunt here."

Yumiko growled, opening her mouth to deny his words - but a sight of something made her pause. Right there, visible on the window just behind the manager.

"W-What…?"

That was because what she was looking at… it was the strangest thing that she had ever seen. It was a floating head, with a rope fastened under it. Like the most surreal balloon in existence.

All concern on the present situation was replaced with panic, and she turned to the girls to see if she was seeing things correctly. They were all focused on her and her fellow manager, who was now looking quite smug, misinterpreting her shock as him managing to get one over her verbally. They showed no sign of seeing those creatures floating outside, not even taking the slightest glance at the window.

Was she turning insane? What exactly was happening?

Her fellow manager smirked. "What? Can't say anything back? If I were you, I'd be returning to my office and packing up. This sort of slander is unforgivable and…" he blinked as his words trailed off. The manager then brought something out from his pocket, revealing a phone receiving a call. The man clicked his tongue and angrily took it. "What? I'm in the middle of something here." a pause. "Yanai who? What are you on about?"

Then the man suddenly froze in place.

"Fired!? Me!? What the hell did I do!? I'm covering up all our asses here and—!"

He stopped, suddenly aware of the gazes of every idol and staff aimed towards him, before backing away with an awkward expression. "T-There's, there's something I need to do." he stuttered.

Yumiko can only stare as the now ex-manager then ran out of the dance studio as fast as he could. That was a bit sudden.

"Does he have something to do with the incident?" she heard Sayaka-chan mutter, once more demonstrating her uncanny intuition. "And he mentioned the Yanai… he must mean the family of politicians."

In the back of her mind she noticed the same thing, meaning that Yuki-chan's family had already caught on to the people that were involved in the scandal and were removing them from the company. Considering that it's only been a couple of hours since the incident, the speed of it would've been alarming.

Unfortunately, she was still stuck on the floating head creatures that were right outside the window. Something that no one noticed even now, despite the many people here. Even Sayaka-chan who was facing that direction! If she noticed such minute details from the manager, shouldn't be noticing that there's something wrong in the sky right now!?

Before she could fully lose her mind on what was happening she felt her phone buzz in her pocket. Yumiko took it out in a daze - and then suddenly blinked, when she noticed who had sent her a message.

It was Basa-kun.

Keep calm and don't worry, we have things under control. We'll be containing these things for now. Be rest assured that people won't notice or get hurt by those things - though, I'm going to need your help with that.

Yumiko read the instructions and details that he sent, gradually losing her hysteria as she finally settled into a course of action where she wouldn't be left floundering without a clue. All that was left was determination so that she could keep her girls and coworkers safe - along with the undercurrent of nervousness towards the young man and his two girlfriends for what they would be facing.

She put the phone down and took a deep breath.

Then, she clapped her hands and gained the attention of the people inside the studio, cutting their mumbling as they turned to look at her.

"So!" she said, the mask of confidence returning to her as she addressed them all. "Where were we again?"

Right now, she has a role to play.


Yuki felt the heaviness within her body disappear as her training mystic code deactivated, and for the first time in a few days, her body felt as light as the wind. She did a couple of swings on her sword to test her strength, finding it much easier without the artificial burden done by the training tool, before taking a deep breath to calm her nervousness and anticipation for the upcoming battle.

Most of her forays with Basa-kun could be described as 'cleaning up' so to speak; where they just kept themselves hidden and defeated monsters or manipulated events in certain plots to not make it worse. She even just took her first life a few days ago. This was going to be the first time she would partake in such a large-scale battle.

Yuki made to focus her mind on the task at hand, then looked at Basa-kun, who was currently looking at his phone.

"...Hm, looks like this was just a local phenomenon. None of these creatures seem to be appearing in other places, so these balloon head creatures might just be spilling continuously from this certain area." Basa-kun inferred, bringing down his phone.

Rias-san frowned as she stared at the creatures in the sky, a readied magical circle spinning idly on her hand thrumming with her demonic magic.

"There's way too much of these things… How are we going to deal with this, Basa-kun?" she asked gravely.

A neutral hum answered her, before he spoke. "I asked Aoki-san to gather the idols so the supernatural ones inside wouldn't notice and to prevent unnecessary risks. But with the monsters grouped up like this it makes things easier."

With that, Yuki watched as Basa-kun made a gesture, bringing his two fingers up like shinobi in modern media, and watched as her supernatural senses registered as he did… something that she didn't know, and probably haven't learned yet.

Then she watched as a sphere, registered in her magical senses as something black as ink, suddenly appeared up in the sky right where the creatures were. She watched as it expanded, enveloping the entirety of the area where the creatures are at, before it solidified and changed itself - warping light around it and making the black turn similar to its surroundings thus appearing completely camouflaged.

Although she was unfamiliar with the process, the end result was something that she knew from her studies - a bounded field, aiming to entrap the monsters from within that certain area, along with other uses that she didn't recognize.

"Huh…" Beside her, Rias-san blinked in surprise. "What was that, Basa-kun? I don't recognize that sort of magic." she said curiously.

"It's from an isolated plot involving Japanese exorcists. It's unique in a way that they seem to think that their magical system is the only one that exists, even overseas." he answered. "Not much going on for them, but they do have a fast bounded field casting spell."

He glanced at them. "By the way, those monsters maintain a connection with the people who they have as heads. That barrier should prevent any backlash from traveling to those they connected to. No one should notice the barrier and everything inside it - even from the people from which the setting the barrier comes from due to my little modification." he added. "So go ahead and let loose."

"Alright! I'll go do that!" Rias-san shouted excitedly. Yuki watched as the redhead flapped her wings and ascended into the sky. The monsters were visibly surprised at her, before it turned into fear when she started shooting demonic spells conjured out of her magic circles. The monsters around her died easily.

It was looking at her friend that Yuki realized a certain problem.

"...How can I reach that?" she muttered.

She never learned anything that would make her fly. Her ranged attacks are don't reach that high either.

"You don't have anything to fly with, but I can teach you a trick to reach those heights." Yuki blinked as she realized that Basa-kun was now standing beside her. She tilted her head at his words.

"A trick? What do you mean by— Eek!"

Yuki let out a squeak of surprise when Basa-kun suddenly grabbed her waist, pulling her up against his side. She felt the familiar sensation of her face pressed against his pectorals and unconsciously breathed his scent, the position reminding her of what happened after her talk with her clubmates - yet before she could register all that and become flustered, Basa-kun suddenly jumped high towards the monsters.

Her mouth felt dry when she glanced down and saw that the building they stood in was so far below now. Then as Basa-kun reached the apex of his jump, she felt herself pale when gravity reasserted itself since they were going to fall down this great height and—

They stopped, with Basa-kun landing midair like he was standing on invisible steps.

"W-What?" Yuki said in surprise.

"This is a trick in the same setting as your spirit weapon. With your level of control, you should be able to accomplish this easily." Basa-kun explained as he tapped his foot midair in demonstration. "Focus your spiritual energy like summoning your katanas, but isolate it in the bottom of your feet instead. The energy should act like a platform for you."

Yuki was quiet for a moment as she tried to set her head straight. "...Right."

She took a deep breath and then did what he instructed. Pulling the spiritual energy from the depths of her soul, she focused on letting it out on her feet only - then tentatively, she brought down a foot. She then felt some sort of invisible ground she was stepping on.

Feeling a bit confident she left Basa-kun's grasp and stood on her own. It's somewhat jarring to do this - her sense of touch registered that she was standing on a surface yet her sight clearly shows that she isn't. Her legs also felt a bit weak due to the instinctual fear associated with heights, but she managed to push through it.

"Good job." Basa-kun congratulated her. "Those will act as platforms you can jump from or steps if you're feeling lazy. Just remember that you're not on the ground though, so no rolling or anything like that. You're going to need to channel spiritual energy from different parts of your body if you want to attempt it."

"...Right." Yuki replied. For a moment she was silent, before she looked away. "...Please tell me next time before you'd grab me like that." she muttered.

Basa-kun stared at her. Yuki didn't meet his eyes, out of desire not to show her emotions and to not be reminded of… what would've flustered her earlier, and by extension, her little breakdown at school. Not like it worked though, considering Basa-kun raised a brow at her.

He then shrugged. "Sure." he acquiesced easily. After that, he looked above. "Better get ready though - here they come."

The words were like a bucket of ice that removed all flustered feelings from her. She turned in the direction he was looking and saw that the floating head creatures were moving towards them, giving malevolent smiles as they did so.

With that, Yuki readied her two katanas in a stance.

"Come join us…" the monsters muttered.

The ropes tied underneath them all reached towards her, moving tenderly as if it tried to take her in a sweet embrace… and when it approached her range—

"—Hah!"

Yuki let loose and slashed her swords, moving instinctually as her weapons cut the ropes into pieces before they could even reach her. The monsters screeched in pain, their grotesque faces twisting into ugly expressions.

Her body moved. The aerial steps were made without difficulty as she danced around the monsters and slashing their heads, deflating them like balloons and killing them. She felt a foreign energy coming out of them as they died, reaching to some far-away target but splashing harmlessly on the barrier Basa-kun set up. That must be the backlash that Basa-kun said earlier.

Seeing there was nothing to worry about, she moved onto the nearest monster. She jumped, falling in the air as her target was below her and slashed the unknowing monster midair, then landed herself on a created platform. The one monster near it looked at her in surprise, but wasn't able to do anything as she moved once again and punctured it with her sword.

Yuki danced around the sky; horror monsters dying all around her as her swords slashed and cut everything around it. Tattered ruins of the balloon-like skin flew around and decorated her like demented cherry blossom petals, all accompanied with a cacophony of the monsters' dying screams.

Despite the fact this situation was all strange and messed up…

Yuki let out a smile.

Somehow, she could get used to this.


She lost herself in the action, her mind stuck in a trance where she would dodge, block and slash. Yuki didn't know how many monsters she had cut already; but everytime she looked around, there seemed to be just as many as before.

She was starting to get a bit tired now. While the monsters were easy to kill, the sheer amount of them is proving to be a chore. They just seemed to be spilling continuously from the sky. Even Rias-san, who had been throwing spells and even let out a huge one that killed a lot of monsters in a single area, hadn't had much effect as the defeated monsters were replaced with new ones.

Yuki was starting to wonder if there was even an end to it.

She furrowed her brow and looked around. Perhaps she could voice her concern to Basa-kun, if he didn't already realize such a possibility. However, when she did so, she froze when a strange sight appeared near her.

"What…?"

A monster was floating near her. Yet unlike the other ones, this particular balloon… It had her face.

It was surreal, seeing her own face put into a malformed creature like that. She even felt a bit insulted looking at it. Like someone had taken her photo, made a deformed picture of her in a photo editing program and then showed it to her.

"Greetings… Me." it greeted her with an evil grin, one that she never imagined she would make. "I must say, it's a surprise to meet you here."

Her eyes narrowed at its words. There was a certain smugness in its tone - it must know that she can't just cut it down because of the connection it has with her, and since she's inside the barrier the backlash would actually affect her.

"No words? Not even deigning to engage in conversation?" the monster continued to speak. "I suppose it seems fitting for someone that has the 'Ice queen' moniker in all schools they have gone through. Trying to act as if she's above everyone else - but then we both know that's just a facade to make yourself not feel lonely, right?"

…And it looks like the monster also has some supernatural connection to her to the point that it knows her memories. She didn't even acknowledge the possibility of this monster actually being her, of course - since if that was the case then there should be no 'cursed energy' present in the monster, and Basa-kun would've said something about it.

"I recognize that expression. You must be denying that I'm actually a part of you." the monster smiled. "Even if I am a distinct entity created supernaturally, it doesn't change the fact that we are connected to one another. Your soul is intrinsically linked with mine; or more accurately, they are one and the same." her eyes narrowed. "And though Basa-kun had not said so, are you willing to trust the judgment of someone you've barely known?"

"I'd trust him more than a monster that aims to murder people." she muttered.

"And she finally speaks." the monster said with a smile. Its patronizing, playful tone… Yuki can't help but feel irritated, reminding her of someone in her family that she doesn't like. The fact that it's her face that speaks makes her hate it even more. "Still, you trust him? How can you be so sure when you've only met him for a month?"

She frowned, looking around while keeping an eye on the monster. She may not be able to harm this particular one, but it doesn't stop her from killing the others. Yuki moved to eliminate the ones nearby.

Annoyingly, the monster kept up with her. "Don't think you can ignore me by focusing on other things. After all, don't you think it's strange? Things have changed ever since he appeared, but are they really for the better? Sure, the club's atmosphere had moved from its painful stages, but now you were left alone. Makoto-kun chose Kaede. If it weren't for Basa-kun, there's a chance that might've not happened, right?"

Her lips twitched downwards even as she slashed her swords on the monsters. The logic it was spouting was nonsensical; Basa-kun wasn't at fault for her turning meta, nor Makoto-kun choosing Kaede-san in the first place. She wouldn't blame him for something like that, and doing so would be the height of shallowness.

"But then again, you wouldn't blame him for that." the monster said, somewhat mirroring her thoughts. "After all, you like him don't you?"

She stopped in her tracks, before regaining the presence of mind to dodge a rope that reached out from the floating head monster in front of her. "What?" she growled.

"Don't deny it. You like him, don't you? You find him attractive. He's tall, fit, and quite handsome - unlike Makoto-kun, who you only liked since he's the first person who treated you differently." the monster let out a grin. "Perhaps that's why you were able to bounce back so fast from Makoto-kun's rejection - you were already harboring an attraction for someone else. Were you perhaps hoping even to be rejected by him? It's not quite cheating… but then again, changing loyalties in such a short time is quite strange, isn't it? And to think that you were judging girls your age for being shallow."

Yuki clicked her tongue. She knows that the monster was messing with her mind and was trying to distract her. The best way to deal with it was to make it shut up or incapacitate it, but she doesn't have any way to do that.

"And not only that, you were harboring an attraction to a man that looks like he has a harem of girls waiting for him! And don't even hide your discovery of liking girls. Who could've known that you were such a whore?" the monster continued to speak. "Was this really what Yuki Yanai all amounted to? A side piece for someone she had barely met? Whatever happened to that prideful self of yours?"

…Annoying.

It was annoying. It was clearly trying to poke at her insecurities and the thoughts weighing in her mind recently, and she can feel its words stabbing into her heart since it's just verbalizing the ones she had thought on her own. She could see another person losing their composure from its words, confronting the monster in anger.

But not her. She had dwelled in her own thoughts to recognize that such things were useless. She also has enough self-awareness to realize that what was being verbalized by the monster wasn't her complete thoughts, and most of those are truths by technicalities and lies by omission. And even then, anger seems to be an overreaction; if anything, it's more appropriate for her to turtle in herself than lash out.

So she could only look at the monster following her with an annoyed expression.

"...?"

And in response, the monster looked confused. It truly expected her to fully lash out at it in anger.

Perhaps this was a fundamental difference between a drama character like her and someone from the horror genre. It would be expected that someone from horror would exhibit irrational and reckless responses; so psychological tricks like these, where one is confronted by their own insecurities, would be somewhat of a weakness for them.

Still, for it to be baiting her… she can recognize the signs in some of the lessons Basa-kun had given her and her own familiarity with tropes. In these types of scenarios, after a particularly emotional response, there would be a surprise waiting for the character… but what exactly?

Yuki looked around and saw that none of the monsters were near her. There were many, but all of them were outside her range and their own range of attack as well. There seemed to be quite a lot of them grouped up though… like they were keeping distance from her.

…Hold on, now that she realized it, some of their ropes… It was longer than usual. Could it be—?

Yuki looked around again in a new light and realized that countless ropes were attempting to extend towards her, boxing her in while they were well outside their range. She managed to read where the situation was going - since if she did get angry at the monster wearing her face she wouldn't have noticed all this - but her lack of options beside her swords made the prediction useless. They grouped each other in a way that even if she were to launch herself to them, it would still be difficult to defeat without being ensnared. The alternative was to just sit there and wait for the countless ropes to get to her.

She tried to find a smaller group that she could try and break through - but it seemed that the monster realized that their jig was up.

"Tch. She noticed." it grunted. "Quick, cluster up!"

It tried to reach her with its rope but she just dodged. She glanced around in a hurry as the monsters abandoned stealth to just try and surround her from all sides, ropes extending farther than their usual range as they did so.

This… this is dangerous. She could be in trouble.

—Or at least that was what she would've thought, if it weren't for the presence of someone.

It was a sudden thing. Without so much a sound or a whistle, all the monsters surrounding her were torn to shreds, blasted by precise magic that targeted the same spot in all their foreheads. The monsters died instantaneously and simultaneously, popping and disappearing easily like the balloons that they try to hopelessly resemble.

Then out of nowhere, as if he had been there the entire time…

"Yo. Can't help but notice you're in a bad spot."

Basa-kun said so from behind the monster wearing her face. It stiffened, especially when he reached out and touched its cheek, almost caressing it with his hand.

"Let me deal with this, yeah?" he said with a smile.


I watched as the heroine blink in surprise at my sudden appearance. She was caught in a trap made by the enemy - but that was fine. It's these sort of lessons that needed to be taught to her through actual experience so that it'll stick. Good for her to be savvy enough to read the flow of battle though, even if she depended too much on her swords this time. That'd also remind her again the value of having different tools at her disposal while also making her desire to add more to her repertoire on her own.

She'd be the type to reflect on her mistakes as a drama character. Her growth continued in a steady progress, and a controlled battlefield like this is important for her betterment. A few more battles and she'll probably be a decent enough fighter that reaches my standards.

But now that she had her fun, it was time to deal with the problem.

"...Did you hear all that?" Yuki asked in a soft tone.

I was quiet for a moment. It was obvious what she was referring to. "...No need to worry." I answered. "I was aware of what it was saying. It's natural for developments like that to occur, and you could even say I fully expected it."

"Right…" she looked away, an embarrassed blush appearing on her face. "Of course you fully expected it, you did call those who become meta as love interests…" she muttered.

I guess it would be embarrassing for the enemy to reveal your private thoughts in the middle of the fight, with the person themselves listening in.

But going back to the monster - no, rather than a horror monster that acted more mindless, I suppose it would be accurate to call these things as an actual antagonist. Callous, malevolent, and one-dimensional 'Villains' that wanted to cause evil. If handled wrong, they have the curious tendency to pop up again and again in some genres. There's no shortage of them in this world though, and I knew well enough on how to deal with them.

"Now… what to do with you?" I said, leaning in and saying so near its ear.

First step: catch them off guard. I caught it in a vulnerable position, then started blasting it with the fear aura. In an ironic turn of events the monster that was supposed to be feared shook as it was left in my mercy; unable to do anything and feeling as if it's in mortal peril.

"W-W-Wait, Basa-kun! Please don't kill me! I'm Yuki Yanai, just another side of her!" it cried out, making a pathetic expression that the heroine would be caught dead making. Yuki clicked her tongue, probably feeling a little insulted at its display. "I'm her true and unreleased form! You're making a mistake by killing me, by killing us all!"

Of course it would say something like that. A completely vague description, one that probably is technically correct but far off the mark if judged in its entirety. Now normally I'd just ignore it, but addressing this was also a crucial action.

"True and unreleased form you say?" I said in faux-curiosity. "Do you perhaps mean that you came from the collective subconscious of humanity or something?"

"Y-Yes! We came from that! We've come to reunite with all of you to experience the truth!"

"Cool." I smiled. "Then, where's my balloon?"

It froze up. "P-Pardon?"

"You don't have mine, don't you?" I said, and after a moment of silence from it, I went on. "Because you can't form a connection with me, the cursed energy being rebuffed by defenses. Heck you probably have no idea who I am beyond my name, don't you? All you know is from your connection with Yuki. And even then, that's not enough." my smile widened a tinge. "You've been working on a guesswork this entire time, keeping things vague even as you tried to catch her off guard."

"I… I don't know what you're talking about." it protested. "Your balloon is on its way! Just wait for a moment!"

"Heck, you probably don't even have a balloon for Rias either, with her being a demon and all. Not that you'd be aware of her setting anyway. Nor anything meta-related." I continued, ignoring its words. I didn't need a truth-verifying spell to realize it was lying. "You're not the true facet of humanity or whatever you're claiming as. You're just a parasite with a weak connection to humans all around the world."

The monster was silent, unable to refute my words.

Second step: in the event that the villain speaks for some cause, shut them down so utterly that they couldn't muster any way to deny their nature. I investigated what sort of monster it was in the short time I had earlier and was able to verify its true identity - it was a more powerful sort of monster in a way that it has a connection to humanity itself. That gave it a large range, almost endless numbers, and a handy voodoo-like ability. It was a predator for normal humans, but facing anything else supernatural or even technological it has nothing else going for it.

And faced with the truth, it of course began to show its true face. The pitiful face of the heroine morphed into an ugly sneer.

"S-So what?" it sneered out. There was a slight waver in its tone though, perhaps disturbed by the accuracy of my deduction. "Even if you know what we are, you can't stop us all! Our numbers are endless - and even if you did something strange and trapped us here, it won't last forever!"

It glared at me with bloodshot eyes, and then shouted.

"You have no way of defeating us!"

Unbeknownst to it, I was waiting for those words.

I grinned sharply. "Gotcha."

Third step: as the villain was cornered, it of course will lash out. It'll act tough, then do something that will mark its own downfall… it will declare a flag.

With its actions, the flow of narrative fate was decided to move in a certain direction; the one where I wanted to get it to. Essentially guaranteeing the scenario I hoped for to happen without question.

And most important of all, it was the most opportune moment to strike.

I snapped my fingers, the sound of it echoing in the sky, and making everything in the vicinity freeze.

What followed was all implosion of magical energy from a localized point in space - the tear in reality from where all these monsters came from that I located earlier and entered when investigating the true nature of the monster. I was able to access its main body without it noticing, managing to locate its true form.

Behind the tear in reality was a hivemind-like entity that stuck itself in the human gestalt. It was a bit tricky to navigate such a conceptual space, translating myself from the physical into something more abstract just so I could get to it, before putting the equivalent of putting the conceptual equivalent of a hundred megaton warhead near it ready for detonation.

And now I set it off.

All the monsters present looked in horror as it watched its main body essentially vaporize amidst the conceptual explosion, one with a payload powerful enough to translate from the conceptual to the physical as seen in the implosion from the tear in reality. And from its little declaration of the flag there's no chance that it would survive such an assault - the narrative being on my side in showing the villain its place.

From the death of its main body, all the monsters around us began to slowly disintegrate. But of course, things weren't over just yet.

"You… You…!" even while it disintegrated, the monster looked at me in rage. It didn't even try to act like separate entities anymore, discarding the illusion and fully embracing the hivemind that it was. All monsters turned to me, displaying the same maddened expression.

"I'LL KILL YOU!!!" they all shouted.

Final step: the villain, in the face of its complete defeat, will attack in rage. Block, dodge, or prevent it - and then you'll defeat them in such a way that it will let them fade into irrelevance.

It was a last attack of desperation. In more powerful opponents that could dish out dangerous attacks it would be a concern - but for a pathetic monster like this, all it could do was hopelessly reach out with its ropes to try and strangle me.

Surprisingly it wasn't me who dealt with it.

Before the monster in front of me could reach out and strangle me with the rope, a katana sliced it in half. The monster could only look on in shock as it died, unable to expect such an action, as its tattered eyes stared at the heroine.

"W-What…?!" it said in shock.

Yuki scoffed, looking at it coldly.

"Pathetic." she stated.

The monster died, unable to say anything back as its remains fell down in the sky. Idly, I batted away the cursed energy backlash before it could reach the heroine and hurt her.

Due to being too far away, the other monsters all disintegrated into nothingness before they could reach me. The heroine sheathed her swords, looking at the direction of the dead monster who had her face before it completely disappeared.

She clicked her tongue. "Good riddance." she muttered.

Rias flapped her wings and hovered near us. "Oh! Looks like you managed to do it!" she said with a smile, having an idea of the plan when she acted as a flashy distraction for the monster while I snuck towards its body. "Great job, Basa-kun!"

Just like that, all that was left was a quiet sky - free of the monsters that plagued it minutes prior.

"...Let's go back." I said.


After that little debacle, I quickly dispersed the curtain that I set up and went to check on the idol, Terumi Fuuka, one more time. She seemed to be in good health and the defeat of the monster in the plot she belonged to didn't affect her in any way either. With her death flag dealt with, the task we came here for was done now.

Seeing as the danger was over I woke the idol up from her unconscious state, and seeing as there's no alternative way to create a reason for her unconsciousness or to explain her temporary death, I manipulated her memories with hypnosis.

When I was done the idol looked dazed, but it was better than her getting traumatized with what the monsters did to her.

"Are you okay, Fuuka-san?" Rias asked in concern.

"Sorry, I guess I'm feeling a bit dizzy." the idol said, holding a hand to her head before looking around. "...Right, looks like I lost track. What were we doing again?"

"You were showing us the roof." Yuki answered. "It's quite a beautiful place."

She blinked. "Oh." Then, she smiled. "It really is, isn't it? Hope you enjoyed this place as much as I do."

The idol then looked down and glanced at her wristwatch, before her brows shot up in surprise. "Oh my, I can't believe that time passed by so fast! We should probably get going." she put a finger on her lip, miming a shushing gesture. "Don't tell anyone we came here, okay? This place will be our little secret!"

Rias grinned and Yuki responded with a smile. I nodded my head to go along with them.

"I guess this concludes the tour for our idol agency! Now, let's go back. Yumiko-san might be looking for all of you now."

With that said, we went ahead and retraced our steps, going back to the ground floor and towards the management offices where Aoki's own office is located. We ran into her in a corridor on the way there though, with the blue-haired woman approaching us in a rush once we came into her view.

"Basa-kun!" the woman scrutinized all of us with worried eyes, but seeing as we have no visible injuries she calmed down. "...Thank goodness…" she sighed out.

"What's got you worried, Yumiko-san?" the idol asked curiously.

"Oh, nothing, nothing…" she then approached the idol and suddenly embraced the woman, much to her surprise. "Be careful Terumi-chan, okay? Even if you're graduating soon, you're still a precious member of this place." Aoki said tenderly.

The idol blinked before her gaze softened. I could already see her misinterpreting Aoki's actions as her being worried from the blackmailing incident earlier, and not out of worry for her imminent and already foregone death. Not like she's going to be aware of it anyway.

"I will." the idol replied with a smile.

Aoki let her go from her embrace before stepping back. "So did you all have a nice tour of the place? I hope nothing went wrong." she said, glancing at me meaningfully.

The idol spoke up. "Nope! These three are well-behaved! It's been very pleasant." she looked at us. "If you three come here again, be sure to say hello! I'd love to hang out with you all again." she paused, before giving me a teasing glance. "Well, maybe not you. You're not allowed."

I raised a brow, but played along. "Why assume that I'd want to hang out with you in the first place?"

The idol chuckled and shook her head. She approached me and leaned in, then gestured for me to do the same. For a moment I was left wondering what she was going to do but I did what she asked.

Then I felt something soft touch my cheek.

I blinked.

Beside me, Rias, Yuki, and Aoki also blinked.

"...Fuuka-san?" Yuki said in surprise. It was understandable. The woman suddenly kissed my cheek out of nowhere, after all. And that was the same woman who accused me of being some sort of pervert.

As for the idol herself, she seemed also surprised by her own actions.

"O-Oh my." the idol muttered, putting a hand on her mouth in shock. "I don't know why I did that…"

"Did you suddenly lose your mind or something?" I asked, looking at her in confusion.

She looked dazed for a moment, and her confusion disappears as she regains composure. "...Perhaps." she says, stepping back. Then she let out a hum. "Thank you, by the way." she said.

My eyes narrowed. "For what?"

She smiled. It was a beautiful, yet mysterious smile. "Who knows~?"

With that, she turned around and walked away, giving a wave as she did so. "See you guys! It's been fun. Be sure to visit us again, alright? I'd love to invite you all to our wedding when the time comes!"

And so we watch her leave, the idol disappearing as she turned on a corridor with a smile.

Rias glanced at me. "...Ne, Basa-kun. Did you apply the hypnosis right? You wouldn't make such an amateur mistake, would you?"

"Who do you think I am? Of course I did it right." I replied blandly. "Don't worry, she has no memory at all. I peaked in her mind a little bit as she left - most likely it's just her subconscious recalling something. You should at least be familiar with hypnotized people acting like that."

The redhead nodded. "Yeah, I guess that checks out."

"Oh? I suppose everything must be in order now then."

I paused, then looked at Aoki-san, who was staring at me with a smile. It looked quite fixed.

"I know that you've given me the general information earlier, but would you mind expanding it quite a bit? It's a bit of a shock to realize that the idols I manage turns out to be some sort of yokai, alien, or zombie. It makes me wonder how I haven't even noticed." the blue-haired woman continued. It was in the middle of thinking that when the sound of her apartment's door chime rang out. The smile that worked up on her face turned into a frown, and she turned to the direction of the door with something akin to caution.

"My sister's here." she said needlessly. Then, she sighed. "I'll get it."

Basa-kun didn't answer and she stood up from her seat, walking towards the front door. She took a deep breath to center herself as she arrived at the entrance - then, she reached for the door knob and twisted it open.

A familiar face greeted her.


Spoiler

"Yahallo, Yuki-chan!" her sister, Haru Yanai, greeted with a smile. A fake smile, perfected to let people's guards down. "Looks like you were expecting me to arrive. How's my little sister doing?"

Yuki glanced around. "You don't have your guards with you?"

"Nope, just alone this time!" her sister answered cheerfully. "Why, is it better if I had them? Or is it if I didn't? What a suspicious thing to take note of, Yuki-chan!"

Her eyes narrowed. "I was simply—"

"—Anyway, I did bring them with me, but they're waiting downstairs. I don't think I'll be needing guards whenever I come to my dear sister's apartment, would I?" her sister interrupted, making Yuki's lips frown. "So? Are you going to invite me in, Yuki-chan? It feels terribly hot being outside in the middle of noon."

"...Sure."

She stepped aside and her sister let herself in. The older woman looked around the place curiously, humming in thought as she did so. Her eyes locked in on Basa-kun's shoes placed on the shoe rack, however.

"Not even trying to hide it, huh…" her sister muttered, amusement coloring her tone. "So, did that dour boy you were pining for choose the genki girl in the end?"

Yuki felt a pang of hurt from the reminder of not being chosen by Makoto-kun, but it was buried by the rest of other positive feelings from the fact that the drama is just over now. They were the still club that she treasured and they still the same things, with the only difference being that two of her members had a relationship.

Still, her sister must have caught some reaction from her and she continued talking. "Oh, so she did? A shame, the boy was kinda interesting. So, how long was it until you moved on and met a new boy as a replacement?" she then let out a scandalized gasp. "Or was it before that you were hanging out with this new one? What a spicy thought."

She didn't like the way she insinuated things. The condescending tone and the way her sister looks at her like she knows everything about her - one that her own balloon she fought a few days ago reminded of - needled her and got under her skin.

Although the genre divide must have forced her sister to reach the wrong conclusions. For all she knew, this might be what she genuinely thinks. She can never really be sure when it comes to her.

…However, there was one thing she's sure of when it comes to her sister.

"You don't have to ask questions you already know the answer to, nee-san." she said, staring at her sister straight in the eyes. "I know you have eyes around me."

Haru blinked in surprise at that for some reason. "...Huh. Didn't expect that." her sister leaned back to survey her whole form. Yuki looked at her in confusion. "Something seems to have changed about you but I can't pin down what…"

It was her turn to blink. Did her sister detect that she became meta…? No, that didn't make sense; it was most likely her more confident demeanor. She wasn't getting stuck on her thoughts like usual, after all.

Her sister hummed in thought as she looked at her up and down - and then spoke.

"So, was the sex with this boy that good?"

Yuki's face turned red. "W-W-What are you saying all of a sudden!?"

"Kidding, kidding." her sister said with a giggle. "Still the same old Yuki-chan, always so proper and easy to rile up."

To others who knew her for her icy demeanor, the statement would be plain untrue - but for her sister, it was a fact. Yuki tried to keep her composure and control the blush on her face. "C-Can we please focus on the important things at hand?"

Her sister stopped her giggles, settling into a smile instead. Yuki can notice that her eyes were hardened however, like it was targeted at some prey. "Yes." she said cheerfully, ominously. "I suppose we should."

Haru walked further inside her apartment without her input, forcing her to follow her and keep up with her, and then spotted Basa-kun seated on the sofa. "There he is!" the older woman said. "So that's the boy you were hanging out with, huh?"

Basa-kun didn't even glance at them but her sister didn't care nor wait for him to do anything, already walking in front of the sofa and in the face of Basa-kun. Her sister, with a smile, leaned down in front of Basa-kun with her hands on her hips. It casted a shadow on her cheerful face, showing a slightly intimidating appearance as she loomed over him.

"Your name is Basa-kun, correct?" her sister asked, somehow knowing his name without her telling anything. "Why don't we have a nice long chat? You, me, and what you want regarding my sister."

Basa-kun glanced up to meet her gaze, his face completely blank.

There was a moment of tense silence.

"No."

…

…Another moment of silence. Her sister's brow slightly twitched as Basa-kun's attention returned to the TV.

In response to all of this, Yuki can only sigh.

This… this was going to be a mess to deal with.

Chapter 16

In my journey to become strong in the godforsaken world, using clones in conjunction with parallel thought processes has been a boon in expanding my range significantly. It took a while to become skilled enough to multitask for me to what could essentially be described as some sort of hivemind with my real body as a center, but I've gotten used to it in time as I had gotten stronger and gained more skills at my disposal. The path to this point had been painful however, and I recall many times that I've had a literal aneurysm because of all the micromanaging that I needed to do.

But that headache cannot compare to the one that I'm experiencing right now - all because I got swept up in this certain situation.

Rias, the main heroine, had turned meta. And that meant that her shounen and thus very destructive plot is now heading in a direction that even I don't know will end up. What's more, I was dragged into that new development - one that I, as Rias' love interest, would require to involve myself in.

What a shitshow.

And so I sat on the sofa in the familiar room that is Rias' office. Beside me was Rias herself, and to her other side were the members of her club. Similarly, on the sofa opposite us sat the two guests that appeared earlier; a strong demon that dressed like a maid, and the other being the gyaru-looking guy who was Rias' supposed fiance. The maid sat properly like her duty intended while the fiance just slouched with his legs crossed and one hand draping over the back of the sofa, looking completely casual about the whole thing.

"Hey… who exactly are they?"

"Ryuusei-kun, listen closely. These two are…"

The atmosphere was tense. Rias' club members muttered lowly to one another, or rather the protagonist was as he gossiped with the others about what was happening. Perhaps this would be a scene that would provide context for who they are as an introduction for these two new characters.

Of course, being familiar with Rias' own setting, I have some general information as to who these two are. One of them I even had a particular interest in when I knew of their existence.

Rias' fiance, Riser Twining, was the second son of a particularly powerful family in hell. Nothing special about him, but he's moderately strong along with a cocky attitude towards everything. If Rias hadn't turned meta, then he would be the perfect antagonist for the protagonist to test his skills and to make him and Rias get closer together. Despite that plot line out of the picture though, it seems like he still appeared here as an antagonist.

The other guest was a bit special. From my investigations in people to look out for in Rias' setting, this woman was included in that particular list of people - Grayfia Satanichia, one of the stronger demons in hell and Rias' sister-in-law. Pretty long-lived and fought in some sort of war in the setting's past… and she also dresses as a maid, for some reason. Something that caught my eye due to a striking similarity to another maid character in a similar setting but for Yokais instead.

Something like that immediately earned my attention. I thought that it meant that the two settings could be connected but after a bit of investigation there doesn't seem to be anything aside from a superficial similarity. I concluded that she was an 'expy' or 'reference' character - and she was the first of her type that I discovered. And that stuck to my mind.

Anyway, Rias' fiance was frowning at me, Rias' earlier comment about him imitating him seemingly stuck in his mind. In contrast, the maid kept her neutral expression the same ever since she arrived but I could tell that she was observing me along with the others.

And Sona was here too, apparently. Because having them as guests is important enough to warrant her presence, being the student council president and the one running this school and all.

"Welcome to our school, Grayfia-san." the bespectacled girl greeted. She was seated on another sofa between us two, making her look like some sort of mediator. "I'd have prepared things better to suit this meeting if I was notified of your visit, but a certain person had neglected to do her duties, you see."

"Hey!" Rias shouted indignantly at her friend throwing her under the bus, but she wilted when the girl gave her a glare. "...I-I just forgot about it, okay? It's not like you haven't done that once or twice…" she mumbled.

"It's no problem, Vignette-sama. I suspected something like that might happen."

Rias looked at the blank-faced maid in shock. "—Grayfia!?"

"I suppose her family would know her best." Sona said with a nod of her head.

"We are well aware of the young lady's flaws." Grayfia continued on without a change in expression. If there was an exasperated tinge on her tone, no one knows. "We are also doing our best to correct it… No matter how impossible it may seem."

"Okay, that's enough! Look, I'm really sorry alright? I'm not gonna do something like this again, I promise." Rias sighed out. She then turned to Grayfia, a glare beginning to form on her face. "But in the first place, why am I getting engaged? I certainly never got involved into any discussions with my family regarding this. So why is it suddenly sprung that I got engaged to… that person?" she said pointing to the fiance in question.

Her fiance's brows furrowed, an offended expression appearing on his face. "'That person'? How rude. Is this how the Satanichia show their courtesy? To one that represents their allied family, no less?" Rias frowned, and the guy turned to Sona. "And you. While Grayfia-san here is fine with your lack of preparations - I'm not. The Twining does not hold the same closeness for the Vignette, so you better watch your attitude unless it colors our views of yours."

The atmosphere of the room immediately turned cold at his words.

Beside Rias, the protagonist suddenly stood up from his seat with his fists clenched. "Hey, what the hell is your problem—!"

"Ryuusei-kun."

He stopped at hearing Rias' grave tone. The boy turned to her, a protest about to leave his lips, but in the end stopped himself and relented. He sat down back to the sofa, glaring harshly at the fiance as he did so.

Rias took a deep breath and gathered her composure. After doing so, her normal impulsive and clumsy self was nowhere to be found, replaced with the graceful persona that she carries whenever she means business. The redhead stared straight at her supposed fiance, expression neutral.

"Once again I apologize. As I have said, this whole meeting was a bit sudden and the news of my betrothal is new to me." Rias enunciated her words clearly, and unlike her earlier whiny tone she spoke in a serious manner befitting of her status as a scion of a powerful demonic line. "I was caught off-guard. I hope this doesn't cause any offense."

Her fiance waved a hand. "It's fine. I'll forgive you because you're my fiance." he then inclined his head to the protagonist beside her. "Make sure you discipline your underlings though. As amusing as it is to hear a weakling act tough, it might get annoying. It would be rude to make an example of him right in front of my fiance after all."

The protagonist grit his teeth at that - although he didn't rise to the bait, following Rias' orders to stay put. As for the girl herself, Rias looked visibly displeased but aside from a slight twitch to her brow she didn't show any sign of it. The redhead had a mean poker-face if she needed to have one.

"While Ryuusei-kun is our most recent member, I believe 'making an example' of him would be something you might have difficulty doing. Especially since there are other people stronger than you here." she retorted.

The guy sneered. "Stronger? Aside from Grayfia-san, all of you in this room are weaklings. I've heard about you, Rias Satanachia - you spend your days up here in the human realm and play with humans instead of dealing with real competition in hell. Even with your three demons and succubus, you're still nothing compared to me." he mocked, words dripping with sarcasm as he gazed at each of Rias' club members. Then, his eyes eventually settled on mine. "...Not unless of course you mean that?" he asked, amused.

Rias smiled sweetly. "Yes."

Her fiance paused, before he let out a sharp singular laugh. "Ha! Are you serious? You're comparing this to me? A meager human?"

"You insult me."

What followed after was something many in the room didn't expect - he sat straight up from his seat, a burst of power coming off from him as he did so. The wave passed over all the people in the room, startling the majority of Rias' club and even left the protagonist shaken from the display.

The guy's earlier mirth was wiped clean. He glared at Rias who simply blinked at his show of power but didn't do anything else. "Don't think you can get away with stating those words. You may be my fiance… but even my patience can only get so far."

He then glared at me, pinning me with his gaze. I could feel his power emanating from him as he tried to loom over me metaphorically. With this much focus on me, I'm guessing that he was trying to make me afraid or something just to make an example of Rias.

Unfortunately, the display was absolutely pathetic. It's even less terrifying than the one Yuki had endured when she had a first encounter with a horror monster. I returned his glare with a blank stare of my own, completely unaffected.

The guy frowned. Then, he opened his mouth—

"Twining-sama. I believe that's enough."

The maid's stern voice cut in the tension gathering in the room. Hearing it, the fiance clicked his tongue and cut off his power before slouching back on his seat once more.

"Tch. Like some human could compare to a pure demon. What the hell do you even keep them for? Is that supposed to be your boy toy or something?" after grumbling that he glanced at Rias, leering her body from down up. "…Well you probably wouldn't need him any longer. I'd keep you satisfied along with the rest of my harem."

The maid cleared her throat.

"Twining-sama, while ojou-sama was rude for forgetting this meeting - I believe respect works both ways. I shouldn't have to tell you how to act like a guest. So please, behave yourself." she admonished the guy, who simply looked away. The maid then exhaled. "Nevertheless, I believe that things have turned out of hand." she stood up from her seat. "Perhaps it would be best for us to leave you two alone, just so that you may know each other better."

Her implied order to leave the room wasn't missed and Rias' club members along with Sona stood up from their seats as well. I did the same. Happily so even, since I don't want to deal with this sort of thing in the first place.

Meanwhile Rias grimaced, not even bothering to disguise her disgusted expression at the thought of being alone with her fiance.

"Do I have to?" she asked.

The maid shook her head. "Please, ojou-sama. At the very least, follow your brother's wishes. He was the one to arrange all of this after all."

"Oh, he was…? I'll remember that the next time I talk to him."

We were already walking towards the door as they said that and I was the last to exit to the hallway. As I did so, I felt a hand tap me on my shoulder and I turned to see that it was the protagonist. He gave me a worried look.

"Hey, are you fine letting this happen? Leaving those two alone like that?" he whispered. "I mean, aren't you two together?"

…To think that he'd be concerned for me, the guy who supposedly stole the main heroine he's attracted to; As expected, the protagonist really is a nice person. You'd think that he'd be vindicated or something but no, he genuinely seems to be worried.

Then again, he seems to be in a relationship with his childhood friend. It'd be unreasonable for him to act that way at this point.

"It's fine. Rias isn't the type to take things lying down." I answered him with a shrug. "And this is entirely Rias' problem to deal with. I'll help when she says she needs help."

The protagonist didn't seem to like my decision to respect Rias' own capabilities judging by his frown, but he was interrupted by someone who I didn't expect to speak up.

"Basa's right. Trust on Buchou, Ryuusei-kun. She can take care of herself." Koneko spoke up in her usual laconic manner beside him, making him look at her in surprise. "She always gets what she wants in the end."

As thanks for not making me argue with the guy, I brought out a cookie from my subspace and offered it to Koneko, making her blink. Still, the guy still didn't look convinced. He glanced at me and Koneko, then to his fellow club members. "Really? But…"

"If there's one thing that I know about our leader is that while she may get herself in trouble, she always somehow finds a way to overcome it. It's sorta fascinating really." Kiba added with a smile. Koneko also swiped the cookie out of my hand and immediately scarfed it down.

Sona agreed as well with a nod. "That she does. While she may have made a mistake, this whole betrothal really does seem to be a bit sudden and I won't blame her for not wanting it to go through." the girl looked like she was giving me a meaningful glance as she said that, but I ignored it in favor of giving more cookies to Koneko when she outstretched her hand, demanding more. "If she can find a way around it, she will. Although… she does have a tendency to create more problems as a result."

"And that's where we come in, Ryuusei-kun." Akeno said with a smile. Koneko also nodded her head, satisfied after I gave her the whole pack and began scarfing it down one by one. "So really, there's no need to worry. As Basa-kun said, we'll help when Buchou asks for it."

"I guess…"

The door opened behind us and the maid walked out. She took one look at us and inclined her head politely in greeting. "I apologize for kicking you all out of the room. In the meantime, you can spend the rest of the time however you want. I will notify all of you once things are done." she glanced at Sona. "And thank you again for allowing this meeting to happen in the school, Vignette-sama. And on such short notice at that."

The bespectacled girl shook her head. "There's no need for that, Grayfia-san. It's not a big deal at all."

The maid nodded wordlessly at that, then her eyes settled onto mine. "If I may have a moment of your time?" she prompted, gesturing for me to accompany her.

…I suppose it's time.

I trailed behind her, her heels clacking on the hallway as we separated away from the rest of the group, who were watching us in poorly-hidden curiosity. The maid led me to a room in Rias' mansion, one that looked like a small storage room filled with cabinets and shelves, for privacy. The door closed behind me as the maid entered last, locking it behind her.

"You are Basa, correct?" she asked. "A human magus? I believe you were a classmate and a longtime friend of ojou-sama, but aside from your description and some stories on your exploits, what she had said about you is… concerningly little."

"Ask me all you want. I'll answer." Well, those that can be answered, anyway.

There were a few moments of silence before the maid spoke once more. "...Very well. I suppose I shall ask the most important one regarding ojou-sama."

With that said, the maid's eyes sharpened. Power exuded from her form as she repeated the earlier stunt of Rias' fiance - but this time, it would actually be effective and make strong enemies pause. The difference of what I felt earlier was that the fiance was like a child's attempt to act tough. Right here, it felt like the real thing.

This was, after all, one of the strongest demons in Rias' setting.

"Then I shall ask you, Basa."

She spoke her words, staring at me straight into my soul.

"What exactly—"


"—do you want with her?"

I looked blankly at the heroine's smiling sister, who mirrored the same words that the maid had told me. She too was trying to learn about my aim regarding Yuki, who was looking over us with a strange expression on her face.

She had laughed out my earlier refusal to which I tried to do because, as seen in what's happening right at this very moment, I was trying to avoid suffering from being subjected to a shovel talk on two sides along with all the headache associated with it. Just like the maid who was talking to my other self, the heroine's sister was also trying to act intimidating.

An ambiguously neutral smile, looking at me straight in the eyes with her eyes slightly wide, entire body facing me fully at a slightly elevated height than mine, along with a lower tone of voice as she spoke - her entire body language was tailored for her on the 'upper hand' so to speak. A mundane person would be put unconsciously in the backfoot if they were subjected to this and would even be intimidated.

The woman was well aware of what she was doing too. Surprising, considering that drama characters are more realistic than perhaps the other genres but then again there are exceptions to the rule. Her ability spoke of a competence that made her one of these exceptions.

Haru Yanai was a side character. She can afford to be more one-dimensional than the rest, and that is characterized by her unrealistic levels of competence in all things social compared to the rest of the usual cast. That meant that she was more of a plot device used to move the story along than a character to be explored.

Anyway, looking at her right now, Yuki's sister's attempts of intimidation are superimposed on the maid's.

…Needs some work, I think.

"Well?" the woman smiled, a touch of smugness appearing in her features. I have a feeling that she misunderstood my silence somehow. "Are you going to answer my question?"

"I don't plan on doing anything to your sister. She just accompanies me to attempt the world from turning into a shitty mess of a setting." I answered bluntly.

From the corner of my eye I could see Yuki looking at me with deadpan eyes mouthing 'What the hell are you saying?' but I ignored it. Not like it meant anything, considering her sister just blinked at my answer, tilting her head in confusion.

"Eh? What's that supposed to mean?"

Yuki sighed. "He's just a friend, nee-san. Our relationship isn't… whatever you were thinking. There's no need for you to act like this."

"Friends don't visit each other's apartments casually, little sister. Especially when they do it every other day of the week." the woman retorted with a smile. "Are you still going to act like that doesn't mean anything?"

The heroine went quiet at that. There was no way for her sister to believe that they were just friends now. I waited, curious as to how she would spin this around without resorting for my help. She never did tell me what excuses she'll use.

"...Maybe it does mean something." the girl eventually replied. "But we're not at that stage yet. Maybe in the future, but not now."

…That's her approach?

I stared at the girl. She pointedly didn't look in my direction, but I could see her cheeks coloring slightly.

"Hmm…? Is that so?" her sister remarked, her thoughtful gaze alternating between the two of us. "Then it's true that the dour boy chose the other girl. I don't know why you'd want to have a delinquent as a rebound, but I guess the spite of rejection can do that."

"Basa-kun is not a rebound." Yuki interrupted with a sigh. "And he's not a delinquent either. You have eyes around me, so you should know about him - he just looks like that naturally. Basa-kun has been a perfect gentleman ever since we met."

Her sister hummed in thought. "Perhaps he might be."

I saw Yuki's shoulder relax a tiny bit, enough for me to conclude that she was relieved. Her sister's tone indicated that she accepted the explanation so that's one question dealt with… but of course, that's just a prelude to what is to come.

And I was vindicated when the woman let out a serene smile before speaking again.

"That doesn't answer why you'd suddenly involve yourself with an idol scandal, though. Mind telling me the series of events that led to it, little sister?"

Yuki's eyes imperceptibly sharpen before disappearing in a flash - replaced entirely by a sad and mournful expression in what could only be a practiced move. It looked genuine enough however, and the only tell would be the sharpening of her eyes which I only caught because I can keep up with shounen reaction times.

"Ah, yes… that." she muttered. "An acquaintance of mine was a friend of someone working in that idol agency, and they contacted me explaining what happened and asked for help. I just didn't want to sit by doing nothing, especially after seeing the proof sent to me. What happened there… it was unfortunate."

Yuki was grave and mournful. Genuinely so that I suspect that she was channeling her real feelings on what happened to those idols. Haru frowned, noticing the same.

"I see. Quite fortunate then that those idols had someone that knew you. And that someone is from your school?" Yuki nodded at that. "Hm, we benefited quite a lot from the whole thing. We placed some of our people on their board of the agency with that. I might even consider showing some gratitude to them for it. Do you mind telling me who this person is?"

Yuki hesitated a bit from that. "I… I don't think they'd like that, nee-san. They requested that they don't want to be involved in the spotlight at all."

"Really?"

"Yes." the heroine answered firmly.

Her sister hummed in thought again, staring at Yuki with an enigmatic smile.

"I don't believe you." she stated.

Yuki frowned. "...What do you mean? What do you not believe—"

"—You see, I visited the agency and had a talk with the idols of what happened. You know, since it was going to be one of the assets our family can use." the woman interrupted, her smile still in place. "There were some fuddy-duddy old men that protested on our involvement you see, which is why I had to be around, talking to people and making sure that there's going to be changes there and stuff,"

Her smile sharpened as she stared at her sister. Yuki flinched.

"Imagine when I got to talk with one of the victims and they said that they were helped by a man with blonde hair and tanned skin, along with two girls. One of them who, as they described, slightly looked like me… now isn't that strange?"

Silence followed her words. Yuki was looking at her sister in surprise, and I could tell that her mind was racing to figure out how to explain herself out of this one. Yet none were forthcoming. Her eyes then glanced at me and I could tell that she now wants my assistance.

And I know that I said that I'd ensnare her sister in a hypnosis, then modify her memories but…

"Hoh? I wonder what exactly you're insinuating with that?"

…There's something that I needed to do first, or all this set up would've been all for nought.

The heroine's sister turned to me, her attention gained from my interjection after sitting quietly. Her own sharp smile dimmed when she saw my small smirk - the first show of emotion that she had witnessed from me ever since she showed up.

"Are you saying that we were there in the idol agency when the arrests happened? That we were somehow the ones who helped those idols?" I asked as I slouched on the sofa. "What a strange claim to make. I'm sure that since you apparently have people guiding Yuki, you'd know that she was in school at that time. And by extension me, Yanai-san. Those people in the idol agency couldn't be us."

My smirk widened a bit.

"Unless, of course, you're saying that we were somehow in two places at once?"

Yuki was staring at me in confusion as I uttered the statement. That didn't make my words less true of course - there were always people around Yuki whenever she went outside. They were even with us when we dealt with some chores around town, but the genre divide made them go somewhere else whenever we involve ourselves in something not within the bounds of their setting's genre.

Still, that meant that Yuki's sister had confirmation that we were at school at the time of the director's arrest in the agency… along with confirmation that we were on the idol agency as well. Two conflicting sources of information that would make no sense. And not only that, I had been looking at the cameras whenever her spies took photos. She would definitely take notice of that.

Looking at her perspective, everything around me and this situation is mysterious.

Not unless of course they belong in a different setting that allows for it to happen plausibly. Perhaps one where magic is involved, or in those detective settings with ridiculously intricate plots. Both of which Haru Yukino isn't part of as she belongs in a drama genre.

There was really no way for her to know… not unless she turned meta, that is.

But then again, what are the chances of that? There's no way Yuki's sister would turn meta after I pointed out such a thing, right? That'd be stupid. All scenarios where someone turned meta occurred to those who are my 'love interests'., but there's no way something like that would happen to someone like Yuki's sister.

Right?

From my words, Haru's expression didn't change from her slightly dimmed smile. Of course, I also didn't miss the imperceptible narrowing of her eyes before forcing to keep her expression the same. A tell that is amusingly similar to what Yuki did earlier.

Yet she didn't speak, my statement remaining unchallenged.

And only a tense silence between us remained.


"I don't have anything I want with Rias. She's… a friend, or something along those lines."

I said those words to the quietly waiting Grayfia. Incredible demonic power that would quail even the strongest of men exudes from her form, attempting to intimidate me in hopes for an honest answer. Of course, having experienced worse, it didn't work at all.

My calm answer however had her raising a single brow. She wasn't surprised though, since she saw my reaction to what Rias' fiance did, but I was still managing to react calmly on being subjected to something leagues stronger. She was probably reassessing my strength in her mind.
