"Since you're here as a spectator you'll be watching with the others. Please follow me." the maid stated.

I did so and we walked to another teleportation array different from the one Rias used. It activated as soon as we stepped into it, and my scenery changed after another flash.

I looked around and saw that we were in another luxurious room. There were velvet chairs strewn about facing a large window overlooking a vast area that was covered in a large barrier - meaning that must be the arena. It was sorta far, but I suppose the visual projection magic arrays installed in the place helped with that.

In short, the place looked like a luxury suit of a sports stadium. The one where VIPs would watch in while the rest of the plebeians get the stands.

There weren't many people watching however. There were only three who sat on the velvet chairs. They stared at the large view while chatting with one another - or at least one of them was with the other two just sitting quietly - looking as if they didn't notice me arriving at all.

Of course, that couldn't be any more wrong.


Spoiler


Spoiler


Spoiler

After all, these people are one of the strongest characters in the setting.

One of them, a woman, turned around as I approached with Grayfia. She then stood up, approaching us while sending the maid a bright smile.

"Hey, Grayfia! You're back!" she greeted before turning her gaze to me. "So this is our special guest, huh… You're Basa-kun, right? I'm Serafall. Nice to meet you!"

I nodded my head politely. "It's a pleasure to meet you as well."

"You're polite. That's a good sign." she commented with a smile. "I've heard interesting things about you. Say, you're a human magus, right? I know Rias-chan is staying in Japan because she likes her anime but you don't look like you're from there. And last I knew, they don't have an active supernatural community aside from their Yokai and Shinto gods."

"I'm not Japanese, yes. As for how we met, we were classmates when I transferred to a local elementary school when I arrived here in Japan." I answered to her unasked question. "As for learning magic, I had some encounters here and there. There's many things you can encounter if you know where to look."

"I see. You must be a great magus then, considering Rias asked you to train them for this." she then paused, looking me over in my entirety. "I had thought for a moment that you're just a normal human that learned a few tricks, but I guess this makes the next part easier."

For a moment I was confused at what she meant, but then the woman casually put her hands on my shoulders, trapping me from moving. She gave me a smile.

"...Did you know? My sister was one of the people you trained. Apparently she's incapacitated right now."

I then felt an incredible amount of power emanating from this woman that visibly made the surroundings shake, disturbing the mana from the surrounding air. The woman was small, about a foot smaller than me, but facing the brunt of this display of power would make anyone feel like an ant.

It felt different from what I had felt from Riser and possibly even Grayfia. This one was definitely orders of magnitude higher compared to them, and this was only a fraction of her power she was displaying. What a dangerous woman.

"—So, what's this I heard about you wearing her out, running her ragged for hours straight, and doing it until she can't walk properly anymore and to a point where she couldn't even leave her bed?" she continued in a sweet tone of voice. "Something you want to explain, mister?"

…Oi. There's definitely a misunderstanding here.

Or at least, it looks like there is. For some reason these demons like to display their powers for dominance and it's getting quite old, but I can tell that this intimidation attempt meant something beyond that. I can see this particular stunt acting as a comedic scene but that doesn't mean that it can serve a different purpose as well. Probably a test or something. I could play along, but…

I looked at her blankly, tanking the powerful aura she was letting out head on. And my hunch was proven right when I saw a faint trace of surprise - although not much - and a sudden curious look on her eye when I did so.

"Hoh…?" she muttered.

Well, now I certainly got her interest. And most likely the others around here as well. One of the other guys seated, the green-haired one, glanced at us with a raised brow before looking back at the view. I also saw Grayfia's eyes narrow slightly from the edge of my vision.

I never did like getting this sort of attention after getting so used to being treated as an unknown for many settings. Oh well.

Fortunately though, I was saved from having to answer inconvenient questions when Grayfia took pity on me. The sound of the maid clearing her throat made the woman retract her demonic power, returning things back to normal.

"Vignette-sama. I believe that's enough of your teasing." she interjected. "Your little sister had apparently just pushed herself a little too hard when she accompanied ojou-sama in her training. It would be unfair to blame Basa-kun when she was the one who volunteered to join."

"Call me Serafall! Really, how many decades have we known each other by now? Lighten up a bit!" the woman said with a pout.

"I'm on shift right now." the maid simply answered. "I shall also attend to some other business so please behave in the meantime. I will return once the preparations are finished and the duel is ready to start."

Serafall sighed as the maid disappeared, using a teleport spell. "Oh fine. Seriously, that woman and her obsession with maids…" she turned to me, lips curving to a teasing smile. "By the way - I'm not really blaming you. If anything, it's little Sona's fault for being weak! She hasn't been training lately so it's a good wakeup call for her. Sorry for the scare, I guess I just wanted to see you spooked. Teehee~!"

My blank stare remained pointed to her. It's a lie, I know. But she knew I knew as well. Her teasing smile widened slightly, goading me to call her out. Kinda bratty of her. She's just begging for correction.

Still, this is interesting. I know this is a shounen setting focused on action, but it seems that with politics involved in it there would be side characters similar to Yuki's sister. The woman in front of me was one such person, even if she may not show the same level of skill as Haru's own.

I'm not interested in playing her games though.

"Okay." I answered in monotone.

The woman blinked. "...Really? Very forgiving of you." she muttered, before eyeing me consideringly. "Hm… I did wonder why Sona would try to join out of her own volition, but looking at you now I can see how it appeals to her." she then smiled and gave me a thumbs up. "As expected, Sona has good tastes! She might not like magical girls, but at least she likes the 'corruption' part of it! Us sisters truly are alike in ways that matter!"

…I don't know how to respond to that.

"—Anyway, why don't you sit down with us? Let's watch the duel together. Come on, I'll even introduce you to those two who have been ignoring you for a while now." the woman then leaned in to whisper to my ear in a conspiratorial manner. "Sorry about them, by the way. It's not because they don't acknowledge you because you're human or anything like that. They're not that kind of people. It's just that one has the social skills of a brick and the other one is a cucked siscon."

The redhead twitched in his seat.

"We can hear you, Serafall." the green-haired demon spoke for the first time. "And I assume that I am the one you're referring to as someone who has terrible social skills. That is false. I am simply courteously waiting for you to finish talking with him before I introduce myself."

He glanced at me and nodded his head politely.

"Greetings. I am Ajuka." he greeted. "Do not pay any mind to what Serafall had said… except for the last part. There's certainly a cucked siscon here, and it is not I."

The redhead twitched again.

Both Ajuka and Serafall then stared at him for a few moments, as if waiting for him to speak. The redhead man simply stayed silent and stared at the view outside with a dignified look, ignoring everything happening around him like a prince who wouldn't deign his attention to his lessers. When it was clear that he wasn't speaking anytime soon, the two looked back at each other, a wordless conversation passing between their gazes.

Then they both turned to me.

"Apologies if our friend is rude. As I said, he is a siscon cucked out of his own sister. I implore you to forgive him." Ajuka stated.

Serafall nodded empathically. "Un un! Imagine loving your sister so much throughout your life and a random tanned, delinquent would steal her and deflower her. It's kinda pathetic and undoubtedly sad, so I hope you understand him acting like this."

"And not just that." Ajuka added. "To even suggest the betrothal himself to some upstart demon that has his own harem, rationalizing that he was the best choice as a strong spouse and citing his own duty for the good of his family - it makes you think if he has some fetish for it or something along those lines."

"Then there's the shock when it turns out a different tanned delinquent is apparently seeing his sister! And for so long at that!" Serafall cried dramatically. The woman closed her (fake) tearful eyes and closed her fist. "How long was his sister hiding it? Why did she not tell him anything? Does she not trust him? Was she even saying the truth to him all this time? Was she even pure anymore!?" she shouted, before dropping her fist and looking blankly at me. "Et cetera, et cetera."

"And there is also how, at moments when he thinks he's alone while we're working, he tearfully cries to himself while whispering—"

"—Alright, that's enough!"

The redhead stood up from his seat, heaving deep breaths with a mixed expression of furious and embarrassment on his face. There was no trace of his dignified expression earlier, and he glared at the two culprits who looked entirely unregretful of what they just did.

…Was this bullying? I think this was just bullying.

"Enough, you two. I can speak for myself." the redhead growled, before turning his glare at me.

For a moment I thought he was about to explode, but he seemed to manage to calm himself. The redhead took a deep breath and looked away again. But this time, he didn't just ignore me.

"Take a seat." he commanded. "You know who I am, as Rias undoubtedly has said something about me. I hope there is no need for me to introduce myself to you."

…She actually didn't since the girl was surprisingly private when it comes to her family, so most of my information about him was something I gathered myself. But I'm not going to mention that now. He might really get angry if I did.

Sirzechs Satanichia. Rias' brother and Grayfia's husband.

One of the top contenders in taking the seat of hell's sole ruler and has the power to back it up. This person was another one of the strongest characters in the setting, and arguably the most powerful person in the room when compared to the others here.

I took a seat beside Serafall, the woman acting as the wall between me and Rias' brother. She didn't look uncomfortable in the slightest but rather, she actually seemed to be excited about it. I ignored that and looked at the view outside what was displayed on the visual projection arrays.

It showed the two opposing teams, each on the opposite sides of the arena as they waited for the signal to start. I could see Rias preparing with her club and discussing something or another with determined looks on their faces. Compared to her though, Riser was just relaxing with his harem as if he didn't treat the fight seriously.

"...You are leading Rias to the wrong path." Sirzechs stated after a moment.

"What do you mean?" I asked.

My question was answered with a deep exhale.

"Don't act stupid. I can see that you're strong enough to withstand some of our power but you're infecting my little sister with that cockiness of yours. Perhaps in the human world you might be something - however, here in hell, that strength of yours is nothing special." the man said in a cold voice. He wasn't looking at me, but he was glaring nonetheless. "It is unfair to force the betrothal to her, but even so, Rias knows her duty to the family. She clearly didn't accept it because of you. And that will lead her down a reckless path."

I stayed quiet. In a certain perspective, he was completely correct that it was my presence that stopped her from accepting the proposal. I can see her accepting it in the original plot, knowing her insecurities about herself and thinking it was a way to help her family, but even if that was the case the protagonist would prevent that from happening because she's the heroine.

But he didn't know that. And even then, that wasn't the important thing right now.

"You don't believe Rias can beat him." I stated.

My words made Rias' brother stare at me. I could feel his temper rising from that blunt statement, but it was the truth. One that he acknowledges himself, judging by the sudden guilty and regretful expression on his face.

"...My little sister is many things. She is beautiful, passionate, and has a heart of gold. But while she may be an exceptional demonic being she wasn't someone who'd pursue strength given the chance. That is a weakness in our society, and her lack of strength will be used for someone's own ends." he sighed. "Perhaps she may hate me today and many years from now on, but I'd rather she hate me than see her hurt because of it."

Again, another rational thing for him to conclude. Demon politics in this setting is a strange mix of slimy politicking filled with blackmail and deceit along with a might makes right attitude. Rias was never good at the former and was the type to tackle a problem head on. But what if she wasn't strong as well?

She'll be devoured alive by the pit of snakes that is the demonic society. Rias and the rest of these characters being decent people was the exception, after all. Most of the demons around act like Riser, and maybe even worse.

"I know that you trained her and must think that Rias has some sort of chance to beat him. I get it, I really do. In a perfect world perhaps she might be able to - but she had spent far too long in the human world lazing around. I want nothing more than for her to stand on her own two feet and try to compete with me for the title of hell's ruler like she always declares as a child. But even I know that it's wishful thinking."

"Grayfia did say that Rias-chan returned to that sort of attitude when she visited her." Serafall interjected with a smile.

"I know, and I'm happy about it." Sirzechs replied, before frowning. "But it's far too late. Perhaps if such a change in attitude occurred early, things might be salvageable and Rias would use all the things in our family's resources for her disposal to keep up with the rest of her peers. But at this point? Even if I try to help her I'd have a hard time doing such a thing." he then glanced at the woman. "...And you do know your own little sister is in the same situation right? You might do the same thing as me."

Serafall shrugged. "Sure, but I know my way around to keep her safe instead of doing something stupid like this—"

"You're wrong, by the way."

The two turned to me in surprise as I said those words.

"Rias might have been slacking off but that doesn't mean she's weak. She's talented and with the right circumstances she can turn strong in no time. All it takes is a push to do it. You can take that with a grain of salt if you wish, but it remains the truth." I explained.

I stared straight at them in the eyes.

"She's not a normal person in this world. Don't define her with such limited standards."

Serafall blinked, while Rias' brother just raised a brow skeptically at that and clearly did not believe what I said. However, before he could speak out his mind he was interrupted by Grayfia returning back to the luxury suite, stepping out of a teleportation magic circle.

"I have returned. The duel will start once the signal is given." the maid stated.

With that our attention turned to the view outside and to the visual projection arrays. There, we saw that the two teams now looked ready for a fight as they waited for the signal for the duel to begin. Sirzechs looked at them with a severe frown, as if he was watching something inevitably horrible, yet something he must also see through.

In a completely normal perspective the man is correct in his thoughts. He must think that we're just foolish teenagers stupidly believing in their own hype, only to be crashing down in the face of reality once this is over. His thoughts were realistic and logical enough that at any different place I might agree to it.

But this was a shounen setting. And that meant something different.

What else sort of story has its characters breaking their limits? Of beating unfavorable odds? Of being disposed to the more beautiful romanticism and idealistic values, instead of the harsh truth offered by reality?

It wasn't faith that I had. It was simply basic pattern recognition. And now, a perfect set-up was laid down.

—So it didn't surprise me when the world turned bright as Riser's side of the field was enveloped by a large explosion of destructive energy, before dying down and revealing a large crater on the ground and destroying half of the arena entirely.

Rias' graceful form as she floated up high was displayed in the projections, her body crackling with demonic energy and still ready to go despite such a destructive attack.

"H-Half of Riser's harem was eliminated!" Grayfia shouted, looking truly taken aback for the first time since I met her. "T-There's only five left on the opposing team now!"

Sirzech and the rest looked on with their mouths hanging agape, and the redhead spoke the generic words of any anime bystander watching something shocking.

"I-Impossible…! (B-Baka na…!)"

I smiled.

So how would someone like Rias fare in this fight, one might ask?

Turns out, people are in for a surprise indeed.

Chapter 18

"Attention: all contestants of this duel, ready yourselves. The duel begins now!"

Rias looked high up in the sky as she heard the sound of Grayfia's voice echoing throughout the arena, signaling the start of the duel.

The sky was very dark, lacking any stars nor a moon to light it up compared to the human world. Many humans that turned into demons have lamented the lack of it, with some others even saying that it represented the true darkness and hopelessness found in hell. Her time spent up there certainly made her understand about such a sentiment but in her own eyes, even when she was a child, she had always seen it as something different.

The sheer umbral color it brings almost looks like a beautiful shade of purple. A darkness that doesn't evoke fear, but rather fascinates. It wasn't a night sky that brought about the feeling of absence; it was a welcoming darkness that all demons had lived and been born under, mesmerizing and otherworldly in sight.

Just like what her kind was supposed to represent.

It had been a long time since she returned to her place of birth, having spent most of her teenage years up in the human world… So much so that she might have forgotten the very reason why she left in the first place.

Was it because of her supposed role as a heroine that she had forgotten? Or was it because of her own weakness of character? She didn't know that answer. Both options seemed plausible, and they aren't mutually exclusive with each other as well…

Rias smiled.

…But then again, something like that doesn't matter, doesn't it? There's no need to complicate things.

She had an opportunity to fix things now. And she's going to take it.

"Buchou."

Akeno's voice called out to her. Rias didn't need for her to speak any further to understand what she wanted.

"We proceed as planned. Go and find the rest of his harem while I confront Riser alone." Rias ordered, before she sent a smile to her treasured vice-president. "Good luck and kick their asses, alright?"

Akeno smiled, accompanied by determined expressions by the rest of her club members. "We will." she answered.

With that, Rias nodded her head and unfurled her wings. With a single flap, she launched herself high up before stopping then hovered just below the dome acting as the barrier. She had a great aerial view of the entire arena, and with her sharp demon eyes she could see the opposite team scuttling around like ants.

They had split up to fight her club most likely one-by-one. It seems that they were truly underestimating them all - but they had already predicted things going this way in their plans, so she wasn't bothered. No, what she needed to do was to capitalize on their inattention as they still haven't spotted her.

She thrust out her hand.

In a practiced movement, a great amount of demonic energy poured out of her and coalesced in a single point. However, that wasn't all that she did - the demonic energy wasn't solely being turned into an attack for her to use, but to also fuel and fill in the gaps of the attack in an intricate manner.

The magic system for demons in her setting worked through the imagination of the user. So long as there is sufficient power behind it, just about anything demons could imagine can be brought into reality. Lots of demons brute force their way into having a powerful attack by just having more power. However there were some that made use of it differently, taking advantage of the demonic magic's nature to obtain more results applying less.

From what she could recall one of her brother's friends is one of those people. But they were the exception that rose to power because of their genius and strength. She knew she wasn't that smart, but she had something that was as strong as them never had.

Thousands of other settings worth of inspiration.

Her demonic energy surged, instinctively taking form into a destructive influence that ruined and corrupted everything that it touched due to the affinity and innate nature of demons from Satanichia. Rias closed her eyes in concentration to guide the flow of the energy with her unlocked magical circuits that can only be compared to a roaring and raging beast, trying to focus its destruction as opposed to letting it run rampant everywhere.

She made it focus on the surrounding mana, eating it and letting it fuel itself more. She made it corrupt the bonds of compounds from surrounding matter, producing small amounts of heat and energy that will cascade into something more for each molecule. And from a sudden influx of new molecules, a high pressure would rapidly spike.

All of which will combine into a large, devastating attack.

"Breath of a dying star, consume and bring forth light—"

And so, with a large grin on her face - she launched the projectile and its name to the world.

"—Apocalyptic Nova!"

Everything burned.

There was a great deafening explosion; a raging ball of inferno that enveloped a certain radius from which the projectile hit. Trees, rocks, and everything else unfortunate enough to be caught in it burned while the ground trembled and cracked, and pressure waves that formed even reached her from above from great rushes of air displaced by the explosion. It was like a dying star that exploded in the middle of the arena, hence it was named such.

The explosion died down, leaving a crater bereft of everything but ash. A solemn silence had suddenly fallen into the arena. Rias tilted her head in confusion.

Did she not hit anyone from that? She was pretty sure she aimed where—

"H-Half of Riser's harem was eliminated!" Grayfia's shocked voice suddenly announced. "T-There's only five left on the opposing team now!"

—Ah, there it was. Hehe, were they shocked? She really worked hard making this one attack. To think that even the usually unflappable Grayfia has such a reaction… Umu, not a bad feeling. This wasn't a bad feeling at all!

She floated down on the crater, where she spotted a body which was half-buried on the ground. It was Riser, who looked completely baffled and disoriented at what happened. He looks kinda hurt from the attack but not debilitatingly so, and Rias can't help but feel smug at the look on his face.

"Mwahahaha! Is that you, Riser? What a pitiful sight!" she said, floating down in front of him with hands on her hips and gaining his attention. "Did I use a bit too much power perhaps? You're already down half your team. Sorry about that, teehee~!"

"Y-You—!" Riser shakingly stood up from the ground. "What the hell was that!?"

Rias blinked. "Eh? You obviously got hit by my attack. Are you stupid?" she paused. "Did you hit your head perhaps?"

A vein throbbed on his head. "Who the hell are you calling stupid, you bitch!? I—!" He looked like he was about to shout some more, but then he visibly held himself back to calm himself. "...Tch. Whatever. So you learned a few tricks in the past few days. Guess what, something like that wouldn't change the result of this duel!"

Large amounts of demonic energy surged out from him, matching her earlier display. The ground trembled, displacing wind that rushed away from him in the form of pressure waves.

"Don't get cocky now. You might have caught us off guard and knocked out half my girls, but the rest noticed and got away quickly. Tricks that weaklings like you use to get to our level won't work anymore." More and more power gathered around him, intensifying the tremors. "I'm the genius powerhouse that has defeated many of the demons in our generation: Riser H. Twining! Within our family carries the blood of Solomon and a trace of his keys. And as the most powerful member of it, I carry the title to become the rightful ruler of hell! How someone like you, a demon who spent her time playing in the human world, would ever hope to be—"

"Apocalyptic Nova!"

"—Gffwoughh!!!"

Riser was caught in another blast from her attack, thrown headfirst into the ground and burying him from the sheer force of it once more. The earth shook again from the ensuing explosion, and after the light show finished and dissipated, all that was left was a deeper crater compared to the first one with Riser in the middle of it. The guy's head and torso was buried with his lower body sticking out, leaving him in a kinda shameful position.

Rias just looked at her enemy with a disapproving frown.

"The hell are you doing, monologuing to me and powering up? You think I'll just let you do that?" she shook her head in disappointment. "Talking isn't a free action, you know."

Riser slowly extracted himself out of the ground, his blonde hair and high-quality clothes stained with soil and ash. He then slowly looked up at Rias who remained floating in the sky.

"You're dead." he stated.

Then, fire ignited around him and burned the surroundings. It was hot enough that she could feel it from up high. And from Riser's back manifested two wings of fire - holy fire, she now realized - which after a single flap let him ascend towards her in concerningly fast speeds.

Rias readied herself, even as she mentally chuckled.

Guess she must have pissed him off, huh?


"Ara… it seems like she's enjoying herself."

She spotted the lightshow happening midair a far out in the distance, with it being quite noticeable from the fiery infernos and great bursts of explosive projectiles being thrown around. Thankfully they were on the opposite side of the arena, so the risk of getting caught in those attacks was minimal.

Akeno can only sigh internally at her club president's enthusiasm in showing off her new technique. That girl… she could understand being excited at finally using it, but surely she could conserve her energy instead of using her energy for attacks like that? She's clearly getting swept away by the excitement of it all, just like the usual.

But then again, the display of power seems to be helping them in this case.

"W-What…?"

Akeno smiled at the sight of her enemy, the 'head' of Riser's harem based on their research, who looked gobsmacked at Rias throwing around incredibly devastating attacks like they're nothing. The fear and awe in her face looked so exquisite that she could taste it!

"You seem quite shocked." she pointed out with a giggle, gaining her enemy's attention. "Didn't expect our president to be this strong, did you? Were you perhaps thinking that we're small fry just because we were up in the human world?"

The woman frowned in displeasure. "...Maybe we did. Your initial attack caught us off-guard, but we won't make that mistake again." she brandished her weapon - a thorny whip that produced lightning and electrocuted anyone caught in it. "We will defeat you and join Riser-sama as he claims the girl as his wife." she growled.

Akeno noted the slight displeasure in her voice at that. Interesting, it seems that Rias isn't the only one who didn't like the arrangement, but then again politics cannot be avoided even in harems. She could imagine the main girl managing the harem would be under the betrothed wife.

But from her expression and tone of voice… Was that jealousy she was also hearing? How strange. Harems are usually treated badly by their masters as they're just another type of slaves. Being in a harem can give you a connection to a powerful demon at the cost of your own freedom, and most of the time they're usually treated as toys or something to collect. Affection has no place in harems, so why is she jealous?

Still, strangeness aside, even if the woman may feel that way…

Akeno raised a brow. "Oh, really? How is that going for you?"

One look around the place would make anyone realize that what the woman was saying was a complete lie - her club was absolutely demolishing the other harem members that each of them were facing. Kiba-kun and his affinity with swords allowed him to maneuver and expertly dismantle his opponent with ease, Koneko-chan and her incredible strength overwhelmed her enemy who tried to dodge desperately, knowing that she couldn't take even a single hit, and…

"—Take this! Hyah!"

There was Ryuusei-kun, who was a descendant of a human hero. Like any other descendants of those blessed by God he has the ability to summon their chosen weapon of war - one that took the form of a gauntlet. His great potential and innate battle skills allowed him to use it to great effect on fighting his opponent despite the disparity in experience.

After they regrouped in Rias' opening act, she and the other club members struck, preventing them from reaching Riser and allowing Rias to face him alone and them doing the same to Riser's harem. And now here they are, doing a great job of doing so.

Even more fortunate, half of the harem was caught in the blast leaving just enough for her club to face the harem members one on one instead of their original plan. Not like it would change things - Basa-kun's training in his special time-dilating room had helped them improve their fighting so much that their enemies felt weak. Their improvement was unreal, to the point that even she can't believe that she had become this strong in such a short amount of time.

Her enemy also knew this judging her sudden grimace. "How can demons up on the surface get this strong for such a short time…?" the woman muttered, almost absentmindedly.

Akeno simply answered with a fake serene smile. The woman didn't seem to like the expression on her face, as she grew angered and resumed attacking her with her dangerous whip.

To be completely honest, Riser and his harem expecting them to be weaklings was completely valid on their part. They were weak. All combat experience that they have in the human world was stray demons or the occasional violent supernatural dispute. They did train… but it was an occasional thing, and not really something that they've focused on. Their days up there was a simple leisure life away from the barbaric nest of politics here in hell. Something that she considered precious, and she knows that it's an opinion shared with the rest of the club - aside from Ryuusei-kun who didn't come from hell to have an opinion about it.

It seems like they were in Basa-kun's debt for allowing all this to be possible. The human magus had always been a mysterious person even when they were kids, and she can only imagine what sort of secrets he was keeping close to his chest. It was what made Rias drawn to him in the first place, persuading him to join their club because of the novelty of it - which eventually transitioned into something else.

Akeno's fake smile turned genuine at that thought.

She certainly wasn't blind to the changes her president had. While she didn't want to say it, Rias had been somewhat… lackluster when it comes to acting on her ambitions, for the past few years. She was affected by the leisure life up in the human world like the rest of them, and perhaps that had dulled her motivation somewhat. That changed as of late though as it was clear that the girl was returning to her roots, and it reminded her of why she had followed the impulsive and reckless girl out of hell in the first place instead of just laughing off her silly dream when she heard her say it.

Was this the power of love, perhaps? Really, they owed Basa-kun a lot. She certainly is very grateful about it - enough that she might consider bedding him because of it, and the man certainly had the looks that she wouldn't mind doing it even without the favors involved. But while a big part of her felt that way, an even bigger part of her wanted to watch Rias cutely pursue him from the sidelines. It was seriously the best, even better than any show that a television can offer.

Although if he did try to pursue him… can she get in on the action with Rias? She heard from her president that there were two other women too. And from what she heard about them, they must be great to have Rias gunning for them as well. Hm, maybe it really is a great idea to—

"You—! Are you daydreaming in the middle of a fight?!"

Her thoughts were interrupted by the indignant shout of her enemy, whose whip attacks she was dodging almost automatically and with ease. Ah, it seems that she had been distracted by her musings. That was quite embarrassing.

Oh well, she supposed it was about time to wrap things up anyway.

Dodging another whip strike that gouged a deep line on the ground, she called upon her demonic magic and manipulated elemental magic at her behest. With the woman incensed from her behavior she didn't even register her magic gathering under her - and with a surprised cry, tendrils of earth suddenly sprouted out from the ground and disabled her opponent by wrapping itself around her. She tried to struggle, but with Akeno reinforcing it to be stronger than steel and lacking any sort of leverage, her opponent can only remain tied up uselessly.

Akeno approached the struggling woman. "Apologies for the rudeness. I had a lot of things in mind, you see." she said with a giggle, to which she then received an angry glare in response. "Ara~? No need to be so angry. Quite a shame though, as while I might try to turn that grimace upside down with you tied up like this…"

She touched the woman's cheek and unleashed her succubus magic by draining her life essence. She licked her lips as she felt herself turning invigorated, at the cost of her opponent who was quickly turning sluggish… before she eventually turned unconscious, unable to muster the strength to stay awake.

"...We still have a duel to get to." she finished.

The tendrils of earth turned into normal soil losing its form, and her opponent dropped to the ground, out cold. She then watched as the body glowed white before disappearing without a trace. Those who were defeated will immediately be teleported out and will receive medical attention, as agreed upon in the duel's terms.

"...All of Riser's harem is now eliminated. Only Riser remains in the opposing team." Grayfia-san's announcement made Akeno blink and she turned around.

All other members of her club had more or less finished off their opponents as well. Kiba and Koneko were already standing around, having defeated their opponents earlier than her, but she glanced just in time to see Ryuusei-kun knocking out his opponent with a well-placed blow on the gut. The girl had dropped on the ground and was teleported after.

"Yoshaaaa!!! I woooon!!!" Ryuusei-kun shouted in jubilation as he raised his hands to the sky. He was covered in bruises and heaved deep breaths, but otherwise he remained totally fine.

"Very nice showing on your first official fight, Ryuusei-kun." Kiba-kun congratulated him with a smile on his face. "Looks like being a hero descendant really is something else, if you can fight that good despite being new in combat."

"Still have ways to go." Koneko-can added laconically, though that didn't deter the slight smile on her face. "But you did good."

Ryuusei-kun rubbed the back of his head at that. "Ahahaha… Thanks a lot, guys."

Akeno chose that moment to step in. "You all did good, everyone." she congratulated all of them with a proud smile on her face. They all worked for this, and it felt nice seeing the results of it all. "Now, let's regroup with Buchou and help her, shall we?"

Her question was answered with determined nods, and they all didn't waste time to get to Rias' position to assist her in any way that they could in defeating Riser and finishing this duel.

Akeno internally chuckled.

But knowing her club president and how much she trained for this though, she likely didn't need them to do that.

Oh well, at least the show would be good to watch.





Rias floated leisurely in the sky with Riser a distance away in front of her. She had a slight sheen of sweat on her face after the intense aerial combat which had occurred earlier, but it was nothing compared to how exhausted Riser looked.

The guy was breathing hard after throwing so much of his holy fire to her. The fire was dangerous, but she was agile enough to remain untouched. In contrast, Riser kept getting caught in explosions due to the large range of her own move, pretty much making him either expend more energy to dodge it or tank it instead.

Strangely, his attention was also split during their fight. She realized that he was also paying attention to his own harem while they fought her own club. His movements were directed to bait her into shooting her destructive attacks away from their direction, but it's not like she would risk hurting her own club to eliminate his harem. Her own club can very much do that on their own.

He was also glancing to the direction of the spectator stands. She doesn't know the reason for that one though.

That strange behavior… Maybe Riser was planning something. Maybe it was something else. In the end though, in their whole exchange Rias remained as the one with the advantage.

"How…" Riser growled, gaining her attention. "How the hell did you get this strong!? How can a demon like you keep up with me, of all people!?"

Rias stared at him quietly, simply calling up her demonic energy for another volley of attacks.

He must not have liked or misunderstood something in her expression, as his facial features twisted into anger. "You… don't think that you can look down on me!" he shouted, mirroring her by calling up his demonic energy as well.

And so went another bout between them, with Rias focusing on dodging the blazing ball of fire sent to her and ignoring the searing heat even as she avoided it, completely untouched, before dodging more that was sent to her. In between those attacks she sent her own, which was similarly avoided.

"Burn to ash!" Riser shouted in rage.

He closed in and tried to move for a punch on his flame-covered fist, a blanket of flame extending from his strike.. Rias went under before peppering him with lesser powered projectiles and making more distance. She couldn't touch him normally nor could she get into close quarters with his flames - something that he knew and tried to take advantage of by forcing himself close every time.

It was a game of cat and mouse where the one with lesser endurance loses.

"I'd rather not, thank you!" Rias shouted back.

Again much like earlier, she was gaining the advantage even when the intensity of Riser's attacks ramped up. He was getting tired for essentially nothing while she kept it safe and waited for opportunities to deliver attacks from far away. It clearly wasn't working for Riser - yet he kept doing it anyway. Had he lost his cool so much that he didn't care anymore?

Her question was eventually answered.

"—Eh!?"

There was a sound of metal rushing through the air, and Rias let out a cry of shock.

Fiery chains suddenly came out of nowhere and wrapped itself around her arms and legs. She felt the sizzling hot metals dig deep and burn her skin, making her cry out in pain. Rias grit her teeth and looked around to see where it came from: there, she saw some balls of fire that he threw earlier floating around had magic circles around it where the chains of fire sprouted from. She hadn't noticed - he used his barrage to hide it from her and put them in hard to spot positions as well.

Riser's enraged face disappeared and was replaced with a smirk. Ah, he was just acting!

"That was dirty…" she complained. She tried to struggle, but even as she tried to use all her strength it remained unbroken, only making her wince some more as the burning hot chains tightened further.

What exactly was this? Some sort of technique?

"Hmph. What a hypocritical thing to say to a fellow demon. Especially when a weakling like you kept doing tricks to keep up with me." Riser spoke, making her look his way. He had a hand extended towards her with a focused expression. "Struggle all you want but it will all be for naught. These are heirlooms of our family: a fragment of the Chains of Ars Goetia, which had controlled powerful demons of old. A weakling like you has no chance of breaking it."

Rias looked at him in surprise. What the hell was that? They'd researched all that they possibly could about Riser and his followers in preparation but something like this never came up, even borrowing the files that Basa-kun had about him. She knew she had a connection with King Solomon and all other stuff, but 'Chains of Ars Goetia'? That she never heard at all!

A memory surfaced from Basa-kun's lessons. She recognized this.

It was an asspull technique. A spontaneous power or ability that will surprise you and turn the tides of battle the way the plot wants it to go. The world changes retroactively so that it makes sense, but as a person who turned meta she would be the only one to remember the change. No amount of research will give you information about it and the only way to deal with something like it is by being flexible.

Something like that was easier said than done. Still, she chided herself. She should've at least expected something like this to happen.

"It's a shame that I had to reveal this now, but I suppose that I wouldn't lose anything here. You're going to be my wife once I finish this after all. Information about my trump card would be kept within the alliance." Riser continued to speak, justifying the asspull. "Do you see how fruitless your attempt to fight back is now? You should've just acted like a good girl and agreed with the betrothal."

His smirk widened as his gaze looked up and down on her restrained body.

"But I suppose I do like my girls feisty." he said with a dark chuckle. "Nothing better than the sight of delusional trash being humbled; there's a certain charm in seeing an arrogant weakling being brought to heel."

A vein throbbed on her forehead at that comment. "Arrogant weakling!? If anything that's you, since I was just beating your ass a while ago! Don't get so smug just because you had a relic or something to pull out of your ass—Owowow, hot!" she yelped as the chains dug deeper.

Riser's smile turned fixed as his extended hand closed into a fist, the chains tightening further in response. "Talk what you want about strength, but all that matters is the victor of the fight. That is what only matters when it comes to us demons." he said in a tight tone. "And need I remind you that you're in my mercy right now?"

Rias frowned thoughtfully at that. What he said was true, so how exactly…?

She then blinked, before putting on a sad expression. "...I-I'm sorry, forgive me for acting out of line… Can you please let me go? I'll be your fiance for real and I won't protest the betrothal this time. So please?" she pleaded desperately.

"...What the hell are you even doing?" Riser deadpanned.

"Tch." her sad expression immediately disappeared as she looked away. "Didn't work, huh."

"Apocalyptic Nova!"

"—gffwoughh!!!"

A magic circle appeared in her palm and launched a shot towards Riser who got hit by the projectile directly, engulfing him in another explosion. He was launched away, wings of fire flickering for a bit, but he managed to right himself before he could fall down on the ground. Rias also felt the chains around her slacken, but it immediately tightened again when he brought his hand back up and retained control of the chains once more.

Heh, looks like baiting a comedy scene to let an enemy's guard down is pretty effective. As expected, Basa-kun gives great advice! She could see how it was pretty handy.

Still… at least with this she had confirmed something.

Rias observed Riser's focused yet enraged expression as he floated to her once more. The chains moved to bring her hands together on her back in an uncomfortable position, making it impossible for her to point her palms to Riser again to repeat the stunt while also turning the burning pain a lot more worse. The guy also put a bit of distance between them now, making any more attacks connect harder.

Such a strange thing to do. Here she was completely restrained, and yet he wasn't making use of it by attacking her or anything. He couldn't even dodge her half-assed attack properly when he easily did so earlier in the fight. She was beginning to have an idea as to why that was the case.

"You're useless right now. You can't even fight." she continued. "You're just stalling for time waiting for others to arrive."

He couldn't wield those chains effectively yet. Quite fortunate. Or was it perhaps deliberate?

Basa-kun suspected that she was the one taking the role of the protagonist now, being proactive about everything and in the center stage of all things. Despite it though, it doesn't mean that she'll win every conflict as the plot cannot predict her actions due to her meta nature, but it should at least assist her in ways that would make every conflict thrown to her as something that is not outright impossible. Perhaps this was a manifestation of that.

Of course, that's ignoring the fact that the plot needed for there to be a conflict and hence the reason why it created such an asspull technique in the first place. If she had defeated Riser immediately it wouldn't happen at all, but since she didn't, the plot likely had leeway to add such a conflict to match her.

That's kinda annoying to deal with.

"..."

Riser went quiet at her deductions. Then, seemingly in response, the chains even tightened further. It was digging deep into her muscles now and she was kind of scared what the scars would look like, but she didn't care. She endured the pain and met his gaze back unflinchingly.

His face betrayed no emotion at all, but a bead of sweat fell down on Riser's forehead. It wasn't because of the heat or exhaustion.

Still, he spoke as if he didn't have a single problem about it. "...Perhaps you're correct, but as I said: the only thing that matters is who is the victor. No matter how dirty or despicable our methods are, so long as we win, then it doesn't matter." he muttered. "That is the way of us demons, and how it will always be."

Riser explained the words coldly, but for some reason, Rias heard a tinge of bitterness in how he said it. She blinked in surprise at that, but all thoughts about it were shelved when Riser continued.

"This is checkmate." he declared. "There's no way for you to win."

…She wouldn't ignore such a blatant setup now, would she?

Confusion, shock, then to incredulity - he turned to the direction of where his harem and her club were fighting and, even from a distance, saw the telltale blink of light of what can only be teleportation magic being used to transport the unconscious bodies of defeated opponents.

She trusted her club to be on top of it, and they definitely delivered. She really was lucky to have such competent people by her side.

And now, it was her turn to do her job.

"W-What…!?" Riser muttered in complete disbelief. "My harem… completely defeated!? How!?"

"Those chains freaking hurt! Take this!"

Nor the rest of the beatdown coming his way.

"Oraoraoraoraora!"

Rias unleashed a flurry of blows. "You… I can't believe all this…!" Riser growled out. His expression was complicated; a mix of outrage, humiliation, anger, and panic at the same time. Everything was going out of his control. "This… Am I losing!? This is impossible! How can I lose to a no-name demon like you!?"

Many others have tried to unite the underworld in one banner and failed! "And I'm not going to let you stop me by letting this betrothal go through!"

Rias frowned in concentration as she readied her own attack. Her own Apocalyptic Nova, no holds barred this time. The destructive energy thrummed loudly above her hands, roaring like a beast in a cage that wanted to devour and destroy everything in its way.

The two of them launched the attacks at each other, and the projectiles sailed through the air before colliding and engulfing them in heat and light.

At that very moment, the day rose earlier in hell.


Rias floated down on the charred ground. Her uniform had burns in some places, but aside from the scars that she gained from the chains, she was unharmed.

In contrast to that was Riser's own battered form, laid down on the ground facing up covered in burns and wounds. Something like that is so impossible that it's useless to even try!"

I'm sick of us demons fighting each other for the stupidest reasons, even when we can be better. Why can't we just be friends and get along with everyone? Has someone even tried?"

Rias stared behind her. In the distance, she could see the very tip of the artificial sun of hell rising up as the dawn broke. She gazed at it with a solemn look on her face.

I'd probably regret it more if I didn't try to even do it. And thankfully, there's a surefire way to make sure it happens."

Rias turned around, her gaze locking onto Riser's own while she gave him a bright grin. She felt the heat of the sun as the rays of light slowly crept up her back, as the morning twilight had the sun rise to the point that it could cast a shadow in front of her.

A view that somehow made Riser's eyes widen slightly as he stared at her.

Rias saw Ryuusei-kun call out quite a distance away from the destroyed landscape they were in. He was running towards her along with the rest of her club with a bright smile on their faces. They looked a bit banged up, but other than that they looked totally fine. As expected from her club!

"Of course you need your companions with you." Riser scoffed. "Can't even face me without the help of others. As expected of a weakling."

"Why you…!"

"Now, now. There's no need to act that way, Ryuusei-kun. The duel is already over." Rias interrupted the two of them. "Plus, we all should be getting along! Me and Riser just happened to have a rough introduction with each other. That's all fixed because we're friends now!"

"We're not friends. I agreed to put aside our differences and to not take any hard feelings from the slight you gave for rejecting a formal betrothal, but we're not 'friends'. Allies, at best." Riser said with a frown.

"Sure, buddy. Whatever you say!" Rias said with a grin.

The guy looked at her, before slowly looking down at his hands. "…Have I somehow made a mistake?" he whispered to himself.

What a funny person, this guy. She really misunderstood him the first time they met!

She heard Akeno chuckle. "Ara~ Looks like you work fast, Buchou. I wouldn't have expected that your characteristic charm would work its magic in this situation, but I guess I should have." she turned to Riser and gave him a smile. "Looks like you're friends with Rias now. You're better off going along with the flow, it's easier that way."

"Akeno-senpai!? Just like that!? Are you seriously accepting him being friends with us now!?" Ryuusei-kun shouted incredulously, before turning to the others. "Come on, guys. Back me up here!"

Kiba shook his head with a chuckle. "Nothing you can do about it, Ryuusei. Buchou already decided, so it's settled."

Koneko just shrugged noncommittally.

"I can't accept this! Why the hell would I want to be friends with a blonde bastard like him!? He insulted our president and wants to marry her even though he has a harem!" Ryuusei-kun shouted dramatically. "Seriously, why the hell does he have a harem!? That's so unfair! I want to have one too!"

Kiba sweatdropped. "In the end it's because of the harem, huh."

"I'll tell what you said to Aisha." Koneko stated.

Ryuusei-kun immediately bowed down to Koneko. "I sincerely apologize for what I said. I realize that it was a foolish thing to say, please don't tell her." there was a short silence. "…I'll treat you to some lunch after this."

"Breakfast, lunch and dinner."

"Kghh…! Merciless, you're too merciless, Koneko!" she raised a brow. "But of course, I was simply making jest. Anything that you want."

Koneko nodded in satisfaction.

"What is this stooge show… Is this seriously the people who defeated my harem?" Riser muttered on the side, his tone of voice laced with disbelief.

"Shut up! You're the one who got beaten here! If we're stooges then what does that make you!?" Ryuusei-kun immediately went aggressive once more as he heard Riser's comment. "Be thankful that Buchou considers you as a friend or else I'd have kicked your ass! I already have one blonde bastard who pisses me off in my life, I don't need another inferior copy of it walking around!"

"Who the hell are you calling an inferior copy!? We're nothing alike, damn it!"

Rias watched the arguing two with a smile. While those two don't look like they'll be friendly with each other anytime soon, it looks like any hatred that stemmed from this little fight was gone. As her club interacted in their own unique way to their new friend, the noise of it all felt welcoming. Like they were back in the clubroom and enjoying the moment.

The light of the new morning shone upon them, and she drank the warm atmosphere with a bright look on her face.

It's so good to see everyone getting along!


Such an inspiring scene. As expected of the shounen genre, after a dramatic confrontation between the antagonist that seems redeemable, a short inspiring speech will fix it and things will be all's well that ends well. I've seen it happen plenty of times, but despite the innate cheesiness of it I still can't help but think of it as beautiful.

Still, while I may feel that way… I can't help but feel it's marred by the sight beside me.

"Hic! Uuu, R-Rias…! As expected, my sister is so… so…!"

I looked blankly at Rias' brother as he bawled his eyes out. The noble visage that he wore a while ago was nowhere to be found, replaced entirely by this incredibly happy siscon who couldn't care less about appearances. He was shedding tears out of sheer pride of his sister the moment Rias said her speech, making all these weird sounds as well.

I mean, I get that it's supposed to be comedic, but at least wipe your nose instead of letting it run all over you for crying out loud. Even your wife over there was getting embarrassed by your behavior and she's a damn kuudere.

In contrast, Serafall didn't even seem fazed at his reactions. I get the feeling that she was used to it. "That girl never ceases to surprise me. I can definitely see why little Sona felt the need to be in the human world after becoming friends with her." she commented with a smile.

"A demon who'd rather have everyone get along as opposed to ruling them under their own thumb… if we weren't unholy creatures, then I'd say that this must be the work of God's miracles." Ajuka shook his head. "…Perhaps, if she were to be born earlier…" he trailed off.

Sirzechs smiled widely. "Do you now see why my sister is the best there is? She's planning to be the ruler of hell and even beat Riser, one of the many promising demons in their generation! I can already tell that she'd be the greatest demon to ever grace this realm!"

"Now hold on a second. She might be good, but she's no match for my Sona!" Serafall interrupted. "Also you're the one who forced her to marry Riser and caused this problem in the first place. Why are you acting like a die-hard supporter now?"

He grit his teeth and clenched his fist. "—Kghh, I know that! What she said earlier, about the reason why she became so strong…" Sirzechs closed his eyes and shed tears again. "She was 'catching up to someone', she said. She was clearly talking about me. To think Rias would want to reach my level just so she could be side-by-side with her beloved brother, and her determination led to this result… She must've been working on this for a while now. She did all that and made an effort, yet here I am, stopping her from reaching me!"

I suspect that Rias wasn't talking about him when she said those words, but I don't think I have the heart to say that.

"Forgive your brother for not recognizing your efforts! I am a fool! My worry for her had blinded my faith in her abilities, I truly am a failure as a brother!" he wailed dramatically in regret as he kept crying. "I should just go kill myself for penance! I am nothing but a—!"

"I believe that we should meet the winners. The duel is now over after all." Grayfia interrupted him.

The redhead paused and, after a glare from his wife, the man coughed to compose himself. "Y-Yes. Yes, of course." he said sheepishly, before letting out an exhale. "Wouldn't want them to keep waiting." he said a bit more seriously.

With that, the guy stood up and followed his wife. I followed with the rest as we walked towards the teleportation array heading to the duel grounds. As we did so, Serafall discreetly approached me and leaned to my ear to whisper something.

"Say… what Rias was talking about, she was definitely referring to you, right?" the demon woman whispered in a conspiring tone. I glanced at her, and she gave me a devious smile. "You know, you're definitely interesting. I'll be heading over to the human world for a few days sometime after this, so why don't we get to know each other better during that?"

…Great. Looks like I'd have to deal with her attention, but it's natural considering my training just made Rias beat a young powerhouse in just a few days. Especially with me enduring Serafall's power, I imagine everyone here is going to keep a close eye on me from now on.

But then again, something like that is already inevitable. And I'd also have to be in the thick of things in order to observe what happens after all. A meta character for a protagonist in a shounen storyline as big as this will definitely need monitoring, considering this was the first time it happened for me.

I answered her with a wordless nod. That seemed enough as the demon woman separated herself from me with a smile on her face. We then followed the others as they entered the teleportation array.

There was a flash of light as we were displaced from our initial position in an instant before dying down.

"—So what if you're a descendant of Solomon or whatever? I have the blood of heroes with me, but I'm not acting all high and mighty about it!" I heard the ex-protagonist angry voice the moment we arrived.

A scoff. "As if a human hero's blood could ever compare to that Our family—" Rias' ex-fiance paused as he noticed us arrive. He turned to face us respectfully. "...Sirzechs-sama, Serafall and Ajuka-sama. My greetings."

All the people around stopped from whatever they were doing to stare at us. Rias' face brightened as her eyes locked onto mine, giving me an excited look. She was about to say something but then she was interrupted when her brother spoke.

"Riser." Sirzechs spoke, returning to his noble-like demeanor as if he didn't just bawl his eyes out earlier. "You lost. It appears that you must hold up your end of the agreement."

"…I will. No longer will I marry your sister, Sirzechs-sama."

"Very well. We've also heard your plan in regard to your parent's reactions towards this." Riser flinched at that, but the redhead simply gave him a slight smile. "Do not worry about that; we'll be the ones to smooth things over. Rest assured, you won't be caught in the crossfire."

The guy seemed to let out a relieving sigh at that, his shoulders losing the slightest bit of tension. "...My deepest gratitude to you, Sirzechs-sama." he said, giving him a bow. Then, he turned to the maid beside the redhead, an unasked question on his face.

The maid answered him without hearing the question. "Your harem is fine and sleeping the fight off. Just go to the teleportation array." she said, gesturing to the one we just came out of.

He nodded. "Then, by your leave."

With all that said, Riser then walked away from us to teleport to the stands. As he did so though, just before he could step inside to fully leave, Rias raised a hand to him and bid him farewell.

"See ya, Riser! How about you hang out with us in the human world next time? You know, since we're friends now!" she shouted cheerily.

He tripped slightly, but quickly recovered. Then, with a glare towards Rias, he then entered the teleportation array. "I already told you we're not friends!" he shouted back.

The guy disappeared in a flash, leaving them and Rias' club alone.

Rias brought down her hand with a grin. "What a funny guy. He's definitely the type to enjoy life up there. I guess we'll see him up there after a few days or so." her grin then slowly slipped off her face. "But moving on…"

She turned her head to look at her brother with a challenging smile on her face.

"I'm guessing there's no problem with this, nii-san?" she asked.

Sirzechs looked at his sister quietly. Again, looking at the man he looked as every bit as his reputation of a strong demon suggests, having shown no trace of his almost pitiful appearance earlier. It's even hard to believe it was the same person that I'm looking at. I suspect the large difference had to do with his characterization emphasizing on the contrast between his siscon personality and his normal one.

The others haven't seen what I had seen though, so for them the redhead simply looked intimidating. Rias' club looked uncomfortable as he stared at them along with the rest of his allies. Only Rias remained unbothered, truly knowing her brother for who he is.

Then, after a while, he finally spoke.

"I've heard what you said from Grayfia." he started, tone unreadable. "With your stunt here, there's truly no doubt that you're now part of the race to become the Ruler of Hell."

Rias kept quiet.

"There's no more running away from responsibilities or hiding away in the human world, Rias… You're now part of this battle. Others will challenge you, especially due to your status as my sister. Don't expect rationality or honor like Riser, because at this point on, only strength matters." he stated. "Not everyone can be like him, after all."

"....I know. It's something that I've come to realize on my own." Rias answered. "In fact, I've also come to realize that I've been putting this off for a very long time. There's nothing more I would want than this."

"Is that so…" Sirzechs closed his eyes. "Then, if that's the case, then there's one thing that you should know. Consider this as a warning dear sister; If, by chance, it would come to a point where we compete with each other…"

He opened his eyes to glare at Rias.

"...Then, I will show you no mercy." he declared.

What followed after that statement was, predictably, a flex of their power

True to almost all times I've met with demons, they unleashed their demonic energy to show off just how powerful they are. This one was different from the earlier ones though, as while I could tell that he was the most powerful out of the bunch that I've met - the power he was exuding was all muted. What Serafall did to me earlier was worse than this.

But I suppose it was enough for the people it was aimed at. Rias' club stood petrified in fear as they saw what they thought was power incarnate for the very first time in their lives. This would surely be an eye opening experience for them showing that ,despite all their improvements from my training, they were all just frogs in a well.

However… one person was exempt from this.

Rias weathered the show of power and didn't show much reaction to it. The redhead simply looked at her own brother straight in the eyes without backing down, not even the slightest bit intimidated by what he had shown to her.

Then, she let out a grin.

"Of course! I wouldn't expect anything else, nii-san!" she said with a laugh. "Just watch me! I'll get there in no time at all!"

Sirzechs blinked in surprise at her reaction, before his lips slowly curled up into a slight smile. With Rias' resolve tested, his power whittled down, eventually making the surrounding pressure return to normal and allowing Rias' club to breathe again.

"I see. I'm happy to hear that Rias." he shook his head. "I suppose congratulations are in order then. I suspect that you might want to celebrate this victory, but forgive me for not coming with you as I have matters to attend to."

"It's fine, nii-san. I'd like to spend it more with my club anyway." she waved away. "Plus, we have plenty of time to catch up later. It's been a while since I've returned here, after all."

Hearing that, Sirzechs sent her a genuine smile. The man then turned around to leave, but before he did so, he said one last thing. With his cape fluttering behind him along with his long flowing red locks of hair, the man gave them a look of what can only be described as one that invites challenge.

"I'll wait for you at the finish line, Rias."

With that, the man stepped into the teleportation array and disappeared in a flash.

Serafall giggled. "...Look at that guy, can't just resist trying to look cool, huh?" she turned to Rias with a smile. "We need to get going too. Say hi to my sister for me, okay?" as she left, she also waved a hand in farewell to me as well.

Ajuka simply nodded his head politely before following. Leaving Rias and her club, the maid, and then me. For a moment there was a slight silence.

"…That was intense. Who were they?" the ex-protagonist muttered.

"Those are the most powerful demons in hell… the top contenders of becoming its ruler." Kiba answered absentmindedly, before turning to me with a disbelieving look on his face. "Basa-kun, you were with them this whole time? How exactly did you survive that?"

"They seemed like decent people." I answered.

The blonde doesn't look like he was satisfied with the answer. Too bad, it's all that he's going to get.

"Fufufu~ Kiba, you know how Basa-kun and his mysteriousness is. It's one of his main charms." It totally was. This woman gets me, for real. "Now, more importantly - should we get going? I know we defeated Riser's harem easily, but I'm parched. Oh, and Buchou needs to have her arms and legs fixed… Ara, it's already healed?"

Rias brought down the healing potion she just drank. "Hm? What's that?"

"...Are those healing potions, ojou-sama?" Grayfia asked to the side, looking at her strangely.

"Ah, yeah. Basa-kun made them for us. It's really convenient!" she sighed out in relief as the burns in her arms and legs disappeared. "Hahhh… that's the good stuff. Riser would've been really surprised if I had to use this midfight, especially with how many they are! Not that I needed it though."

"..."

I ignored the intense gaze of the maid boring to my side. Probably because this sort of stuff is rare in their setting. I doubt they've heard of anything like this. Way to go tell them about it, Rias.

"Alright, we did good everyone! This whole duel has gone splendidly! Now, there's only one thing left for us to do…" Rias said after recovering from her injuries, pointing onwards like some adventurer of old. "Come on, Basa-kun, Grayfia - everyone! Let's go celebrate our victory!"

"—Yeahhhh! Let's gooo!"

"Fufu~ Good show, everyone."

"Man, that was tiring…"

"Nn. The feast is waiting."

The rest of the club cheered after her, following closely behind as their leader went ahead. Most vocal of all is the ex-protagonist who obnoxiously cheered like some hyped-up sports player after a win, with the rest being a bit more subdued. There was no denying the satisfied smiles and grins on their faces though.

The same went for Grayfia who quietly trailed behind them with a soft smile on her face. I did the same, unwilling to intrude on their first victorious moment as a club.

There's just something great about finishing everything on a good note. With this little arc, Rias had earned not an enemy but rather a friend, as well as proving herself willing to even reach her dream in the process. How would it compare if she hadn't turned meta, I wonder?

Somehow, I just had the feeling it would be less than this.

Because while Rias was clearly someone who was meant to be a heroine…

There was no doubt that being a protagonist suited her at her core.


…

…But not all is happy.

For every smile given, there is someone out there who is crying out of sorrow, pain, or grief. Quite an edgy thing to say, but it nevertheless was a simple truth that lies in the back of our minds during happy times. A wise man had put it eloquently: the feeling called 'happiness' would lose its meaning if it weren't to be balanced by 'sadness'.

And in a world such as this, where even the simplest things hold meaning for the purpose of the story, it applies even more. Not everything can be smiles and pleasant feelings.

Because tragedy exists.

Sadness and sorrow itself can be beautiful in its own way.

And so on the other side of the world, in one of my other clones, my footsteps splashed the pooling water on the wet streets of a war-torn country. I walked under the heavy downpour of rain without an umbrella or a raincoat to cover myself, uncaring of the fact that my hair and clothes were completely drenched, already being used to such a feeling.

The atmosphere was quiet and solemn. It was cold and deep into the night, with the broken infrastructure and streets devoid of any people, having long since evacuated the battlefield or had died trying. There was debris everywhere from the destruction of the once-intact infrastructure and there was not a single thing left standing. A dense fog even settled around the area, carrying the stench of death is evident from wherever one may go.

Many people had died here, both young and old. In this very battlefield there were tales of heroism that happened, undoubtedly just as many as those who had died meaningless deaths.

I stopped walking. At my side was a nondescript alley, it was dirty and left forgotten, destroyed like the rest of the landscape.

However, the water that pooled on my feet here was mixed with flowing blood.

I walked inside, putting away the small crystal ball that I carried. The same crystal ball that can predict the movements of characters who are still firmly within control of the world, who I used with Rias and Yuki to investigate when exactly they turned meta after they didn't match what it predicted.

Exactly like what was happening right now.


Spoiler

The blonde woman leaning at the alley's walls stared at me, her face showing an empty and broken expression. She was covered in dirt and her body was littered with cuts and bruises - but most notable of all was her missing arm where blood flowed out continuously and pooled beside her.

The girl was undoubtedly in her final moments and would've died, ending a tragic life in some sort of beautiful and poetic way like a world like this demands. But instead of seeing what I would expect a cold corpse, what I saw in front of me was a woman impossibly clinging to life despite the despair that she carried within her. A dying woman, crushed and on her lowest point, yet she still goes on.

I also didn't fail to notice her other hand, clutching a hidden grenade out of my view, was thumbing the pin in case I wasn't friendly. She was planning to fight for her life, even now.

Incredible. She was a struggler in the most literal sense. Even without a reason to live, even when her fate was sealed…here she was, still trying to persist. For the life of me, I cannot imagine why a tragedy was decided to be more beautiful than what I'm seeing right now.

Another one to chalk up to this ridiculous world.

There were a few seconds of silence as we stared at each other, broken only with the sound of heavy rain.

"...Who are you?" she weakly whispered in a blank tone of voice.

I met the dying woman's gaze evenly. Then I answered.

"Your savior, most likely."

She looked confused at my statement, but that didn't matter. Explanations can come later after all. Now, I have to make sure this person doesn't die first like she was meant to be.

Because… it seems that I've finally met my fourth heroine.
