Sorry for the long wait for this chapter - I was really busy for the past couple months. Anyway, here's a new chapter in the eyes of our new heroine! And an idea for the upcoming chapter too. Hope you guys enjoy it!


Chapter 19

Blue eyes opened to see a blank ceiling in a simple, unfurnished room.

The woman pulled herself up from laying down. A dull pain felt by her body told her that she was still hurting, but practice allowed her to simply ignore it. She looked around, observing the room she was in, and wondering where exactly she was.

The woman's dead gaze examined her surroundings, analyzing her situation calmly. The room she was in looked similar to the ones in the field hospital, although it wasn't congested with the sick, dying, or dead. She was alone in this small place. Although, she did notice there was a chair and a small table filled with medical instruments to the side of her bed, showing the signs of someone coming into the room and working on her injuries.

Her blonde locks, matted from sweat, fell on her forehead and obscured her vision slightly. She raised her hands to get it out of the way but another bout of pain seemingly followed the simple movement. A glance to the side, and the woman realized that it was because of a specific part of her body. Or rather, the lack of it.

Her entire left forearm was gone. Her limb from elbow and below was seemingly cut off, with the elbow itself covered with bandages so that she wouldn't bleed out. Memories returned, and she distantly recalled her being trapped in rubble after being caught in an explosion while under fire from enemy artillery, and her swift decision to cut it off so she wouldn't get caught.

More memories followed. It was a blurry recollection of her simply trying to survive. Her entire squad was wiped but she managed to escape or avoid her enemies, managing to live for a while before succumbing due to too much loss of her blood. However, just as she had felt her vision dim, she recalled a figure approaching her…

"Looks like you're awake."

She glanced to the side to see the door open and for a person to enter. She calmly observed this new person: it was a man with blonde hair and tanned skin, one with a large build and height similar to her fellow soldiers, but not visibly armed with any weapon. The man closed the door gently behind him before moving to sit on the chair beside her.

"You were in dire shape when I found you. Aside from your left arm missing, you seem to have been shot multiple times along with other injuries due to shrapnel. It's a miracle you were still alive." he stated. "You're fine now though. I managed to fix all of it, but you'd still need to recuperate. Your body still needs to take some time to recover—"

"Why did you save me?"

He stopped when she spoke for the first time. The woman's unnervingly blank gaze was directed at him, yet he showed no signs of being bothered by it. Then, after a moment of deliberation, he answered her question.

"I saved you because we're linked together now." he simply stated, before introducing himself politely. "The name's Basa, by the way. Nice to meet you."

The woman's blank gaze went unabated, but there was a degree of confusion in her gaze now. "…Are you my new commanding officer?" she asked, trying to make sense of it. "If you are, then I must apologize for my state. My efficiency in assisting during missions is lessened." she bowed her head in submission. "…I can serve you, however. My other parts appear to be intact." she added, looking in the direction of his waist.

"No need for that." he assured, frowning slightly at her comment.

It didn't go unnoticed to the woman. "…I see, do you not find me attractive?" she then glanced at her missing arm as if it explained everything, before nodding. "I must be a burden at this point. Does this mean I'm discharged from duty then? Or shall I be sent to die in the field, like the others?" the statement was said as if she was discussing the weather.

"I think you're getting a wrong idea of what's happening." he interrupted. "For all intents and purposes, you've perished in the battlefield and considered officially dead. I'm not your new commanding officer or anything like that, and you're no longer part of the army either."

The woman stared blankly at him again, taking it all in.

"Understood." she said, simply. "Then, what are my orders from now on?"

There was a quiet moment as that question came. Then, the man sighed.

"…Codename V. No legal name. Birthplace, unknown. Birthdate, unknown. Found as a child in a shipwrecked ruin on the coast of an island in the north, specifically the fifth sector, hence the codename. Conscripted into the army shortly after that - but due to the lack of identifiable registration and the almost feral behavior displayed, you were brought in and treated as a weapon. You weren't even human. But you managed to make yourself a passable imitation just by spending sufficient time with other people in your unit, learning enough to speak, read, and write."

The man narrated information about the woman, who simply listened quietly without a single emotion in her face.

"You were treated as a tool and abused by everyone around. You lived a life of tragedy, never knowing anything beyond the battlefield. And that remained until your supposed end during an enemy confrontation. I doubt anyone in your unit misses you in your death. Or at least, I doubt they cared beyond lamenting the loss of the woman they're abusing in their ranks." he said, gaining a grave frown on his face. However, it was wiped seconds later. "And yet, despite all that… you wanted to live, somehow defying fate against all odds. Leading to where we are now."

He stared straight in her gaze.

"You ask what your orders are? There's none. Your life is your own now." he answered. "What do you want to do in your life?"

The woman blinked as the question was asked to her. A furrow in her brow indicated the confusion that she felt as, for the very first time she woke up, she hesitated. It took a very long time for her to answer.

"I… do not know." she eventually replied.

The man, who was waiting patiently, simply nodded. "That's fine. Just think on it for now. It'd be hard to break through the conditioning you were put through, after all." he then stood up. "But before all that, just rest. You still need to recover from wounds healing. You can help yourself to anything in this place. Or you can go ahead and call me if you need assistance."

With that, the man exited the room. Perhaps to deal with other tasks or something else in need of his attention. And as he left, the door closed gently, leaving the woman stewing in the quiet stillness of the unfurnished room once more.

And so, V was left alone with her own thoughts. Along with the alien uncertainty that came along with it.



She had managed to recover relatively quickly. It took a single day for the pain of her amputated arm to dull into something manageable and for her to regain the strength to stand up straight. Seeing no reason to stay on the bed anymore, she took it upon herself to finally leave the room she was in.

The place they were in was a simple household. A single story house constructed mostly from wood, similar to the cabins constructed in the woody forests they were sometimes stationed in to headquarter their officers, or the ruins of what used to be homes to families within the area. Looking at a window, the outside of the house was similar, although it seems that they were far from the battlefield considering the lack of sounds of enemy gunfire or artillery around.

When she left the room she found the man, Basa, seated at the dining table, attending to some files piled on top of it while sipping hot coffee. He turned to her when she exited her room, inclining his head in greeting.

"Good morning. Want to take a seat? There's breakfast."

V nodded her head obediently and sat down in the seat in front of what looked like a hot frothy soup, as he instructed. The woman used her single right arm to use the spoon, before putting the food in her mouth. She paused for a moment, before eating the rest quickly.

She consumed it all in record time and put the spoon down after she was finished. The man smiled. "How was it?"

"It was very delicious." she stated factually.

"I see. I'll say that to the woman who cooked it. She'll be very happy to hear that." he then indicated the pot on the table, right in front of her. "There's plenty in that pot there. Help yourself if you want more. Don't worry about me - I already ate. You can have the rest."

She nodded and began eating some more. The woman noticeably ate in a more lively manner this time, seemingly savoring each spoonful. Still, she ate quite fast, and her body must have been demanding nutrients and fuel since she managed to devour it all. Then when it was over, she went back to staring at Basa quietly.

For a while they did just that. The only sound that interrupted the quiet was the noise of him leafing through the sheets of paper.

Sometimes, he would stand up to do something else. V stood up from her chair as well when that happened, following him closely behind. Then, when he returned back to the dining table, she would also sit back down and return to staring at him.

"I'm not giving you orders, you know." he suddenly commented, his gaze still on the files before him.

V tilted her head at that. "You are not?"

"As I said, you're responsible for what you want now. What do you want to do? Any desires? Any sort of dreams you want done?"

She was quiet for a moment, furrowing her brows and feeling the swirl of uncertainty in her chest once more, much like how she felt yesterday as she tried to answer those questions. And much like yesterday, none were coming forth. Then she blinked, seemingly coming to a conclusion.

"…I want to do whatever you order me to do." she stated with a nod.

He gave her a flat gaze. "No, that's clearly a cop out answer."

She tilted her head again. "I don't understand." she muttered. "…May I assist you with what you are doing, then? I can read and write."

The man scrutinized her, before letting out a sigh. "I guess you can. I doubt you can answer it easily anyway. Might as well do it in small steps." he then pushed to her some of the papers. "Here, try to arrange these. And don't hesitate to ask if you have a question."

She nodded obediently, before proceeding to read the pages so that she may sort them properly. She was barely literate, not understanding much of the many words she was reading, but she could make a guess on the contents of the paper. A curious expression appeared on her blank face, although she diligently continued to arrange the papers in order.

However, after arriving at a particular file, she finally spoke.

"Excuse me." she said, gaining Basa's attention. "These files - they're about the war, aren't they?"

"They are." he answered simply.

She tilted her head. "Did you lie about me not being part of the army anymore? Some of the files appear to be highly classified." she stated in a tone with no hint of accusation nor judgement, but rather simple curiosity. "Did I fail a test? Will I be punished?"

"Not really. I stole it." he said casually while leafing through the sheets of paper.

"I see." she nodded in acceptance, reassessing the situation with the information.

She then continued to quietly arrange the papers. However, a certain file caught her attention which made her stop for a moment and call the man's attention dutifully. "Excuse me." she called again. "You said that you stole this information? I believe the information in this particular page is inaccurate."

"Hm? How so?"

She looked down at the page of a certain file. "There should be no battle involving giant mechanical robots in this war. Should I throw this one away?"

The page in question was a brief report detailing the use of giant robots and their effectiveness. And although there were pictures in the file itself, it's easily dismissed as fake since she hadn't witnessed them at any point. Even more, some of the battles it said to have partook in were ones she had been present in as well. Perhaps it was faulty intelligence made to mislead the enemy in case of being stolen, which puts into doubt the certainty of these files as a whole.

Basa simply hummed. "No, that's true. You just didn't notice. Maybe you were preoccupied with the guns and artillery at that time?"

She shook her head. "I would've noticed. And I do not think giant robots exist." she said factually.

He paused, before bringing the files down on top of the table. Then he gave her an enigmatic smile. "The world is more vast than you can imagine. Giant robots exist. And so does the supernatural, and other stuff you thought that aren't real. It's just that there are restrictions imposed on people that make them unable to see them if they don't meet the requirements." he explained. "And now, you're one of the rare people that meet it all. Isn't that incredible?"

V stared at him blankly.

"I see." she said with another accepting nod. "Understood. Should I keep this paper then?"

"…Somehow, I don't think you believe me." Basa said, gaining a deadpan look.

"I believe you, sir. Giant robots and magic definitely exist."

"And now you're being sarcastic too. Didn't expect that with that emotionless archetype going on." he said with a sigh. Then, he brought up his hand with the palms open facing the ceiling. "Here, look at my hand. Not holding a lighter or anything, right? Watch."

A ball of fire suddenly manifested atop his palm. She blinked once, and twice. Then, in a manner that would've had her disciplined due to moving without permission, she approached him and went to touch the fire with a curious expression. It was hot, but not burning hot. She moved her fingers around the man's palm; there was nothing that could make it levitate like that.

"Ohh." she muttered, letting out an amazed sound that didn't quite match the relatively blank face that she wore.

"So? Convinced? I can show you more if you still doubt it." he said.

She shook her head. For some time there was a considering silence as V simply did nothing but stare at the magical flame on his palm. Then, after a while, she spoke once more.

"You said that things that I thought were real, are." she began, speaking out the thoughts that raced in her mind. "Then, does that mean Santa is real?"

Basa blinked, seemingly surprised at the unexpected question. He looked at the still-blank face of the woman that, if looked closely, one might be able to see the sparkling shine in her eyes that showed child-like wonder.

Then, he smiled. "Definitely."

"The tooth fairy?"

"They exist." Basa answered.

"I see." she replied as she settled down. "Despite them being real, I never met them. I suppose Santa wouldn't give gifts to bad girls who kill people. Does the same go for the tooth fairy? I tried to put the teeth that got knocked out of me when I got disciplined under my pillow, but it didn't seem to work." she said curiously, one that seemed to wipe the smile on his face. "What about God? Other soldiers pray a lot, but they don't seem to be answered and they all still die during battle." she added.

Hearing that, Basa scratched his head for a moment before replying. "…As I said, if you don't fulfill the requirements, you can't really meet with them. It's all complicated." he gave her a grave look. "You being able to meet them is a recent development. But I believe that they would've wanted to do the same, given that they had a chance. It's just that the world prevented them from doing so."

She nodded at that, before turning silent in contemplation. The man stared for a short while, exhaled, and then stood up from his seat while putting down the files he held neatly on the table. Seeing him stand up, she also did the same.

"Sir?" she asked.

"No need for that. Just call me Basa." he interjected. "Say, you seem recovered now. Would you like to come with me and go outside?"

V felt a bit curious on what he plans to do, but in the end it was never her role to question. And so, she nodded.


The man apparently was able to travel throughout the entire country with ease. After stepping foot outside the lodge, he demonstrated his magic once more by teleporting the both of them aiming to arrive at the sparsely populated places throughout the warzones. She was also given a change of clothes, an old cloak to hide her face and injuries as well as to protect herself from the almost constant drizzle within the wartorn country, which the man also wore before they fully left.

They arrived at their destination after a flash and walked a bit before that. Usually, they would arrive in places near active firefights. Basa would bring out a notepad before writing something there, taking note of the events for something she wasn't privy of. And while he informed her that his magic made them unable to be spotted, seeing they were this close to the action she still tried to keep on guard.

However, at some point, the warzones they arrived in were fought not with soldiers, artillery or vehicles. The first thing that caught her attention when they teleported at such a place was the rhythmic shaking of earth like the roars of a flak gun battery shooting targets, or a piledriver being used for construction of fortifications. This was followed by intense explosions. She wondered at first if this was some new artillery she'd never heard before.

When they were able to reach a vantage point however, she bore witness to something she didn't expect.


Spoiler

Basa did say that these giant robots existed, and while he proved his word by showing that magic is also real and demonstrating it, hearing about it and seeing it in person are two different things. V blinked in surprise at the humongous warmachines - about three stories tall - that lay waste on the ruined city, fighting other similar robots like it. She recognized that those robots also wore the enemy's and her own country's coat of arms - leading more credence to what the man said regarding the situation of the war.

The robots moved with grace like normal humans, assisted by thrusters not out of place in jet fighters. They also seem to be strong enough to crush or break through ruins of entire buildings, and take hits from gunfire or shells from the sparse infantry or artillery support participating in the battle. Along with being outfitted with large weapons, they all make for destructive instruments of death.

Perhaps a normal person would react with wonder or fear at the sight of those machines. However, the woman can only tilt her head in confusion as she stared at those robots destroying their enemies and everything around them with advanced weaponry she'd never seen before.

"How did I miss this…?" she muttered.

"Don't bother with the specifics of how you missed it. It's very situational. Like I said earlier, this world has the tendency to make you avoid certain things if you don't meet the requirements." Basa said as he continued to take note of things, looking at the robots with a scrutinizing eye. "That doesn't apply to you now. You're one of the few exceptions."

She listened to him, digesting what he said. She then turned to him and stared at him in a considering manner.

"You said that we were linked yesterday. Are you one of the exceptions too?" she asked.

"Sharp of you." he praised. "Yes, I am. Along with a few others. I think you'll get along with them."

V nodded her head. She watched without much emotion on her face as the robots continued to fight, taking it just as another weapon to take note of and not much else. Still, she remained vigilant in case they were attacked by those machines as the man tried to accomplish whatever he was trying to do in these kinds of places.

…At some point however, they stopped visiting active warzones.

They would travel to other places. Locations where both sides of the conflict have no interest to be in, and where the refugees usually run off to. They passed people that tried to seek shelter in the ruined concrete buildings which looked as if it was about to collapse. Many eyed them warily as they passed by out of fear that they were soldiers but it was abated when they saw the old cloaks they wore, similar to the makeshift ones that the refugees also own.

V looked around. The man never specified which places they teleported in, but she followed him dutifully without any questions asked. Still, the place they arrived in was something she was familiar with, having taken part in a battle here once.

"Something matter?" Basa asked, noticing her lapse in attention.

"This is in enemy territory. Beyond the borders." she turned to look at the refugees. "And that must mean that these people are enemy citizens. Should they be eliminated?"

The man hummed. "Well, you're not part of the army anymore. As I keep saying, your orders are your own." he said, repeating the words earlier that made her uncertain. "What do you want to do? Should you eliminate them?"

She went quiet, staring at the people. Many were huddled together with their families in a makeshift fire to keep themselves warm from the constant cold drizzle that settled in the area. From what she could see, they were also gaunt and weak, likely from rationing their food or the lack of it. Nevertheless, they were in no shape to pose any sort of danger.

"…No." she answered simply.

"Is that so?" Basa commented, observing her quietly. Then, he started to approach the group of refugees. For a moment they seemed wary of his actions but he raised both of his hands before he started to speak, the words too soft for her to hear.

Then, he brought out the bulky bag he carried underneath his cloak, opened it, before distributing what looked like medicine, water and rations to the refugees. Seeing what he was doing, the others in the area also started to gather around him. She watched carefully as the refugees received it from Basa, but it looked as if they were too grateful to try anything untoward to him.

The number of people doesn't seem to be a concern either as he continued to produce supplies from his bag. It doesn't look like he'll run out of things to pull out from it, despite the bag looking ordinary. And the people don't seem to question it either. Was this another one of his magics?

Basa turned to look at her. "Would you like to help?"

V stared at the refugees, citizens of the country that she fought. They were dirty and covered with injuries, forcing themselves to move so that they could survive. It reminded her of herself on a particularly bad day on duty. The only difference however was the glimmer of light that shimmered in their eyes, due to the help of this man right in front of her.

After a bit of deliberation, she nodded and moved to assist him distribute the supplies.

Time passed like that as they simply traveled throughout the warzone, teleporting in places where refugees ranging from whole groups or a single person are located. The ones they helped weren't only from the enemy country but her own as well, although the difference between what they looked like seemed nonexistent. Strangely, Basa would also use his magic so that they would forget the encounter with him so that they wouldn't gather attention. She didn't oppose it, seeing it wasn't her role to question.


It eventually turned into sunset as the hours passed. They were helping a particularly large group of refugees, larger than the rest they had encountered for the past day. She was helping a small girl with her limited first aid by bandaging her wound - something that wasn't serious, just a wound she earned by tripping on some debris. It was a bit difficult to do with one hand, but she managed.

"Thank you, miss!" the girl said, giving her a bright smile when she gave her a ration bar to snack on after.

She nodded and the girl ran off to the other kids. It was with a detached expression as she watched she and the other kids, likely her friends, talk animatedly to one another. It was a great contrast to the quiet and solemn look on their faces when they encountered them earlier.

Seeing as she was done with her task, V turned around and went back to Basa. The man was finished giving off the supplies to the group and was giving directions on where they should go to reach the borders. She waited for a while for them to finish, and after being deeply thanked by the adults, he eventually walked to her.

"Done with yours already?" he asked.

"I finished treating the wounded. I've also distributed the supplies." she reported. She tried to add something as well, but hesitated and stopped herself.

He glanced at her. "Do you have something on your mind? You look like you want to ask something."

There was a pause. "…Why are you helping these people?" she eventually asked.

"Because I want to, and I can." he said with a shrug.

"Then why not simply teleport them to the borders? Why give them supplies so that they'll reach it themselves?" she said curiously. "It seems safer and faster that way."

"Lots of factors to that one. I can't simply bring people to their destination, especially this large number of people. You can say it messes up their futures, and it can affect other types of conflict in this place." he explained. "The best I could do is to ease their pain in their journey, so it won't be as difficult. Or at least, those that I can afford to help."

"You can see the future?" she asked, tilting her head.

"Yes. The people that we've helped can be helped. The others, I'd have to leave alone since their fate is intertwined with different events." he said with an exhale. "As I said, it's very complicated. And the sheer number of people affected in this war doesn't help as well. Helping them all is impossible, especially since similar situations never seem to run out because of this war."

She didn't quite understand, but it's likely because she just doesn't have the full picture. "If that is a problem, why not simply join the army so that the war would end? Your teleporting magic could help assassinate enemy officers and transport troops in great distances with ease. There should be no more refugees if that happens."

"A very martial mindset." he said with a deadpan look. "Putting aside the amount of death that'll still happen, it's not a matter of one side winning or not."

V gave him a curious look at his comment and the man sighed.

"Tell me, do you know why this war started? Why did you declare war on this country?"

"It's because they are our enemy. Monsters and demons that desecrate our country's soil." she replied automatically.

He raised a brow at her answer. "Do you really believe that?"

She glanced at the kids nearby, playing cheerfully with each other with smiles on their faces. The sight of it was alien to her, having never experienced something like a childhood due to her early drafting in the military, but even she knew that the description was false.

"No, I do not." she answered. She knew it wasn't true, but it was her duty to follow orders as a soldier. She never knew the reason for this war nor questioned it. "If that's not it, then what is the real reason?"

"There are many reasons for why this war started, but the main reason… You saw what happened earlier, with the giant robots." he stated, making her nod her head. "The truth is, this war was forced into a stalemate. No matter the advantage one side has, things will eventually return to where both are at the same strength so that it'll continue. This war that had gone on for decades already will stretch on until those responsible are done with it."

The man turned to her, looking her straight in the eye.

"This war serves as the testing ground for those advanced weaponry. An organization manipulated both countries so that they could test their work on active warzones." he revealed. "They're the root cause for all this, and the reason why the war will go on."

As she heard that, the woman's brows furrowed. Then, for the very first time ever since she woke up, her voice slightly wavered in a show of emotion: one filled with incredulity and disbelief, as if what she heard was ridiculous and she struggled to understand it all.

"An organization… used this war as a testing ground…?" she repeated.

"That's right."

"Isn't there a much better way to test it? Why cause a war? What is the point of it?" she asked in confusion.

"There's none. It's just a selfish and cruel choice on an antagonist's part because they don't explore other options, or likely, because this gives them the most profit. The high-ranking officials in both countries seem to be benefiting from this as well. Combine that with the long-standing hate of both sides…" he shook his head. "This shitty world really has it out for this place. And especially to you, a tragic nobody forced into this conflict, that would've died in said place."

As V listened to his explanation, a heavy feeling settled on her chest. She didn't know if Basa was telling the truth, but he had never given her a reason to not trust his words. But if what he was saying is true… she began to feel something that she never really felt for very long. A strange, complicated emotion that she had difficulty understanding, and something that she quashed to keep living. Perhaps she began feeling it because she was no longer part of the army, even if it was just a day or so.

How undisciplined of her. Yet before she could ignore it, Basa spoke.

"You think it's unfair, don't you?" he asked.

She glanced at the man, who simply gave her a steady stare. "It's fine to feel it. It must be difficult to understand, but it's not something you should run away from. You might've had to in the past, to cope with your circumstance… but you don't have to do that anymore." he told her factually. "You're free now. And as I said, you're responsible for what you want."

And so, the words he kept repeating for the past day were once more asked.

"Tell me. What do you want to do?"

Her mouth went dry. She still felt uncertain, but there was something stirring inside her that she didn't think she had, or rather refused to acknowledge: another desire besides wanting to live another day. She brought up a hand to her chest, struggling to understand what it even was.

She was a tool, and tools do not want things. They simply follow orders. She might speak, read, and write like a human, but in the end that is what she was. And that is how she was treated for all her life, until her supposed death.

And yet this person in front of her claimed otherwise.

"I… I want…"

She was free. All her orders are her own, and her life is now in her own hands. That was what he said.

So wishing something on her own like this was fine, right?

"…I want to end all of this."

Why was she even forced into this war? Why was she forced to participate in something like this? All that she'd experienced in her life - all of that was just because of something as ridiculous as testing and selling their weapons?

It was unacceptable.

Perhaps from realizing that - all the feelings, ones that are likely kept in her subconscious from constant repression, sprung out. Feelings that are so hard for her to articulate, but somehow managed to.

"…I want to hold them responsible."

All the pain, the unfairness that she lived through. Why was she treated this way and not them? Why did she have to suffer? Although she could never fully understand, she had an idea of what it means to have a normal life. Why was she denied such a privilege? Was there a difference between her and them?

Her only remaining hand shook, and she had to force herself to keep it steady. It took a great force of will to even say what she wanted, with all her life being denied of it just so that she could survive. It was difficult, but somehow, she managed.

She managed to voice out what she wanted to do the most.

"I… I want to make them pay!" she shouted.

—And so, the woman who had to live without feeling anything finally showed her full emotions for the very first time, telling her deepest desire to the world. The purest wish of someone who had suffered a life of tragedy, and who had experienced the unjustness of the world forthright.

And, in response to it, Basa spoke.

"I was hoping you'd say that." he said. "I'll help you, then."

The man put a hand on her shoulder, stabilizing her from her outburst as she breathed harshly. V stared at him with wide eyes as the man simply gave her a satisfied-looking smile that seemed so dazzling amidst her turbulent emotions.

"Let's make your revenge story, shall we?"

As he said that with a reassuring tone, a stray thought had appeared in her mind.

Perhaps her worries were smaller than she thought.

#2,473
A bit short, but the original plan for chapters in this fic is around ~5K words. So this chapter is perfectly average sized. Don't get caught up in the unrealistic standards set by the world! That's how they get you!

Anyhow, here's the beginning of V's revenge story and the shit that would get caught up in it.


Chapter 20

What does it mean to make a revenge story?

Consider a psychological perspective. Revenge can be understood as an emotional response when a person is felt wronged. One's self-esteem and identity is threatened in the face of injustice due to our innate sense of selfishness. Therefore, the act of taking revenge is seen as the path to restore it.

To take revenge is a means of reaffirming control and proving a sense of self-worth, and doing so will give feelings of satisfaction and relief.

"Hey, there's a woman approaching the camp. That blonde hair looks familiar… "

Although it is different from satisfaction brought upon the accomplishment of solving one's difficulties, it is still another way to activate the rewarding parts of the brain. Hence, it still carries a particular appeal. It can even be described as a unique taste as the satisfaction is muddled by unjust acts that couldn't be changed.

And the greater the injustice, the greater the satisfaction derived from it. But not many people would like to experience such an injustice themselves. So, they turn to stories. Fiction and fantasy where they could immerse themselves in another persona who would experience said events. At such a place, one could run wild and create the worst things a person could experience to feel the greatest high once revenge is achieved.

"W-Wait, she's armed—!"

And to live in a world such as this, where stories are reality, means that such experiences would become truths as well. Thankfully, a world that operates on stories would mean that revenge will be served. It is destined to happen according to the plot, after all.

Although not everyone has that privilege. Some people are unable to do anything about injustices directed to them and simply take it. They live and die, tragically, like the victims they are supposed to take role of - because there has to be someone like that in the world. Even fiction turning into reality cannot make the world into a utopia.

"Why are you losing against her!? Kill her! It's just one person!"

But, if there was a chance… if there was a single chance, that one such person who lived through a life like that would be given the opportunity to take revenge… What would happen?

It was a logical conclusion. As said earlier: the greater the injustice, the greater the satisfaction. And to those that had lived a life of tragedy, the satisfaction is immense. A chance for retribution is all it takes to create a truly cathartic revenge story for a tragic character.

And from there, a proper plot is formed.

"How…? She's not human…!

Thus, the world paved the way on its own towards a path of catharsis. A great momentum is given to the character, making them seem unstoppable. This is because to stop them is the antithesis of what it was trying to make, as lowering the satisfaction the story was supposed to invoke is unacceptable.

Just like that, the world ordained that revenge is fated to happen. There was only a simple division on such a story's characters: the revenge-seeker and the wrongdoers, with the wrongdoers themselves powerless in the face of their former victim.

What simply happens after is poetic justice.

"Monster!"

"No! S-Stay away!"

"Don't shoot—!"

"F-Forgive me…"

But I digress.

In the end, what does it mean to make a revenge story? There was only one answer, if put into context in this world.

It was a complete reversal of one's fate, and a simple case of people getting what they deserved.


Gloomy skies without the hint of daylight, and a near constant drizzle. The atmosphere felt suffocatingly tense as if all hints of hope were snuffed away. It was a scenery that invoked despair and helplessness, a perfect background provided by this world for the particular scenario.

The current location was a military encampment. The place had turned deathly quiet. Once, it was filled with sounds and shouting of soldiers fighting, only to be ended unceremoniously with the voices turning feeble and drowned out by the ambient sound of rain as they died.

The only thing interrupting the sound of the pitter-patter of rain was the panicked running of the remaining soldier - one who had cowered in the largest tent within the camp and hid behind all of his men during the fighting. He was the one who had the highest rank here, a Lieutenant Colonel, but that doesn't matter now that all his men were dead and he was the only one that remained.

What he was now is simply prey, desperately trying to escape from the one chasing him.

"—Gah!"

Unfortunately, he failed to do so. Perhaps by misfortune or simply his weakness, the lieutenant colonel tripped and fell on the ground. That simple mistake took away all chances of his escape. And even as he tried to desperately stand upright, it was too late.

There were sounds of wet footsteps behind him. Hearing that, the lieutenant colonel turned.

There he saw a blonde woman wearing a cloak approaching. He might've shot her by now, but his gun was already destroyed because the same woman shot it from afar earlier with her own firearm, leaving him no choice but to run away. Now, he couldn't even do that.

To him, the blonde woman was someone he recognized. Personally attended to, even. There was no doubt in his head he knew the reason why the woman was doing this. Yet despite all that, in his realization that this might be it, he desperately tried to appeal for his life.

"W-Wait, please, we can talk about this." he begged. "I know I've done a lot of wrong towards you, but please! Please forgive me!"

He was met with silence.

"It's not my fault! I had no way of controlling my men! I would've stopped them, but I had no choice! What was I supposed to do when I was suddenly given an orphaned girl in my unit!? There was nothing that I could do!"

Again, silence.

"I… I was just doing what I could do! All that I've done, I've done it all just to survive!" Perhaps sensing the inevitability of it all, he stopped begging and started to unleash his frustrations. The lieutenant colonel glared at the woman in a manic, hateful gaze. "I'm blameless in this! And you, you've been given food, drink and shelter - way more than an orphan could ever have! And in the end, this is what you do!? So what if we used you!? Something like that… something like that is…!"

The man was unable to finish his words, his mouth unable to articulate whatever he was feeling right now. However, it was unnecessary, as the footsteps finally stopped and he was left looking up at the woman who pointed a pistol at him.

There was not a single word said, not even a hint of acknowledgement. Because whatever the man said in front of her, no matter how he tried to spin his words or give reason for his actions - it didn't matter one bit.

This war, the situation the lieutenant colonel and the others following him found themselves in, muddled the lines of right and wrong. What mattered in their minds was simply selfishness for one's own desire for survival and everything else to keep themselves stable. Something which makes a man callous and commit monstrous acts without guilt.

It was that same selfishness the lieutenant colonel is facing right now. This wasn't an act of justice - it was a selfish act of revenge.

And it is that poetic mirroring that would cost his life.

The trigger is pulled, and the bullet is fired. Three shots in the abdomen, one going through the lung, the other aimed at his center going through the spine. The lieutenant colonel fell on the ground, groaning, and slowly dying a painful death.

V watched him impassively as the light slowly disappeared in his eyes. Then, after a long while, the man finally breathed his last.

And with his death, every soldier in the camp is gone.

There was a long silence that followed.

"…You finally dealt with the main unit you've been with."

V glanced back to where I was positioned to watch her kill the lieutenant colonel, wet from the rain like she was. She simply answered my question with a nod of her head. Observing her for a few moments, I then followed it by glancing at her new appendage.

"Was the arm fine?" I asked.

"It performed splendidly." she replied, flexing her new metal arm. Mechanical actuators moved in conjunction with magical components to make the movement fluid. V stared at her arm thoughtfully, before giving me a slightly unsure look. "…Is it really fine to have this?"

"It's fine. I'm pretty rich anyways." An understatement, considering the stuff I've hoarded my entire life. "I'm more surprised that you took this option instead of just regenerating the arm you lost."

She tilted her head at that. "This arm is stronger and could be outfitted with weapons. It is logical that this is superior to my normal arm. Why shouldn't I pick this one given the option?"

"...I guess that makes sense."

I suppose with her soldier mindset devoid of common sense it would be reasonable. And she wasn't wrong with its effectiveness either. With her new arm her marksmanship improved by eliminating the need to account for physiological tremors, and her strength had tremendously increased to the point where she can punch a person's head clean off their neck without effort.

To be honest this woman was already quite a monster in anything related to combat. Perhaps it was because of her upbringing or just her characterization, but she easily learned how to use her arm in killing people effectively. She even took to learning reinforcement magic like a fish to water after I unlocked her circuits. Perhaps her lack of sense of self contributed to that. Simply thinking oneself as a tool or weapon can go a long way in the setting that magic system comes from, after all.

Anyways, combine all that to the meta-narrative weight of being a protagonist of a revenge plot and, well… the results are clear from the camp we were in, and the others before. It's full of dead bodies now.

Although, we weren't quite finished with our business here just yet. There were still others that remained alive in the camp. The blonde looked at the direction of the place where the remaining living people were, before turning to me.

"Should we go?" she asked curiously.

"I'll let you deal with that." I answered.

Hearing that, the blonde nodded before approaching the place. It was a simple roughshod shed constructed from wood that looked like it'll fall apart from the slightest breeze. It certainly wasn't something you'd trust to shelter in when under enemy fire, but that wasn't its purpose. All it needed was to keep things in.

As V neared the door and pulled the handle - halfway from opening the door, a small figure suddenly sprang out and jumped towards the blonde. The ambush didn't take her by surprise and she was vigilant enough to react accordingly. She avoided the attack before grabbing their arm with her metallic own, before twisting them into a hold.

The child cried out in pain and surprise. His weapon, just a pointy rock, clattered on the ground as his hand reflexively let go of it. It was then that the door to the shed fully opened and revealed what was inside.

Women and children dressed in rags were within the shed. They looked helplessly at V's appearance, but seemed ready to fight in case they needed it despite the resignation present in their eyes, knowing that they have little chance of winning. A fact reinforced judging by their states; they looked barely fed or taken care of despite the soldiers earlier looking relatively fine in comparison.

It was easy to tell what they are, especially when you have an idea of the camp's situation. These women and children were hostages from the villages they raided. They were used as ransom by these soldiers who found themselves deep into enemy territory in order to get supplies.

People do desperate things for their own survival. Some of these soldiers killed could possibly be good people and just accosted into doing things because they have no choice. But even though things are morally gray instead of black and white, these sorts of things tend to lean on one side rather than the other. Especially in a world like this where everything has to have purpose for the sake of story.

And with how my senses registered the traces of substances that clung in the pitiful rags given to the women as clothing, and how there were some small corpses on a dark corner of the shed that were likely not caused by hunger or sickness, gave me an idea on which way these soldiers leaned in.

The hostages stiffened when V grabbed the child into a hold after the failed ambush attempt and hesitated at what to do. That hesitation however quickly turned into confusion when she suddenly let go of the child, who quickly scurried back with the others.

The blonde straightened to look at the hostages. Her blank eyes seemed to mirror theirs, despite the contrast of their appearances. It was ironic given that objectively, the blonde likely suffered more than they did no matter how terrible what had happened here.

Then, she spoke, addressing them all.

"You're all free now." V announced. "You can raid this base's supplies and weapons, if you wish. That should be enough for you to get to your homes."

After saying those words the blonde then turned around and left. Despite what she said, the women and children inside are undoubtedly afraid and doubtful of her, watching V with cautious eyes. They would likely only try to heed her words once we've fully left. And unlike the refugees we've helped from the past few days, there likely wasn't a single word of gratitude that would be given to her.

But the blonde didn't care a single thing about that. This whole operation was made for her own satisfaction after all. Instead she approached me after leaving those hostages alone and, much to my confusion, gave me an expectant look.

"…You did good." I said, after a while of her doing that.

She nodded silently. The expression on her face didn't change a single bit, but I didn't miss the subtle way her eyes brightened.

I sighed. The reasons for her wanting my approval of all things elude me, especially with her messed-up thinking that's likely far from common sense due to her upbringing. And while I can read her mind, I'd like to think that I respect people's privacy where it matters.

And so, leaving it alone, I went ahead and readied to cast a spell. I already added the supplies these hostages would need along with a few luck-bending cantrips which would ensure a safer journey for them once they decided to snoop around and take things from the camp. At this point, things were just about done here.

"Shall we head back, then?" I prompted.

"Yes." the blonde said, stepping right beside me a bit closely. "We shall."


The small cabin in the remote parts of these woods, far away from the active warzones, had become something of a base for us. It's a place where we would return every time we would complete an operation so that the blonde could grow ever closer to her desires, as she had emotionally divulged not too long ago.

Of course, now that we were taking a more active approach, I took the liberty of changing the place to fit our purposes. I originally made it more homely to not alert the blonde when she woke up from her injuries but that's not relevant anymore.

And so, what used to be the dining table was now a table where I put a map of the two countries. Furthermore, it was enchanted to display the state of the troops in real time, making it look like a holographic display. The data I gathered when I was out with V checking out each battlefield helped a lot in making this, along with other things.

The both of us removed our wet cloaks in favor of more comfortable clothing. I was wearing a shirt, while V wore a simple tank top. She was tinkering with her guns, cleaning them after the earlier battle and preparing for the upcoming operation. Meanwhile, I did something else.

I was observing the situation on the map closely. A lot of units in it disappeared, being a target of V's revenge, but this last one would definitely catch attention.

"The lieutenant colonel's unit was feeding information on the movements of their enemies. They're deep in enemy territory, staging guerilla warfare and sowing chaos as much as they can." A notable feat, considering you usually do that in your own territory. The fact that they survived this long is impressive, even if their ways of doing so are heartless. "Their disappearance would definitely warrant attention. And although they weren't as involved, the other units we got rid of might also influence how this war would go… This should be monitored closely."

V tilted her head curiously as she listened to my words. "Why? Is there something to be cautious about?"

I hummed. "Maybe, maybe not. It could just be my paranoia."

While I have encountered plenty of settings and involved myself quite a lot as well, it was always usually small-scale. A conversation here, a monster killed there… It's usually a single event I involve myself in, because that's generally what I only need to affect the whole. I always approach my actions with caution since recklessly involving myself might mess things up and, in the worst case, might cause a world-affecting scenario and bring an end to the current 21st century setting.

But this time… Well, this was a special case. I promised to fulfill the wishes of Miss emotionless blonde here, so it comes first before any possible consequence that might arise. Oh well, I suppose that just means more workload for me. Not the worst problem I've dealt with.

The blonde nodded at my words. "It is always good to be vigilant - being paranoid is a trait of an effective soldier. I always try to be alert at all times in case of an ambush myself. Any surprises will be quickly dealt with."

…With that attitude, I just have this feeling that introducing her to a peaceful setting will go swimmingly well. It really was the right choice to not transport her to my apartment when I saved her. "I see. Anyway, I'm just slightly worried that our actions might affect things in the plot of other settings. You remember how we're exceptions to the rules that divide the world, right? That's what I'm concerned about."

There was a slight pause, before V's eyes brightened as she understood. "Ohh, I see." she said with her tone the slightest bit higher than her usual flat one. "You must think those soldiers that we killed could have a role in some story?"

I smiled at her assessment. "That's right. There's a chance a person there has a significant role and could affect the plot they were in. Although that might also change now, considering they're dead. It could turn the plot for the worse but… considering they're bad people, it likely didn't change much. And they all became the characters in your revenge story, so the world must've at least changed to account for their deaths."

"And the people we've rescued too. It could affect the stories as well." the blonde added. "That means the tragic stories where loved ones die won't happen, correct?"

"Yeah, that too." I agreed with a nod.

She was following along well. As seen by her display of knowledge, I had started to explain to her how the world works piece by piece. It was clearly challenging because of her upbringing, having no knowledge of any fictional stories aside from the most common children ones, much less those stories filled with anime tropes that are nonsensical without context, but nevertheless I did my best. And judging by how she followed my thoughts, I think I did a decent job.

How did I do it, one might ask?

V's lips curved ever-so-slightly upward indicating she was pleased at my compliment and being proven right. Then, she gave me a look that showed an excited gleam in her eyes.

"Will you tell me more of your stories that you encountered? They are very interesting."

—Of course, the explanations involved telling her some of the plots I've encountered to give her an idea of the tropes in this world, along with what sort of life people lived in outside of the constant war. It was something that she never had herself and she was understandably fascinated by it. I would've found it cute if it wasn't so sad as well.

And normally, I would have entertained her request seeing her excitement, but as of now…

I shook my head. "Sorry, maybe next time. We might not have the time for it." the blonde's expression turned blank at that. She nodded obediently, but I didn't need to see emotions on her face to know that she was disappointed. "I'll make it up for you later. But for now, I think you'd be more interested in having this."

I took out the small decorated box from my pocket before extending it to her. The blank expression on the woman's face was wiped away in favor of a curious look.

"What is it?" she asked, taking it. Then, she read the fine cursive label on the decorated box. "'A gift to Miss V, from Rias'..." she muttered. "This is one of the people who turned meta like us, correct?"

"Yeah, she is. Rias and the others have been wanting to meet you, but couldn't because of other circumstances." That, and they also seem to understand that dealing with V's situation requires… finesse, so to speak. And they all agreed to dump that responsibility to me. "As for what's inside, I don't know. I didn't check."

She nodded silently before slowly opening the box. Then, when the contents were revealed, the blonde blinked.

It was a red-colored ribbon. Simple in design, yet the material is clearly made of fine silk and linen that belied how valuable it must've cost to make. There was also a note inside where a personalized message from Rias was written. I definitely recognize it from her handwriting.

'This definitely goes great with your hair! Try it on!'

The blonde took one look at the note, then at the ribbon. There was a strange look on her face. I've become quite familiar with her mannerisms as of late and I recognized this one: it was the look where she couldn't quite understand what to feel, emotionally repressed as she was.

"This is…" she muttered.

"Why don't you put it on like she said?" I prompted her.

She looked uncertain, but nodded in the end. V took the ribbon from the box and, after a slight hesitation on what to do, decided to tie her hair in a simple ponytail. When she finished and brought her hands down, I was left with a pretty sight.


Spoiler

Looks like Rias was spot on with her pick.

"It suits you." I said sincerely.

The blonde squirmed as I said that, the same uncertain expression appearing in her face. "T-Thank you." she said, stuttering slightly and displaying more emotion for the first time in a while. Then, she gave me a concerned look. "Is it fine for me to have this…" she paused, as if trying to place an unfamiliar word. "Gift?"

I gave her a smile. "Why shouldn't it? It's a gift."

"I see." she muttered, her hand touching the ribbon on her hair as she said so. "Then… Please extend my thanks to Miss Rias. It is beautiful."

"I will. She'll definitely be happy to hear that you liked it." I said as the blonde continued to marvel at the simple ribbon. "Moving on, I think it's time to discuss the next steps of our plan. It'll take a while though, so we can discuss it while we're having a late lunch."

With a wave of my hand, I took something out from my subspace and placed it on the table. It was a largely packed bento, fresh and hot as if it was just placed there after being cooked. The blonde's eyes locked to it immediately.

"Aoki cooked these ones like usual, but Yuki helped out as well." I explained. The latter helped because she also wanted to contribute, but thought that sending two gifts was a bit much like the considerate drama character that she was. "They said these should be extra delicious. Apparently they tried to use techniques in some of the cooking-related stories out there."

And the statement is likely true, considering the divine smell it exuded. I've had the honor of tasting meals made from those cooking stories and they're always incredibly delicious. The thought of tasting it once again is definitely tempting.

Clearly, V also thought the same. She took her utensils and quickly began eating, stuffing her face in great speed that definitely would be a standard from now on. Not like I judged her - I was pretty much the same.

The hearty meal was enjoyed, and it was great to see the life that was injected into this emotionless blonde, even if it was little by little.

…And along with it, we started the preparations that we needed to do.

It was about time to make the major moves after all.


…A few hours after, once the sun disappeared and gave way into night, a certain military gala was being held within the country's capital.

Much like any other gatherings held by those in power, it was luxurious to showcase the great station of those attending. The prepared feast, the decorations, and the servants within the venue - it all showed that a vast amount of fortune was spent, contrasting heavily to the poor state of the nation beyond.

Or, in a very likely manner, it simply showed where the money was really being spent: Into the pockets of political parasites that the country calls its government. With the people themselves being left rotten and destitute, surviving from the scraps of the elite.

Various people attended the event. Everywhere one looked, one could see men and women wearing suits or gowns. There was an occasional military uniform showing an officer with a high background, their vests decorated with badges of honor that likely served no purpose or something they didn't really deserve.

All the people here were clearly politicians. This made the gala itself the most deplorable place in the country.

And the young man forced to come here couldn't feel more out of place.


Spoiler

He was asked to wear a high-quality three-piece ensemble instead of his usual bodysuit, one that he wore whenever he was asked to fight in his armored mech. His purpose here wasn't to complete some operation and fight in the war. Instead, he was here as a display meant to be lauded and paraded, so that those he worked under would achieve their own ends.

The head researcher came here to emphasize the contributions the armored mechs had given to the war. Showing off a pilot of said mechs is an effective way to do so. As the squad leader, he was dumped with the dubious honor to be the person attending. While he didn't like it, it wasn't like he would refuse and potentially make someone else in his unit come here instead. And it's not like he could refuse orders anyway.

Right now he was alone since his role as a conversation starter finished, and now he was asked to mill about while the head researcher and his tagalongs conversed with the military general and other higher officers. He was clearly catching the eyes of the guests around, but no one would strike a conversation with him. They simply looked at him in slight interest before going on their way, concerned more in pursuing their own ends to further their hedonistic lives.

After all, he was simply a soldier among the presence of elites. A peasant like him wasn't worth talking to.

The young man clenched his teeth in distaste and resignation. He did his best to reign in his anger, trying not to glare at those around him. He knew that eyes were all around him, but despite that it took a titanic effort to do so.

These were people he and other pilots were fighting and even died for. People who don't care less, who wouldn't even bat an eye if they bled or were killed. These were people who reaped the benefits of the war others were fighting, parasites that enjoy a lavish life while others suffered for them. Yet despite all that, they carried the attitude as if they were superior.

It was disgusting, sickening even.

And he knew that he couldn't do a single thing about it.

…He was clearly getting carried away. These were treasonous thoughts.

The young man exhaled to center himself and he continued to simply roam around just so that he wouldn't appear like some abandoned child in the corner. At least this way, he could avoid getting involved further in the head researcher's conversations if he distanced himself. And since others wouldn't converse with him, then it's all the better.

There was no point in harboring such things when he knew that it wouldn't mean anything in the end. Resignation was a familiar feeling, but at least it meant that he was still alive. All that mattered was to live for another day and hope that maybe, maybe things would be better after… even though the hope grows dimmer and dimmer, each passing day.

As he roamed around, he tried to think of other matters to get things off his mind. As he did so however, he stumbled upon a strange sight.

There was a guest seated on a table alone. It was a man around his own age or maybe older, one with passing similarity to him in skin tone but differed on their blonde hair as opposed to his own white. He was drinking a glass of wine serenely, even as other guests seemed to avoid him.

The young man frowned as he looked closely. That person was a foreigner, and that perhaps was enough of a reason why those politicians would avoid him, but he didn't know what he was and why he would be attending this gala. He was the only young person to attend this place, or at least that was what he thought.

Who was he? Another pilot like him? He didn't recognize this person from others that he'd worked with, and he certainly wasn't in his unit. Or maybe it was different. He could just be a representative from an organization in another country. He was sure the head researcher collaborated with other corporations from time to time.

…In the end though, it wasn't his business. So, after what simply appeared to be a passing glance from the outside, he walked past the man like the others around him.

"You look quite angry."

But then the man spoke something that made him stop in his tracks. He carefully looked at the man, who didn't even turn in his direction and simply kept swirling the wine glass in his hand. There was no doubt however that he was the person being addressed.

"Pardon, sir?" he asked politely. "Are you referring to me?"

"Who else could I be referring to? The others here are too absorbed living a life of luxury." he answered. "I suppose it's understandable for you to be angry. You and others with you are fighting in the frontlines, while the rest of these people are just partying. Worse still, these are the sort of people dictating the course of the war. Finding it unacceptable is an understatement."

His heart stopped when those statements were said so brazenly out in the open. Who was he to say that without worry? Thankfully the other guests didn't seem to hear, judging how they were still being ignored. Otherwise, they would've definitely homed in on them—interacting with a peasant, foreigner, or no.

"…I do not know what you are talking about." he said, trying to hide his panic.

The man let out a smile as if amused by his attempt of acting clueless. "There's no need to worry about that. Nobody would deign to listen to us." he reassured.

"I see." he muttered, looking at the man with caution. Whoever this person is, it's someone that he'd rather not be caught associating with. "I apologize, but I'm a bit busy." he said with a fake apologetic voice. "I'd like to excuse myself if you wouldn't mind—"

"Are you satisfied with the way things are, Orga? Is this the life you envisioned with your sworn brother?"

With a flinch, Orga fully turned to face the man with wide-eyes. "What? How…?"

The blonde foreigner remained calmly seated like he always was, as if he hadn't just said something he shouldn't have known. Orga's evaluation of him steadily grew more and more dangerous by the second as his mind raced, trying to settle on possible explanations on how he knew such things, and he watched him cautiously when the man brought down the wine glass on the table.

"Have I finally caught your attention?" he asked rhetorically.

Orga narrowed his eyes at him. "…Who are you?"

He shook his head at that. "My name isn't important. " he simply answered. "You wouldn't know me even if I told you anyway."

Then, after wiping his hands with a napkin and putting that down on the table as well, he stood up from his seat. It was then that he realized that this man was taller than him and powerfully built too. Orga tensed, watching him in case of any sudden movements.

"What matters is the role I play here." the man continued.

Orga's brows furrowed. "And what is that supposed to be?"

The man shrugged, before looking at his direction - Or rather, somewhere behind him. He might've wondered what this person was looking at, but the next thing that came out of his mouth stopped him from doing so.

"Just someone assisting a person that wants to end a war."

It took a moment for Orga to even register what he said. His eyes widened, but before he could even react to it, the sudden sound of glass shattering made him reflexively turn around - right in the direction the man was looking at from behind him.

And there he saw the head researcher falling to the floor, along with his other colleagues and the military officers he was conversing with. There was a shocked silence within the gala as everyone turned the fallen bodies, already pooling blood from the sudden holes that appeared on their heads.

Then the panic started.

"A-Assassin!"

"Someone was shot!"

"E-Evacuate! Evacuate now!"

Orga couldn't believe his eyes. As the gala quickly turned into chaos, he could only stare in shock at the sight of the head researcher along with the other high military officers being dead. It was an incongruous sight that he didn't even think was possible.

All those powerful people that he had considered untouchable all his life… they're just gone, their lives snuffed in an instant. Not even a trace of their absolute power was found in their hollow-eyed corpses, mortality stripping them of any self-imposed importance.

—And there was one person here that was undoubtedly involved in this.

He quickly turned back around to the mysterious man and realized that he was nowhere to be found. Orga tried to look for him, swivelling his head across the place, and he spotted a glimpse of the man's blonde hair amidst the crowd before he disappeared in the chaos as he walked away.

With clenched teeth, Orga quickly tried to find a way to catch up. He looked around trying to find a fast route where he wouldn't be swallowed by the panicking crowd... but something else caught his attention instead. One that, for some reason, his instincts honed into.

On the table where the man sat was a napkin he put down earlier. But observing it closely clearly showed that it wasn't just a simple napkin he used to clean himself with. The stains, or what looked like it, were too orderly and arranged.

He approached the table and picked it up. There weren't any stains on the napkin. It was writing.

And written there were precise coordinates and a time.

"Pilot Orga! What the hell are you doing!?" A voice suddenly interrupted his thoughts. It was the security with the now-deceased head researcher, giving him a glare even as he kept a cautious eye on his surroundings. "Hurry up and leave immediately!" he shouted.

In a swift movement that would've been missed by the security guard, he pocketed the napkin. Then, internally resolving himself to memorize the contents before destroying it as fast as possible, he gave a nod to the guard.

"Yes, sir." he said obediently.

With that, Orga left the premises, his mind in great turmoil as he did so. Even now, he tried to make sense of what happened. From what that strange man had said about stopping the war to the sudden death of the head researcher, it all just seemed to breed more questions instead of answers the more that he thought about it.

There was one thing that he was sure of, though.

From this point on… things are never going to be the same.
