Chapter 21

Far from the chaos of war between certain two countries, in the open seas of their territories, an unassuming freighter that operated within the contested waters and cruised under a starless night sky.

It was a rust bucket of a cargo ship that looked poorly maintained that it was only useful in being scrapped, yet for some insane reasoning it was still judged as seaworthy. In its rusted deck where a single cut might lead to tetanus, armed guards patrolled to and fro, taking watch for potential pirates or other ships. It was clear, however, from their unkempt appearances and lack of discipline that they were being awfully casual about the whole thing.

None of the two countries locked in war would let a single ship in their navy operate this way. It was because these people aren't proper soldiers. Nor part of their army at all.

They were smugglers; criminals making use of the war to further their own ends.

"…Hey, look at this. Apparently the general of the country we were just in got assassinated. Said that an assassin got into their capital and killed 'em."

And further in the cargo ship, inside one of the many small cabins, a man who sat down reading a newspaper began to talk to his colleague as they rested after their own shift. His colleague, who was taking a smoke break, glanced at him before puffing his cigarette with a bored expression.

"Yeah, so?" he replied. "Couldn't care less."

"Course you'd think that. If you don't know, this sort of shit changes the war. And not in a good way either. I should know - I used to work with terrorists." the man with the newspaper said. "Things are gonna be chaotic to say the least."

"Again, how does that matter? More business for us."

"Say that again when they start adding more ships here at sea. We were lucky that security is pretty much nonexistent here and we can go in and out without trouble. Now, that might just change since things might get heated." the man replied with a shake of his head. "I just know our bosses are probably sweating buckets at this."

There was a pause from his colleague, before he spoke once more. "…There's probably no need. Heard that we're set to go back. The ship's full now, apparently."

The man looked at him in surprise. "Huh? We are?"

A shrug. "You saw those heavy equipment earlier, didn't you? Apparently some haul was found last minute. Said they were pretty important too." he answered. "Pretty hefty though. Heard the bosses got angry when they had to leave some wares 'cause the ship got too heavy."

"What wares? Don't tell me…"

"Just the ones that don't pay as much." his colleague reassured. "Things that get taxed high, stuff like that. Didn't touch the drug stash and the weapons…" he smiled. "And of course, none of our 'rescuees' either."

The man let out a laugh at the last part. It was a horrible sound, one that betrayed sadistic amusement. "Some of them still believe that, you know? What a joke. They'd be in for a surprise when they finally realize we're selling them off."

His colleague cracked a smirk, letting out another puff of smoke as he did so.

"You'd think they'd be suspicious when we're offering a ride for free, but I guess this war made them desperate to just get out of here. Even if it meant being trafficked out." he commented. "Think the situation is sinking in for them at this point, though. You can see it in their faces."

"Really? Guess that's why the girl I was doing earlier was glaring at me the whole time."

His colleague looked at him with an amused expression. "What was that? You know that you can't dirty those products right? Those women are probably going to get sent to be married by some rich guy or something. We can't sell used goods."

"Hahaha, as if you all don't do the same. This batch had some real pretty ladies in it. Very different from the usual people that we get."

"Can't deny that. They're a pretty lively bunch though." his colleague said with a gravelly chuckle. "You know just the other day, some kid cursed me? Said something about some grim reaper coming to kill us all. Really believed it too. Laughed at the kid's face so much when I fucked her sister in front of her."

The man paused after hearing that. "Hm? Now that you mentioned it, I think I heard something similar too… What a superstitious lot. Wonder where they got that from?"

"You know how backwater these countries can get. It's probably some legend in their village or something."

"Probably." the man replied, going back to reading his newspaper again. "Or probably not. You know, I heard some legends pop up in my time fighting in a war myself. Mostly strange things… This sounds like one of them."

"Yeah, yeah. Can't stop bragging about fighting in a war, huh? All the boys on the ship know that already."

"Shut up, will ya? As I was saying, that sounds like one of those kinds of legends. Some have some truth in them, but most are just bullshit people make up to cope with things. They probably heard it in passing from soldiers or something."

"You're seriously getting worried about that?"

The man shrugged. "Hey, being paranoid saved my life more times than I can count. Still, maybe I'd worry about it if I was fighting out there but… well, we're in the middle of the damn ocean."

He chuckled, the sound accompanying the rustle of him turning a page from the newspaper.

"I'd love to see the grim reaper swim to get here on this ship. So even if it's somehow true that they exist, there's no way they'd get here." he commented with mirth. "Not that I really believe what they're saying is true, though. You get me?"

"…"

The man frowned at the sudden silence. Expecting to see a judgemental expression on his colleague's face from what he said, the man looked away from his newspaper and turned around.

"Hey, what's with the—"

However, anything he might've spoken remained unsaid as his voice faltered, dying midway. The man's eyes widened when he saw a sight that he didn't expect, but no less made his hair stand on its end.

His colleague, living and breathing just a few seconds prior, was now on the ground bleeding from his neck. He slumped down on the wall with a hand on his neck, choking uselessly and decorated it with his blood, with confusion, pain, and panic in his eyes as he was suddenly met with his impending death.

And standing right in front of him was something unknown.

The man could barely even comprehend what he was looking at. His eyes seemed to slide off when he looked as if his body knew that he shouldn't be staring at it. Yet, in the mere flash where he managed to even perceive its form, the man recognized what looked like a cloaked figure. A figure that was looking in his direction, facing him with a face of jet-black darkness underneath the hood of its cloak.

The man couldn't understand what it was. It was beyond what he could do. But, the one thing that he knew was that his death was coming - and with that realization, he knew what the identity of this thing in front of him was.

It was the Grim Reaper.

Before the man could even scream in terror, before he could call for help, or even regret his earlier words of doubt - he barely perceived the being of death reaching out to him, grabbing him in a blink of an eye.

Then, after the pure agony of his neck being slashed open and drowning in his own blood…

The man died.



I followed after the emotionless blonde, teleporting in the room just as she had finished disposing of the two men inside. V expertly used her knife to slash their necks, spilling blood on the floor and walls. It's all quite messy but at least they died gurgling in their own blood unable to scream and alert the others around.

Those two were marked for death, and the world seems to have acknowledged it considering the flag one of them raised before we arrived. I haven't removed the memories of those who witnessed V's bloodbath (or more specifically, those she wasn't targeting and saved in the process) seeing that the genre divide will sort it on its own. Her actions also definitely altered the tragic plots out there and letting V remain in their memories could potentially change the direction of their stories overall. But considering the nature of tragic plots, changing it is better than letting the original plot happen at all.

Anyhow I judged it was more beneficial to just let it go. Predictably, it looks like it turned into something of a legend. If there was one thing that proliferated during war times, it was that.

But to call her 'Grim Reaper', huh…? I suppose it fits. This woman has been leaving dead bodies everywhere she went after all. And the cloak certainly gives off an impression.

"Area clear. Let's proceed to the next one."

The emotionless blonde softly muttered those words, moving towards the door of the cabin with a calm expression on her face. I quietly trailed after her as we exited the room and went further into the cargo ship's hull.

The goal was to quickly neutralize all the armed criminals in this ship as quickly as possible and capture the ship. Using the information obtained from spying the place with some animal familiars, we can utilize my teleportation abilities so we could enter from the hull with a presence concealment spell to avoid the detection of those in watch. Then we would move on to eliminate them all before they even manage to realize there are enemies boarding them.

V contributed quite a lot in forming that plan, just as she had in the past when dealing with her transgressors. I keep being surprised by this woman really - her potential really was stifled by being a tragic character. She may be limited when it comes to being human, but she's undeniably a good soldier with a knack for strategy and a lifetime of experience in warfare.

Anyway, how she went about this operation is certainly a contrast to my usual brute-force approach… which just usually involved my vast amount of out-of-context abilities that the current genre or setting couldn't deal with. I mean, I might be able to create a bounded field or something that will make the enemies kill themselves for us, but I'd rather not spend time, effort, or resources for something like that. While doing that is faster, I can't deny it's much smoother done this way.

And so, as we silently and quickly traversed the halls, we stumbled upon a group of armed guards loitering about. From our presence concealment they couldn't even spot us, and V unholstered her pistol with her metallic arm and began to shoot.

The gun didn't even make a peep even when it fired. A truly silent gun, modified by yours truly, along with a few other things to make it deadly. The bullet hit one of the guard's head and the man died instantly, his brains spilling on the wall beside him.

"Wha—!?"

The others with the now-dead man reacted in shock. They weren't able to respond to it however as more bullets followed and killed them as well. V brought the gun down but didn't holster back her weapon, and we kept moving.

The next group was similarly killed, dying with a bullet to the head. So did the next one. But by the third encounter, we encountered a particularly large group and a few dove off for cover before V could shoot them, meaning that I had to move and assist.

"Shit, shit! Call for help!"

In a great burst of speed I dashed to where they were. I turned my presence concealment off to take them by surprise. It was effective, and they all looked at me with wide eyes since from their perspective, it looked like I appeared behind their cover out of nowhere.

I grabbed the arm of the one reaching for the transceiver on his waist and kneed him on the stomach, my reinforced limbs hurting his mundane body quite easily, and he fell down in pain clutching his abdomen with a pained groan. Then I followed it by punching the remaining two men right in their jaws in a single fluid movement. Their eyes rolled up and they flopped to the ground bonelessly.

Seeing that, V didn't hesitate and followed it by shooting them in their heads when she neared. Brutal, but mercy was only given to those that deserve it. And these people are textbook one-dimensional villains from what I've been seeing.

Anyway, they're dead before one of them managed to call for help… not that it mattered really. I brought a jammer with us, so they couldn't alert others even if they managed to use the transceiver.

We moved once more. Eventually we eliminated quite a lot of the men posted inside the hull and those patrolling up on the ship's deck as well. Then, we got rid of those up on the ship's bridge. I stopped the ship on its course with the controls, letting it drift aimlessly at sea instead.

Perhaps those remaining might have noticed the ship suddenly stopping along with the lack of usual communication, but it had only been a few minutes. By the time they fully notice that there was something strange going on for them, we're already onto them.

There was only one place left to take care of anyway.

"…Looks like we'd have to be careful here."

The last location was a place where a lot of people were concentrated considering its purpose. It was the storage area where plenty of guards were on standby, keeping an eye out on their wares. It made sense for them to be cautious when protecting their sold products. We observed them up on a catwalk on an upper deck overseeing the whole area, and jumping down can get us there.

I eyed one of the many particular cargo containers that caught my attention. On the outside, it didn't look that much different from the others. But if one were to notice the way the guards took watch of them and have an actual look inside, then it's easy to realize what it was.

They were trafficking people. And from what I could see, they're likely refugees too. Not that it surprised us at all anyway - we had an idea of what the ship was carrying before boarding and the two men we killed earlier had just confirmed it. Still, it would be bad if they got hurt in the crossfire or get used as hostages, or something along those lines.

V nodded at my statement, looking over the guards with a critical eye. I can tell she was planning the way she engaged them in a way that ensures utmost efficiency.

"They'd have to be eliminated quickly." she quietly said, coming to the same conclusion as I did. "I will need to draw their fire as well. Otherwise I would risk those people in the containers."

Hearing her unspoken request, I grabbed her shoulder and lifted the presence concealment spell I casted on her. "There. You should be noticeable again." I told her, before giving her a light smile. "Go get them, soldier."

She gave me a thankful nod before reinforcing her limbs and jumping into the fray. The blonde landed in the middle of the entire storage area with a heavy thud, making every head turn to her direction no matter what they were doing. Their eyes widened in disbelief at the sight of a cloaked figure coming out of nowhere.

One of the men nearest to her stood up from his seat. "Who in the hell—?"

His brains were blown out of his head before he could finish his sentence. The others, seeing this, reacted quickly and brought up their guns to aim at her.

Before their fingers even managed to pull the trigger she darted into the cover of one of the containers. It was one that stored drugs from what I could see, not where those trafficked refugees are. In fact, she moved to make their guns aim away from those containers as much as possible.

The amount of guns aimed at her didn't pin her down. In fact, she used it to her advantage. She jumped into one particular group of gunners much to their surprise, and the normally insane action contributed to others around them hesitating to continue spraying their bullets since they could potentially shoot their allies.

The woman quickly dispatched the group. Grabbing the arm of one man that stopped him from shooting, she then twisted around him and fired her pistol in quick succession to kill the other two around her. Then, in a single fluid movement, the hold she locked the man in transitioned into a throw - her mechanical arm and reinforced body giving her enough strength to do so.

The men around watched in horror as the man flew in the air screaming - before it was gruesomely cut short when he struck the wall, splattering on it bloodily before slowly sliding down on the ground. He didn't get back up.

"M-Monster!" one man shouted before getting jumped on by V, who lifted him on the neck with her mechanical arm as well. The man struggled desperately but died when the woman used him as a shield from bullets coming on her way.

She dropped him on the ground lifeless. Then, she moved on to the others.

"Damn it! Who is that!? What is that!?"

"Call for backup! Alert the others!"

"N-Nobody's answering!"

"What do you mean nobody's—! Wait, no! S-Stay away!"

"God, help us…!"

And so, the soldier went about her rampage. Her enemy's pleas went unheard as she reaped their lives, in accord to her newfound title. But no matter what they tried to do they were helpless to it all.

It was like watching an action movie, except that there were no stakes involved at all. It was the consequence of mixing unrealistic action abilities to a normally realistic setting; an absolute curbstomp where no one can even hope to defeat the character, and the enemies are absolutely decimated with intense gore to match.

It was fascinating in the way one couldn't look away from a car crash. It took one's attention, giving them a clear reminder of mortality. It was so very different from shounen which, despite the copious amount of blood that comes out in fights, almost seems kid-friendly in comparison to the viscerality I was witnessing now.

…Still, there was a time for reflecting about such things. Now would not be one of them.

I could see the flow of the fight, even if just a few seconds had passed when the V started. While the guards were getting killed left and right there were still quite many around. As said by the blonde earlier, we needed to deal with these guys quickly. While she may have drawn their fire, the longer the engagement the greater the risk of those trafficked refugees being hurt.

"Looks like I need to assist again." I muttered in thought before reaching in my subspace.

I think I have the appropriate tool for the situation considering the amount of firearms present. My hand grasped a familiar weapon, bringing it out for the first time in a while.

It was a simple pistol.

The handgun used to be a Colt 1911 model that I snatched from somebody long ago, but with the modifications I added to it the firearm was more definitely than that now. Carrying it in my grip gave me a nostalgic feeling, like remembering a lost part of myself. Or maybe I was just being dramatic.

Guns are something that I utilized quite a lot in my early days when I didn't have the vast amount of abilities that I have now. I usually forgo these weapons and use magic instead. Mostly because it's more convenient. Still, they find their use from time to time.

Kind of like right now.

I outstretched my arm, aiming the gun with a steady hand. However, I wasn't really aiming at any person in particular. Instead, I activated a particular ability of the gun that I used when I needed to deal with large amounts of mooks in a short time.

A portal appeared in front of the barrel. And unseen by the rest aside from the emotionless blonde, the portals that acted as its other end opened.

It was a kaleidoscoping ability that aimed at every enemy I located in a limited area. The portals themselves are positioned randomly, utilizing the nature of those outside of the supernatural genre where they wouldn't notice it. But no matter what position though, it was all aimed at their heads.

It was a single headshot aimed for all.

I pulled the trigger, and the gun fired.

"—!?"

The effect was immediate - the remaining gunners that weren't killed by V had their heads blown off by a bullet. Blood and gray matter decorated the floor, containers, and walls. Then, all bodies simultaneously fell down to the ground like something out of a scripted play.

The blonde, after finishing off the man she held on a headlock by shooting her gun point blank, stopped in surprise at what happened.

I went ahead and joined her in the storage area. She glanced at me, before understanding colored her face as she realized I was the one that did it. Her expression then transitioned into a frown.

"…I took too long." she muttered, disappointment for herself clear.

"No, you did good." I reassured. "You're definitely better than most considering you just learned magic recently and you still did all this. I just wanted to help you, that's all."

She blinked. "Really?"

"Really."

She digested that before nodding her head, looking a bit brightened at my compliment. I felt slightly surprised at how fast she believed that but I suppose it's to be expected. While tragic stories have some drama in them, V's setting has the drama focused more on external conflicts as opposed to introspections.

It's good that there's no misunderstandings. That made her easier to deal with than the heroine. If it was Yuki then she'd probably spend quite a while brooding… although she was getting better at that recently, at least.

I moved to pat her head when I passed and she stiffened. It was just a short thing, not even a few seconds. Then, I dropped it and moved to the cargo containers, where the trafficked refugees were likely in fear and wondering what was happening.

"Let's go and help some people, shall we?" I said, turning to the blonde with a smile.

V was still standing there, stunned.

I blinked at her reaction, but before I could speak, she managed to recover from the fugue she was in. I might've wondered what the problem was, but the reason for it was quickly made apparent as the blonde turned to me and - for the very first time ever since I met her - had a bit of color on her face.

It couldn't be quite called a blush, but it was there.

"R-Right." she stuttered before walking past me in a stiff manner. "Let's do it."

I watched her with a blank expression.

…Maybe I should be careful with patting heads from now on.



When we opened the cargo containers holding the trafficked refugees, we were predictably met with fear and caution similar to how the hostages treated V a while ago - that is, when she got rid of the main unit she was in that was led by the lieutenant colonel. Understandable, since hearing people scream and dying horribly when you have no idea what's going on outside would make anyone paranoid.

Fortunately, unlike that time with the hostages, no one attempted to attack us. Although it's also likely because their attention was focused on the dead bodies around the storage area and feared the consequence of attempting to do it, as opposed to any real consideration on their part.

Strangely, there were some that looked at us with recognition… or rather, our appearances. These people probably were familiar with the Grim Reaper stories associated with us. Still, while the stories must have portrayed us on the good side, they remained cautious.

And so the trafficked refugees simply stared at both V and myself; two suspicious-looking figures that covered themselves underneath a cloak, and who massacred an entire ship's worth of criminals leaving not a single one alive. They stared at us in bated breath, wondering who we were. Asking themselves why we were here.

Waiting for the other shoe to drop.

I couldn't leave the task of speaking to them on V. After all, she had a role to play for our entire plan. Something as insignificant as this - it was a task more suited to the likes of me.

With that in mind I stepped up. Adjusting my body language to something harmless, I went in front to address them all. Some tensed for a second as I approached but otherwise did nothing.

"Apologies for the late arrival, but we have come here to rescue all of you." I began with a firm, but careful tone. "Every criminal on this ship is dealt with. You're all free from them - there's no longer any need to be trafficked by them in order to escape your wartorn country. Not anymore."

The combination of body language and tone of voice tailored to be as affable as possible by some bullshit martial arts that puts the manipulations of Yuki's sister to shame, and along with my words, clearly had a great effect on lowering their guard. Tense postures slowly eased as I spoke, and the refugees looked at me with something akin to hope in their eyes.

"I imagine this ship doesn't give any good memories to you all, so we can get all of you out of the place using a different boat. All of you would just simply need to travel with my colleagues there." I pointed to the side, opening a portal there as I did. "With them, you'll get out of this place in no time. It travels much faster than this ship anyway."

When they witnessed the portal open I had casted a hypnosis spell simultaneously. Their eyes glazed for a second before it disappeared. When the hypnosis ended they didn't question the portal, their minds perceiving it as another boat beside the ship or something.

The portal itself was connected to a coast of a neighboring country and there, a standby clone of mine prepared everything else they needed. In their perspective they would just ride the boat and they'd be dropped there. The rest that comes after is up to them - but they're at least out of danger.

"This… this isn't a trick, is it?" one of them muttered, their hopes tempered by their previous mistake. "How do we know you're telling the truth?"

"The dead bodies around you and the fact all of you remain alive are enough proof. If we're after money for trafficking people as slaves or selling their organs, then we could've left some of these criminals alive as well. We're certainly capable, as you might've heard by their screams and begging for mercy earlier." I said bluntly.

I could spout some rhetoric about justice and stuff like that, but these people don't need it. And they wouldn't want that either. Things like that belong to a different genre. In here, grim reality checks carry more influence.

And I could see my words getting through them. They considered the dead bodies with thought, mulling my words. Staring at the dead bodies clearly made them uncomfortable, although there's also a general feeling of schadenfreude with it considering how they suffered under their captors.

That might be enough to convince them. However, I wasn't done.

"If that is not enough, then I will tell you our main purpose here." I continued. "Truthfully, rescuing all of you is just a bonus. The fact that all of you are here is a lucky coincidence."

Frame the scenario as simply a side benefit, as making our main goal to save them would make it suspicious. After all, why would saving a bunch of nobodies be in our priority? These people couldn't offer anything and they knew that. Nothing, except themselves.

"Hijacking this ship and using it as our base of operations is what we wanted. We have some use for it. It was being used by these smugglers however, so we got rid of them."

In front of all these people, I can gauge the general reaction of those around. A majority were looking hopeful after hearing that they had a ticket out of their hell. However, I can see that there are some that simply looked tired and empty, even as the prospect of arriving at a safe place was guaranteed.

As many are the people who try to get to safety with their loved ones, there were just as many who had their lives upturned with their precious people taken away from them, left with nothing and only moving just to survive. I doubt that even when arriving at a safe place they would live a fulfilling life with their pasts haunting them.

"As for why we saved you instead of getting rid of you like everyone else? Simple. It's because it aligns with what we want."

And to these people, I stared at each of them straight in the eye.

"That is to say, we want to stop this war and deal with those who are responsible for it."

Bodies stiffened at my words and gazes snapped to me.

While every single person was already listening to me right now, being one of their supposed saviors and all, the moment I said those words I had gained their undivided focus. Why wouldn't they, when I said something they hadn't expected at all?

What I spoke of was something that appealed deep in their hearts. A wish unsaid, buried deep within themselves to focus more on the important things, and something that they don't think is possible and would only likely remain as a dream.

Not until now.

"This is an invitation: to those who have a score to settle, to those who want to save people left behind, to those that want to take revenge, to those that want to uphold their own duty and morals… or to those that don't have anyone or anything left waiting for them. We extend our hand towards you all, and implore you to join us to our cause."

I bowed my head slightly.

"However, we are not forcing you to do this. So please, if you want to leave then feel free to do so. We will still do our best to help you." I said, gesturing again to the portal. "This decision is in your hands."

My words were met with silence.

There was hesitation as they digested my words. Clearly, it had a great effect on them. They also likely have plenty of questions in their minds about our goals and how we intend to achieve them. However, they couldn't be answered because there are other things to prioritize.

And so a decision was made. One person went through the portal, followed by another. Then, more and more continued to choose to go to safety - most of these being the people who had loved ones remaining to protect. I couldn't blame them for making the choice. In fact, I actually supported them doing that.

I watched in silence as the last one went through the portal… before turning to the rest.

The ones who chose to be left behind. Out of about two hundred or so refugees, there were only around fifty left.

"…It seems that you all decided to stay. Are you truly sure of this choice?"

My question was answered with unsure looks and hesitant expressions. I expected that. After all, no realistic person wouldn't be feeling doubt at throwing away the prospect of safety after experiencing hell once more. Even worse, fighting in it as an active participant.

But these people - these brave, strong people who had endured so much - remained rooted on the spot. All for the sake of a cause they believe is worth fighting for.

And they're perfect for what we need for the next step.

"Very well." I said with a smile, before turning to V who was watching silently. "Then, it seems that we have some new recruits, my glorious leader. Will you allow them to be accepted?"

All the refugees who remained turned to my 'leader' who remained quiet the whole time. Because of said leader's face being shadowed by the cloak, from an outside perspective it looked like she was ruminating my statement. However, I was familiar enough to make out that she was just confused.

I just smiled at her and, after a long moment, it seemed like she at least came into the conclusion to play along. The woman nodded her head and my smile widened.

And with that, we can finally get to do the major moves.

The next step of the plan: After crippling the heads of the nation and extending invitations to the mecha genre…

We create an organization that would bring about the end of the war.


"…Why?"

I glanced at V as the woman suddenly asked me a question. "Hm? Why, what?"

"Why do all this? Why make an organization, and why did you make it like I was the leader?"

It was just about an hour after my recruitment attempt.

The two of us are currently at the ship's bridge, which was now free of bodies and blood after a bit of cleaning. Once I sorted out what the first members of our organization were supposed to do, bringing them up to speed with the help of some disguised clones of mine acting like organization members to help them settle in, we went up here to gain some privacy and to attend to our own tasks.

"Did you like the surprise?" I said with a smile, and she tilted her head.

"…I don't understand. Was I supposed to be happy about it?" she asked in confusion. "You said you want to stop the war, but it all seems unnecessary when you have the power to get rid of the government. You said to make our influence as small as possible in the plot and stated it's the reason why you can't make large changes without thinking it through, but isn't this also quite a large change?"

"Ah, well. I guess I can understand your confusion." I paused for a moment to think on how to phrase this. "I didn't teach you about that part yet regarding this world since, as you said, I advocate for minimum changes regarding the plot. But that doesn't apply to the current situation so there are other things to consider." I nodded at her table. "It's actually something related to what we're doing right now."

"Right now…? You mean, these plans?"

V currently sat on the table clearly meant for the captain of the ship as she checked on files of new key targets and planned how to engage them while I assisted her at her side. The ones killed during the military gala where I met mecha pilot wasn't the only one we planned on targeting, as the ensuing power struggle would cripple war efforts on both sides of the conflict, and it had to be planned accordingly.

"You and I are the most free people in the world. That means that we won't be influenced by it whenever it makes some plot, and it can only adjust to us." I explained to her. "However, that doesn't mean our actions do not have any consequences."

I gestured to the plans we were making. There, different approaches of how to kill the targets while pinning the blame on other factors are detailed. No one would suspect that it was some outside factor that would be the one to do it.

"There was always an option to kill all those who are corrupt instead of doing this. As you said, I could easily do it. Just teleport there, then kill them. Nobody would know, especially with the genre divide preventing normal people from looking more into the supernatural genre. However, you should know that such an action as drastic as that can hold unexpected consequences, especially when the setting requires for the war to continue."

Turning back to the emotionless blonde, I saw her focusing solely on me. I could feel her curiosity from her gaze as she listened to my words attentively. And so, I continued to speak.

"If unexplained killings or strange phenomenons happen, it could change things. If you want to change where the plot is headed while also preserving the setting, then you have to work within the boundaries of it. Or at least, make it look that way." I emphasized. "If we're not cautious, random cabals or supernatural organizations would pop up just so the world could make up some narrative consistency for it."

I frowned in thought as I reminisced about how I've come to know that particular fact and the lessons learned at that time.

"I made the mistake of being reckless long ago." I said, bitterly admitting that fact. "It was just a single school setting but it turned it into a big mess. Espers, aliens and time travelers suddenly started appearing, all because some girl got indirectly affected and the plot somehow made her into a reality warper. I imagine it would be much messier here when it involves two countries."

She blinked in surprise, but whether it was at my admission of mistake or the craziness of that setting, I do not know. But just like always the blonde simply digested what I told her and, after a moment, nodded her head in acceptance before speaking once more.

"I understand. I suppose making these plans are necessary, knowing that." she remarked. "However, this narrative consistency… What exactly do you mean by that?"

"It just means that for every action done, it must advance the plot in some way and could potentially be done by a character within the story itself." I explained. "If we make great changes, or many small ones, without taking that into account - then the world will inevitably add something just to make things consistent. There's only so much that the world can adjust to before it starts to get contrived, after all."

"I see." she paused. "So the reason why you want to create this organization… it's so that the plot doesn't add or modify anything when we stop the war. And the reason why you couldn't just waltz in and kill or hypnotize everyone." she deduced.

"Very astute of you. That's correct." I praised her. I was getting good at reading her expressions, so I didn't miss the miniscule way her face brightened and how she straightened on her seat.

"I did not think things would be this complicated. It seems that there are a lot of things to consider before acting." V commented.

"…Yes, it's strange isn't it? That we're the most free people in the world, but it still affects us even if it wasn't in the usual way. Although these restrictions are mostly self-imposed, really."

I moved to sit down on a nearby chair and relaxed on the seat. Then, I looked at the windows on the ship's bridge, staring at the vast expanse of the ocean. Speaking to her about all this brought about some reflections I've been ruminating time and time again.

"So many constraints and restrictions… Of course, there's always a choice to just do whatever you want despite the consequences but…" I frowned, before shaking my head. "Anyway, I won't blame you if you think my methods are a shame, and that living the way I do will only hinder the potential that we have. With the life you lived, I think you of all people deserve to think that."

Why did I consider such constraints, I wonder? Perhaps I might have done great things if I just do what I want. In fact, perhaps I might have found a way to prevent the looming future apocalypse instead of just trying to delay it as much as possible.

The path to where I am currently hasn't been innocent. And I wasn't this powerful at first either. People suffered and lives were lost for the sake of advancing the plot and reaching a good ending. Even now that is happening. And I couldn't even help all the people in plots that finish without said good ending, because I'm not omnipotent. I can only extend my help to those I could reach.

V, if she hadn't turned meta, would likely be one of those people who I failed to help.

Would I have saved more lives than I currently am if I just did what I want, despite the consequences? I do not know. But what I do know is that those consequences will likely hurt people even if I try to mitigate it. And that fact was enough to stop me.

I can phrase it whatever I want and reason it however I try, but the sole reason why those constraints and restrictions are up in the first place… it was because I was afraid.

Afraid of hurting people because of my actions.

As I reflected on that however, V suddenly spoke, interrupting me from my thoughts.

"—I disagree. I do not think that way at all."

Those words were said with surprising conviction. I glanced back at the blonde, who stared at me with an intense look on her face. Or at least, by her standards. There was a pause from her as she tried to speak the thoughts in her mind.

"I think… I think it is great that you act with these restrictions in mind." she began. "You have saved me and all these people. And I know that you will save many more, just as you have helped countless others before."

She stared at me with a sharp glint in her eye.

"That you do it, even without things forcing you, makes you more kind than others I have met… No, perhaps the kindest person that I have ever known in my life. The constraints you try to limit yourself in is a testament to that." she declared. "I may not know much, and I may have only spent a little time with you… however, I can say for sure that…"

The blonde looked down to her mechanical arm, flexing her digits while staring at it in thought. Then, she clenched it tight and brought it close to her chest, closing her eyes as she did so.

"…I can say for sure that I am happy to have met someone like you, Basa." V muttered softly. "I wouldn't have you any other way. And I will follow your example, because of it."

I paused at the heartfelt manner she said those words. I didn't really know what to say, so I just scratched the back of my head while letting out a deep exhale.

Things certainly turned emotional out of nowhere. Maybe the heroine was rubbing off me with all her brooding.

"Is that so? I guess I'm glad to hear that." I said, looking away from her as I did so. "…Although you should be careful with how you phrase your words. That normally would be taken as a confession, you know?"

"Confession? Did I confess something?" the woman said with a clueless look on her face.

"It's because Japanese people seem to be allergic to being direct, so even alluding to a hint of affection might as well be a confession of love. And for some godforsaken reason, we both know the world operates that way as well." I let out a smirk. "Wouldn't want yourself to say 'I like you' to someone by accident, would you?"

"I understand." she said with a nod. "However, I think it is appropriate for this circumstance. I do like you after all."

…

…This woman…

I let out a sigh. I'd be blind if I didn't know this with the hints I've seen until now. She really is my fourth heroine, I suppose. "Do whatever you want." I said in resignation.

The girl simply nodded without shame as if she didn't just say something so forward. "Yes. However, you still haven't answered one question." V remarked. "Why did you say that I am the leader of this organization? It shouldn't be me."

"Why shouldn't it be you? This is your revenge, isn't it?"

Her eyes narrowed slightly. "This might be my wish, but a proper chain of command requires you to be the leader. This is especially true considering that I am the one following your orders."

"Orders? What orders? I don't recall giving you one." I said with a smirk. "All I remember saying is that you don't need to follow orders and that your life is your own, or something along those lines."

I could see a hint of annoyance from acting deliberately obtuse, throwing back the words I said to her from the time we first met. The woman stared at me and… hold on, was she pouting? This woman really is getting more and more emotive by the day.

"Just accept the role for now. It holds more meaning to someone like you anyway." I said with an apologetic smile, taking pity at her. "Plus, it's good practice. You've never been in a position of power, haven't you? It'll be a new experience too."

The blonde looked unconvinced. However, when she opened her mouth to protest, she was suddenly interrupted with a knock on the bridge's door.

V glanced at me with a blank expression on her face, and I just returned it with a smile. When it was obvious that I wasn't going to speak, the blonde let out a breath that almost felt like an exasperated sigh.

"Come in." she muttered.

The door opened and a person entered the ship's bridge. Said person was a tall woman with brown hair, olive skin and green eyes. The woman was clearly beautiful, but the most eye-catching thing about her was the scar that ran onto her chest and down to her abdomen.


Spoiler

I recognized her. From what I recall, her name was Amida. She was one of the refugees, and the woman who I suggested to represent their group as they coordinated with my disguised clones. She seemed to act as the de-facto leader of the group she was with when they were forced into the cargo containers.

The woman looked nervous as she entered, clearly dreading a meeting with her bosses, but her eyes widened the moment it landed on us.

"…Y-You're younger than me…?" she muttered.

Ah, right. We had the hood of our cloaks down. That makes this the first time any of them had seen our faces. I suppose it would be a shock when your supposed saviors and now leaders are actually younger than you are… Perhaps it would be good to not let them have any doubts because of that.

"I had been told that I have quite a baby face. Thank you for noticing." I said, making the woman snap out of her shock. "As for our glorious leader… Well, she is quite young. But don't let your looks fool you. Her body count probably exceeds the ages of all the people in this ship combined."

That was likely true, and it would probably increase as time went on. Amida looked shocked at that, her gaze turning to V who remained quiet behind the desk. My, looking at her right now she looks like a criminal mastermind. That blank look that seemed to pierce your being appears quite intimidating if you have no idea it was because she just didn't know how to emote.

"Anyway, what brings you here?" I asked the woman.

It took a slight pause, but Amida recovered her composure after I asked the question. "R-Right. I came here to say that all the preparations are finished. I gathered up the people who could help operate the ship, but there are still some issues to take care of…"

"I guess I have time to spare. Please, lead the way." I responded before standing up on my seat. Then, I sent a meaningful glance at V. "I'll take care of this, boss. You should continue working on that."

The blonde nodded obediently. Although it probably looked like an imperious nod for Amida, considering her intimidatingly blank look that disturbed the woman. And so, with the woman beside me, the both of us exited the bridge.

Let's see how our fledgling group is doing, shall we?


Creating an organization is not an easy task.

Putting aside the logistics involved for operating it, it comes with responsibilities of managing people with different personalities and goals. While in theory all members are united under a single vision and mission, in practice it isn't quite as simple. The responsibility of a leader is to deal with such problems and succeed despite it.

It requires a very unique situation for me to even attempt doing something like creating an organization. I find it all tiring to deal with to be honest, so I tend to avoid it. I like to do things alone and it was only due to recent circumstances that I worked closely with other people.

If I require tasks which need multiple people, I usually default to my clones. In fact, that was what I thought of doing at first. Until I changed my mind, thinking it would be better to just guide the people whose tragic plots we interfered with and involve them in this, instead of letting the whims of the world decide for them.

But I digress. The point is that I don't usually do this.

However, it doesn't mean I'm unfamiliar with how to deal with these sorts of things.

"We've found the supplies of the smugglers but it seems to be running out. The same for the fuel of the ship too. One of our group, who claimed that she worked on machines, also said that the state of the ship is dangerously poor too. Some of your men agreed with her."

Amida reported to me as we walked along the ship's deck. Truthfully, I already knew all these but I let her do it to be acclimated with her role. Around us, the refugees who stayed behind along with my disguised clones were busy with other tasks, which was mainly cleaning the place up. The bodies were already thrown out into the ocean but there was still plenty of blood, weapons, and spent ammunition around.

Eyes were upon us when I walked beside Amida, and like her, they reacted with shock at my seemingly young age. I didn't will my clones to act the same since it could be excused due to their own 'familiarity' with me, but I did attempt conversing with those who commented on my age. I wouldn't want them to form harmful opinions because of it.

…But then again, such a thing is natural.

"All in all, it looks like this ship is on its last trip. It's in no shape to sail. And unless the supplies are replenished, then we'll run out of food and water." she muttered. I noticed her glance on me for a moment with an assessing look on her eye, but it was gone in a flash. "…I do not know why you wanted to take this place. This wouldn't survive even a single hit from a cannon from a proper naval ship."

Doubt. Hesitation.

She didn't show it outright, but I don't need to read her mind to know what she was thinking. The earlier appeal of joining settled down and gave way to more realistic thoughts. And I doubt that she was the only one feeling this way within the ship, because while I may have touched their hearts earlier by revealing our goal, the support they've given will disappear if they think I have no way of backing it up.

It would be great if people could be steadfast in their beliefs, but this wasn't shounen. Nobody wants to throw their lives away on a useless endeavor after all.

"Hm, is that all of our problems? Then it should be a simple fix."

Thankfully, those are easily addressed by yours truly.

The woman blinked in surprise at my seemingly nonchalant reaction. "A… simple fix?"

"Yes. It should be. You didn't think that we'd try to fight two countries if we couldn't do something as simple as that, did you?" I rhetorically asked with a knowing smile, making her momentarily flinch in surprise. "That said, you work fast. It's only been an hour since you're out and already you accomplished all this; perhaps you have experience in being a leader? I've seen military officers who work with less efficiency." I glanced at the large scar on her body. "Did you work for them in the past?"

"…Nothing as glamorous as that. I was a site manager for a factory and oversaw a bunch of girl workers. Then we got hit by the war. That's how I got the scar." the woman muttered. Still, my sincere praise had the effect of pleasing her in some way, making her relax her tense shoulders due to my earlier accurate guess. "That said, what do you mean by simple fix? Will your boat earlier come back and give us supplies? They didn't drop things earlier so I found it strange…"

"No, our supplies are already here."

"Already here? What do you mean—?" I pointed at the side. "…Eh?"

Indeed, right where I was pointing had some stacked boxes on it. It seemingly appeared out of nowhere and how it got there, no one knows. But then again it wasn't like there was anyone paying any attention to that part of the ship anyway, so they couldn't really deny that nobody just walked up and placed something there.

"Hmm, did you perhaps not check all the wares in here yet?" I asked.

"T-That's… we're not yet done, but we shouldn't have missed this…" Amida stuttered, wrong-footed. Then, she recovered and turned around to call out to the men hanging around the area. "Hey, someone check these boxes!"

They did, and once it was opened the insides revealed various canned and fresh foods along with a healthy supply of different beverages. There were quite many, and it should be enough to last them a long time. It should also give them quite an enjoyable meal considering it's been a long time these refugees ate anything palatable.

"How fortunate. Seems like you all would be eating great today." I said amidst the joyful mood that the people around had gained once seeing all the supplies.

Meanwhile, Amida looked like she was in shock. "R-Right… This should be enough to feed us a lot." she muttered. Then, she frowned thoughtfully. "But all of these appear to be food. That's great, but there's still other things that we need. There's still the ship's fuel—"

"Could you be referring to those things?"

"—Eh!? There's still some more!?" Amida exclaimed in surprise again, gaze following to another place I was pointing. This time it was a cargo's worth of barrels containing said fuel. "W-Where did that come from…? Hey, someone call our mechanics here too!"

Her shouting seems to have gained the attention of others and someone immediately went down to the ship's inner deck to get who she asked for. After a short moment of waiting, they went back up with a woman. She seemed quite a unique character, considering her curly set of twintails.


Spoiler

"Someone said there's fuel? Let me see." the woman checked the barrels, opening one of them and then wincing as the fumes of the tar-like ship fuel revealed inside wafted out. "Y-Yeah, that's fuel alright. With this much… Can anyone bring them down with me to the ship's hull?"

I acted like I didn't notice the intense stare of Amida beside me while observing our mechanic bring down the barrels with the help of others. It was only after a while that I turned back to her, and when I did, I simply gave her a calm look.

"Is there something wrong?" I asked.

"How…?" the woman trailed off in an unsure tone, question hanging on her lips.

She clearly thought that I did something. The genre divide wouldn't let them witness the fact that I took it out of subspace before putting it there. As I said earlier, I already knew about the problems we had considering my clones around, and I already made the preparations.

Maybe I could've put it somewhere where they'll find it in a more natural manner. But that wasn't the point. One of the most precarious stages in creating an organization is at its start since, in most cases, you need to prove that you're worth following.

"Who knows?" I said with a smile. "Maybe it was just because you didn't notice? Or maybe it was some sort of technology? Or maybe something else entirely?"

Show off, then bring out a sense of mystery. The formula of how to make others perceive you as strong.

I couldn't exactly tell her the whole truth considering there is no organization in the first place. Yet with my actions here, she would have an idea that she didn't at least join a weak group. And being the leader, there's a great chance of her convincing the rest of the same. And then I don't need to repeat this stunt for quite some time.

All in all, typical politics with its complicated posturing. Such a drag.

"I see." the woman dropped the topic, clearly realizing she wouldn't get anything from me. Still, the way she looked at me clearly changed. "Thank you, then. This should get rid of some worries. And the food and drink should make a lot of people very happy."

"There's no need for thanks. It's all you people deserve, at the very least."

She eyed me strangely at that, as if she didn't know what to think. "…I suppose so."

Before we could continue and move on to other things however, a man came out of the ship's deck and rushed towards us. "Miss Amida! There's something that you need to see!" he shouted urgently. Then, he spotted me and stopped in his tracks. "Oh…"

I gave him a smile. "You mentioned needing to see something? Please, lead the way."

Seems like they found out the other reason why we're here.

And so, with Amida beside me, we both went back into the vast storage area within the ship. There was quite a lot of wares being transported so it might take a few hours to catalogue every single one. However, if there was one thing here that stands out, it would be one particularly large thing.

Or rather, many things I suppose. It's quite modular.

"This is…!"

When we arrived, Amida gaped as the open-top cargo container opened to reveal a large mechanical arm. It was large enough for an average person to fit within the span of the palm itself. Scaled up pneumatics and circuitry are also visible underneath the plated armor, clearly making it functional instead of being some sort of artistic piece.

"O-Open the other containers!" Amida commanded immediately. "Check all of them!"

They were opened and, just as the woman suspected, similar mechanical body parts are around. Amida and the others were stunned at what they were seeing. As for me, I just acknowledged a conjecture of mine was correct about these people being involved in this type of setting.

Because what was in front of us was undoubtedly, and indisputably, a mech.

The criminals are planning to smuggle it out of the place and sell it. It looked quite damaged, but that was understandable considering it was a wreck when they found it.

As the others exploded into action, Amida turned to me and noted my lack of surprise. "Y-You…" she muttered nervously. "Was this the reason why you wanted this ship?"

I smiled at her again. "Who knows?" I said, repeating my earlier statement.

The woman clearly had an idea of what this thing was. The moment she saw it, I saw haunted recognition in her eyes. Very likely it was something that was tied into her past. And also very likely it would be the reason for the scar as well, as well as the motivation for her joining up in the first place.

And with the colorful cast of characters here, there would be plenty of others here with the same background.

Really, it seems like I made the right choice. Doing this rather than creating a group of clones for an organization is far more efficient.

"Say, Amida." I began, gaining the woman's complete attention.

"What do you think of learning how to pilot a mech?"
