Chapter 22

Their ship cruised at dawn peacefully.

Waves gently crashed on the hull of the ship as it crossed the vast expanse of the ocean. It was a sound which had turned into a background noise for her that she could easily ignore. In fact, after hearing it almost constantly when she had boarded this ship, she had come to appreciate it as comforting at some point.

And right in the ocean horizon, one could see the hints of the sun piercing through the dusk - giving a beautiful scene of the morning twilight. She marveled at the view right in front of her. While she had traveled far and wide to escape the war, there was never a moment to appreciate a sight like this. In the first place, she wasn't the type to even think about this really.

But here she was. Standing right in the bow of the ship, taking it all in.

She had changed. But whether it was due to her settling down somewhere relatively peaceful, or coming to terms with what to do with what she wanted to do with the rest of her life… she didn't know.

After all, she might've just sent her own death warrant. Her days were likely limited - she was already fearing for her life even when crossing warzones without much fighting in it, and here she was now, volunteering to be in the frontlines. What was she thinking, throwing away the life of peace she yearned for something like this?

But just like always, there was no choice but to grit your teeth and keep moving.

Amida had always lived her life that way, and it wasn't going to stop now.

…At the very least, the things she had seen didn't give her much reason to regret her choices. She had a good idea of what was happening on the ship right now because, for some goddamn reason, she was chosen to be the leader of this group despite being just a simple woman who worked as a factory manager.

She could never know what's going on in their leaders' minds. Even now the stunt one of them displayed - the young man with blonde hair and tanned skin - remained firmly entrenched in her mind. And for the past few days, after somehow repairing the damaged mech, the same man had been teaching her how to operate it as if he was familiar with how it worked.

There were too many questions about them. But she could at least tell they were sincere with their aim for this group they've gathered. They had certainly been helping other refugees on escaping this wretched war behind for the past few days like some charity organization, after all. Their numbers have been swelling these past few days as they also found new recruits. And so are the supplies they've been getting.

But she also knew what all of that meant. And she was proven correct on her suspicion when, the day before, they were finally given instructions and asked to prepare. And it was clear that this was different from their usual operations.

The fighting would start soon, and she can only hope she was ready for it.

"…Amida."

A voice called out to her from behind, interrupting her from her thoughts. She turned around and saw that many people had already gathered on the deck at some point while she was thinking. Amida looked at the person who spoke - it was a woman with white hair and pale complexion, staring at her with her perpetually calm face that Amida never saw change much even in the direst of times.


Spoiler

"Azee." Amida greeted her. "I see that the volunteers are here. Is everything ready?"

She was someone who Amida had delegated some of her tasks to and acted as her second. One who had traveled with her and stayed when Amida chose to stay as well. If there was someone who she trusted would complete her orders without giving in to the pressure of it all, it would be her.

"Yes, everything is prepared." she answered simply. "The explosives are stored properly but otherwise, they should be easily transported out once we get to our destination. We've already instructed the others how to place them properly as well."

"I see. And the weapons?"

"I can answer that." another woman said with a smile, stepping beside Azee. "I was the one who attended to it while Azee went to the more important stuff."

It was another one of the people that she trusted and had stayed with her all this time. A woman with blondish hair styled in a set of twintails and dressed in a fashion that showed more skin than Amida. She was someone that seemed to always act cheerful, almost childish at times, no matter the situation - something that contrasted to Azee's own indifference. Nevertheless, she knew firsthand the spunk hidden beneath the girl that could make people respect her despite the way that she acted.


Spoiler

"The weapons were fine. We tested it. Except for the RPGs, of course. Can't exactly test that inside this ship." Lafter said with a slight chuckle, before speaking more seriously. "Although, I did speak with Eco. She assured me that they should work. Top of the line, even. Apparently, they're even better than the ones used by the army."

Amida noted the name. That was the mechanic that they found in her group, not the ones that came with their leaders. She didn't know what sort of past that she had to know that, but she supposed it didn't matter at this point.

"All in all, we have enough to arm everyone in this ship and a spare. There should be more than enough to give to those that will be going with us." Lafter finished.

"I see. Thank you." Amida said, before pausing when the two remained where they were. "…Is there something else?"

The two looked at each other for a moment, before Azee spoke. "Amida… we know you've been practicing on that mech, but is everything really fine?" her voice was soft enough that others around couldn't hear it. "Putting aside getting into that dreaded thing, you're going into the thick of the fight. And now, with everything that's going to happen…"

"Are you going to be okay, Amida?" Lafter asked worriedly, voicing both of their concerns.

She paused. That was the question she had been asking herself for a while now. Aside from being chosen as the leader of their group, why was she also chosen as the mech's pilot? She tried to think of the reason why, but the reason always eludes her.

Nevertheless, it wasn't like there was any other qualified person aside from their leaders, who surely are busy with other things or perhaps already have a mech with their own judging by the man's experience when teaching her. So, she agreed.

Piloting the mech had been something of an overwhelming experience. Those behemoths had been the source of her nightmares whenever she slept after their fighting destroyed her hometown. It had been an eye opening experience for her, and made her aware of just how dangerous the world is. When it was time to enter one, it had already been quite an ordeal.

Thankfully, her instructor had been patient. He even consoled her when she broke down, remembering all the deaths of her loved ones and seeing the memory vividly in her mind's eye, because standing in front of that weapon was a painful reminder of it.

"—Things aren't the same."

The man simply told her those words, his voice cutting through the din of her trauma. It was spoken with a calm resoluteness that she couldn't help but latch onto it just to remain sane in the storm of thoughts consuming her.

"You're remembering it all. The despair, the powerlessness. But right now, know that it isn't the same." he told her. "Because now, Amida - now you can fight. It's an opportunity to prevent what came to be from ever happening again. All you need to do is to get that fear in your hand and grip it tight."

She looked up at the blonde man who gazed at her without a hint of judgement. In his eyes was only understanding and respect. He extended a hand towards her, pulling her up.

"You couldn't fight before. Now, you can."

…That was an embarrassing moment for her. She fancied herself as a hard woman and yet she showed that kind of face to him. Amida tried to not let the heat get to her face as she recalled the memory.

Still, after that vulnerable moment, she had quickly grasped the basics of how to operate such a large machine. The mech can thankfully operate underwater and they could practice on the ocean because the ship didn't have much space. Practicing in the ocean had been difficult, but she was at least confident that she could brawl and shoot other mechs.

It was honestly surprising how fast she had learned to use it. But whether it was due to her own talent, or because her instructor was good at teaching, she didn't know.

The two women waited for her to speak. Amida looked at them and sighed, finally answering them.

"I don't know the answer to that, you two. But I've done all I could to practice and prepare for this. At the very least, I know how to fight there." Amida told them bluntly. "All we can do is to hope for the best, just like always." she declared.

They both frowned. Still, they said nothing in protest either. Her answer clearly wasn't satisfactory for the both of them, but Amida knew that they understood that it was the best answer they could get.

"I guess that's how it always goes." Azee said with a sigh. "I already knew things would go this way, but maybe I should've volunteered to go instead."

"I feel the same, but… In the first place, you shouldn't be alone. If we're planning to stop this war, just you going there wouldn't be enough right? They should at least get more of those mechs. Then maybe Azee and I could join you." Lafter commented.

Amida frowned. Perhaps that was true, but how would they get the mechs? They never did know the full circumstance of the organization they joined, after all. Hell, they still don't even know its name - much like the identities of their superiors.

Still, the blonde man told her that they will get more, but the specifics were never fully revealed to her. Only that he will notify her once it was confirmed. Perhaps they already have it or there was something else planned.

She opened her mouth to speak those thoughts—

"We are going to get that from this operation."

—Before stopping when another soft voice replied instead.

All three of them stiffened in shock. Amida turned her head, then registered the fact that the entire deck had quieted down and made way for a certain person, staring at them with a mixture of great respect and fear. They hadn't even noticed her approach once the said person managed to get to them.

There was only one person in the ship who could inspire such a presence.

Amida stared at the blonde woman with wide eyes.

"B-Boss!" Lafter shouted in surprise as Amida froze beside her. "S-Since when were you…?"

She was their boss. The Boss. They never gave their names, so that was what they referred to her.

It didn't look like it with her young age and a stature shorter than Aida herself, but she was the leader of their organization. One who that blonde man followed on his own volition, and the person who he had killed all those criminals with. And if rumors are to be believed, then she would be the reaper that had taken so many lives of those in the battlefield and saved just as much as well.

Amida met the blank, emotionless gaze aimed at her. She swallowed, feeling very nervous yet still wanting to meet her expectations. She stood straight under her attention.

"W-What do you mean by that, ma'am?" she asked.

The boss paused for a moment to answer that.

"This operation will give us new members piloting mechs that will join our group. My… second-in-command made sure that they'll arrive at our destination. They will require our help since they will be fighting enemy pilots, and you will be assisting them." she revealed, making Amida blink. Then she continued, sweeping her gaze at the three of them. "I assume that things are prepared?"

"Yes, ma'am." they all answered.

She nodded at that. "Then, we simply need to wait. I will tell you what we need to do once we make landfall."

Their boss looked at the horizon, and Amida mirrored it. She narrowed her eyes as the sun's light shined as it finally started to rise fully, and as she did, she could see hints of what looked like a coast from the far distance.

…It seems like their destination is here.

Amida didn't know what might happen now, but she supposed that with everything going to be told to them shortly after this, there's not much to complain about. However, the Boss' explanation of this operation being done to get new members who can pilot mechs did make her feel a little anxious.

They were finally fighting, doing their first steps on stopping the madness that had upended countless lives. And unlike their earlier tasks of helping other refugees escape, she knew there was a chance that people might die, the reality of what group they joined in only sinking in truly right now.

But there was nothing they could do about that now.

The only thing that Amida can do is to hope that these new members are worth risking their life on.


"—Pilot Orga. Do you copy?"

Orga's head snapped up when his name was called by the person speaking in the comms. He was seated on an APC headed to the hangar where their mechs were stationed, the other pilots being transported with him. In his hands he held a tablet containing the mission briefing, given for them to review.

Or at least, that was what he should be doing.

"This is Orga. What is it?" he responded.

"Intel suggests that there are new developments about the situation. You will go to another location, and your goals for this mission have been updated." the voice coldly answered him. "The updated mission briefing will be forwarded to you along with the rest of your squad. Review them properly before you are deployed."

"Under—" the line cut out before he could finish. "—stood."

Orga frowned at that. Still, faced with that impoliteness, he reacted little and simply went back to look down on his tablet. He stared at the now-outdated report, his eyes taking in the orders and maps despite not really reading them.

"…Rude of them, don't you think?" a voice on his side broke him out of his thoughts. Orga turned to glance at the black-haired teen looking at him with an unreadable gaze. "At first they were content with ignoring us, but now they're acting pretty bossy. Things are certainly getting different lately."


Spoiler

Orga sent a warning glare at his sworn brother. He had always told him to watch his mouth when they're being deployed since there was a good chance that their 'employers' were listening. "Augus…"

"They're not listening. They aren't going to put recording devices on a dingy vehicle like this. Plus, the engine is too noisy anyways." he reasoned. "We can talk all we want here. Or at least, not until we get to the mechs."

Orga's glare abated, turning back to stare at his tablet. "…That's because things are turning different." he finally replied to his earlier comment.

The teen tilted his head consideringly at that. "I suppose that's what happens when someone like the head researcher dies. I wonder why they're so aggressive now, though? I've heard some rumors that they've added more 'orphans' to join us… maybe they're starting to understand our usefulness here."

"I don't know. But I wouldn't bet on it."

"Yes, I thought so too." Augus agreed easily. "So, with that out of the way - can you finally tell me what's going on in your mind? It's clear that you've been troubled with something for the past few days, Orga."

Orga stiffened at his blunt words.

He knew he was never the greatest when it comes to acting. And now that they're being deployed, he was too consumed with his thoughts to even bother trying to hide in anymore. He can only chastise himself for his lack of discipline. Likely, everyone in his squad realized how strange he was acting.

But, at the very least… he'd like to think that his mishap was understandable.

A few days had passed since that fateful night when the head researcher was assassinated and, more importantly, when he was left with that message by that mysterious blonde man. Orga had memorized it, burning the coordinates and the date written there in his mind. Yet, he could never decide on what to do with that information, simply agonizing over it for the past few days.

What would even happen if he went there? Would he get wrapped up in some conspiracy to end the war, like what the blonde man had suggested he was aiming to do? Or was it a trick to secure pilots like him? Could he trust someone like that, when everything about them is so unknown?

He refrained from telling the others in his squad because he didn't want them to be troubled by something like this.

…And in the first place, besides those doubts, there were quite a few problems in even acting on the information given to him.

He was just a pilot, one that was monitored by the entire company because he was an asset. He couldn't go anywhere without permission which essentially made getting to these coordinates impossible. And from what he could tell, these coordinates were literally in the middle of nowhere, far away from any cities in this country. How can he even get there in the first place?

Was that blonde man ignorant of his lack of freedom? Did he think pilots could get to anywhere that they wanted? It was certainly possible - but then, how would that explain him knowing Orga and Augus were sworn brothers? Even his 'employers' likely didn't even know that. Someone who could assassinate the head researcher so easily shouldn't be unaware of the organization they were working under as well.

So many questions that he didn't know the answer to. And before he knew it, the time had come. Today was the date stated in the note. He thought he might have to do something, but…

Suddenly, Orga and his squad were called for a mission. And he has no choice but to comply.

Perhaps his worrying had led to nothing, after all. Yet for some reason, he couldn't shake this feeling that there was something more going on - something more that he should do. Would his absence be interpreted as a refusal? If so, what would happen to him, who had witnessed someone clearly associated with the murder of the head researcher? Those thoughts - it made him antsy up to now.

And he didn't need to include others on it. If it meant that making the wrong choice would, even in the slightest chance, affect them too - then he would keep what happened as a secret to his grave. His paranoid mind wouldn't allow anything less.

"It's nothing, Augus. Leave it alone." Orga answered the teen beside him, who frowned.

"It's clearly not just 'nothing'. You've been like this ever since you returned from that gala." Augus insisted. "We're starting to get worried about you, Orga. Did you see something at that time? Something that made you disturbed?"

Orga's lips pressed into a thin line. Augus' eyes narrowed, noticing it.

"You did." he said, suspicions confirmed.

"…I'm telling you to leave it alone, Augus. I did see something, but it's not something I can just spread lightly." Orga stated with a firm tone. The boy's mouth opened to protest, but he brought a hand up to interrupt it. "Make no mistake, it's not a matter of trust. I will tell you once I'm sure that things are over, but for now let me think on it on my own."

Once the date passed and nothing still happened to him for not going to the coordinates, he doubted it would matter anymore. But for now…

"This is my burden to bear." Orga finished, resolve evident in his expression.

Augus stared at him for a few moments before nodding. "Understood… Then, I'll wait until you can finally tell me, Orga."

The teen said those words with a tone filled with faith and loyalty in him just as always. And just as always too, Orga felt the weight of his expectations for him to carry and see through. It was suffocating, but it was something that must be done. He can only hope to do it just as well like everything else in the past.

"We'll see." Orga replied, promising him nothing.

Any more possibility of talk was dashed when the APC had finally stopped in its tracks. Then, the door opened, revealing armed guards that were on standby from the outside. One of them glanced around the truck to do a headcount before reaching into his earpiece.

"They're all here. Yes, everything is accounted for… Understood." the man spoke to his comms, before bringing his arm down and looking at them. He didn't seem all that hostile but instead treated them in a rather casual manner. Must be one of the rare decent people here, then. "All of you. Please listen up."

Unusual. He wondered if there was something wrong. Orga listened carefully as the man spoke to them.

"There will be changes to procedures due to the newly instated heads. I don't know how you kids used to run things during missions, but expect that things might be different this time." the man warned. "Though I doubt that things would change much with you guys just riding mechs and fighting… still, keep that in mind, just to be on the safe side."

"We will, sir." Orga answered for them.

"Good. Then, stand up and follow us."

His squad obeyed. They stood up from their seats and walked outside, following the man as they entered the mech hangar while the other guard kept an eye on them. It always struck him as strange: this entire building was meant for them, but they were being treated as prisoners instead as guests.

Nevertheless, this was a life he was stuck with. This was just routine now, and it was evident with how everyone in his squad appeared fine with everything. Although, he could see that some of them were glancing at him and Augus in concern, likely showing the same worries as the teen did.

When they caught Augus' eyes the teen shook his head discreetly, making them frown. Orga knew that he might have to explain a bit more about this later.

After a while of being led through various corridors they finally arrive at their destination. It was the hangar's ready room, where they'd have to wait in until their mechs were ready. Although, it looked more like a holding cell than anything from how barren it is aside from chairs they can sit on. At the very least, their employers were merciful enough to put cushions in it and make it slightly comfortable.

The guards made them go in the room before guarding the door outside. Then, they all sat in their usual places. Orga took his position at the front, where he'd relay the mission information given to him by command to the rest of his squad.

They all looked at him in various degrees of concern. Although, they didn't ask the question in their minds. Everyone knew this room was bugged as hell and anything they spoke of here would reach the ears of their employers. So, they remained quiet.

Orga checked the tablet he was holding again. He idly realized that the new information finally arrived as they walked here. He lightly read through it, checking the changes.

"So, what are we going to do this time?" one of his squad members, a young man with short spiky hair and a burly physique, spoke up.

"Give me a moment, Altland. I was told that they updated the mission during our trip here." Orga replied as he kept reading through the information. Then, his eyes narrowed. "…It looks like we aren't going back to the frontlines this time."

"What do you mean?" Augus asked.

"We're going to a secret facility from our employers. It seems like our enemies found out about it and are staging an attack. They want us to defend the place while they retrieve important things in it and destroy those that they can't bring back. Looks like they don't want them stealing their research."

"Really? What are they even keeping in there?" another one of his squad, Norba, who was another young man with short hair but colored brown unlike Altland, asked curiously. "It must be important if we're being called there."

"I don't know. And we don't need to know that to do this mission." Orga replied. The files seem to agree, considering there's not a single information about that. "What matters is that we defend the place and prevent them from shooting down retreating personnel. Then after that, we leave as well."

Orga looked at the eye of every single member of his squad.

"This is a textbook extraction mission, everybody. That means we'll go with part seven section two of our field operations manual. I hope everyone is familiar with that?" Orga was answered with nods all around. "Good. Are there any questions?"

One raised a hand. This time the question came from a more intellectual member of their group - a blonde boy named Eugene. "What are we working with here?" he asked.

"There will be air support but they're mostly there for the extraction. We're going to be the ones doing most of the fighting. Don't expect any assistance from them."

"And our enemies?"

He frowned. "Unknown. However, intel suggests that the enemy would be using their mechs first. Their reinforcements will come later, but keep an eye for surprises. We never know what might happen."

Eugene nodded. "I see. Just the usual then."

Indeed, it seems like the answer for mechs is to fight it with other mechs. Eighty percent of the time they were deployed, chances are that they'd be fighting other pilots like them. His squad was used to fighting them now - but it didn't make them any less dangerous.

"That's right." Orga said, agreeing with his words, before turning to the rest of his squad. "…And just like usual, I'm going to have to depend on you guys again."

Orga closed his eyes and took a deep breath to center himself - then, when he opened his eyes again, it was with a determined gaze that he stared at each of the members of his squad straight in their eyes.

"Lend me your strength, and I'll find a way for us to finish this mission together alive and well." he swore. "We'll survive this. I promise all of you that."

There was a moment of surprise… then, smiles and grins were given to him for his declaration, the expression on their faces clear that they trusted him on that. Orga allowed himself a small smile on his face at the show of faith at him even as he felt the pressure of it all. He couldn't allow himself to lose any single one of them… more than what he already had, anyway.

"We'll be sure to kill all of them for you, Orga." Augus promised, his faith in him absolute as always. The others also stated their support for him… although not as ruthless as Augus had promised it.

In any case, Orga nodded, grateful for their trust in him. He was about to order the squad to wait and relax until things were ready, but it seems like preparations for their mechs were short.

In perfect timing as if they were waiting for them to finish their little moment (likely coincidence, as Orga knows they care little if push comes to shove), the door suddenly opened revealing the armed guard that escorted them earlier.

The man assessed them, then spoke. "Everything is ready. Get up those seats and follow us."

His squad did so. Before he followed them, Orga took another moment to glance at the tablet he was holding before he would leave it here. He double-checked for anything that he might've missed, even glancing at the more technical aspects with figures and statistics in it.

But that was when something immediately jumped at his attention - one that made his eyes go wide in shock, a reaction that was missed by everyone as they went on their way out.

It was a single line of information. Easily ignored, and definitely just put there for the sake of meticulousness instead of being anything important. Yet for him, it made his heart almost stop in its tracks.

He could never forget it. He had burned it in his mind, after all. And while it wasn't exactly the same, it was close enough for it to definitely matter.

Because, what Orga saw displayed on the file… It was, undoubtedly, the coordinates of where the mission will take place.

One that was very near to the coordinates he had memorized. They only needed around fifty kilometers or so of travel to get there, practically nothing for pilots like him once they rode a mech.

"…"

He was worried what would happen if he refused their invitation, but it turned out to be nothing because here it was, taunting him right in his face. And now, there was no excuse for his lack of freedom to hide behind.

"Orga?" Augus called out to him.

"…I'll be there. Just double-checking things."

Orga put the tablet down and quickly followed to catch up with the others. His face betrayed nothing about what he had just learned, yet his mind was filled with turbulent thoughts and emotions.

Things… certainly just turned complicated.


The mission had begun.

Orga's mind raced. Questions that he thought would no longer matter after today were once again in the forefront of his mind, eating him from the inside.

Even as they were led inside to their mechs and were put in the cockpit, despite being surrounded by heavy armor that even artillery shells couldn't penetrate which arguably made him in the safest places around - Orga felt as if he was at his most vulnerable.

Why is the mission taking place in those coordinates of all places? Does it mean that whoever that blonde man is and who they're working for predicted they would have a mission there? Or perhaps were they the ones responsible for this mission, influencing things without their employers even knowing?

Whatever it was though, they're definitely involved in this. He was sure of it. He had thought that there wasn't a choice due to his lack of freedom as a pilot, but perhaps this was the opportunity he'd been given to meet with their group.

Now, if only it didn't feel like he'd be walking in a trap…

"—Approaching destination." the sudden call out by one of his squad members penetrated his thoughts. "ETA: sixty seconds."

…No, this isn't the time for that.

Orga breathed in and centered himself. While recent revelations were disturbing, entertaining such worries would only impede his performance in battle. He'd worry about it later and focus more on making everyone here survive. Just as he had promised.

Right now, it was time to fight.

The Organic Interface Implant on his spine, connected to the mech's systems, fed him information that made it feel like it was simply an extension of his body. Vital information that was displayed on the gauges and monitors are interpreted intuitively. The surveillance sensors felt as if it was his eyes, the armored plates protecting him were like a second skin.

"I see the place." Orga said, spotting the secret facility in the distance. "Everyone, fan out and take your positions." he commanded.

With a flex of his will and a movement in the cockpit, Orga increased the thrust of his propulsion unit which accelerated him to greater speeds; enough that a kilometer was traversed in about a few seconds. Idly, he noticed the others behind him did the same.

When Orga arrived in his position, he killed the jets. His mech landed on its legs with a deep and heavy thud. The leftover momentum made him carve deep gouges in the ground, knock over some trees on the way and kick up a cloud of dirt and debris around him.

He slowed to a stop. For a short while his mech was hidden from view because of the dust cloud. Then, he stood straight up from the landing posture and walked out of it, allowing him to be in view once more.


Spoiler

Orga ran a self-diagnostic command to check if there were any problems after their rush to get here. The propulsion unit was at great temperatures but that was expected. Fuel reserves are also low, but not low enough that it couldn't be used for short bursts. Still, he doubted that he could go for a return trip.

"We're in position, Orga." Augus called in from his unit.

"Us too." Norba mirrored. "By the way, where are the rest? You told us that this was an extraction mission." he asked after a pause.

Altland grunted. "We probably got here faster than them."

"Really? But shouldn't they be rushing to get their stuff out right now? Our mission is to defend them until they finish, but from what I can see, not a single vehicle or person is around." Norba pointed out.

"…Indeed, it is strange." Eugene muttered in thought.

Orga frowned. The report did say that the mission was done urgently and should be accomplished as fast as it could, but the fact that none of the extractors are here in the first place is making that a bit complicated. Where the hell are they?

With that in mind, he radioed his superiors. "Command. This is Pilot Orga. We arrived at the destination, but none of the extraction personnel and units were present. What is their status?"

Orga waited for an answer. Then, after a few seconds or so, he received a reply.

"This is Command. Extraction units are on their way. Just wait and defend the objective."

"How long will that take?" Orga asked.

"Just wait. They'll arrive."

Orga's eyes narrowed at the brusque tone of the operator before they cut the line. He was used to being treated like nothing, but them acting this unprofessional during a mission was few and far between. Especially when they weren't given any reason to. Suddenly, he was reminded by Augus' comment about others being more aggressive towards them.

Before he could fully reflect on that however, a warning from another unit grabbed his full attention.

"They're here! Enemies, approaching from the northeast!"

"How many?" Orga quickly asked.

"At least twenty…no, twenty-five!"

That was too many for them to handle on their own. He quickly moved to assist. "Augus, Altland. With me! The rest defend the other sides and support from a distance!" he commanded.

His mech flew through the air as he willed the propulsion unit jetted him through the air once more. He quickly arrived at the destination and spotted the enemies making contact with his squad members.


Spoiler

One spotted him flying through the air and aimed their weapon at him, but he was faster on the draw. Orga fired his weapon, an armor-penetrating submachine gun, to the enemy mech. The resounding boom of the firearm that was more artillery than gun echoed as it fired.

The shells hit the mech's center of mass and punched through the steel easily like it was nothing. The shot mech fell to the ground and crashed heavily, unable to carry its own weight. Then, bright arcs of electricity jutted out of it before exploding, taking the life of its pilot with it.

The other mechs around the one he took down moved to turn to him. It was a clunky and awkward movement - a consequence of being a pilot without implants like them - and he moved to capitalize on that weakness. The moment he landed on the ground he had fired three more shots and hit the enemy mechs in their most vulnerable areas, defeating them.

More explosions around him. His radar registered the friendly units in his vicinity. It seems like his other squad members had arrived along with their units.

"Take care of the enemies. Make sure to save your ammo and fuel while doing so." Orga ordered. "We could be staying here as long as a few hours—"

He raised his shoulder when he saw an enemy aim at him from the side, and the shell from its firearm hit his shoulder plate instead of his head. Orga grit his mouth as the implant translated the hit as pain, but he shrugged it off and shot the mech with payback in mind.

"…So make sure that you'll still be able to fight or retreat after this." Orga finished.

"I'll keep that in mind." Altland grunted as he engaged with the enemy. "Thirteen left. Dealt with five myself."

"Twelve, you mean." Augus calmly replied, followed by an audible explosion. The teen had just finished cutting an enemy in half with a knife - a dedicated melee weapon he preferred. "One was still moving when you left it. As an aside, I also dealt with six."

His own mech then kept ducking and weaving through the shots fired at him by the remaining enemies, his propulsion units activating in bursts for him to hover and skate around the battlefield. Orga shot his own firearm as he did so, granting him more kills as well as the enemy pilots were unable to keep up.

Like he observed earlier, these pilots are all likely trained soldiers and not given implants like them. The difference shows in how easily his squad took care of it. They reacted faster, and intuitively moved with their mechs as opposed to their enemies, who relied on manual and AI-assisted controls.

And from what he could tell, the enemy mechs were constructed in a more shabby manner as well. Orga and his squad's mechs moved with far greater mobility, had better firepower, and took more punishment. But considering their enemies are trying to steal from their employers - the company who introduced these mechs in the first place - it was clear that they were creating inferior products and stealing the designs.

But despite all that, they're still undeniably dangerous. Orga had no plans on underestimating them and dying because of it.

"Focus. You can compare body count after this is over." Orga ordered, before pausing when he heard an explosion from farther away. "Other units, what was that? Report." he barked.

"Something just fired at us. More mechs coming in. This one from the south." Eugene replied. "My radar is reading… twenty two. Norba and I will deal with them."

"—Enemy reinforcements here as well!" a female pilot in his unit also reported. "I spot eight more coming in the horizon!"

Orga turned his head and witnessed more mechs approaching them from a distance. More mechs, their models similar to the ones they have defeated. Suddenly, Orga thought that with how easily they beat them, the reason might have been because they focused their design on quantity instead of quality. He had a sneaking suspicion that their enemies have many of these to spare if that was the case.

"That's a lot. They must really want to have this place." Norba muttered in comms. "Still, that's not the problem, isn't it? Orga, where the hell are the extractors?" he growled. "They're still not here! How long are they gonna make us wait!?"

He was wondering about that himself. He thought they'd have arrived by now. The fact that they still haven't arrived speaks to their incompetence. And so, in the middle of firing the approaching mechs, he radioed his superiors once more.

"Command. This is Pilot Orga. " he reported with a clipped tone that he tried to mask. "We've already engaged with the enemy. Where are the extraction units?"

There was a tense few seconds as he waited for an answer.

"They're on their way."

His brow twitched from the vague reply. "…Sir, if you could give me a more specific timeframe, then that would be appreciated."

"Duly noted." the operator replied dryly.

"And you still wouldn't tell us?"

He heard a tongue click on the other side of the line.

"They are on their way. That is all you need to know, pilot."

…Orga grit his teeth. They've never done this, never acted in a way that jeopardizes the mission. His patience was already wearing thin. And perhaps because of the stress of everything else - something inside him snapped.

"Like hell it is!" Orga exploded, unable to contain his frustration as he kept firing his gun. They were engaging with the enemy now, and focusing on the combat and talking to the operator made it difficult to control his emotions. "Tell us when they'll get here, or better yet, tell them to hurry up! We're going to get overrun at this rate!"

"You think you can mouth off a superior like that?" the operator suddenly warned. "I'll report this."

He paused at what he just heard.

"…What? Are you fucking serious?"

Sheer incredulity filled him with how the operator acted offended of all things. Being ignored or treated as just a tool of war, he could tolerate. But thinking themselves better and demanding respect, despite the fact that they stay somewhere safe behind Orga and his squad, as they risked their lives and fought their battles for them?

He couldn't ignore that. Not even if they were in the middle of a mission.

"Are you looking down on us so much that your head got stuck in your ass?" Orga shouted. "I don't see you risking your life fighting here! You're just an operator! If you want respect, then tell us what is happening and do your fucking job!"

"What the hell did you just say to me, pilot?" the man growled.

"You fucking heard me. Tell us what's happening. Otherwise, I'll find you after this and there will be hell to pay. I'll beat the shit out of you. I swear to that, no matter what happens to me right after." Orga snarled back. "And I doubt that my other superiors would fault me for it. After all, if you couldn't even act like a proper operator for us pilots, then you're nothing but a useless piece shit."

It seems like that had been the breaking point for the entitled bastard on the other side of the line, as he started to snarl at him as well.

"Oh, is that what you think? Too bad. You won't have a chance to return at all."

A sudden chill went down his spine at those words.

"…What the hell did you just say?"

"What, you didn't know? I guess you wouldn't." the operator sneered. "There's no extraction mission! It's all a ruse since you're left there as bait. You're not getting back here to beat me up, or whatever you threatened to do."

He spoke of the horrifying truth of what was happening so casually, contempt dripping in his tone as he did so. With wide eyes, Orga listened in his cockpit unheeding of everything else in the battlefield, the words stunning him more than any of his enemy's attacks ever could.

"You're already outdated wares, you stupid kids. With the death of the head researcher a lot has changed. And we're already working on your replacements." the man told him, each sentence pounding him in his brain. "Now, all we need to do is to take out the trash. And what better use than to trick thieves into thinking that a facility without anything actually has something important?"

Orga breathed in sharply. "You…!"

"You were left there to die, pilot. That's all there is." the man declared with finality. "Now, leave me alone. I have better things to do than babysit kids. At least I'll have a promotion after this is finally over."

With that, the operator cut the line.

He doubted that he would be hearing from the operator ever again.

"—Orga, look out!"

A shout from Augus warned him of an enemy aiming a gun at him from the side. Orga realized that at some point, he had stopped fighting entirely and just stood there. He looked at it in shock, but was thankfully saved when his sworn brother shot the mech before it could to him.

"What are you doing, Orga? You've stopped moving and suddenly gone quiet!" Altland scolded him. "You told us to focus but you're not doing it yourself! Is this how a leader is supposed to act!?"

His squad member had a point. And perhaps normally he would scold himself for it.

But right now, he was far from worrying about that.

"Damn it…"

With the operator's words, Orga's mind, which had been feeling like there was something important he was missing in the current situation, finally connected the dots.

Information mentioned earlier in passing, something he thought were all previously unrelated and not even important, all turned into crucial information that allowed him to construct an idea of what was happening.

"I've heard some rumors that they've added more 'orphans' to join us… maybe they're starting to understand our usefulness here."

Augus' earlier statement about rumors of more 'orphans' besides them… it wasn't that their employers finally understood their importance, but rather they were being replaced. They've gone from valuable assets to now being disposable. And the attitudes of the others around them reflected that.

"There will be changes to procedures due to the newly instated heads. I don't know how you kids used to run things during missions, but expect that things might be different this time."

Then, there were the changes and reforms made because of the death of the head researcher and his retinue. He had firsthand seen the politics in the company he was working at from his few interactions with his higher ups. He wasn't familiar with their ways, nor did he want to be, but he could imagine how those new in power wanted to remove the influence of their predecessor, or perhaps to surpass him and prove themselves worthy in the eyes of others.

Outdated wares. That operator called us outdated wares. We were the prized cow of the previous head researcher… and with us gone, the new heads could replace it with their own.

—They were all caught up into a web of politics, treated as pieces of a now failed player. And with the player's disappearance, they were going to be thrown away to make room for others.

…Orga didn't expect them to do something like that so fast. Or act so wasteful. He'd have thought that having fought for quite a few years already and being subjected to various implants, they would be treated with more value instead of just being thrown away like trash along with their mechs.

Truly, it was the ruthlessness he had expected from adults. Did they do this out of stupidity perhaps? He was a veteran in all rights - could those paper-pushers and researchers not see how that made them valuable? Or were the replacements something they were really confident in, that their experience means nothing at all?

But whatever the answer… he knew that didn't matter. In the end, their current predicament wouldn't change.

"Orga! Orga, speak to us! What's happening!?" from the edges of his hearing, he could hear Norba shout in worry. "Did you speak with Command? Why are the extraction units still not here!? We've already been here for half an hour and there's still going to be more reinforcements coming in! Where are they!?"

The sentiment was mirrored with the rest of the squad. There were still no casualties, but that was only a matter of time. He could feel the anxiety of others when he went silent, uncharacteristic of his usual self.

But, as usual, their smartest had managed to realize what had been going on.

"…O-Orga, this…" Eugene muttered, horror slowly creeping in his tone. "No one is coming for us, is there?"

A heavy silence settled in the comms at that. Stating it out loud was something that he didn't want but the damage has been done. And while his squad members may have no idea the cause of what was happening, the results of it were still obvious to anyone in here.

And his lack of reply was the only confirmation they needed.

Orga knew firsthand that there are various ways his squad would react to it. None of it was truly voiced, perhaps because of the sheer shock from this revelation. One of them, however, voiced about what they all felt. It was said in a whisper but they might as well just have shouted it with how it cut through the din of everyone's minds.

"Are we going to die?"

Orga gritted his teeth and gripped his mech's controls tight.

"—No." he growled. "We're not going to die."

But before anyone could say anything else, he spoke those words.

He wouldn't accept that. He had promised they'd live together. And he wouldn't fail them now.

Perhaps things would truly be hopeless on any other occasion. In another world, this might be they're last stand. But right now, there was one thing. One thing that doesn't fit to it all, yet with this recent revelation, made him realize what it really was.

That note given to him in that gala… it wasn't a request nor a choice that Orga could decide on.

Instead, it was a warning. And also an opportunity.

"Abandon your posts! To hell with this mission! We're not going to die for those pieces of trash!" Orga shouted, determination filling his veins. "All units, cover each other and retreat! Then follow the coordinates I'll send to you! We're taking this somewhere else!"

His sudden order preceded whatever that would've happened from a broken morale. His squad thankfully latched onto his orders instead giving into despair, and they quickly moved their mechs to retreat. Orga went last to cover for the rest, before moving on.

Their enemies were clearly befuddled by their actions, considering they had essentially abandoned the place they were protecting. There was a short pause as they likely relayed what was happening to their superiors before a large group detached to move and capture the now vulnerable facility. The others meanwhile moved to chase them.

Orga clicked his tongue before moving to retreat like the rest, taking care to avoid the potshots aimed on his way. He hoped that they'd ignore them all entirely.

"Orga, where are we going?" Augus asked privately through the comms.

"Somewhere safe." he answered back. "We're going to die if we stay there."

"Yes, but at this rate…"

Orga exhaled.

"I know."

His Organic Interface Implant made him intuitively understand it more than anything. It was like in the back of his mind, warning him of what was to come if he and his squad continued what he was doing.

There were warnings that alerted him of his mech getting farther away from their objective. They were meant to defend it after all, and the fact that they weren't doing it is an important matter. It was a clear case of disobedience to their superiors, despite them betraying Orga and his squad first. And that was unacceptable.

Pilots like them were made to be tools. But still, they were humans that can make their own choices. And being able to pilot a weapon of war clearly meant that restrictions had to be put into place.

"M-My gun is unresponsive!" one female pilot shouted after a few kilometers of travel.

He clicked his tongue. It was starting.

"Protect her!" Orga shouted, before addressing the pilot. "And you, throw the gun away and keep moving!"

Their answer to potential disobedience? Make the AI of the mech stop them from doing certain things. Going out of bounds is discouraged, with some of the functions shutting off if they went too far from the objective. It was the same mechanism that stopped them from hitting 'friendlies' as well, making them unable to fire or even move a limb to hit them. It was why they weren't just able to kill his employers once they were put in the cockpit, because if it wasn't for it, then he would've probably done it long ago.

Put enough distance away from the objective and the mech will be unable to move entirely, although it would take about a hundred kilometers away or so. He was thankful that they weren't hard-coded to stop at a closer point but certain situations in the past must have proved that it was detrimental. Said certain situations also require special consideration, and that was when they usually needed to talk to the operator to request for the restrictions to be lifted.

Unfortunately, they had nothing like that now. He doubted the operator would answer nor even entertain his request.

"If your arms and guns stop working, keep running! If someone's legs stop moving, then carry them!" Orga kept shouting. "We're going to get out of this!"

The coordinates were now just a few kilometers away. The coordinates themselves were within the boundaries of the desertion restriction, likely taken into account by those who wanted them there. Still, they'd be slowed to a crawl at that point. They had a good lead from the enemy's inferior-made mechs, but with the restrictions in place, they'd eventually catch up.

They persevered. And eventually, it paid off as they reached it. However…

"I see it." Augus said through the comms. "It's… a coast?"

Indeed, what they were looking at was not a secret facility or anything that he would've expected. It was just a simple coast with no sight of anything man-made. It looked untouched by everything in the war. If their salvation was there, then it didn't look like it.

"What the hell are we going to do here!?" Norba shouted incredulously.

He didn't know. But they had no choice at this point.

"Just keep moving!" Orga shouted, keeping up a strong image. "That's where everything will be!"

"…Ahh, damn it all!" the young man shouted. "I swear if this is nothing, then I'll beat you up - you hear me Orga!?"

They moved. And just as he predicted, the restrictions were reaching in its fullest form. Their movements slowed to a point where they couldn't even walk a single step properly. A few had fallen to the ground, crashing heavily. Most couldn't even move. None of them could shoot their guns.

They were helpless.

And the enemy finally caught up. Behind them, he could hear the thrusters of the mechs as they finally arrived at their position. Orga could barely even turn his own mech to look back and stare at their would-be killers approaching them.

"So this is it, huh…? What the hell did we even go here for?" Altland muttered through the comms.

"At least the view is good." Eugene chucked, his macabre humor shining through. "Would've liked to swim on a beach for the first time in my life before I die though."

"That can't be right. Orga wouldn't want that to happen. He promised us." Augus defended him. "We're here for a reason aren't we, Orga…?"

He wanted to say yes. He wanted to convince himself of the fact as well.

But he didn't know. This was all a gamble - chasing the slightest chance for their survival when everything has gone wrong. But all they got was this coast with nothing in it.

Was there something supposed to be here? Did he miss whatever it was? Was he supposed to get here earlier, or later? Or worse, could he have mistakenly remembered the wrong coordinates entirely?

In the end, Orga could only ask those questions, wondering if he really did just lead them to a useless death.

…

…But it seems like he didn't need to wonder about it, after all.

Orga's eyes widened as one of the mechs landed on the ground - before an earth-shattering explosion suddenly engulfed it, destroying it fully. The others stopped as if in shock of what happened, before they too were engulfed by explosions.

"What the hell!?" Altland shouted bewilderedly, and the others also shared the same sentiment.

Bombs. Orga thought. There were bombs around the place.

Those that weren't caught up by the bombs or didn't get damaged much looked around for their enemies. They appeared in the form of rocket-propelled grenades that launched from somewhere within the trees. The explosive projectiles hit their large targets - not quite destroying them because they weren't artillery grade weapons - but still damaging them severely because of their inferior make.

Some of the mechs tried to shoot back from where it came from. However, their weapons were meant for obvious, heavy targets - kind of like armored vehicles or other mechs like them. Using it on infantry who made use of the dense forest terrain as cover and easily scattered was less than ideal.

"Orga, these people… were they who you were waiting for?" Augus asked in shock as they watched this new group engage with their enemies.

"Yeah, they are." he grunted, watching the situation with observant eyes.

He frowned at what he was seeing. While Orga was shocked and relieved at the sight of reinforcements, it was clear that it wasn't enough. There were still quite a few of the mechs remaining. Unless they were able to deal with that, then everything would be useless.

—But then came the last surprise.

There was a great splash from behind, and when Orga turned to look, he saw the sea parting as it made way for something gargantuan. Far out, a humanoid figure stood up from the deeper parts of the coastal waters, seawater gushing out of its parts like a torrential waterfall.

His eyes widened. Because what he was looking at…

It was definitely another mech.


Spoiler

Its eyes shined with blue light, targeting the remaining enemy mechs who reeled in surprise. But before they could do anything, the new mech suddenly activated its thrusters which kicked up a large wave behind it while quickly propelling it forwards, before it leveled its own gun at them.

Staccato gunfire echoed. Each payload from its firearm was like a death sentence. They punched through the mech's armors cleanly like his own weapon, and they were easily destroyed as the mech caught fire and exploded from damaged components.

Orga watched, mesmerized as their enemies were made short work of. He could see from the movements that their pilots also lacked the implants, but the ambush with the bombs and RPGs served as a great equalizer to the mechs outnumbering them. Eventually, all mechs were defeated, leaving only this new mech and Orga's squad.

And just like that, they were saved.

"Hello, is this on? It should be…" an unknown woman's voice began to speak in his private comms. It was when the mech had turned to his direction that he realized that he was speaking to the pilot of the mech that saved them. "Greetings. You would be Orga, correct?"

He realized that his throat was dry, and he resisted the urge to gulp down.

"Yeah. I am." he finally answered.

"I see. Then, the operation went exactly as planned. To think we'll get this many mechs as well… as expected of the Boss." the woman chuckled. It was with a mixed tone that she did so, one that showed awe and fear. He wondered why that is, before thinking he might be better off not knowing. "From what I understand you're interested in joining us?"

"…Yeah."

"Then, we give you our warmest welcome." she said. "Now, we'll have to move quickly. I believe that we have some people that can remove the restrictions in those mechs of yours. Then we'll haul those in the ship once it gets here."

As the woman continued to explain what they were going to do, Orga realized that whatever this group was, they planned for this whole thing to happen. From assassinating the head researcher and general, to influencing even their employers as well as their enemies…

As far as they're employers knew, they're unmoving mechs indicated they were defeated. They'd probably be thinking they were captured or something. Their enemies wouldn't be thinking the same, but it's not like they would be telling their employers that either. But for them - they were in the perfect position to disappear.

They were all masterfully manipulated, and all that stemmed from a single meeting in that gala.

There were plenty of questions that floated in Orga's mind as of late, but now, there was only one. One that only truly mattered.

What in the hell did they get themselves into?


…Seems like the mech pilot and his group finally got involved with us mischievous bunch.

I walked in the ship's hallway. The ship had exploded into action and was as busy as it could get due to recent events, but people still greeted me or gave me nods of respect, recognizing me as their super mysterious benefactor due to my super mysterious cloak that I usually garbed myself in.

It's like an identifier for us at this point. Kinda like those goofily-dressed guys in that punch ghost setting, but more tame. The world did like to emphasize characters with more importance by giving them distinct appearances, and this was just an extension of that.

In any case, everyone seemed to have their hands full as I passed by. I took it as a sign of everything going well.

The moment the fight was finished, we had quickly docked our ship on the coast and hauled the mechs inside the hull using the heavy machinery available to us and our own mech. Removing the wares of those smugglers made more than enough space for their whole group, with some to spare for the remaining intact mech parts we salvaged from their enemies.

And just like that, we finally have lots of mechs on our end. Furthermore, I could probably fix some of those me parts and make another one. We do have many potential pilots here after all.

Just as planned by our leader, as the others say. Her legend grows more and more.

Anyhow, while this was happening, I was officially 'out' making things smooth in the sidelines. And it was true - I did help the transition of the mech pilot's group into their masters into joining ours a smooth one. Little events were influenced to lead to this situation, and as far as he knew it was luck that prevented anyone from dying, not knowing I had something to do with it.

I also helped out a few enemy pilots that were actually decent here and there. I infiltrated both their enemies and the people they're working for, after all. Narratively, those pilots survived the crash and would probably live out to some peaceful village or some other war survivor story.

And now, once the mech pilot's group was comfortable in the ship, I took the opportunity to 'return' with one of my clones present and get out of my disguise.

I was currently going on my way to the ship's bridge. The mech pilot was there talking with V now that he planned to join our group, while the rest of his squad mingled with the others. I doubt he's comfortable right now, with how much of a conversation partner that emotionless blonde is.

"—Say, did you meet those mech pilots, Azee?"

As I walked towards the place however, I heard interesting people hanging around nearby the destination itself. Three women, one of them being Amida who was taking a smoke, and the other two… Ah, they would be the trusted people of our forewoman. Lafter and Azee, if I remember correctly.

"I did, but I didn't interact much. I was too busy with other things." the white-haired woman answered. "Why, what about them?"

"Well, it's just that they're clearly all younger than us. I just finished talking to a girl with them and she couldn't be more than fourteen. I wonder what the people they're working for are thinking, sending those kids to fight for them?" the twin-tailed woman asked with a frown.

There was a pause. "I'm thinking they don't care. From what I heard from them, their group was treated like nothing by their employers. Or masters, to be more accurate. Apparently, the reason why they joined now was because they were sent to die as bait for their enemies."

"…Things really are getting worse for this place, huh?"

"It's not like we haven't seen them drafting teenagers into war, though. At this point, age is just a meaningless number." Azee pointed out. "The Boss is as young or younger than we are, but you've seen how scary she is."

Lafter frowned. "I guess you have a point. Still, I can't help but feel ashamed. We're the adults here and yet we leave the fighting to those younger than us…"

"—You don't have to feel that way. I doubt they'd appreciate that." Amida suddenly interrupted them both. "They're all adults in their own right. Just treat them with the respect they deserve. Doing more would just be patronizing and insulting."

Both women blinked at her words. "You really think so? But…" Azee trailed off.

Amida shrugged. "That was what their leader said in his own words. And I have to say, I have to agree with him. All of them have this steel inside of them that most adults don't even have." she puffed a smoke with her cigarette, and continued. "It was already horrifying for us when we tried to cross warzones, so imagine fighting in the thick of it all like they did. Younger than us or not, they're definitely people to be respected."

Her statement was met with thoughtful expressions of the two.

"Hmm… I guess that makes sense. Maybe age really is just a number." Lafter said, a smile slowly growing on her face. "But if we're thinking that way… you know, one of them looks like my type. That big, burly pilot with them? Definitely caught my eye. And he looks like he's not that younger than me too." she hummed. "Maybe I should hang out with him?"

Azee choked beside her, before glaring at the twin-tailed woman. "W-Wha—? Are you serious? You're really thinking about that now?" she asked incredulously.

"What? What's wrong about it? Am I not allowed to think that?" Lafter gave her a smirk. "Plus, I don't think you're in any position to talk. Don't think that I didn't notice you appreciating the Boss' second-in-command too. Not that I blame you though, he's definitely my type as well. And killing those smugglers definitely gave him lots of points."

"Y-You…" Azee hissed. Her usual blank expression that I've associated with her, which was similar but not quite on the level of V's, broke slightly and gave way to a slight blush. "I don't know what you're talking about."

"Really? You really don't?" Lafter elbowed the white-haired woman with a grin, making her receive an annoyed expression. "Guess it's more for me then~!" she teased.

"S-Stop that!"

Amida sighed. "You two should really quiet down. You guys are making a scene."

"She's right, you know."

They all stiffened when I interrupted, finally reaching where they were. The two women who were talking about me in particular stared with their eyes and mouth wide, clearly not expecting me to be around after being a subject of their flattering talk.

"E-Eh!? S-S-Since when were you…?" Lafter stuttered nervously.

I shrugged. "Caught the last part, I'm afraid. I'll keep it a secret though. Don't worry." I reassured them, but a high-pitched noise from her indicated she didn't feel reassured at all.

Azee, meanwhile, was losing her cool. "I— W-We, we weren't…"

I gave them a deadpan look. What's with these people? Last I checked, this was a war setting, not a school one. So why are they acting like a bunch of shy school girls?

"It's fine." I reassured them again, a touch exasperated this time. Then, I tilted my head in consideration, before speaking once more. "As an aside though, I'll also say that I find you two quite beautiful. That makes us all even. So there's no need to act like that."

The two women looked speechless at my words - and then reddened, blushing intensely from my compliment and from the sheer embarrassment from being caught earlier. They turned away from my gaze, with Lafter looking to the side and Azee palming her face, both women unable to speak or even look at me straight.

Amida looked at them and took pity. She then turned to me, giving me a nod. "It's nice to see you back. I assume you're here to talk with Orga and the Boss?" she asked.

"I am. I hope things went smoothly?"

Amida nodded. "Yes, everything went as the Boss said it would."

"That's great to hear. Now we have more mechs, and with the parts we obtained we could probably construct some more…" I trailed off, before turning to the two women. "Say, you two. Are you interested in being pilots?"

They both blinked, embarrassment momentarily forgotten.

"E-Eh? What?" Lafter said in shock.

"I was offering if you wanted to be the pilots from the mechs we could make." I repeated with a shrug.

With how they're connected to Amida, they likely shared the same backstory and motivation as she did. And as a consequence, they would have the same potential as the tanned woman has. All they need is a little bit of character growth and a training montage to be skilled. That's what I did with Amida, and she turned out great.

"I'll do it." the white-haired woman instantly accepted with a determined expression. "I want to help Amida when it comes to a fight."

"…I guess I feel the same way." the twin-tailed woman followed after recovering from her shock. "I'm in this too."

"You two… you don't have to do this." Amida looked conflicted, likely unable to decide whether to feel touched or worried about their desire to fight with her. Still, a hard look from both of them made her back down.

"We've already remained here with you even when we could've left all this behind. What makes you think we'll leave you fighting without us?" Lafter asked rhetorically with a smile.

Azee nodded. "We owe you too much for that."

Amida stared at both women, before letting out a sigh. "…Fine. Suit yourselves."

I smiled at the sight. Touching, but in the end they don't need to worry. I'll make this as bloodless as I could after all, even if the remaining themes of the genre are the same. Not a single innocent or undeserving person would die - and that included these people right in front of me.

They'll get their good ending. I'll make sure of it.

"Very well. I suppose you two will be pilots once those intact parts are repaired and assembled. I request that you find other volunteers who want to fight in mechs as well. There's quite a lot of those parts, after all." I said to them.

"We'll ask around." Amida said with a nod of her head.

"Thank you." I started to walk past them, but stopped right before passing Amida. "Oh, and before I forget—"

I put a hand on the tanned woman's shoulder. She was startled for a bit at my action before relaxing when she realized what I was doing. Still, Amida looked at me in great surprise, and I gave the woman a smile.

"—You've done great, Amida. You were incredible out there." I said, sincerely praising her for efforts.

The woman's eyes widened, and her cheeks reddened from my compliment in a similar manner from the two women earlier. The woman then nodded her head in thanks, grumbling something inaudibly out of embarrassment.

"U-Um, thanks." she muttered.

I gave her a final smile. And with that, I resumed walking to make my way to my destination. As I left behind the group though, I heard them mutter a few things that I managed to catch with my sharp hearing.

"Amida… could it be your type is also—?"

"Shut up. Both of you."

…I'm going to go ahead and ignore that.

With that said, after walking a bit further, I finally arrived on the bridge. I knocked on the door for politeness' sake, before opening it and entering inside. The only two people there turned to me - one of which was already aware of my presence even before I opened the door, and the other, reacting more with surprise.

Orga stood up from his seat. "You're… It's you. From the gala."

"It's great to see you again, Orga." I greeted him amicably.

"You've returned." V stated behind her usual desk, keeping up the facade that I was gone doing something. "Did everything go well?"

"Yes, everything went as well as it could've been. As expected of you, 'Boss'." I praised, much like how everyone was doing so after the success of this mission. "Things went just as you planned."

The woman looked as blank as ever, but a sharp eye from that of the supernatural or the drama genre could notice the slight twitch of her eyebrow. She really didn't like it when I referred to her as my superior. She's been so used to acting like a slave in her life that being treated as a superior was something she wasn't used to. Even just being complimented makes her squirm.

I'm not a person who would needlessly tease someone, but I made an exception for this. This was one of the most harmless ways to break the conditioning she was subjected to her whole life. And the woman certainly needs more opportunities to emote.

In other words, therapeutic bullying. Helps that her reactions are sorta cute too.

"…No thanks to your part." V said, trying to brush off the praise.

"Ah, but it pales in comparison to your greatness." I embellished, making her twitch again. Then, I looked at Orga who glanced at V with an unreadable expression, clearly thinking of her as some mastermind. "But more importantly, I see that both of you have acquainted yourselves already - I hoped I didn't interrupt you two, Orga?"

The mech pilot stiffened from suddenly being addressed but he swiftly recovered to answer. Still, I saw him gain an uncertain look as he considered my question. I suppose it's because they weren't really 'talking' before I came here.

"I… I was just asking a few questions to your boss… or rather, I suppose it's going to be my boss now." he answered, before pausing. "…You guys are really planning to stop the war?" he asked me.

"Yes. That is what this organization is all about."

"You all must be confident in doing it then. But I suppose I can't deny it with how easily you assassinated the head researcher and his retinue. Or how you manipulated things so that we could meet this way." he muttered, sitting back down in his seat. "Oh well. With how things are, we literally have no choice but to join here. It's not like we can go anywhere else at this point."

I hummed. "I think you have the wrong idea. You can refuse, you know? We're not forcing our members to join us here." I said, clarifying his situation. "If you do so, we give you a way out of this place and you move on with your lives, leaving all the fighting behind. We'll even give you some help, something to prop you up when starting your new lives."

The mech pilot looked doubtful. "Really now?"

"You can ask around the place. Everyone joined out of their free will." I said with a shrug. "We've done this to others, so why would you be an exception?"

His eyes narrowed. "Because we're pilots. Weapons. Tools of war."

"And there are plenty of others like that. Your refusal will not be a setback." I responded simply.

And it was true. The reason why we were doing this in the first place was to only provide a way for things to be consistent in the story. If they refuse, I can find other people willing to pilot it. Or perhaps, I'll pilot it with other identities. Both are pretty much the same in the eyes of the story if done properly.

"But the thing is…"

I stared at the mech pilot's hard eyes. His gaze was one that blazed with anger and ideals. Just like the rest of the people in this ship, our aims and goals - it all spoke to his heart. It was these qualities that led me to him in the first place. His unique qualities make him a great addition to the group.

"…You wouldn't refuse this at all, would you?"

A seinen and shounen mix. Idealism, tempered with reality. They make the most compelling characters, especially for a war setting like this.

Orga gritted his teeth at my words. "I know you're manipulating me. With how you've manipulated everything else, I'm pretty sure that this is all part of your plan. You did all of this pretty much thinking that I'll join your merry little band as if it's to be expected already. I don't like it one bit."

The mech pilot looked down to his hands, glaring hard at it… then, he sighed.

"…And I can't believe I'm falling for all this. I can't even muster the desire to refuse. Even out of spite, I couldn't." he chuckled mirthlessly. "I must be an idiot, throwing away the chance to live a peaceful life for more fighting."

"You'll find similar idiots in this ship, Orga." I said with a smile.

The mech pilot went quiet at that, getting his thoughts in order as he sat on his chair. Then, after a while, the young man spoke once more.

"…I can't speak for the others, but fine, I'll join." he said, before glaring at me and V. "But I'm going to warn you. I don't care if you saved us - if I find out that you're lying with what you're doing, then I'm calling it quits. And we're not going to be following orders that'll kill us either."

"That goes without saying. You're going to command the entire mech units that we have, after all. You'll be given authority and would be joining us when making plans during an operation."

He blinked in surprise, before recovering. "…I see. That's good. " he said with a nod of his head. "Then, with this, I'll be helping your… organization, to stop the war." he paused. "What did you call yourselves again? I never did find out."

I could feel V glance at me discreetly from that. I've avoided providing a name for our mysterious organization this whole time, after all. And while I could let it remain unnamed, there is power and weight in names, and I don't just mean that in a metaphorical sense.

This world did like things being poetic.

I glanced at the blonde. Yeah, I think that I have the perfect name for our little group.

"Golden Dawn."

The mech pilot blinked. And despite the blank face of the emotionless blonde, I could still feel her confusion behind it as she stared at me behind her table.

"Golden… Dawn?" Orga asked.

"Yes. That's the name of our group." I answered.

I suppose the confusion is understandable. It did come a bit from nowhere. Still, it was the perfect fit for this context. With everything we need already attained, and only needing a few more preparations on my part, we're already approaching the turning point in our plan. Such a name describes it perfectly.

Why was that the case, one might ask?

I smiled.

"—That's going to be the time it takes to end this war, after all."
