Wow, who's this guy again?



Chapter 23

In anime world, historical transitions are complicated.

The world, being such a mess of genres, means that things don't go as linearly as one might imagine. Attempting to force a change in such a large area is harder than it looks. After all, that area houses a lot of different stories happening altogether.

A historical transition is in essence a change of settings; It touches on a hodgepodge storylines that manages to not interact with each other due to increasingly contrived reasons from a country-wide to a global scale. This means that a historical transition, something acknowledged by everyone, has to touch every single different setting present in the area the change itself encompasses.

In short: if you want something to change on a large scale, then it has to make sense for the stories involved. Otherwise it wouldn't work, and things would go back to how it usually is.

So how do historical transitions happen then? How can a place change if all stories had to be taken into account for it to occur? After all, the world is slowly heading to a post-apocalyptic setting. There must be some condition for it to spontaneously take place or else this world will remain static.

The answer is simple. There just has to be enough stories for it to result that way.

The world is controlled by the narrative. But the narrative follows specific rules, and like any system which has a set of rules like classical and quantum physics - it follows the principle of least action, or in other words, 'takes the path of least resistance'.

So to make the setting change as a whole, many of the larger and more influential stories need to be steered into the direction of the desired change. Then once that happens, the others will follow. Because the only way to change the world in such a large way is to make it change itself.

And that's what we need to end the war.

…Though, there are some things to take note of.

Consider the following situations.

I could kill as many key officials or powerful people as I want. In fact, I could have easily done it during that time at the Gala. If I had chosen to install a bomb instead of having V shoot select people, then I could have eliminated enough people to affect the war effort. Logically, it works… but that isn't enough for the narrative, since the war would just continue on without them, or perhaps they would be replaced with people in similar roles.

I could also completely annihilate one side without care just so someone would win already. But more than likely, it would result in a complete asspull on the other side. Unexplainable events will usually result in unexplained measures by the narrative after all. And then, new elements would be introduced to explain that. Which follows with things spiralling out of control.

There are also other methods I can do. From efficient large-scale hypnosis to control every person in the nation, making them stop the war, to maybe something more outlandish like confiscating all weapons present so that no one can shoot or blow up each other anymore.

All hard stops to the current situation. A Deus ex Machina solution that came out of nowhere, resulting in an overall bad story in general. And of course, this wouldn't be accepted by the narrative itself. If I do something remotely similarly drastic to that, the world will stop my actions from taking effect.

So to make any effective changes, it must make sense narratively.

For the war to truly end, there must be an effective precedent. A perfectly reasonable cause, and something that would probably occur in the future naturally, with the only difference being the fact that we sped it up a bit and made it more certain to win.

That is the heart of why this organization, Golden Dawn, was created. It was a vessel to shift the narrative to our desired destination, embodying itself as the idea which, thematically and historically, makes sense after the tragedy and horror of a long-enduring war because of untouchable tyrants.

By that, I meant a single thing.

—Revolution.

…And then, it was decided.

The only thing needed to be done was to set the board, and once things were put into motion - every piece would easily and smoothly fall into place.

A preparation for the play that is to be.

"Hey… Did you hear about the rumors?"

It was honestly easy to gather support.

I am an out of context problem who can freely act in settings they do not belong in. My vast array of skills and abilities are abused to the unsuspecting populace so that they will be persuaded to join. They had no chance of dealing with it, and it's likely that they wouldn't even want to.

"There are whispers. About a group you can join."

Men and women, along with many of my own clones, blended among the people. We helped and took in the poor and the powerless. We sowed discontent, formed secret societies, and spread the word. We convinced those who are unwilling, struck by fear and cynicism, and gave them courage to let them join the cause.

I knew where to strike and how hard it needed to be, inserting myself into the countless storylines and skillfully guiding their narratives to align with what I wanted.

"They say that these people… they want to end the war."

Time went by. And our group grew.

Refugees, whose lives were upended and forced to traverse the battlefield, found themselves given the choice to truly leave it all behind and live a new life. Or to fight the very cause of their suffering.

Oppressed citizens, who live under the shadow of the elite, are given the chance to truly express their discontent and the opportunity to live in a far better place. Or to bring down the oppressors that trample on them for their own gain.

Sympathizers in power, who had lived far too long in war, are emboldened to finally stop the madness happening in the country. For them, it was an opportunity for a long-sought peace. But others also see a chance to steal power from the existing regime.

People joined, either forced due to their circumstance or out of their free will. To them our organization was a mysterious benefactor, filled with secretive darkness as much as it acted as their hopeful light, and joined one of the many secretive cabals in the world.

But what mattered was that in the end, it all seamlessly integrated into their own stories.

For those consumed with revenge and fights for righteousness, we are allies and people to swear their loyalty to. For those who are on the wrong side, we are a looming foe and people who cast doubt on their cause. For the majority, we are simply an afterthought - but involved in their story nonetheless.

And so, our organization became a key part of the setting. The tides had changed. And the narrative, despite being ever so tumultuous, finally headed into a certain direction.

One that was whispered in secret by those who are involved.

"A new dawn is near."

Tensions rose, yet strangely the nation simply waited with a bated breath. This was the calm of the storm, a stage where the world waited for the necessary flag for each and every storyline to be planted. One, where tripped, would set off everything.

And then, on that fateful day.

When their guards are down, and when they least expect it.

The day broke golden.





At the Imperial Palace, right in the country's capital. A few hours past midnight.

Right now the place, which is undoubtedly described as the den of the most corrupt and indulgent people in the country, is holding a banquet. The event itself is almost identical from the military galas thrown in the capital almost every week. From the luxury displayed to the point of gaudiness, and to the sinister undertone of snakes plotting around one another.

However, if there was one thing that could be said as different from the ordinary galas hosted - it would be because of those participating in the banquet itself. The mere fact they are allowed to set foot in the Imperial Palace makes them a very big deal. These 'guests' have the power to decide the state of the country; the backbone of the war effort, one can say. They are the ones which the crown cannot afford to lose support from.

In short, the elite of the elite. Untouchable, immovable people that the normal ruling class can only dream to become, carrying enough wealth that an average person could never comprehend.

There's a reason why they didn't care about the assassination in the recent gala. Even as the ruling class was still shaken by what had happened, they still attended the banquet. With that much power they hold in their hands, these people have nothing to worry about.

And furthermore, the banquet was held in undoubtedly the most secure place in the country. The Imperial Palace contains hundreds of veteran soldiers outfitted with the finest arms guarding the perimeter. And not only that, the palace was defended with various anti-aircraft systems if planes were nearby.

However the statement of this place being the most secure place still holds true.

Tanya was, in fact, a reincarnator.

Because for some reason, their secretive organization decided that this particular event was important enough for them to use their mages as guards and assigned the best ones that they have available.

Tanya had a feeling that their superiors are just looking to boost their funding and that they're being used as toys to show off, but she honestly didn't find it bad. In fact, this sort of mission is what she preferred. A comfortable life in the rear, without the chaos of the battlefield.

And so, she had prepared herself for a peaceful mission, about to treat this as some sort of break… Until she remembered that a certain petty god probably wouldn't allow that to happen.

…Allow me to ask a question.

Who benefits in war?

Objectively, war is many things. In a literal sense, it can be understood as a means of achieving political objectives, where the nation has no choice but to resort to violence as rational bargaining has failed. In a philosophical sense, it could be interpreted as a product of our deeply-rooted human aggressiveness, or perhaps as learned behavior due to the creation of social ills such as private property, institutionalized greed, or nationalism.

War is many things, but what is definite about it is that it's bloody and full of tragedy and despair. So why does it happen? Why does it exist? Who benefits from it to make it happen in the first place?

The answer to all those things is simple.

Those who don't participate in war, yet profit from it.

You know the most common type. The governing elite; those who don't participate in the war itself, but stand to gain power just by doing nothing. The rich use their power to get richer, using the lives of those under them without regard. A bunch of parasites, in short.

But then there's also the others. These ones are more than parasites, but rather people who make a living from war and use it as a business. They thrive on global conflict, profiting from wars through government contracts, rising stock values, and political influence.

And by that, I meant defense contractors and weapon manufacturers. These people are usually based on places far away from the conflicts they benefit in, treating war as a distant money-making machine. And unlike the governing elite, they usually have nothing to gain once the war is over.

Which is why they do everything in their power to extend it. Contractors, lobbying, you name it. And of course, in anime world, you exaggerate that to a hundred - because of secret evil cabals and organizations that manipulate everything.

—And right now, the focus is on one such organization. Across the Atlantic ocean, far removed from everything going on, a robotics development company was based in a certain country that was imagined to be violent, chaotic, and alien in most japanese media due to an internalized bitter and nationalistic hate.

And in their headquarters, the founder of the mech company sat in his office late at night, listening as his aide delivered him news of what was happening.

"…So you're telling me that there's been a revolution right as we speak?" the founder asked. "And that somehow, despite their overwhelming military might, the government can't do anything about it?"

The aide nodded his head. "Yes, sir. But the thing is, the revolutionaries have apparently gathered support from many of the aristocrats and military leaders. In effect, they're fighting their own military right now." he reported. "And furthermore, our rogue orphan pilots have joined them as well."

"What?" the founder asked, confused.

"The Orphan Project, sir. We've taken in orphans and used them as pilots for the mechs, before we sent them to our contractors." the aide reminded him. "Apparently, some had defected and managed to join up with the local resistance. Apparently they have also defeated the following batch, but new generations are on their way."

The information was met with indifference. "Hm. Right, that project existed. It's novel, but AI programs are producing more results." he commented. "And what about the mechs?"

"The mechs sent in those battlefields are considered outdated and disposable compared to our latest prototypes. Anything salvaged will mostly be something our competitors would be already aware of."

"And the losses? How much money did we lose because of this?"

The aide looked at his tablet. "We've lost 205 million dollars in the last few hours due to delays. The stock indices also dropped by 0.5 percent."

"That's it? Then it's nothing." the founder commented, before exhaling. "Go bribe some people and get some of our hired contractors to make some trouble. That war is minor compared to our main sources of profit anyway. Just keep the war going, and it's fine. Don't bother me with this news next time."

"Yes, sir."

The founder waved his hand dismissively at the aide. "Now leave. I have a meeting with the Defense Secretary in half an hour. Don't let anyone contact me unless it's a real emergency."

The aide didn't move. Instead, he just stood there, looking at his tablet. Seeing this, the founder narrowed his eyes and glared at him, impatience evident in his expression.

"Are you deaf? I told you to leave." the founder growled irritably.

And in response to that, the aide replied while staring at the tablet's screen, reading the latest message that had appeared on the messaging app which he had opened the entire time he was talking to the founder.

Everything is finished. The war is over. - V

"I'm afraid I can't do that, sir. I still have something to do." I answered.

Saying that, I put down the tablet before bringing up my old gun with my other free hand. The moment the pistol was pointed right at his head, the founder stiffened in his chair - but like many politically-inclined characters out there, he had immediately regained his composure.

Perhaps it would be through calling help, or more likely, using some technology that his company developed. But in the end he would live and the assassin failed.

It was the classic way to glaze the main antagonist because it wasn't time yet for them to die. His death would likely be at the hands of the protagonist… or probably not, considering the bleak seinen mixed within Orga's setting. I suspect that it's very likely that this guy wouldn't meet Orga and the others at all, roaming free despite the suffering he had caused, and highlighting how apathetic the world is to their plight.

So let's try and change that shall we?

Without answering him, I pulled the trigger. I watched as the bullet left my pistol and headed right towards the founder's face - before it halted, as a dome of blue light suddenly appeared out of nowhere, seemingly blocking its way.

It was an energy shield. Understandable, considering their mechs had one. It was only logical that they would want it to be made portable for personal use.

Unfortunately, the bullet wouldn't be stopped with something as simple as that. My gun was modified with undistilled anime bullshit, after all.

"—!?"

The shield only managed to block the bullet for a split second before it cracked, and I saw the founder's eyes widen momentarily as he registered that he was going to die. But it was a quick thing, and the bullet reached his forehead before he could even think of attempting something, splattering his brains behind him. His entire body then slacked as he instantaneously lost muscle control, leaving his dead self slumping on the seat.

And just like that, the main antagonist was dead.

This was the straw that broke the camel's back. With the main villain dead and the main plotline deviating so far from what was intended - it was far easier for the narrative force to just continue the closest existing story from what was left instead of forcefully bringing back what was before.

And my next words would cement what this story was going to be.

"For the glory of Westalis."

For the very first time, I uttered the name of V's country out of my mouth. To an outside observer looking at the scene, I would be some sort of spy that had traveled across the country to settle a final task - and combined that with our successful efforts to stop the war, it was a victorious conclusion that would usher a new era of peace.

And with this, the war would truly be over.

The transition of settings is complete.

I closed my eyes and let the moment sink in. Then, I turned around and left the room, leaving the corpse of the founder behind me. I opened the door and stepped out into the hallway.

And what greeted my sight was a bunch of dead bodies. A person wearing a suit stood in the middle of it, reloading the pistol in his hand calmly.


Spoiler

He glanced at me, and our eyes met.

"An assassin." he noted calmly. "The Garden didn't say anything about sending another one. And you arrived here much quicker than I did. There were no signs of you being around, and if I was a minute late, then I likely wouldn't have known you were here at all. It reminds me of a certain someone's work…"

I stayed quiet.

"…You're 'Twilight', aren't you? The spy who comes and goes so easily in our country." the assassin concluded. "Westalis must have sent you here. Have you come to kill the founder of this company just like I am?"

—Literally who?

The name wasn't something that came up in my investigations before. This was likely something new. It looks like I'm seeing the effects of the new change in the narrative fairly quickly, considering I just literally walked out of the door.

But 'Twilight', they say. Hm. I suppose it fits. Our organization was supposed to be called Golden Dawn after all.

And it is true that I have gone to their country to investigate some things. I just did my usual thing where I went there and used the genre divide to my advantage to get what I want - but if they explain my (relatively) unexplainable ways of infiltrating them by attributing me as a very good spy, then I guess it makes sense as well.

In any case, it would be rude to not answer a man who had helpfully provided me much needed information. He may be another assassin, but it looks like there's an unspoken truce between us here.

"The founder is dead. Your mission is finished." I told him straight. "And Westalis will finally stop pushing for war."

The man paused. "So they say. We've heard of your group staging a revolution to put a stop to all the madness." he said, before closing his eyes. "…And we did the same as well. Ostania now has had enough of bloodshed, and our policy makers all push for a ceasefire, and eventually a treaty."

I nodded. It was a natural conclusion.

After all, I also pushed things in their country to that direction.

While V was busy with Golden Dawn, I sorted things out in the other country - because stopping the war effort in one country doesn't mean the other would stop itself too. Fortunately for me, they already have a group that existed similarly to ours: an organization called the Garden, which was meant to be a secretive internal policing organization filled with assassins.

It took quite a lot of clones, hypnotism, and effort on my part, but I managed to guide them into fulfilling a similar role to Golden Dawn. I didn't manage them closely however, but they simply need to ride out the narrative's waves for it to work. And with their actions, peace between the two countries is finally possible.

But… it wasn't true peace. Not yet.

And the assassin felt the same, considering his next words.

"The war will continue." he stated grimly. "It won't be through guns, fire, or steel, but rather through whispers, shadows, and betrayal. Too many had died for peace to be easily achieved, and Ostania can't forgive the sins Westalis had committed."

"And Westalis can't forgive Ostania either." I said back.

He nodded, easily acknowledging crimes from both country's sides. Because that was what war is - a series of increasingly questionable, dumb, and selfish decisions that exploded and dragged everyone unfortunate enough in the vicinity into shit. Lines are blurred, and morality becomes a complex shade.

And he was right that the war wouldn't stop as well. At least in the figurative sense. The narrative might have been forced to stop the war setting, but the easiest setting would be what comes after that: A post-war society, and all the difficulties that come with it.

With that said, I turned around and started to leave. He made no move to stop me, and as I did that - I spoke out my true thoughts about the matter.

"Then we'll just have to see how things will develop from here. Because peace has to start from somewhere, no?"

Maybe the war didn't stop. Maybe the suffering would still continue, only in a different medium. Maybe a new kind of conflict would emerge. Maybe it will all be useless, and war will be brought back once again.

But still… It's a welcome change from how things used to be.

And like all the things that I changed so utterly to the point that the original plotline was nowhere to be found, I'm not going to just abandon it and let it go in its own way - No, I'm going to see it through to the end. No matter what.

Because that was my sole responsibility in this stupidly freakish world where I'm the only one with freedom.

I turned a corner and teleported after disappearing from the Ostania assassin's sight. In an instant I arrived in my humble abode in Japan, right into my office, where I plucked out a file on the shelf to update the situation regarding the two countries.

As I did that however, the door to my office opened and someone entered. I glanced behind me.

And then, I blinked.


Spoiler

"Welcome home, master." V stated blankly while in a complete maid uniform.

"…What are you doing?"

"Serving you." she answered simply. "With the war already over, my revenge is complete. And as such I have no other things to do. Therefore my next task is to serve you, master."

My brow twitched. It reminded me of her first answer when she first woke up, when she still had no idea how to feel or how to act human. I'd like to think that we'd made some progress - yet here she was again, repeating this stunt like nothing ever happened.

"You don't have to do that." I said, feeling slightly irritated. "When I told you that you can do whatever you want, I meant that—"

"—On the contrary, I am very aware of my decision."

I paused, before looking at the woman in the eye.

V met my gaze, eyes purposeful and determined. It wasn't the blank and servile gaze which stared at me when I first saved her - instead, there was a spark of something there. A spark of defiance, one that dared me to tell her off for making her decision.

"You believe that I am better off free and acting like a normal person, to heal me from my past experiences. To give me the taste of independence, giving me a chance to live my life my own way. Perhaps it would help but… you are wrong."

"I am not a normal person. Nor will I ever be one. Because I do not want to be." she stated simply. "Instead, I want to be with you. You have saved my life, taught me so many things and given me so many opportunities. You, all of you, have shown me that there is more to life than what I have previously known."

She put her hand on her chest, closing her eyes as she did so.

And then, the doll that barely acted human, who had always seemed to struggle to know what she wanted, easily bared her pure and unadulterated feelings for me to hear.

"I have no orders. My life is my own. And what I want in my life… is nothing more but to be by your side, Basa."


Spoiler

I stared at V, who said that with a soft, and almost relaxed expression. There was a moment of silence as I considered her words… and then I looked away and exhaled, also scratching the back of my head as I did so.

Well, if she says that, I guess I can't deny her. But it's not like I was planning to leave her or anything.

Still though, despite all that she said…

"That still doesn't explain why you're in a maid outfit while calling me master." I pointed out.

My statement made the woman blink. Then, she answered.

"It would be because I would be living in your house." Oi, this is the first I've heard of that. "Furthermore, I am currently unemployed and would have no way of paying any rent, therefore the only way to stay is to be your servant. This is the logical conclusion."

Is it? Is it really?

"No, take that off. You're not wearing that." I told her. "And you don't have to pay any rent or whatever. Actually, I can even arrange to get you another house. I imagine my apartment is a bit too small for two people to live in."

She frowned slightly. "…I wish to live with you under the same roof. And I don't wish to take this off."

"What? Why?"

"Because that's what I want." her gaze was as blank as always, but I could see the slight way her eyes gleamed. "That is what you've said, correct? You wanted me to make my own decisions… Or is this supposed to be an absolute order from my master? Are you perhaps undermining my freedom and forcing your own, despite your earlier words? How sad. I am saddened."

What's with this woman.

I met her blank and clearly unsaddened gaze with my own, and she showed not a single indication that she's going to change her mind.

Honestly, since when did she get this much lip? Or was she always like this, and she couldn't just express it until now? No, wait - now that I recall, she showed a little bit of it the first time I met her. During the time when she couldn't believe the existence of other genres.

Damn kuuderes. You never really know what's going on in their minds with that blank face of theirs.

…She's going to be a nightmare to live with.

"—Fine. Go wear that maid outfit or whatever." I grumbled, accepting her wish. "Do what you want."

She bowed. "As you ordered, master… Then, I shall go and tell Rias that our plan in convincing you to let me stay here was successful. And that it was also quite an amusing revenge after your stunt of making me the leader of Golden Dawn, and then acting dramatically subservient in various occasions. I believe the right thing to say here is: serves you right."

I stiffened at her words.

What.

"I also advise that you go to the dining room, or else the dinner that Aoki cooked up would've gotten cold. Or finished." she quickly added before I could register what the hell she said earlier. "Her curry dish is very delicious, and I might have eaten some of your portions as well. That is all."

And with that, the woman turned around and exited the office, leaving me behind. I stared at her direction for a long while even after she left. Then I let out a sigh.

…I amend my earlier words.

It seems that I'm not the one with freedom in this stupidly freakish world.

—Because that girl seems to be making good use of her free will more than I do.

Chapter 24

The streets of Japan were an interesting sight after being in a European warfront for so long.

Today I was inside the shopping district within our town. It was a weekend, and the weather was great for going outside. Many must have thought the same since the place was absolutely bustling with people, all living their lives in accord with the various plots they're involved in.

The general atmosphere was light however, which was a stark contrast to the solemn and grim mood that I had been getting used to seeing back in Westalis and Ostania. I guess that's just how it is in Japan; as a literal first world country and the center of anime world, it's pretty much heaven in comparison to other places. Although any place that's not involved in war would probably be better if compared to places like Westalis or Ostania.

Anyway, that's just some frivolous thoughts from me. But there is someone with us who's thinking the same about the place. And in a much more unironic and appreciative manner at that.

"This is…"

Accompanying us outside was V. With her not wearing maid clothing, of course. But that's not the focus right now.

Because currently, the woman was undergoing an important experience. The blonde's face barely changed from her usual blank expression, yet I can tell from the gleam in her eyes that she was pretty shocked at what she was seeing. The woman's gaze was fixed at the various shops around, taking note of everything that was inside and what they're selling.

She was like a newborn trying to soak in their environment. And considering her experience in life up until now, everything she was seeing was very likely new for her. A stranger might say it's an adorable sight, though it would likely be marred by the sad implication of V's past.

"So this is Japan…" the woman stated as she looked around. "Everything is so vibrant."

Right beside her, two girls showed different reactions. Rias nodded her head in an empathetic manner, while Yuki gave her a soft smile. The two joined us for this occasion since they wanted to hang out with V personally. Aoki wanted to do the same, but certain circumstances like still dealing with the fallout in her idol agency made her busy with work at this time.

Anyway, the redhead looked like she absolutely knew what V was talking about. "I get it. I thought the same as well the first time I arrived here, you know? Well, it's more about the human world as a whole, but I think it's pretty similar."

That made V tilt her head curiously. "The human world… Ah, you were originally from hell. Is it also that different compared to this place?"

"Yeah. Our sun there is artificial so everything is a bit muted. Humans won't notice it though. Our eyes are wired differently compared to you guys."

"I don't think that's what V meant when everything was more vibrant, Rias." Yuki pointed out, before pausing. "...Although, seeing that you're from a more solemn setting, it's also likely that things are literally more muted as well."

"Yes. It's almost always raining or dark. Especially with the constant fog and smoke during the war." V stated. "Seeing a place so clear and bright is a first for me."

Rias grinned. "Then let's enjoy it to the fullest! We're here for a date, after all!" she looked back at me. "Isn't that right, Basa?"

I stared at the three blankly.

A date. Between three girls and a single guy. Now, things like that are typical harem shenanigans - I could literally see one or two groups who are like that right now, so it's actually nothing special.

But that was only because they were cardboard cutout black-haired MCs who look completely identical with one another. And I, who unfortunately looks like a tanned and blonde-haired NTR guy, doesn't fit with these people.

"That guy… is he following them?"

"Two of them are foreigners. He might be asking for their numbers."

"Tch. Some people really are shameless."

—Which of course catches attention. People were glancing at us, and quite many hostile ones were aimed my way.

"Me dating you three? More like a harasser targeting women." I commented. "I'm being mistaken for those guys who pick up girls on the streets. With the way things are going, someone would definitely approach us and cause a scene."

Rias and Yuki blinked, before looking around and realizing that yes, it kinda does look that way on the outside and that the people near us were staring for a while now.

"Huh." Rias muttered thoughtfully. "I did wonder why people were looking at us. And here I thought they're appreciating my beauty more than usual."

"Confident, are you?" Yuki said with a sweatdrop.

Rias puffed her chest. "Of course I am! Demon, remember? Literally the personification of temptation right here!"

"Yes, yes. Of course." Yuki followed without preamble, before turning to me. "…Basa-kun, perhaps if you were to walk with us instead of just following behind, then people might think differently? The fact that you're also mostly quiet doesn't help."

I waved it off. I was way past caring about what others think, after all.

"Nah, it's fine." I told her. "I mean, how can I act like a mysterious and aloof character if I do that? You're taking my game away, woman."

Yuki gave me a flat look. "Yes, I am aware. And frankly that certain part of your personality is better off gone. Have you tried this certain thing called 'clear communication'? I hear it's better than keeping us in suspense and acting cool later."

You're the last one to talk about clear communication, you drama character.

Anyway, as I ignored Yuki's hypocrisy-filled statement - V tilted her head, expression confused at what we were talking about.

"I don't understand. You mentioned that we're having a date? I thought it's only for two people, or at least that's what was shown in the stories I've read." the woman said cluelessly. "Also, what do you mean by harassment? Basa is not harassing anyone."

That made Yuki sigh. "It's just a figure of speech from Rias. Don't take her seriously. As for the harrassment… Well, let's just say there are some strange people in Japan. And Basa-kun is being mistaken for one of them."

"Mm. Japan is filled with strange people, just like any other place. Except here they've got people who will try to pick up girls by asking for your number and not taking no for an answer! It's pretty creepy." Rias explained. "They also try to target foreigners like us, so you should be careful! Especially since you're so beautiful, V!"

V blinked, then nodded. "...Yes. I'll keep it in mind."

"Yep! Now for the date thing - It's not a figure of speech, you know?" Rias said with a grin. "This really is a date! It can happen even when there's multiple people. Sure, people might call you trash, but it's okay as long as they're your harem! Those who get angry at you are just jealous!"

"W-What are you even saying, Rias!? Don't teach her weird things!" Yuki shouted, expression scandalous. Then she cleared her throat and turned to the blonde. "Ahem! Don't listen to her. We're actually here for you, V."

The blonde looked surprised. "Me…?"

"Yes. Basa-kun mentioned that you've been busy fighting a war to have a normal life so Rias and I thought of us having a shopping trip together. Just to give you a chance to explore everything, since you probably didn't have the time to do so in the past."

The heroine was correct. This thing was something they actually planned on doing once they finally met her. Because while they all left me dealing with the emotionless doll that V was in our early days together, it didn't mean they didn't want to help in their own way.

Plus, it's also a good way to help V familiarize with this new environment. Especially since the girl is going to be living here from now on. Better have her experience culture shock right now and get done with it than some any other time.

Still, the heroine paused, looking unsure for a moment as she finished her earlier statement. "…Or at least, that's what we assumed. We aren't being condescending by assuming you haven't experienced much, are we? Now that I think about it, it's arrogant to think that you wouldn't have visited a shopping district at some point during your time with Basa-kun."

V shook her head. "No, you're correct. Recruiting and doing missions for Golden Dawn made me familiar with more peaceful places within our country, but I didn't spend time acting leisurely then. I am unfamiliar with many things here like you assumed."

Yuki smiled. "I see. That's great, then."

"Then let's go and explore as much as we can!" Rias also said with a smile. "So what do you want to see first, V? This shopping district has a lot of different things in it! It's really cool!"

"I am… unsure. There's just so many things to see." the blonde looked around again, before staring at a particular shop and pointing at it. "What is that place? I don't understand the picture they're displaying."

"Oh, that's a coffee shop! They sell different types of hot or iced coffee drinks there, though they do serve tea and other stuff from time to time. That shop is one of the more popular brands out there. The drinks they make are pretty delicious!" Rias paused. "…Don't know about the green logo they have though. I think it's a naked woman. Or maybe it's the Statue of Liberty? I've never really thought about it."

"Why don't we order some drinks ourselves? We certainly need the energy considering we're going to explore many things in the shopping district." Yuki suggested.

V nodded, looking intrigued. And so the three of them ordered something in the shop. This one was more of a booth than a proper building that this particular coffee chain was known for, and there weren't any lines so they quickly got the drinks they ordered.

The blonde stared at the drink in her hands - it was some sort of latte, but iced. She looked at it like it was a strange and alien thing, before putting the straw in her mouth and taking a sip.

"…It's sweet."

The blonde's face was as blank as ever, but from the lightness in her tone and the gleam in her eyes - it was clear that she liked the taste of the drink a lot. Yuki smiled beside her.

"That drink is mixed with sweetened condensed milk. I thought that you'd be sick with regular bitter coffee, so I ordered a more tasty one for you." she told her.

V nodded, looking like her view of the world had changed. "I didn't know that coffee could be like this. I know that you can add milk and sugar, but getting something like that was rare. And I've never considered that it could be served cold." she sipped her drink again, enjoying the taste. "…This is incredible."

"There's also different other things you can add, like putting whipped cream or flavored syrups on top of the coffee. They're quite popular." Yuki informed, drinking her own coffee. "I personally prefer mine unsweetened, so I have mine with skimmed milk."

"Then, what about Rias' drink?"

"Hers? Well…" Yuki then turned to Rias. "Hers is more unique."

Unlike the other two who were enjoying their drinks, Rias looked green when she took a sip of hers. The girl wanted to order something new since she was pretty much familiar with the most popular drinks there already, but it seems that she had forgotten the risks in doing that.

"Bleh, salt and honey in coffee doesn't taste good at all. And it's cold as well. Ugh, this is the worst!" Rias said with disgust. Then she turned to me with upturned eyes. "Ne, Basa-kun. Switch drinks with me!"

I ignored her while I sipped on my own drink. Vanilla milkshake, because its pure whiteness brightens my twisted and edgy heart. "Why would I? You ordered that yourself so you finish it. Or just throw it away if you can't."

"U-Ugh, but I really don't want to waste it…"

What a cheapskate, this demon.

Yuki let out a chuckle seeing Rias' exaggerated sad face. Then, she turned to V. "…Should we go and check out other shops? There's still plenty of things to look at."

That made the blonde nod firmly. And again, despite looking relatively emotionless, there were tiny signs that a pedantic eye could see. Signs like the small furrow in her brows and slight purse in her lips, showing what the woman had truly felt about the matter.

"Yes. Let's do it." V replied, looking excited.

—And with that, the four of us explored the shopping district.

With the point of this trip making V learn different things she'd never really encountered before, we pretty much went from different shops that gathered her curiosity and interest. And considering that this city's shopping districts cover quite a wide amount of products and services, it meant that we went through a lot of different things.

In just a span of a couple hours here, we went ahead and checked out a bakery and tasted the specialty bread they have there. Then the next, we went to a cosmetic store near it, where Rias and Yuki went ahead and bought some make up and perfume for V who's very inexperienced about that sort of thing.

We also bought some snacks in a vending machine after the blonde saw it for the first time when we passed by. Then, the next thing we did was go to check out a tech shop where we bought V her own phone to use, considering she didn't have one yet. And after, we went to a nearby toy shop just because and bought stupid toys there that caught our fancy.

And then after that, we passed by a certain popular fast food restaurant. Then, after getting curious about what it was and how it tastes, the blonde then bought a meal for takeout. We continued walking again after that.

…Actually, doesn't this girl go to food shops a little too often?

"—This is quite tasty."

I gave a flat look to the blonde as she said those words while munching on a mouthful of burger. She somehow still has the appetite to eat despite consuming a lot of different snacks and drinks for the past couple hours. And it wasn't even lunch yet.

Yuki also expressed the same concern. "Um, is it alright for you to eat that much? I hoped that we would have lunch together since it's almost noon…"

That made V tilt her head. "Why wouldn't it be fine? There's still plenty of room for me to eat."

"I-Is that so?" Yuki replied, a faint disbelief evident in her voice as she stared at the blonde. "You still have room for more despite all that...?"

"Yes? I eat as much as I can if there's food available. And I can eat much more than this." she replied, making the heroine blink.

That was when Rias interjected with a nod. "A soldier has to eat as much as they can, because they know that this meal might be the last one they have in a battlefield!" she declared. "Or at least, that's what they've said from a manga I've read. V is an incredible soldier, so she must know it by heart!"

"Yes. Starving while fighting for your life on the battlefield is a terrible experience. Everything is rationed. So whenever I have the opportunity to have extra rations, I try to eat them all." V agreed, before pausing. "Although, that doesn't really happen anymore after Basa saved me. Perhaps there really is no need to eat as much…?"

"As long as you're not getting hurt by it, it should be fine." I told her.

Thinking about it, this wasn't really a cause of concern. While she had been eating a lot for a realistic character within her serious seinen setting, it was still within believable standards. And out of all the people here - she was the one who was deserving to eat as much food as she likes. She certainly didn't have much opportunity to do so before.

Although… "You do have to be careful though. If eating a lot before was a requirement for you, doing the same now might be different. It could become your little quirk or something."

"Quirk? What do you mean?" V asked, and the other two looked curious as well.

"Getting wet enough times convinced the world that my side character quirk was that. So if you were to eat a lot when there is an opportunity, then you'll likely be the same." I explained. "You'd be seen as a big eater in the eyes of the world if that was the case."

"Big eater…?" V muttered for a moment, before her eyes lit up in recognition. "Ah, do you mean those characters who eat a comical amount of food? I'd be like them?"

"Yeah. Like them." I replied. "It's not the case now, but in the future it could mean that you'd have the urge to eat very large servings of food during meals regularly. But consequently, it might also mean that there's always enough food available to do that. Likely because the world needs to—"

"I am fine with it."

"—show the scene… what?" I took a moment to register what she just said. "You're fine with it?"

She nodded firmly, blank-faced but with eyes gleaming with determination.

"I am fine with it." she repeated. "I will eat as much as I can from now on."

…Well, alright. You do you I guess.

Looking at V with a smile, Yuki then spoke up. "If that's the case, I suppose that we should go and get a meal right now? It's almost time for lunch anyway."

Rias seemingly agreed. "Yeah, all this talk about food is making me hungry. Although, what restaurant should we go to? There's a lot in here." she hummed in thought. "We could go Japanese, Western or maybe some other cuisine… but I really want V to experience it all, considering this trip is for her. Maybe we could find a restaurant that serves all those different foods?"

"We're not really on a deadline. We can go back here again just to experience new things if we need to." the heroine gently reminded. "…Although, I might know somewhere that fits the bill. I investigated the different plots in the shopping district and I've learned that there's a buffet restaurant near here that serves as a fighting arena for a cooking genre today. Some characters there are chefs from different countries, so there will likely be different cuisines that's going to be served."

Rias' eyes widened. "What the heck? That sounds awesome! Let's go there then!"

"Cooking genre? That sounds very wonderful." the blonde agreed, clenching her fists in front of her. "I will eat as much as I can in that buffet." she declared.

Looks like they're getting pretty excited. Can't blame them about that really - After all, cooking anime food was always a treat. Even just imagining it right now makes my mouth water.

And so, the four of us went to the location where the heroine said that buffet would be. And just like always, me being a gyaru-looking guy following three beautiful girls rubbed people wrong, so the stares continued like usual.

Although, I've been feeling a different type of stare mixed in with those usual ones. Someone… No, some people are observing me. For a moment I wondered why these people took interest in me considering I'm a side character in the eyes of the world - until I realized who these people are.

You know what? I'll deal with that later.

However, as I was thinking that and resigned myself to delaying a potentially troublesome problem, a different one suddenly popped up. From the stares that persisted around us due to the unfortunate biases associated with my appearance - inevitably, there would be at least one person who wouldn't care about causing a scene to express their concern.

And this time, it came in the form of a guy who approached us from a nearby cafe while holding boba tea in his hand. The guy had blonde hair that was likely colored and looked somewhere V's age. Based on his looks, he was probably the stereotypical popular college student, kinda similar to that blonde guy within Yuki's narrative.

He looks a bit dumber though.


Spoiler

"Excuse me!" the guy greeted the three girls. "Are the three of you shopping together?"

"I see. That's reassuring." V commented, before tilting her head. "…I suppose I can wear the dress we bought today for that event then. What about you, Yuki? Will you need to buy your own dress as well?"

She shook her head. "I'm actually fine. I have dresses in my wardrobe for these formal occasions."

"Oh, that's a shame, I wanted to see you in a dress too…" Rias muttered pitifully.

The sight of it made her giggle a bit. "Maybe next time." she told her, before pausing when a thought crossed her mind. "Actually, what about Basa-kun? He'll also be in that event as well, right? It might be good if we get him an outfit too, right?"

Somehow, her statement made Rias regain her vitality, and the girl crossed her arms while letting out a huff. Yuki blinked, surprised. Was there something that she said?

As it turns out, the girl was just being petulant. "Hmph! That guy, I bet that if we say that, he'll say something along the lines of 'I already have plenty of clothes for those kinds of things, so why the hell would I buy them?'" the girl said that with a lowered tone and a neutral expression on her face. Yuki blinked. "—Or something along those lines. Seriously, for someone as powerful as him, that guy's a cheapskate!"

"That was a very good impression of him, Rias." V complimented.

"Thanks! I worked hard on it!" Worked hard? What did she even mean by that…? "Hm, although, maybe we do need to have him wear something matching with me or something. Just to make him look a little special. Because from what I can tell, a lot of people are pretty curious about him… Especially after knowing just how much he helped us."

"…I suppose that we should go fetch him then?" Yuki asked.

"Oh, alright. I guess he's already waited long enough anyway." Rias nodded. "Let's go get Basa-kun dressed up! And as revenge for his lousy boyfriend acts - I'm going to definitely make him wear some funny and strange clothes!"

A smile made its way on her face. That was definitely something to look forward to.

And with that, after a short moment of Rias changing back to her previous clothes - all of them went back outside the clothing store to go and get Basa-kun. The man likely would've been hanging around the store, looking something like a normal delinquent hanging suspiciously around as dictated by his character status, and Yuki glanced around the outside of the store looking someone like that.

Strangely however, there wasn't anyone around that fit the description. But extending her search to other shops nearby the clothing store - she did manage to spot something. One that had caught her complete attention.

"…That's…"

On a cafe opposite the street and slightly to the right, on the outdoor seating. There, seated on one of the tables, she spotted someone who was unmistakably Basa-kun… and along with him were two other women, each seated on the same table as he was and chatting with one another.

A person's first thought of him hanging around other women like this would definitely be 'he's trash' or something along those lines. But Yuki was beyond that, and because she was able to instantly recognize the women with him. Or at least, one of them.

"Nee-san…?" Yuki muttered, staring at her sister.

"Wait, isn't that Serafall-san too? Why are they here?" Rias wondered, spotting the same scene as well.

V stared at them both, and then to where Basa-kun was. "Are they people that you know?"

She nodded. "Yes. One of them is my sister. And as for the other one…" Yuki turned to Rias. "I believe that she's one of your family's allies? That's what I remember from the files in your setting."

"Yeah, she is. It's strange that she's here in the human world though. She's usually busy with work, and I don't think she said anything about visiting us either." Rias observed, looking puzzled at the woman's presence.

And she felt the same went for her sister. She usually visits without notice, but it's only whenever Yuki is in her apartment. She had never encountered her outside like this. And the fact that she was here brings up massive warnings. Her sister usually had eyes around people she deemed important, but if she was physically present…

Did she follow them while they were enjoying the outing?

Many thoughts appeared in her mind as it raced for a possible explanation of what was happening. However, her questions and hypothesis about the current situation were interrupted when V spoke, offering a straightforward solution.

"Let's greet and ask them then." the blonde stated. "They noticed us the moment we left the store. And even much earlier for this 'Serafall-san'. They're just waiting for us to approach."

True to her words, the moment V finished saying her statement, the two women stopped chatting and turned to their direction. 'Serafall-san' started waving at us cheerily, while the other woman stared straight at Yuki's eyes and then smiled.

Yuki had to stop her initial reaction to flinch. It was strange, really. Despite already facing much worse opponents - she still somehow couldn't help but feel little under her older sister's gaze.

Nevertheless, she had already stared defiantly at her sister the last time they had met, and doing it again for the second time was slightly easier. And together with her friends, they approached the cafe where the group were sitting.

"Yahallo, everyone!" her sister greeted, her amicable smile perfectly in place. "Are you guys done with your shopping? That was earlier than we thought."

"We're just here to fetch Basa-kun, nee-san. We're not yet done shopping." Yuki briefly answered. "But more importantly - what exactly are you doing here? Did you follow us?" she asked.

Her sister opened her mouth. She was likely about to say some excuse or deflect her question entirely, but before she could do so, she was interrupted when the woman beside her answered instead.

"Yep! We followed you guys and got caught! Te he~☆!" Serafall-san replied, sticking out her tongue and bumping a fist on her head. "As for why we're here, we've got some business that actually concerns Basa-kun so we had a chat with him. Isn't that right, Haru-chan?"

It was then that Yuki saw the peculiar sight of her sister's constant perfect smile dim slightly. It wasn't immediately clear to see, but to someone like her who had known her sister her entire life - the difference was obvious.

The signs appeared only for a moment however. "Yes, that's right." her sister said, tone slightly emphasized indicating her annoyance. "I would've preferred to tell her that myself though."

Serafall-san tilted her head. "Hm? Why?" she then paused as if realizing something. "…Ah, are you trying to act like an invincible sister or something? I get it, I really get it! I tried doing that to my little sister Sona one time you know? But as it turns out it really stresses her. So I eventually thought—"

Yuki watched with a strange look as the demon started talking her sister's ear off about the topic of little sisters and how she acted about them. While the topic was indeed strange and probably implied that the demon had an unhealthy degree of obsession to her own sibling, she was mostly focused on her sister's reactions.

The talk with Basa-kun had Yuki seeing her sister not have things going her way for the first time in her life. This one was quite similar, and Yuki was able to see Haru act uncomfortable. She witnessed the way her sister's actions and expressions turn strained, and her attempts of trying to dominate and control the conversation were easily sidestepped.

What exactly was going on here…?

Yuki glanced to the side, where she met the eyes of Basa-kun who was drinking canned coffee in a cafe for some reason. Then with practiced ease, she started talking to the man with the telepathic skill she learned from him.

Do you mind telling us what is happening?

He calmly sipped his drink.

…Just something troublesome. They'll explain it, don't worry.

A frustratingly vague answer like usual. But before Yuki could press some more about it, Serafall-san suddenly paused from her talk with her sister and gave them a mildly disapproving frown.

"Hey now, isn't it rude to converse that way when there's people right in front of you?" the demon scolded with a petulant tone. "You could just ask us straight, you know? No need for that!"

Yuki blinked.

"R-Right. My apologies." she muttered sheepishly, feeling the need to kick herself because of course a supernatural being like her would detect that. "May I ask what exactly your business here is, then?"

"Yeah, Serafall-san. You didn't tell us you were visiting the human world." Rias commented with a curious tone. "And Sona definitely doesn't know either. Did you not tell her yet? I'll call her for you if you—"

That made the older demon wave her hands frantically. "O-Oh, no no! No need for that, Rias-chan. I'll tell her that myself. You know how she feels about surprise visits." she then let out a breath and turned to Yuki. "Now as for your question… Well, we're to ascertain some things about Basa-kun!"

"Ascertain?"

Serafall-san grinned. "Yep!"

And with that, the demon launched an explanation about the current state of their faction, and how they're not sure whether he can be trusted to join the faction or not. And to smooth things out, they needed to make Basa-kun do something that would prove that he's fit to join the faction. Yuki could tell that the situation was dumbed down and more complicated than that, but it's likely the gist of it.

And throughout it all, she watched her sister react to the information. It looks like she had already heard it before, and Yuki could tell that Haru doesn't believe a lick of it due to the genre divide. Still, it was strange to see her acting like she did, listening to them talk with a smile on her face.

Nevertheless… "Does that apply to us as well?" Yuki asked when the demon finished.

"Hm? Oh, no. Don't worry about that. They're only focused on Basa-kun here."

She furrowed her brow in confusion. "Why? We're also with Rias, aren't we?"

"I think I get it. It's because he's the only strong one, Yuki-chan." Rias answered in Serafall's stead. "Basa-kun is the only person they feel threatened about because they don't know about him. But as for you, Aoki-san and V…"

Serafall nodded. "Yep, that's exactly it! You look like a very skilled human for your age, but you're not really that powerful. Probably falling below mid-level, at best." she then turned to V, who was being quiet the whole time. "As for you… You're the one that held off that old demon, right? That's impressive, actually."

"It isn't anything noteworthy. That demon was just playing around and didn't take me seriously." V replied.

"I guess that's true. Still impressive you survived him though!" she complimented, before continuing on with her explanation. "Anyway, going back on our way to Basa-kun - we've come to an agreement that we'll be involving your schools for this. So we've decided to make an interschool event!"

…What?

"I don't recall there ever being an agreement. The whole thing was just your whim." Basa-kun flatly stated.

"Oh, but it was an agreement though? After all, both Haru-chan and I wanted the same thing. I'm just making things easier for the both of us. And for you as well!" Serafall-san turned to her sister with a smile. "Isn't that right, Haru-chan?"

"Well, I do want Basa-kun to do something for me, so… I suppose it's convenient enough?" her sister answered, tilting her head. Then she shrugged. "Oh well, this seems interesting. So I guess it should be fine if we do it."

Yuki frowned, turning to her sister.

"Nee-san, what exactly are you trying to do…?" she muttered, completely confused. "Why are you even here? And what's this about wanting to do the same thing as Serafall-san? And asking Basa-kun to do something for you?"

Her sister just sipped her drink and gave her a calm smile.

"I'm just here to see what my sister is up to, Yuki-chan. After all, you've seemingly surrounded yourself with many interesting people who talk about strange things." Haru answered cheerily. "And you know me. I just hate it whenever I can't figure out a puzzle. So I tried to find out what was going on myself!"

Yuki's eyes narrowed a bit at that.

Her sister was lying. Or at least, not telling the entire truth.

"…I see." she settled.

Serafall-san clapped her hands. "It's decided then! An interschool event with our two schools! How exciting!"

And just like that, two undoubtedly powerful authorities within the city suddenly decided to collaborate on making a school event. However, while that was surprising in its own way, Yuki's attention was more on her sister and the strange things that she said.

Her sister was plotting something. She can never really tell with her, but putting aside the fact that her sister was an incredibly competent side character, she knew that the woman she grew up with wouldn't make such strange decisions only on a whim.

So why this…? Why follow them and ask Basa-kun? To what end does she do all this?

Yuki stared at her sister, whose true thoughts remained unknown like always.

…

Then, she blinked.

There was a sudden thought that appeared in her mind. A thought that she wouldn't have entertained before, and something that finds slightly ludicrous even now. Her life before turning meta had closed her mind about many things after all, forcing her to become subjected to many misunderstandings just for the sake of drama.

And one of the relationships it had affected the most was between her sister and herself. She had thought of her sister as a monstrous machine that locks on insecurities and controls people with just her words. And nothing beyond that. They had never been proper siblings for a very long time.

But what if… what if that wasn't the case?

"Nee-san," Yuki spoke with a soft tone."Are you perhaps worried about me?"

Again, her sister's smiling expression remained unchanged. The mask that she put on her face remained firmly in place and there was little to no reaction from her question.

But Yuki witnessed it.

A miniscule flinch, easily missed if it wasn't for her training and natural aptitude for spotting those things. Her sister tensed up after she asked her question as if she didn't expect what she said, and her entire body language closed off just for a single moment.

But it wasn't due to anxiety, distrust, or other similar reasons. Because the way that Yuki saw it…

It felt like her sister was embarrassed.

"Worried? A bit of a sudden question there, little sister." Haru quickly followed her question with those words, accompanying it with an enigmatic smile. "And it's also not the right question. After all, what you want to know is the reason why I'm doing this, right? 'I wonder what my elder sister is planning now'… That's what you should be asking."

The question was sidestepped, then she cut off any further thought about it by bringing up Yuki's usual worry whenever she interacts with her. In the past, it might have worked. And Yuki would be dancing in her palm like usual.

But now it only served as another piece of evidence. Evidence that she had misunderstood someone for a very long time due to their circumstances. Evidence that someone couldn't seem to just say what she felt to others straight, and had to resort to strange actions such as this.

She closed her eyes.

…It looks like her sister really was a drama character, after all.

Yuki found her lips turning upwards slightly, much to her sister's confusion.

"Thank you for worrying, nee-san." she told her directly, making the woman pause again. "But you don't need to worry. I've learned many things and I'm also surrounded by many reliable people. That said, I know my words aren't enough for you… so I'll go along with this and prove it myself."

Haru stared, silent.

"…Is that so." her sister stated in a completely neutral tone. "Good for you then."

There was a moment of thoughtful silence that followed.

Then, beside her, Serafall-san smiled as if she knew what just happened. "You're a good sister, Yuki-chan." the demon stated. She then followed it by standing up from her seat. "…Welp! That pretty much concludes our business here. Or, well, at least on my end. What about you, Haru-chan?"

Her sister nodded. "Same thing here. I suppose we'll just have to meet again next time." the woman also stood up from her seat. "Now, you guys said earlier that you're planning to buy some clothes for Basa-kun, right? We're pretty much done here now, so all four of you can finish your shopping together."

"Oh? Are you not going to join your sister's friends in hanging out?" Serafall-san asked.

"I wouldn't want to spoil their fun." her sister answered with a sad smile that convinced no one. "Plus, I still have some other things to do. What about you, Leviathan-san? Will you join them?"

"Nope! I have the rest of the day off, and I'm going to spend it having fun! Although…" the demon grinned. "If you're going to leave now, why don't we walk together? You're interesting."

Haru smiled. "I could say the same to you, Leviathan-san. You're an interesting person as well."

"Hehe, that's an understatement~☆!" Serafall-san said to her with a wink, before turning back to them. "Alright then, I'll see you guys later! And I'll probably hang around the school after, Rias! Try not to ruin the surprise for my sister, alright?"

Rias sent her a thumbs up. "Got it!"

And with that, the both of them went ahead and left the cafe. Yuki watched as the two women, one being her sister and the other being a powerful demon, walked in the streets of the crowded shopping district. And she witnessed them chatting together amicably until they were finally out of sight.

"…Welp. There you have it." Basa-kun commented after they were gone. Then, he glanced at her. "You've certainly grown, haven't you?"

Indeed. That was a very enlightening conversation.

She thought that the drama portion of her life had already been resolved, especially with the love triangle within her club already taken care of. But she should've realized that the genre's effects had pervaded every facet in her life, including her very own family.

How many things that should've been spoken out loud remained unsaid? How many misunderstandings piled up and resulted in where they were now? How many problems were left to fester simply because no one dared to face them?

She had grown in a way, since she finally recognized an obvious truth. And perhaps, with this, she could finally improve the state of her household.

…Although that might take a long time and considerable effort on her part, considering the mess she has to unravel. And she probably needs to get over her issues and look at things objectively as well. That's mainly the real reason why she didn't notice her sister's affection beneath her twisted personality, after all.

Yuki sighed. "Why do drama characters need to complicate things…?"

"You don't get to ask that, drama character." Basa-kun retorted flatly.

Rias glanced at the both of them, before turning to the blonde beside her. "Um, V, do you know what they're talking about? I think I completely missed Yuki-chan's last exchange with her sister. I don't really get it…"

"I lack the context so I can't offer a concrete explanation, but from what I spotted, Yuki's sister was embarrassed when Yuki asked if she was worried about her. And she tried deflecting." the blonde answered, before tilting her head. "Perhaps she's some sort of 'tsundere'? That is how they mostly operate, correct?"

Yuki blinked. "Tsundere…"

She tasted the word in her mouth. And with it, she recalled the feelings associated with the person she called a sibling. The manipulations, the feelings of inferiority, and the gradual widening of their distance… she remembered it all.

But accompanying it, she also remembered the other things. Her sister's occasional visits to her house whenever she finally lived alone, to the way she involved herself in her past drama with Kaeda-san and Makoto-kun despite being busy as a politician. And now, much more recently, the way she confronted Basa-kun now that she turned herself meta, involving herself in many strange and absurd things.

Truly, her actions completely contrasted the way she talked.

An involuntary giggle came out of Yuki. "Yes, a tsundere… That seems like an apt way to describe it, V."

Rias still looked confused. Still, she nodded her head. "Well, alright." Then she regained her vitality and pumped her fist. "But moving on from that - they said that we'll have an interschool event, right? Then that means I'll get to meet you during school! How cool is that?"

Basa-kun raised a brow. "We already meet each other even when there's school. How is that cool at all?"

"No! I meant that in an official school event! That's, like, a totally different vibe!" Rias argued, before crossing her arms. "I mean, imagine this - you're all going to meet another school, and everyone's pretty nervous, but then bam! We reveal that we know each other!" she nodded emphatically. "That would surely make you popular in the eyes of everyone!"

"What's with the grade-school level fantasy?" Basa-kun retorted. "Also that only works if you're popular in the first place. So that'll only work if you meet Yuki or something."

Rias blinked, before grinning evilly. "Oh? What if I approach you then—?" a hand chopped her head. "Owie!"

"Don't even think about it. That'll be way too troublesome."

"I suppose it would be. I imagine your reputation would become far worse to the point that hypnosis would be required to just have a small profile." And hypnosis wasn't something you'd want to use as a crutch, from an ethical and a psychological perspective. Then, Yuki frowned as a similar thought entered her mind. "…That said, was there really a need for this to happen, Basa-kun?"

The man turned to her, and Rias did the same but with a questioning look. "What do you mean, Yuki-chan?" she asked.

Yuki frowned. "This whole convincing thing could've been avoided by the use of hypnosis, couldn't it? And while I appreciate you not using it on my sister, it isn't the same for the demons." she pointed out. "This could've been easily avoided and dealt with in a much more controlled manner. That way, this… spontaneous event wouldn't have had to happen. It doesn't fit your methods."

Rias paused as she realized what she was talking about, and now her questioning look was directed to Basa-kun. It was at that moment that V, who had been listening quietly, spoke up.

"I understand what you mean. But from my limited experience with him, I think it usually means he was forced to do so by outside circumstances. And not following through could possibly lead to worse results. Is that accurate?" the girl asked the man.

The man was quiet for a moment, glancing at them.

Then, he scratched the back of his head.

"…Yeah, that's pretty much the case." he confessed. "I thought about doing what Yuki suggested earlier, but it looks like this damn world had something planned. So in the end, I had no choice but to let it be."

"Something planned…? What do you mean by that?" Yuki asked.

"Take a look."

His answer was accompanied with him bringing out his phone, before showing it to them. And there, they saw the alert that was displayed right on the screen. A familiar alert, or at least familiar to Rias and her, considering that they had seen it before.

A world-affecting scenario. Scenarios that could eventually turn the setting of the world into an apocalypse.

And what was written there was something that made her eyes widen.

Because right in front of her eyes…




- ALERT: WORLD-AFFECTING SCENARIO DETECTED - ​

Probability of affecting neighboring genres: 91.1% - Very Likely.​
STATUS: Active, Source: Sector 3A - Hakoniwa Academy
SETTINGS: Supernatural, Sci-Fi, School life, Delinquent, (-Pending-)
THREAT:
Reality Warper (Subject Name: Haruhi Ajimu) generating city-wide, destructive school war scenarios involving delinquent gangs, super-powered students, espers, aliens, time travelers, and demons.
More participants in the conflict are possible.



…Was a completely ridiculous scenario that sounded like madness.
