Chapter 26

Reality Warpers.

A very general term thrown around in fiction to describe something powerful.

It carries a certain ominous weight to it, and one that carries the implication of the character being able to twist the logic and the mechanics of what is considered common sense into whatever they will it to be.

It's a very busted power. Or at least, it sounds like it is. People who pit fictional characters between one another certainly throw out the term a lot, saying it like it's a proof of said character being invincible, totally unbeatable, and that their cock tastes good or whatever else they want to claim.

But the thing is - it's not that simple.

In anime world where literally different settings exist in contrived conjunction with one another, the term loses its meaning very easily. Because what does it really mean to warp reality? And what does this 'reality' consist of in the first place, considering there are wildly different interpretations of it?

Let's disregard the fact that characters that operate in different genres such as shounen are almost reality warpers to some extent, with them being able to ignore physics, logic and common sense for the sake of the story. No, our focus should be on what stories and plots have outright said to be 'Reality Warpers', who break established laws and therefore 'reality'.

To a mundane or a sci-fi setting, they are basically using magic. Something that couldn't be explained by their understanding of science or whatever wonder discovery in their setting.

To a supernatural setting, they are… Well, basically a type of magic again. But something more powerful, and also something couldn't be explained by their magic systems.

A Reality Warper, then, is someone who cannot be explained by the setting they are confined in. With the 'reality' they are warping being the setting itself.

Honestly, it's not right to call them reality warpers at all. Just jumped-up characters that the narrative chose to be the exception from the local systems in place. The term 'reality warper' doesn't really offer anything informative. Or at least, in the eyes of someone who exceeds said settings and can move freely between them.

But like every little thing in this world, there are implications about them.

They are exceptions to the rules of a setting. In a way, that makes them very special - which means they fulfill roles that are comparable to protagonists in terms of weight in the story. Perhaps as a final boss, a mentor that dies, or an untouchable being that serves as a plot device.

The story will bend itself around them to suit their needs. There wasn't any need to explain their power. It's literally explained by their title after all. However, there is always a single constant whenever they come up… and that is the fact that they are the undisputed top of the plot and setting that they inhabit.

In a mundane setting, they're nothing different to a normal magus or a spellcaster. But in a supernatural one? What does it mean to be at the top of a setting where a lot of destructive beings are present already? It might mean being able to erase entire countries in seconds, maybe even the world, or the universe.

And right now, we're dealing with one such being.

—Haruhi Ajimu.

A familiar name, one that reminded me of certain memories in the past. A reminder of past mistakes, during the time when I wasn't quite yet used or knowledgeable about this shitty world.

I've monitored her for a very long time and continued to do so even until now. I had thought that things had stabilized, but it seems like she had done something that would quite literally change the world, leading to the alert that I had received.

And one that seems to be related to the tasks and the 'interschool event' that Yuki's sister and the strongest female devil cooked up it seems, considering how contrived the world had set the whole thing up before I was forced to go along due to the alert's appearance.

So, in the end, how exactly could we deal with this? How can we possibly deal with a reality warper that is certainly classified as someone 'Overpowered'?

…The answer is surprisingly simple.

You just have to work harder and smarter, is all.





The school grounds were just like how I remember it.

Not that I was gone here for a long time. My little 'stopping a war and staging revolution' thing with V had been my focus for like several weeks or so, but in the eyes of everyone here including mine, I hadn't gone absent at all. You can thank the convenience of clones and parallel thought processes for that.

And so far, pretty much nothing happened on this end the whole time I was here in the school. Just the same old life as it is, you can say. Nothing out of the ordinary.

Or at least, ordinary in the relative sense of the word. I'm pretty sure in that span of time, there were at least five incidents of hearts being broken in the drama genre, ten fights in the gangster/martial arts genre, and a single match across all the different clubs in the sports genre.

In short, the usual stuff. Probably quite a short time on a narrative scale of things. A single chapter or episode, if viewed from an outside perspective. And not one with timeskips.

Still, there was a degree of normalcy to it all. If you were to consume a manga, light novel or anime this would be the point where you'd get slightly bored and think 'is something interesting going to pop up?', or something along those lines.

And most of the time, it does. Because in a world where an entertainment factor is required within a person's life, the possibility of this imaginary audience getting bored is the worst possible case there is.

—Which is where all of this comes in.

I stood upon the patch of grass bordering the concrete walkway, one that was overlooking the large field of land right in our school's campus. Despite it not being lunchtime yet, I was out and about the school grounds.

And it wasn't because I was skipping class like the delinquent people thought I am.

Instead, I was just using it as a time to observe the people gathering around the place. Or more specifically, the clubs who're going to be using it. I was at the sportsfield after all.

But why, one might ask, are people gathering in their clubs at this time of the day? Don't people usually do that at the end of classes, during the time that those that don't adhere to Japanese standards of a productive student go home?

Well, it has something to do with the event clearly. The clubs themselves look like they're in the middle of preparing something. And considering how they looked like they're in a rush, it seems that they're being chased by a deadline.

And of course, it's caused none other than the very thing discussed on a whim by the two powerful people not too long ago.

"—An interschool exchange event, huh…?"

A female schoolmate near me, someone from the track team based on her clothes, muttered that thoughtfully. The girl looked like she just finished a run, sweating slightly with a towel around her neck and a cold water bottle on her hand. And following right behind her was another girl who was probably in the same club.

"It's a bit sudden, isn't it?" the girl said to her friend. "You'd think they'd announce something like this much earlier. But no - they spring it on us as a surprise! And now everyone is rattled trying to get their preparations done on time." she shook her head. "…Seriously, telling it four days before isn't enough."

"I know right! Though I heard it's a real surprise for the student council as well." her friend replied. "Apparently the student council president and some of the faculty were complaining about it, considering it happened so suddenly. People are still going through with it for some reason though."

"Really?"

"Yeah, Iroha-chan told me all about it. I guess it must be important. Apparently, the school we're going to be meeting is a pretty big name… Kuoh, was it?" the friend muttered, looking unsure.

As the young president and the rest all looked at me in confusion from my nonsensical answer, the heroine quickly cleared her throat loudly, which made their attention turn to her.

"Ignore him, he's just saying random things." Yuki stated as an excuse. "Basa-kun just does that sometimes to mess with people."

Then, she let out a smile. It was, undoubtedly, a type of smile that I've rarely seen from her - mostly because it held a promise of mischief. I glanced at her curiously, wondering what was up with her and what she was planning to do.

And then she spoke once more.

"Actually, the real reason why he has experience would be because Basa-kun has formed a company of his own." she stated, before tilting her head to the side. "From what I remember… it was a consultant agency, I believe?"

The others looked at her in surprise.

I stared blankly.

—What.

"C-Company…?" the young president repeated, before turning to me with a wide-eyed expression. "Wait a minute, senpai - so you made your own company? Like, a real business?" she cried out. "No way. Are you for real? That's not a joke, is it?"

"It's not. I've seen it for myself." Yuki explained, answering the president's question. "He has his own office where he does his work and everything. It's all very professional."

"So there's a deeper part to his hidden side!? That's just way too shocking, isn't it!?" the glasses fujoshi shouted.

"W-Wait a minute, so he has a consultant agency? How does that work?" the queen bee asked as well, looking really curious unlike her earlier disinterest of me. "What exactly does he consult? Does he solve problems for people or something?"

Yuki nodded. "In a way, yes. Many people, from small to big clients, come to him for their problems to be solved."

"What the heck? That's so cool!" the cheerful girl cried out, her eyes sparkling.

The protagonist looked at me weirdly again. "…What are you, some sort of main character in an anime?"

Like you're the one to talk.

"Your own company… That's incredible. No wonder you have the experience and don't have the time for class representative duties." the riajuu breathed out. "Did your parents own it before and give it to you, Basa-kun?"

"No, I believe he made the company on his own. It wasn't handed down to him or anything. Just effort on his part." Yuki answered.

The riajuu's eyes widened some more, looking really speechless. "T-That's… really?" he stared at me, pure undisguised awe visible in his eyes. "You're something else, Basa-kun."

No, it's not. Don't you know how commonplace the 'Odd Jobs' shop business model is? There's way too many of them that you have to wonder how they survive against competition in the first place.

Anyway, all this talk and the impressed gazes aimed my way is making my brow twitch. Unable to stand such a sight, I looked away and continued to focus on the remaining paperwork, trying to ignore… whatever this nonsense was.

And for some reason, my actions made Yuki's smile widen. She tried to hide it with the piece of document in her hand, but I can definitely see it from the edge of my vision.

—Okay, seriously. What was she even doing?

What the heroine had said wasn't exactly a lie - but it's not entirely truthful either. The thing is, I have been operating under the name of many different companies to achieve my own ends and an investigative agency is one of the more convenient ones. And sure, I wasn't really making my connection to them a secret, using my identity freely instead of assuming another one - but I don't freely announce it to others either.

Mostly because putting attention to myself like that would easily remove my status as a side character. As I mentioned, doing so might make me involved with the plot, so I try to be as forgettable as possible in order to not deal with whatever problems the main cast might face.

And yet here's the heroine, throwing all my efforts away… Seriously, what's her deal?

I didn't have much time to wonder about it however, because somehow, the heroine managed to read my mind despite my various mental defenses and answered the question herself within my head.

You look remarkably embarrassed, Basa-kun. Have you been so used to your skills being hidden that getting praised like this affects you so much?

Her telepathic statement made my brow twitch again. Embarrassed? Who is she calling embarrassed? Nobody's getting embarrassed here, only the humiliation of my carefully crafted identity turning into shambles.

I mean, don't you know that I'm a stoic? My entire personality, lifestyle and dialogue is about being stoic. I religiously read books, watch videos and even shit stoicness. That's how unembarrassed I am.

Fufu. Yes, of course.

What's with that tone? It definitely sounds like she's just humoring me or something. Anyway, after saying that, the girl continued speaking in my mind.

In any case, I thought it would be nice for our classmates to know about you, Basa-kun. People don't really appreciate you for who you are, after all. And while you might be fine with it, I still think it's not quite fair for you to not get at least a bit of praise… Which is why I'm telling them all this.

I paused at her words, along with the sincerity that came with it.

…And is that really worth the risk of removing my status as a side character?

It shouldn't matter, doesn't it? After all, my plot has already changed from it once was with me turning meta. You're already established to be heavily involved with me, who used to be the heroine, along with showing off your skills to pass my sister's task. And we're not quite sure where this story is headed towards now and what genre it would be, so what's the point of worrying about that?

…

Hm. Fine, whatever. Do what you want.

I suppose the heroine's words were true. Just like Rias' plot, I have no idea where it was heading due to the fact that a meta character is heavily involved in it. But unlike Rias where the genre remained as action - the fact that the love triangle was already solved meant that the genre of Yuki's plot would be something else entirely.

Perhaps a slice-of-life story between the gloomy protagonist and his cheery, gyaru-like girlfriend? That seems like the most likely candidate.

Anyway, with Yuki's glazing plan having succeeded, these colorful cast of characters would definitely treat me differently from now on - maybe even approach me for their own benefit at times. Especially when Yuki mentioned the consultation agency part. And maybe even my paperwork skills after showing it off.

All in all, definitely more troublesome things to come.

—Or at least, that's what I thought. Because it appears that something troublesome already arrived the moment my little telepathic talk with Yuki finished. Although, in a manner that could be called fortunate or misfortunate, it was a different sort of trouble than what I had been thinking off.

Bang! "Yahallo! Everyone, are you done with the preparations?"


Spoiler

The door opened with a bang, shocking everyone, and what followed was a lively and familiar voice. Mostly because she's one-half the reason why we're dealing with this work in the first place.

Haru Yanai has entered the room… and judging by the familiar people (or at least, one of them) who were following right behind her, it appears that Kuoh had also arrived as well.


Spoiler

"Excuse us for the intrusion." Sona stated, entering with her own student council with her.

The sight of it was clearly a surprise to everyone else in the room.

"W-Wait a minute! Yanai-san!? And Kuoh too!? They're here now!?" the young president shouted, standing from her seat and looking at the group in shock and panic. "I thought that they'd arrive a little later! It's not even time for the school event to start yet!"

Yuki's sister tilted her head as she glanced at her. "Of course we'd arrive a little earlier. It's not like the representatives of the student body would arrive during the event itself, no? That's just bad manners. That said, the students themselves will arrive during the assigned time. "

Then, she looked around the room with an analytical eye, before finally settling her gaze on me with a smile.

"But based on your reaction… are the preparations not done yet, hm~?" she asked with a teasing tone. "That's a shame. I was expecting this to be easily dealt with, especially since I've made Haya-kun called the ever-so-dependable Basa-kun on the case…"

"Hard to do it when you literally dump a mountain of paperwork at the last minute." I said calmly while I continued writing on the papers.

Honestly, I really could deal with this much faster, doing so would require me using more supernatural powers and skills to speed up the process. But doing that in front of all these drama characters would be hard since it would force them to literally do something else due to the genre divide - which is why it would be better for me to actually just lean into my experience and work on it the normal way.

That said, it's not like I'd fail this little 'test' by doing it this way either. Because after a moment or so, I put the pen down on the table and leaned back on my seat, before gesturing on the papers.

"There. Feel free to take a look." I told her.

Haru blinked, before picking up one of the papers there.

"Things like liability waivers, consent forms, and MOUs - all the significant documents are pretty much done and dealt with." I explained to her as she read the document. "The ones left and are being worked on are the minor ones. They can be finished even when the event itself is in progress. That should be good enough for you, right?"

In any case, for a moment, there was a silence on her part as Haru observed our work. The student council president, along with the Service Club (except Yuki) and the riajuu plus his clique, all looked at both me and the woman with nervous looks.

…Then, after a while, Haru spoke.

"Hoh…? Looks like you really managed to do it." the woman said, looking slightly impressed. Then she smiled. "Alright, this is all fine then! You've successfully done one of my required tasks!"

I raised my brow. "'One of'? You asked for a single task, didn't you?"

"Please, do you really think that would be enough? That's just trivial. Anyone could do it in their sleep." Haru said with a grin, before putting the paper back down. "I'm satisfied. Just dump the remaining ones to the student council and let them do the rest of the work."

Trivial? This shit is worse than the workload of an unpaid intern. And why the hell are you including documents like the MOUs for the student council to deal with? That's the faculty's job, and all of it made the student council president almost cry from the sheer stress.

And that same president also looked pretty confused as to what was happening. "T-Task? What are you talking about, Yanai-san?" her eyes watered a bit. "A-Also please don't take Basa-senpai away! Everyone here can't function without him!"

"You just want him to deal with the rest of the remaining work…" the protagonist grumbled.

That guy is completely correct. And clearly, nobody here cared for that young president's crocodile tears, much less Haru who let out a laugh. "Too late, Iroha-chan! I've got a reservation for this guy. I'm the one who called him here." she said with a smile, before turning to the Kuoh student council. "…But for now, how about you converse with your colleagues for today? You'll be cooperating for the event after all."

And with her statement, everyone's attention turned to the tagalongs to Haru. And of course, being in the forefront and representing all of them - they turned to look at Sona.

Perhaps the first thing that they would notice looking at her was just how beautiful she is. Due to the fact that she was a demon, just like her sister Serafall, she has this air around her that surpasses the beauty of a normal human. In fact, the glasses fujoshi, who looked superficially similar and was also similarly popular with boys, couldn't really compare to her. That was just how beautiful she was.

"B-Basa-kun…?"


Spoiler

Then the second thing that they'd notice was the way the girl was staring at me with incredibly wide eyes. And with what she said, she pretty much gave away the fact that we knew each other. And that she looked intimidated by me for some reason, based on her look.

It was gone the next moment however, as that wide-eyed look swiftly turned into a glare. It was a complex glare, one that a person would make when they're scared but determined enough not to back down. The girl was also shaking slightly, but she quickly got rid of it by clenching her fists before approaching me with a resolved gaze.

"Basa-kun. It's good to see you." she greeted. "I didn't expect to see you here or even leading this entire event for your school but… There's something that I want to say."

Then, the girl took a deep breath and met my eyes directly.

"You might be able to beat me in many things, but Kuoh will not lose!" she shouted, no, declared. "We've prepared as much as we could during the four days that we've been given - and we're ready to show you just how superior our school is compared to yours! From sports to academics and everything in between, we'll crush you in every field!"

Everyone stared at her, mostly because the rest of the drama characters here were unable to react to such a hot-blooded shounen declaration from Sona. And for a short moment, there was only silence.

…Ma'am. This is an interschool exchange festival. Not a tournament.

"Ahem!"

As I thought that, one of the girls behind her coughed. It was a voluptuous-looking girl wearing glasses like Sona here, and judging by the energy I feel around her… A magus? Interesting. In any case, she spoke up.

"Please excuse our president here. She got excited regarding the event after a little slump. Now she feels very competitive since the reputation of the school she manages is on the line." she explained. "That said, her declaration isn't any less true. We will surpass you, your student council, and school itself in every way that matters."

…A slump? Ah, right. Her sister did mention doing the whole event thing just for her to get over it. Good for her.

"That's good and all, but you really shouldn't say that to me." I blankly replied.

The demon glasses girl blinked. "What? Why?"

"It's because I'm not the student council president." I said, before pointing my thumb to the side. "She is."

The clueless junior of ours, who was unfortunate enough to be our student council president, blinked when all of the attention turned to her after I pointed at the girl.

"A-Ah…?" the girl stuttered for a moment, before nodding her head politely at them. "H-Hello, I'm Iroha Isshiki, Sobu High School's student council president. It's… nice to meet you…"

Sona stared at her. Then I watched as, in a single fascinating moment, the girl's face turned red as the embarrassment of her mistake caught up with her. She managed to own it up though, keeping her reaction to the mistake as a single cough.

"A-Ahem! Sorry about that. I was… mistaken." she stated, trying to look anywhere besides my direction. "I am Sona Vignette, student council president of Kuoh Academy. It's nice to meet you as well."

A short silence followed after. One that was filled with questions: things like 'what the hell just happened?', or 'how do they know each other?', or maybe 'why does she look so beautiful?', et cetera, et cetera…

Really. This is way too awkward. Get me out of here.

—Clap! "Wow! That amount of energy is just what I want to hear."

Then suddenly, Haru clapped her hands once, interrupting the silence and making the majority of the people in the room stiffen in surprise. Everyone turned to her, and in response the woman just let out one of her iconic enigmatic smiles.

"So, now that you're introduced to one another, why don't you go and prepare when the students finally arrive? For now, I'll go and take Basa-kun with me. And my dear sister, of course!" she said, before heading to the door and waving at both Yuki and I. "Come on, you two."

The both of us shared a glance. Then, Yuki took her book and put it in her bag, before leaving it on the sofa where she sat. The girl then stood up before heading to follow her sister, and I did the same. Yuki did turn around to address her clubmates before she left the room though.

"I'll see you guys later, Kaede, Makoto-kun." Yuki told them.

Understandably they looked confused as to what was happening, but regardless of what they felt - the both of them still nodded their heads, recognizing that Yuki must have some sort of important business to deal with.

"R-Right. See you later, Yuki-chan!" the cheerful girl replied, letting out a smile. "Just give us a text once everything is done!"

Yuki smiled as well. "I will."

And with that we went out of the student council room, following behind Yuki's sister. As we got out the door and walked in the school's halls, Haru turned to Yuki with a curious look.

"You didn't tell them what was going on? Strange, I thought you guys were close?" she asked.

Yuki nodded. "We are. But the circumstances are a bit different now so I can't explain it to them." she glanced at the woman. "Just like how I couldn't explain everything to you, nee-san. Undoubtedly to your frustration."

That made Haru hum in thought. "Hmm. Frustration, huh…?" she repeated. "Well, I suppose that's the right word for it. The fact that you've involved yourself in something that I can't understand is certainly frustrating."

Then she grinned.

"That might change soon enough though."

After saying those words, the woman seemed to decide that it was the best time to end our conversation. Ending it there certainly added some weight to her final words, which the woman definitely recognized and did on purpose.

It was clear that this crafty woman had something planned. I wasn't particularly interested to see what it's about though - instead, I was busy thinking about other things in store for us. And as I heard the voice of the heroine in my head as we walked to the destination once more, it appeared that she was thinking of the same thing.

There doesn't seem to be that much progress, Basa-kun. The girl stated, having brought out her phone earlier and now fiddling with it. Rias just messaged me that they're already near the school. It'll probably take a few minutes before they arrive, but there are no signs of anything unusual when she searched with her familiars.

I glanced at her for a moment, before looking forward again. Is that so? And the others?

V and Aoki-san are currently investigating the espers, aliens and time travelers route. The last I heard from them, they were going to try and gain information from one of Aoki-san's idols since they're apparently an alien.

Hm. Now that I remember, we did encounter something like that when we went to Aoki-san's idol agency. I doubt those two idols had something to do with a city-wide destructive school war like the alert detailed, but it's still better than nothing.

I see. Looks like we'll have to wait for those two tasks to have a better idea, then. I stated.

Yuki's brows furrowed. …Is this really the best way to do this?

What do you mean?

I know you said it's the best way, but why do we have to act so… indirect? Yuki asked, sending me a questioning look. Trying to find all the affected genres and settings before the world-affecting scenario happens, effectively stopping the chaos from spreading once it occurs… Sure, it's a solution - but it's much better to address the source, isn't it? Much like during our time in the idol agency.

Hearing the heroine's question, I didn't answer her for a moment.

It was a valid thing to ask. And Yuki was right with her assessment. That was pretty much the plan on how to deal with this situation.

And it was completely different from the one we did last time, with us directly dealing with the horror monsters that spawned into existence due to the death of Terumi Fuuka. It's akin to isolating an infection and dealing with all the affected parts, as opposed to dealing with the source of infection itself.

In short, it was an inefficient way of dealing with things. You're just literally making yourself work harder. Or at least, that's how it looks.

But, the thing is…

How do you beat the unbeatable?

Yuki blinked. Pardon?

I answered her question fully. …I'm sure you've seen it, but a reality warper is the source of everything in this world-affecting scenario. It's leagues different from the horror monster we fought last time. I replied. I'm doing this for safety's sake. Recklessly entering their setting could prove destructive, so we'll have to deal with the surroundings first and leave the source itself the last.

Yuki digested that for a short moment. Then, she nodded.

…I understand. So right now, the enemy is someone to be very wary of. She concluded. Haruhi Ajimu, was it…? The files mentioned that she was someone you directly caused to become a reality warper, correct?

I couldn't suppress my lips twitching downwards at that.

…Yeah. I did. I thought bitterly. I messed up with her. Big time.

And I suppose that's just asking for the world to utilize it in its plotlines. With V already becoming the fourth and likely the last heroine, the conclusion of her arc meant the narrative could progress to other things. And what could be more hook worthy than a past mistake returning?

What's more, now it just had to tack on this stupid event and the tasks from those two women. Multitasking much, you shitty narrative? This better not be a set up for something else.

Sensing my bad mood however, the heroine spoke up. I think you couldn't be blamed for that. It's natural for you to make mistakes, especially at the beginning. You're completely alone and working blind at that point, after all.

Then, she let out a soft smile.

In fact, it's admirable that you care so much despite being in a position to ignore it. As someone who's essentially the most free person in the world - that you chose to keep yourself responsible for your mistakes is worthy of praise, isn't it?

I frowned at that.

…Not really. Anyone can do it.

The girl's smile widened. Is that so? Very well then.

I have a feeling she doesn't quite believe me.

I exhaled. In any case, those tasks would definitely have something to do with the world-affecting event that would happen. They might even be a direct line to it, and adjacent settings would likely be affected as well. I explained. It's essentially a big hint given to us, so we're lucky in that regard. If we didn't, we'd probably be feeling around in the dark to know which settings would be affected.

Yuki's brows furrowed again. I can't imagine my sister giving you a task which would somehow lead to that. Perhaps Serafall-san would, but nee-san should be affected by the genre divide. What sort of task would it even be?

You're forgetting that it's not all supernatural, Yuki. There's one setting mentioned in the alert that would count as 'mundane', isn't there?

The girl was quiet for a moment, then she blinked. You're thinking of the delinquent gangs? Are you saying that my sister would dabble in that sort of setting?

It's just a guess. I stated. Honestly, with the way things are, it probably involves protecting this event in school from gangs or something. Remember, this event, the tasks, and the world-affecting scenario - it's all connected. Or at least, that's what my instinct is telling me.

…I can't even begin to wonder how that would even come to fruition. What, would my sister be threatened by delinquent gangs? My sister, who's a politician with significant influence? Her?

Who knows, really. This world is governed by a narrative force. Anything could happen.

Or more accurately: it could do whatever the fuck it wants, so long as it doesn't stop the suspension of disbelief from the unseen audience it tries to satisfy.

In any case, it seems that my time to talk with Yuki was over. Mostly because the woman in front of us stopped at a certain room in the school hall, making us stop with her as well.

It seems that we've finally arrived at our destination. The woman turned around and gave us a smile.

"Alright, let's go inside!" Haru said.

And with that, she brought us to a meeting room in the school. It was usually reserved for the faculty, but it seems like it was reserved for our use now. But then again, I suppose this also counts as an important meeting, since one of the greatest authorities between the two schools in this event was with us.

But it seems like the other great authority was already waiting in the meeting room, as evidenced by us receiving a greeting the moment we opened the door to the place.

"Oh, you're back!" Serafall said cheerily, chilling inside the room. "Yahallo Basa-kun, Yuki-chan!"

Yahallo? What, is she using that greeting now as well? Is it spreading?

I looked around for a moment. It's just her in here, looks like. Me, Yuki and her sister all sat down on the meeting table, with me and Yuki directly opposite Haru and Serafall.

"We're not gonna wait for Rias?" I asked.

"She's going to arrive with the rest of the student body. And I already told her what she's going to do." Serafall replied, before tilting her head slightly. "That said - it's going to be different from what you're doing, you know? Remember: you're doing all this to prove your allegiance to us."

"…And that task is? Seriously, just tell me straight. This could've been an email."

Serafall grinned. "And ruin the surprise? Tsk tsk tsk. Young people these days are so impatient…" Everyone here is young compared to you, you centuries-old demon. "And just for that, I'll be saying my task last! Why don't you go first with what you want Basa-kun to do, Haru-chan?"

What a pain in the ass. I turned to Yuki's sister, who also let out a smile.

Haru let out a smile. "Sure, why not?" the woman said, before adjusting her posture to look at us. "Alright… in the interest of saving everyone's time, I'll be brief. I'm also quite impatient as part of said 'young people', you see."

Serafall pouted. "Ne, Haru-chan. Is that a diss? Are you dissing me? I'm not old!" That was a lie.

"—In any case," Haru continued without a hitch. "I think I have a perfect task for you to deal with Basa-kun. But first, I've been told that you apparently run an investigative agency? And a lot of other companies too, apparently. That's very impressive for someone who still isn't out of high school, isn't it?"

She wasn't present when Yuki mentioned it earlier, but I suppose she would know considering how much she likely researched about me.

"Yeah, so?"

"Well consider this a commission then. As for the task itself… Well, I suppose it's better to show you."

Saying that, the woman then went on to retrieve an envelope on her shoulder bag, before dropping it on the table and gesturing for me to pick it up. I shared a short glance with Yuki, before taking the thing and checking what's inside.

And what was revealed to us were… letters.

It wasn't formal letters that one might send through mail; most of them were poorly made and almost looked childish. Kanji made from bold and thick ink brush strokes greeted us, along with different emblem stamps of some sort - one that read 'Declaration of War' in all its shameless glory.

And looking like I am, I was completely familiar with what these letters were.

"—Here you go, Basa-kun! I want you to deal with a little delinquent problem in our school!" Haru said cheerily. "Apparently we're going to be targeted by gangs! Isn't that scary?"

Meanwhile, Serafall blinked beside her.

"Oh my, what a coincidence." she said in surprise. "I'm actually dealing with a delinquent problem as well. Who would've thought?"

Yuki and I stared at them.

"…Delinquent gangs attacking the school while we're in the middle of an event." Yuki muttered. "It seems that things have progressed the way you've said, Basa-kun."

Yeah. Definitely looks like it.

I let out a sigh.

…How entirely fucking predictable.

Chapter 27

A bright sunshine instead of a dreary sky.

A bustling city instead of a quiet and desolated land.

And people smiling and living life, instead of suffering under the horrors of war.

Her eyes beheld the sight of a city, teeming with life and so many different things. Things that she had never seen or known before, due to the nature of her upbringing and the state of the land she had hailed from. A place that is deemed as 'normal', yet seemingly so alien for someone like her.

—A truly peaceful place, this country called Japan.

Putting a hand on the glass window with her feeling right hand, V had thought that statement not for the first time, as she watched the city while on the higher floors of a large building they had found themselves in.

It was a very grand sight, mostly because she had never been inside a tall building like this before to see such a wide view of the landscape, and she took the opportunity to enjoy it and take it all in.

"…V-chan? Is everything alright?" a voice suddenly asked her.


Spoiler

"There is no problem." V answered. "I was simply enjoying the view, Aoki."

"The view…? Oh, I suppose you're right." the blue-haired woman then moved on to stand beside her. "The view of the city here is beautiful, isn't it? There's nothing much blocking the way… I've never really appreciated it before though."

V nodded her head. Indeed, it was quite beautiful.

Just like everything in this place, really. Ever since she had arrived here after deciding that she wanted to live with Basa - she had experienced quite a lot of what a 'normal' life has to offer. For her and likely many of the people back in Westalis, living a life here was similar to living in paradise.

Food, water and shelter being so easily available. Streets so safe that children are allowed to roam freely, and for anyone to go out late at night without fear of being killed. So many opportunities and conveniences available for all, comparable or even exceeding those of the rich elites.

She was truly lucky to be here and experience it all… And perhaps, one day the country she lived in will turn out to be this way. She was effectively controlling the government now, after all.

As thought about that, a glance to the side made her realize that Aoki was staring at her with a motherly smile on her face. She tilted her head.

"Yes?" she asked.

"I'm glad that you're able to enjoy yourself, V-chan." Aoki replied. "I was worried that you'd be really bored here. This place is nothing compared to where you went last time with the others after all."

She looked at her in confusion. "…I fail to see why you should be worried. We're here because of our task to investigate the alien setting, correct? My feelings should have nothing to do with it."

"Hm, I don't think so. This is our first time hanging out together, isn't it? So I was thinking that it should be special. I wasn't able to join you guys last time, after all."

Aoki said those words. Then, her smile turned a bit sad and she continued.

"…But I suppose that was for the best. I think you guys wouldn't enjoy it as much if I joined. An old woman like me would make it look like I'm acting as a chaperone, after all."

V blinked, and she turned to face her.

Buses came in droves bringing the students. They entered the campus with curious and excited looks on their faces, with an atmosphere that one might see during a school field trip or something. And considering the situation where they visited another place to look around - it might as well be.

And of course, Sobu had a similar reaction as well. Many are intrigued on what students have been invited to our school, even excited about the people that they would meet. But besides that, there was also a pervading unspoken atmosphere held upon the student body - an air of apprehension, as the Sobu students looked on what the reactions our 'guests' would take, since we're supposed to be the hosts right now.

The initial meeting was awkward and formal. Mostly because the Kuoh students were still directed by the faculty of their respective schools along with their class representatives. They were sent to the sportsfield where students of Sobu had also gathered, dividing the large track of land into two: with one side being the Kuoh students and the other being the Sobu students.

And right in front was a prepared stage. Standing there were important faculty members and, of course, the two student council presidents of each respective school. One of them looked more centered than the other, but with a bit of encouragement from the riajuu and, strangely, the 'outcast' protagonist (what a casanova) within the Sobu crowd - our young student president started to act more composed.

That was easily missed by everyone else though, mostly because at that point the faculty had been doing a speech about something or another. But it was also just in time since shortly after, it was time for the student council presidents to recite the prepared 'oaths' in the ceremony.

At least our president was able to keep her voice level like the glasses demon did. They then recited stuff about respect, honesty, cooperation between the school, and fair play for the exhibition matches.

Until finally…

"—With that, the curtain rises on our interschool exchange! Let's make these days unforgettable; one full of challenges, laughter, and bonds that will carry on long after it's over! And so, we declare… the Kuoh-Sobu interschool exchange event officially begins now!"

Both students announced the start of the event, and they were met with substantial applause between both student bodies. The gathered student crowd started to dissolve as the Sobu students went to their respective venues and the Kuoh students got to finally explore.

And amongst the latter were some eye-catching people. A club filled with beautiful and handsome people that captured both Kuoh and Sobu students alike - but mostly the latter because they clearly were subjected to their beauty for the very first time.

That said, what was surprising was that the most beautiful of them, the club leader, greeted someone from the Sobu students with great familiarity - raising her hand and calling to them from far away as they approached.

"Hey, Yuki-chan! Nice meeting you here, huh?"


Spoiler

Rias greeted Yuki with a grin right in front of everyone, keeping her promise last time that she'll greet Yuki because it'll 'increase her popularity points' or some nonsense. Although, she might have a point in the end, since people are wondering why Yuki would know about someone like Rias, especially considering she was from another school.

That said, the reaction was mostly confusion though. Yuki's club and the riajuu's clique pretty much stared at Yuki and Rias, puzzled and curious about how they knew each other. As for the Service Club itself - the protagonist and his girlfriend were looking at their leader like she was a different creature entirely.

Yuki's face blushed, completely embarrassed about the whole situation.

"Hello, Rias." she said with a forced tone. "It's nice to meet you here as well."

Unlike the rest of them though - there was me, standing right beside them like a chill guy without a change in expression. Because I'm an oregano male whose face is granite and shows no weakness.

Or at least, a clone of me is. I'm actually nowhere near the sportfield right now. Instead, I was walking in the school halls, heading right to the exit so that I could leave the school gate.

I do have some tasks to attend to after all.

However, it appears that I won't be alone in my little adventure. Since the moment I was about to leave the school, I sensed a presence of someone waiting near the school gates. And that person greeted me the moment I actually went outside.

"So you're really going, huh?"

I actually didn't since I'm technically still there - but then again, the genre divide.

Great, cool entrance done.

Now let's go flyswatting.
