Chapter 28

The Sobu Park. A relatively beautiful park to visit.

Planted in the place were plenty of cherry blossom trees that offered a beautiful view during the flowering season. As of now though, those very same trees were withered, and little to no people had any reason to visit the park leaving it quite deserted.

Once upon a time, this was where a story had begun. The wrong place a certain girl had visited at the wrong time, setting off events that led to everything that was happening now.

However, today was a different occasion.

For today, in this park, a great gathering of people had formed. Young gangsters, thugs and delinquents from different schools - people misspending their youths and yet to bloom, who fit the withered aesthetic of the park so naturally, had all gathered here for one purpose.

They were here to do the behest of a certain crafty woman, one who had been caught off-guard and had no choice but to do so to put her money in her mouth.

Yet the specifics of it was easily forgotten or misunderstood, it seems. Because overhearing one simple conversation can allow a person to know they had escalated a plan to threaten someone into a plan to inflict actual violence.

An unbelievable mistake… However, such is the nature of hotheaded youths. And it was that same nature that led them to treat the others with suspicion as well. A promising reward that everyone wanted to have for themselves - and it was for that reason that they were about to clash.

The strong get to do what they want, while the weak perish. It was the single and greatest rule of nature, muddled by human society, and yet seemingly returned to its purest state in the world of delinquents.

This was a simple fight of dominance amidst hundreds of others, and a way of life for everyone else involved.

—But then, something had changed.

An unknown person had come out of nowhere and toppled one of the beasts that participated in the fight for dominance. No one had anticipated their arrival, and no one knew who they even were.

They simply arrived like a natural calamity: without warning and without mercy.

Yet this was not another player to the dominance game. No, this was different - one that was keenly felt within every delinquent present.

The sixth sense that was honed from years of participating in various fights and conflicts, a privilege which a normal person living in a mundane society would never have. Some might call it fighter's instinct, while to others, it was Nature's gift of judgement.

Nevertheless, it had acted up. And it was with such a unique perspective that they were able to see such a strange sight.

"…Oi oi oi. What the hell is this?"

One of the beasts participating in the game of dominance, muttered in shock as he stared at the aftermath of the entrance. He looked at this new arrival with wide eyes, staring at him and taking in all the details that he could.

Or at least, that was what he attempted to do.

I… I can't see his face? What is going on?

—Because his mind, like everyone else's right now, was in shambles.

The sun was bright and the details were clear to see. Yet no matter what they did, they couldn't focus on the man's face. Even as their gaze was staring at man, instead of taking his appearance, they instead took his entire form - from the graceful way he stood up after burying the toppled beast's face to the ground, his resolute and strong posture, and his relaxed stance that conflicted with the strength that they saw.

It was an indescribable phenomenon. However, it was one with a clear explanation. Or at least, a barely believable one to those in a martial mindset.

It was said that in a flight or fight situation, the amygdala hijacks a person's brain. This hijack triggers a massive dump of adrenaline and cortisol as immediate physical reaction is prioritized over detailed information processing. The eyes' depth of field narrows, and the brain hyperfixates on the threat.

If a knife pointed at a person, a person would have a hard time remembering the shirt of the person wielding it. Then, what if a fighter's instincts register the entire person as a threat? Their brain would then focus on what he considers most important - which is the posture, the movement, and everything that might relate to fighting.

Indeed, it was their own instincts that had betrayed them at this moment.

Yet, it was clearly abnormal to witness. So what does it mean if their instincts and body react in such a manner?

It should've been a mystery, but deep within themselves - they already know the answer. Because the instinctual, amygdalian mind internalizes greater truths far more than the logical, prefrontal cortex ever could.

And from that, they were able to determine that what they faced right now.

It wasn't a rival that was to be dominated or driven off. They weren't even facing an equal.

Instead, they were facing something above their level. Something far more sinister.

Something that wasn't meant to be engaged, but rather to flee and hide from instead.

In other words, what they're looking at right now…


Spoiler

…was clearly nothing other than a predator.


What is flyswatting?

It's a very common thing to see, yet in the perspective of a story, the specific details of it are quite nuanced.

As always in anime or manga, the powerful character making an absolute mess of weaker characters never fails to be entertaining. It's a moment where they get to cut loose after all, and accompanied by colorful animation visuals that could make a Victorian child go into a seizure - it would surely be enough to become memorable in the minds of the viewers.

It's also different from something like, say, a curbstomp. The point of the curbstomp is to humiliate certain characters and showing utter domination in order to provoke catharsis. Flyswatting, in essence, is to show that the character is above conflict. Usually by showing that the vibe of the fight is casual and dismissive. And unlike curbstomping, it's not stretched out at all. In fact, it's usually done as fast as narratively possible.

And right now, I'm going to do it.

…And doing it is a damn chore.

Perhaps if I were a character limited in one setting doing that might be easy. Entertaining even. However, I'm not. And while I might be powerful enough because of my pretty long off-screen training arc, utilizing said power would be pretty hard without forming a headache.

As I've always said, I refuse to stick my nose in troublesome business. I want to minimize my presence so that the narrative doesn't just involve my story to whatever it wants, and flyswatting, in essence, is the direct opposite of that.

To treat beating an opponent as if you were just swatting flies conversely proves you are strong, which essentially turns the story's gaze onto you. So unless I find it absolutely necessary and I have to actually involve myself in the plot (e.g. V and the rest of Golden Dawn's story), I wouldn't even dare to do something like that.

But if that was the case, then what exactly am I doing right now? Has Basa-kun lost his mind and finally exposed himself as the true hypocrite that he was?

Well the thing is, as with all things in life, there are exceptions. There are certain conditions to meet before I'm sure that I can do such things. All of which ensure that there will be no lasting consequence regarding my actions.

—Let me demonstrate.

"B-Boss…?"

There was no answer from the big guy underneath me. Seeing their leader's unmoving form, the delinquents who were under the big guy that I took down all turned to me with enraged confusion - before rushing towards me.

"Take him down!"

"We'll show you for messing with us Yakuza!"

No one took me down, nor anything was shown.

The moment they rushed at me together - the next moment consisted of them being launched away from me together as well, and their beat up bodies ended up sprawled on the ground or colliding with the trees and fellow delinquents around them.

And in response to that, all the people around clearly reacted with shock.

"W-Who the hell is that guy!? Why is he so strong!?"

"A martial artist? I-I've never seen those moves before!"

"I don't recognize him at all…!"

Condition number one. No one actually knows what I look like.

I have casted a minor concealment spell on myself, enough that they won't actually recognize my appearance. If used in a crowd I'd fit seamlessly as a faceless bystander, but being in the focus like this changes its nature slightly.

The specifics of which depend on the person themselves: for example, my face could always be shaded at the right angle so that they can't actually see my features, or it could be explained by some contrived martial artist bullshit due to them thinking I was a threat. Or anything else, really.

This way, it provides some flexibility for the narrative to not outright target me. The narrative could use this scene as a set up for some other character or, best case scenario, it wouldn't touch what I did right now at all.

"—Gabwuh!"

As I finished the last of the mooks under the big guy, punching the wannabe-thug in the abdomen with enough force to launch him flying three feet in the air - I paused as I detected three separate presence, and then adjusted my position accordingly.

I leaned to the side to dodge a strike aimed at my head, letting the fist pass through the space that I occupied earlier. Then I jumped back to avoid a whipcrack of steel, making it hit the ground instead, then also sidestepping after that to barely avoid the large arm brought down behind me like it was a hammer.

With those three consecutive attacks avoided with ease, there was a slight pause in the fight. And clearly, with there being a pause - there was a moment for short dialogue.

I respected it, putting my hands on my pockets for aura points, if only to observe the people I was 'fighting'.

"So you dodged all that… heh, you must be something else." the guy with a weed on his mouth muttered with a grin.

The lady using a chain as a weapon simply spun it around beside her, readying it for another hit towards me. The big guy, meanwhile, just dusted off the dirt on his uniform and threw away his broken glasses. None of them spoke, yet it was clear from their focused eyes that they're taking me seriously.

Clearly, they aren't going to be defeated easily like the mooks. That said, they're not quite part of the main cast either… some of them, at least.

Which leads onto the second requirement.

Condition number two. I'm fighting characters not part of the major cast. Or at least, not part of the major cast yet.

These three representing the whole group look very much like side characters. A fair-looking guy with a weed in his mouth, a beautiful girl with a chain weapon, and a really big guy. They look like they're part of the major cast - but there is something to be noted about each of them here.

"Orya, orya, orya! Take this!"

I dodged the fist thrown at me. I did it easily, because the guy only kept throwing his right hand and the other stayed firmly in his pocket. It was an odd and awkward thing to do, considering he seems to move like a boxer.

A trump card? A cursed arm of some sort? No, the guy eating weed just has one hand paralyzed. And it's in a way that seems completely healable as well by normal martial arts bullshit and not the special ones. Considering the fact that this guy is an antagonist but has a fixable attitude - he seems like the textbook enemy turned friend in an action anime.

"Humph…!"

And as the guy eating weed dished out rapid attacks - the big guy also used the opportunity to hit me with incredibly telegraphed attacks. It was easier to dodge, but it was strong enough to displace air each swipe. Probably deadly for any mundane fighter.

The big guy looked interesting, especially since an idle structural scan made me learn that he's actually fourteen right now. A surprising fact considering he's over six foot tall, but then again I've seen stranger things. Still, I doubt that he's actually part of any ongoing plot right now, because most action anime occur during high school, and this guy would currently be in junior high.

He'd probably be a powerhouse in the future. But right now? He certainly isn't the most dangerous fighter. Mostly because narratively - there was someone here who's in the middle of a story right now, and would therefore be more 'experienced'.

And so I turned to the final and, arguably, the most interesting one.

"...!"

The sound of steel rubbing against steel echoed, and as I kept dodging the hits of the two fighters - there was an opponent that expertly used their chain weapon to slither around, trying to hit me and snag me in places where I wouldn't notice.

The chain lady moved with great skill and precision as if she was a seasoned warrior, and since she's in the middle of a story, she probably already experienced a ton of fights to improve herself. The chain flowed around her like a living being, striking things like a whip with enough force to break the sound barrier.

She actually doesn't fit this second requirement of not fighting the main cast, but… well, I'd involve myself in her plot anyway, considering her school involves one of my tasks.

After all, her uniform clearly says 'Ishiyama High School', which was the school that Serafall told me to deal with.

That said, I think this is enough time observing. It's about time to deal with them… which then connects to the last and most important requirement of flyswatting.

Condition number three. Finish the fight decisively.

Let me get back to an earlier question: What is flyswatting?

The answer is simple.

It's honestly just a way to show off.

And with that, there's no point to keep this charade up. The characters' capabilities have been shown from the short time I did nothing. From that, a clear baseline is established.

And judging with that same baseline… an outside viewer can truly know what 'powerful' really means.

Because what is showing off, if there's no audience to watch?

"...!?" / "K-Kuh…!" / "Tch!"

A simple tug of the chain at the right moment, and the chains entangled in a way that the two guys got themselves snagged. The lady, meanwhile, was unable to tug the chain from my grasp as I held it.

—And then I started beating them down.

I pulled the snagged guys towards me, dodging all their attacks and further entangling them with the chains while I unleashed a combo of moves and skills that I've honed throughout my life in this shitty anime world.

A well-placed strike in their organs.

A piercing knuckle hit their pressure points.

A rapid transition of different katas of martial arts, overwhelming them with unpredictable strikes.

I hit them with all of it. I didn't even need to bring out the bullshit ones to deal with them. I just made sure that I dished out the appropriate amount of damage that they can recover without lasting effects… though that amount can be rather generous.

"Ghgk! H-Huh? My arm…?"

The first to tap out was the guy eating weed. Though that was mostly because I struck a pressure point in his paralyzed arm that somehow caused him to feel it temporarily. Strange, that wasn't supposed to happen… unless the world decided to use me as a background that would push him to martial arts, so that his arm would be healed.

In any case, because of his surprise, he wasn't able to fully dodge my next hit which clocked him right in the stomach. The guy eating weed collapsed on the ground, unconscious.

The big guy though, was more resilient compared to him. Despite not dodging at all and taking all of my attacks directly, the guy managed to still stay conscious despite the copious amount of blood coming out of him.

A perseverance fighter, then. I could even see the wisp of an aura around him, symbolizing his fighting spirit or whatever. If left alone, then he could probably stay fighting despite it being physically impossible. And that probably meant that he's been undefeated for many of his fights.

So let's also give him a humbling experience for his backstory, shall we?

A swung a final punch to his jaw - the picture perfect form of someone hitting a person's knockout button. Except this time, I mixed with a bit of sleeping magic, amplifying the effect even more.

And because of that, the big guy's eyes rolled up, and he fell on his knees. As he slowly fell on the ground, I let go of the chains. Both hit the ground with a loud thump, and I stepped on top of the chain to prevent it from being used once more.

—Then I turned around.

The delinquent lady was looking at me with wide eyes. It was clear that she was shocked and even a bit afraid of what she saw, but mad props to her, the girl still charged towards me with a ferocious expression, abandoning her weapon and rearing back her fist instead.

"Hyaaah…!" she cried out.

Impressive willpower. However, I hit her with the abuser's special: a backhanded fist, mixed with my sleeping magic. It was super effective and the redhead lady flopped down on the ground, no longer conscious.

I'll probably extract some of her memories later. Just to have an idea on what's the state of their story. For now though, I'll leave her alone.

And with that, the three 'leaders' are taken care of.

…Still, the flyswatting wasn't done.

"Y-You gotta be kidding me…"

"Should… should we run away…?"

As if the world wanted to remind their existence, those unsure and fearful voices cut through the grim silence of their leaders' defeat. I turned to the rest of the delinquents, all of whom stared at me with faces of shock and fear - and simply gave them no reaction still, despite showing off my absolute dominance.

Gotta act the part of a cool and nonchalant guy, after all.

Still, something did catch my attention when I looked around. It wasn't those delinquents however - but rather someone else who came here with me and, surprisingly, has been watching me the whole time like those delinquents.

And understandably, she has a similar expression on her face to the delinquents as well. Although, it seems greatly less composed to the shocked look she'd displayed before.


Spoiler

"Hm… Interesting." I muttered under my breath.

So she was able to witness that action segment? The skill we've displayed was borderline superhuman. No mundane person would be allowed to see it with the genre divide around.

Yet here she was, somehow managing to do it. Very interesting, indeed.

…But, oh well. Thinking about that can come later.

I turned back to the rest of the delinquents, who looked stuck between running away or trying to attack me together. Some of the smarter ones already ran away much earlier - but to those who stayed… Well, I suppose I'll just give them a brief reminder of why they can't come near Sobu, despite the fact that I'm the only delinquent here.

—I flexed my hand into a claw, making my knuckles crack.

Not that I consider myself a delinquent, no sir.


"…Hm? Did you hear that…?"

Yuki gave a curious look at Rias, who suddenly said those words. "What do you mean?"

"Oh, I just heard what sounded like a bloodcurdling scream or something…" the redhead frowned. "You think that means Basa-kun is doing good out there?"

That made her tilt her head. "The park might be near, but I doubt a scream from there could be heard up to…" Yuki paused, before seemingly settling upon a realization. "I see. Yes, I suppose he must be."

She closed her eyes and let out a breath.

"…And it looks like this event is undisturbed for now."

Yuki muttered that as she then looked over the event, observing the Kuoh students who were exploring the halls of Sobu curiously. Staring out the window with a direct view of the sportsfield, one can also see the sports exhibition matches in progress - it was baseball right now, it looks like. But there would be opportunities for other sports as well at later times.

"Yep! You guys worked hard on doing this, right?" Rias replied with a smile as she walked beside her. "That must have been hard. I know that Sona-chan was definitely stressed dealing with it at the last minute. You guys must have felt the same."

Yuki shook her head. "Not really. It was only thanks to Basa-kun that we managed to even finish it… although my sister would've probably waved it all away, in the end. She probably didn't expect us to finish it all from the start - in fact, I'm certain she counted on it being unfinished."

"Really? Why?" Rias asked curiously.

"My sister wanted to set the stage. It's likely a ploy to discourage him, even if it's unreasonable to put someone not part of the student council to work on their tasks." she answered. "Not that it worked, however."

The redhead still looked like she didn't understand. "Mmm… I don't get it. What do you mean by ploy?" she tilted her head. "This is one of those drama things that I don't understand, isn't it?"

"It's not exactly a drama thing, Rias. Just a manipulation tactic. I imagine you need to learn those things as well, considering you mentioned that the world of demons is full of tricky people like that."

Rias pulled a face. "Bleh, more studying. I've had enough of it." she then shook her head. "Anyway! Enough about that. We should just enjoy the event with the others! We finally get to hang out with each other 'officially' after all. What we have right now will definitely be a novel experience!"

The redhead then paused.

"Well, maybe not now exactly." she amended. "But I am looking forward to knowing it later!"

Out of context, her words don't make any sense. Yuki and Rias are walking the halls together without their respective clubs while heading towards the school's exit, the both of them clearly going to leave the school campus despite Rias' words of 'wanting to enjoy the event'.

However, looking at the window where they could see the stands on the sportsfield - those with a sharp eye would notice that Yuki was also watching in the stands with the rest of her club. Joining her was Haya-kun and his group of friends along with Basa-kun, and of course, Rias and her club as well who had joined them earlier.

They had left soul copies of themselves behind. Because while they do want to enjoy the event, there are important things to take care of.

"I can't wait to transfer our copies' memories after this." Rias commented with a bright smile. "I wonder what sort of things we're going to be up to…?"

Yuki chuckled. "I imagine it'll be interesting at least, with you always taking the initiative."

"Can't help it! I want to know more about how things usually are around you, after all!" Rias grinned. "I want to know more about you, Yuki! In every way possible!"

The sudden sincere comment caught Yuki off-guard, and she coughed. "R-Right." she muttered. "Then, I hope I can do the same as well. I believe the school visit goes both ways."

"Ohh? Nice! I'll show you around our club mansion, then!"

She'd heard so much about this supposed place. It always struck her odd that Rias could somehow have such a thing in the school campus, but with her family being influential in hell - Yuki guessed that accomplishing it would be easy.

"I'll look forward to it." Yuki replied with a smile, before turning a bit more solemn. "For now though… I suppose we should focus on what we should do."

That made Rias mirror her expression.

"Un. We should." she agreed with a frown. "Especially considering what Serafall-san told me just this morning… Yeah, there's definitely a lot to take care of in this one."

Yuki nodded, feeling the same.

By that point, they were already near the school exit. She and Rias went outside the school grounds, and Yuki led Rias to the agreed venue of all the challenge letters that were given to the school. Coincidentally, it was the same park where she had met Basa-kun for the first time, so the place held a lot of meaning for her.

It took just a bit of walking since it was a short distance away from the school. And when they got there…


Spoiler

…It seems that they were correct in their suspicion that Basa-kun was doing quite well. But then again, she supposed that it was to be expected. The chances of him losing to delinquents of all things is outright impossible.

"Ohh, that's an intimidating sight." Rias commented with an intrigued look.

Indeed, it was very intimidating. And if it weren't for the fact that she knew that these people belonged in an action genre who would easily recover from this, she'd probably call for an ambulance. Or the police. After all, Basa-kun's appearance right now doesn't paint a good picture.

Nevertheless, Yuki sighed as they approached him. "You're covered in blood, Basa-kun."

"I guess it's that time of the month." she blinked at his reply. W-What? "Anyway, don't mind it. As you can see, it's clearly not mine. It doesn't help that the delinquent and martial arts genre is particularly generous with spilling blood… then there's also my little quirk too. And here I thought it activated earlier."

"At this point, I think you're just using that quirk of yours to justify carelessness." she said, before giving him tissues beforehand. "…Here, use this to wipe yourself."

He took it and started doing just that. "What, you're not doing it yourself this time? Shame. I guess you got self-conscious after others pointed it out last time."

Yuki blushed. "I-I did not! And there's nothing to be self-conscious about in the first place!"

"Hehe, he's got you there, Yuki-chan." Rias said with a grin, before looking around. "So these are the delinquents that's going to be involved in that world-affecting scenario… Eh?"

The redhead made a confused noise as she gazed in a particular direction. Yuki turned to where she was looking at - before she blinked, staring at the person standing a bit farther from where they were at.

"Nee-san…?"

It was her sister, Haru. And her expression was… novel, to say the least.

With the way she stood there - eyes almost blank and jaws wide open in sheer shock - Yuki herself couldn't believe what she's seeing. She had never seen her sister's composure broken as much as this in her entire life. In fact, she was questioning if this was even her sister that she was looking at right now.

"W-What? Yuki…?"

She heard her sister mutter, still looking out of it. Her eyes were also now looking at her uncomprehendingly, as if she was trying to unpack the implications of what she saw and what it meant for her.

As Yuki also stared at her sister, Basa-kun explained what was happening.

"Right. She was actually with me when I went on to deal with these delinquents. Probably wanted to make sure nothing goes wrong in her scare or whatever." he explained. "Anyway, clearly she's having trouble understanding reality right now. She never did expect that I could deal with all of these guys, after all."

Yuki blinked. "She saw you fight?"

"She did. Interesting, isn't it?" Basa-kun said with a smile, before returning to a more blank expression. "That said, we should go with the next part. Let's investigate all the schools that these gangs came from. They'll definitely be involved in the world-affecting scenario one way or another."

She took one look at her stunned sister, her mind clearly thinking of the implications regarding what Basa-kun had stated. Still, she turned to him and nodded.

This was more important, after all.

"I've quickly researched the schools mentioned earlier, when you left." Yuki mentioned. "With the demons and the aliens already determined - that leaves the espers, time travelers and those super-powered students as the only undetermined ones, correct?"

"The super-powered students are probably from the main setting which this whole problem comes from. That only leaves the time travelers and the espers." Basa-kun told her. "Why? Did you find something?"

"For the latter, yes. I believe there is a shrine near the school that V and Aoki-san are heading towards. Furthermore, your previous data stated that the place had experienced various occult conflicts before. I've also searched about the shrine online and apparently, there is a renowned spirit medium there. It's not exactly ESP but…"

"No, you might be onto something." Basa interjected thoughtfully. "Sometimes settings with espers also include shrine maidens and onmyoji as well. If it's not actual magic they're using, then it's most likely ESP of some sort."

Yuki nodded. "I'll tell that to the other two then." she stated. "Still, I'm not too sure of my own conclusion, so I think it would be best to keep an eye on things if there were some other surprises."

"Don't underestimate the might of hunches. And the fact that it neatly slides in everything is a plus. The narrative is efficient in using what little toys that it has to craft a story, after all."

She took note of that and nodded. Beside her, Rias made a thoughtful noise.

"Hmm, so that leaves the time traveler one, huh?" Rias tilted her head. "…Do you think it's those 'witches' that have been running around the town recently? They count as time travelers, right?"

Yuki frowned. "Perhaps." she said in thought. "But I hope not, the scale of devastation that some of them can dish out… that would complicate this problem further."

"Don't worry about that. I keep an eye on that particular setting. I'm relatively sure they're not the ones." Basa-kun reassured. "And it would likely have to involve delinquents considering everything. Chances are, we're looking at a time traveler who went back to being a delinquent student and led his gang to victory or something."

She sweatdropped. "That sounds… strange."

That made him raise a brow. "Strange, you say? As opposed to other settings out there? To something like, say, a balloon head monster?"

"…N-No, nevermind." Yuki shook her head, blushing and feeling a little bit silly of herself. "Maybe the concept just doesn't appeal to me."

Surely if you've been brought back in time, there are much more productive things you can do other than make a success story for your gang? Or at least, that's her opinion about it, but it's possible that there's important context she was missing if that was the case.

Rias, however, interjected. "Speak for yourself! I think that sounds really cool." she said with a nod. "Those stories where you go back to the past and walk all over everyone are just so peak! It's up there with power fantasy isekais and romcom harems!"

"Of course you're the type to consume slop." Basa-kun said with a blank gaze, before letting out an exhale. "I suppose the path is cleared out then. I already gained the info I want from the student here, so I can go deal with my other task about demon bullshit… Rias, what did Serafall ask you to do?"

The redhead blinked at the sudden question. "Hm? Well, she told me to not help you beat those demons, but…" she frowned. "Apparently, those pricks also kidnapped someone important and are in cahoots with fallen angels. We're going to have to rescue them."

"And where is that happening?"

"At a chapel near Akumano Academy." she answered with a smile. "I won't be taking my club with me, so I'll be going there with you!"

"Then that leaves me as the one who'd have to search for… a hypothetical time traveling delinquent." Yuki concluded. "Very well. I'll be working on that, then."

"You need help?" Basa-kun asked, to which she shook her head.

"No. This seems simple enough. It's just the usual investigation, isn't it?" Yuki replied easily. "The time traveling part is a bit tricky, but nothing a bit of effort could fix."

Basa-kun stared at her for a moment, before nodding.

And with that, it seems like the next course of action was already set… However, there was still one thing left that had to be dealt with, which Basa-kun acknowledged with a simple glance to Yuki's side.

"Little sister… Do you mind explaining to me what is going on?"

A question asked with a forced tone. Yuki turned, and there she saw her sister, barely managing to hold together her composure. She could almost see the many thoughts that were racing in her sister's mind, questions piling upon further questions, as she was undoubtedly forced to reexamine every single strange thing that they had talked about - including what they were saying right now.

Unfortunately for her, before Yuki could explain - the next thing that happened made everything worse.

"Welp! Honestly, I don't wanna wait when there's someone who needs rescuing, so I'll be heading out, alright?" Rias unfurled her wings and hovered above the ground. "I'll see you later, Yuki-chan, Basa-kun. I'll go and scout the place first—Huh?"

It was then that Rias blinked in surprise and Yuki's eyes widened. Basa-kun, always trying to act cool, meanwhile just raised a brow in response.

All of that was nothing in comparison to her sister's reaction. It was a very familiar expression, especially since she remembered making the same one in her mirror a long time ago. It was almost nostalgic really.

After all, that was the same face she made when she discovered the existence of the supernatural.

"S-S-She's flying…!?" her sister stuttered out.

Her sister paled as she looked at Rias, expression looking shocked and composure truly broken. Yuki was almost feeling the same even if it weren't for the same reasons.

It was one thing to hear that her sister had seen Basa-kun fight, but actually witnessing the supernatural is something else entirely. And one with a clear conclusion at that.

—Somehow, her sister must have gone meta.

How did it happen? And why? Does it have something to do with the location, since this was the same place where she 'awakened'? Or is it something else? And how does that connect into being Basa-kun's heroine? D-Does that mean she's also a love interest…?

The questions and implications she had thought earlier returned, this time with much more intensity. But before she could lose herself amongst the complicated feelings that were starting to overwhelm her - a sudden voice interjected.

"Hold on for a moment." Basa-kun stated, interrupting her thoughts.

While her sister still stared at Rias in shock, he then outstretched his hand and brought something out of subspace. It was a cube of some sort - Yuki didn't recognize it, but she could tell that whatever it is, it was clearly some sort of extremely advanced technology.

Without explanation Basa-kun dropped it into the ground, and there it started to transform, for lack of a better word. The cube started to morph and then collapse in itself, twisting its own dimensions and making a loud keening noise, until it somehow flattened and turned into what was likely a rectangular portal to… somewhere.

It was definitely a fascinating sight. And to a mundane person, it would be just as shocking as seeing a person grow wings and float above ground. After all, it was sci-fi technology in action.

"…"

Except… her sister didn't even comment on it. Despite the fact that the loud, keening noise would've snapped someone out of their daze, her sister's trance was somehow so deep that she didn't even take a single glance at it. In fact, she didn't even show any indication that she noticed it at all.

As if something had contrived it to be so.

Yuki blinked again. T-This is…

"Hm. False alarm." Basa-kun muttered, before heading towards the portal. "Okay. Guess I'll go now as well. See ya."

Almost as if he doesn't want to be bothered dealing with it, the man entered the portal and left, with it closing behind him shortly and leaving no trace of it behind. Yuki was left staring at the spot, slightly shocked at how sudden he had left.

Rias was also sporting a similar expression, looking at the spot Basa-kun and left and to her sister. Then, the redhead gave Yuki an unsure smile.

"U-Umm… Wow! He actually got there earlier than me. I should also go now." she said, awkwardly. "A-Anyway! Best of luck explaining things to your sister, Yuki!"

And after saying that, with a single flap of her wings - the girl ascended up high and disappeared into the clouds, heading towards her destination by air.

Leaving Yuki and her sister alone with a bunch of unconscious delinquents in the park.

Her brow twitched. Those two… it seems like they really left her alone to deal with this.

"Yuki." her sister whispered, looking up above the clouds. "Just what sort of thing did you involve yourself in?"

Yuki closed her eyes and sighed.

Indeed, this was going to be a pain to explain. With how her sister is, she's probably going to get grilled with as much information that she could. She's also not going to leave her alone, despite the fact that Yuki would be doing something important that would quite literally affect the entire world.

She might as well have received the world's greatest distraction at this point.

Here's to hoping the others fared better than she did.

…

…

Yuki paused.

Ah… that was definitely a flag, wasn't it?


Somewhere near Sainan High.

In what appears to be a normal neighborhood - a different sort of occasion was happening between a different pair of sisters. Both who are very unique in their own way in comparison to the rest of the world, even by the standards of an anime bullshit setting.

"Hahaha…! You really haven't lost your touch, nee-san! And here I thought you turned for the worse when you decided to stay on this backwater planet!"

One of said sisters was a redheaded girl whose hair was tied into a long ponytail. She looked much like an ordinary girl - if it weren't for the fact that she was dressed in dark garbs that showed off too much skin, making one wonder if she was dressing up as some sexy grim reaper.

And perhaps also due to the fact that her hair somehow morphed into a futuristic projectile weapon. One that was glowing with power and hummed with foreign energies which could potentially disintegrate her opponents in a single shot.


Spoiler

However, despite the fact that she could - she hadn't. Or perhaps she wasn't able to do so. Whatever the reason though, it's because of the one person fighting her.

"…Noisy."

The other girl's sister had golden blonde hair partially tied with ponytails. And much like the redhead, the blonde was dressed too in a dark outfit, even if it didn't show as much skin as the other one. Although unlike her sister, the blonde didn't yield a futuristic weapon… though her hair did form blades around her, undulating as if alive.

And judging by the large slashes that marked the concrete around the neighborhood, along with the bit of blood that was dripping from the redhead - all of it seems to point that the blonde girl was responsible for it, and that she was winning in their exchange.


Spoiler

It was a fight between two sisters.

Yet, it was nothing but a greeting for the two of them. An unconventional greeting, but then again, there's nothing conventional about these two.

Because if one were to be aware of their reputation out there in space… Then one can immediately say that these two are alien bioweapons. Deadly mercenaries, known as two of the most dangerous beings present in the galaxy.

—Or allegedly, at least. There's no shortage of powerful people in the world, after all.

"Haha… looks like that attitude of yours didn't change as well, huh?" the redhead muttered with a smile. "You're the same as ever… but it's clear that there's something you've lost."

The blonde stared at her without a change in expression - before her minutely widened, as the redhead approached her in a burst of speed that it almost looked like she moved in an instant.

"—!?"

The redhead's hair transformed into a blade-like weapon much like the blonde, except instead of it appearing like bladed hair appendages - it appeared as a monstrous looking sword that she wielded with both hands.

Sparks appeared between the bladed weapons, and the blonde disengaged. The redhead charged towards her, dodging the bladed hair appendages and made strikes of her own.

"Your killer instinct! Your bloodlust! Your willingness to kill!" the redhead shouted with manic glee. "You've clearly gone soft, dear sister! Has this planet changed you so much that you'd think you're nothing other than a weapon, oh legendary mercenary!?"

The blonde grit her teeth. "...Shut up…"

"If it were the old you, then you would have sliced me and this whole place into shreds in a single blink!" the redhead shouted. "Why are you trying to deny your true nature, sister? You weren't made to act this way!"

"I told you to shut up!"

In her heated cry, the blonde's hair seemingly responded, turning much more sharper and swiping everything around her. That made the redhead jump back, dodging the much more lethal attack and leaving her unharmed.

The same, however, didn't apply to the surroundings. With that attack, the houses near them and the street they're in ended up mangled, cut by hair which turned monomolecular blades, and caused the structure's cut off parts to slide off itself and crash.

The blonde's eyes widened, looking at the destruction that she caused. "N-No…"

"Oh? That was pretty good! So am I finally getting through?" the redhead said with a grin. "Exactly like that! Just continue that and you'll be fine!"

The blonde closed her eyes. "…I don't want to do this anymore, Mea."

Her words made the redhead's grin disappear. "Again? Hahh…" she sighed. "Does this planet make people lose their spines or something? If that's how it's going to be, then fine."

The redhead's hair transformed once more. But this time, instead of turning into another blade or a futuristic weapon - it turned into large pillar-like structures that surrounded her. Those strange structures glowed with energy, and one familiar enough with the sci-fi genre can recognize them at first glance.

Those were fin funnels, a powerful weapon system that only the most advanced mechs in this century can offer. And somehow, the redhead alien created it with only her hair, energy output steadily rising until it got to the point that it has enough energy to obliterate the entire neighborhood in a single volley.

The blonde's eyes narrowed. "Mea…!"

"Sorry, sister. But you've forced my hand." the redhead stated. "Originally I didn't want to do this, but I've seen other aliens here who seem to be in the same state as you. Powerful races who I would think twice engaging, yet seemingly acting so docile. I would've been fascinated… if it weren't for the fact that my sister was one of them."

That made the girl pause. "Others…? What others?"

The redhead looked at her sister questioningly. "Oh, you didn't notice them? I guess you've lost some of your touch. Then again, I guess I can't blame you completely for that? I only encountered them out of sheer luck myself."

Then, she shook her head.

"But that's not what matters now. I've come here to accomplish a mission - and that is to return you from who you once were." the girl stated. "All you can do is to make a choice, sister. You value this place, don't you? There are people in this area you're protecting… What happens if I blew up the entire place, I wonder?"

"I won't let you."

"Well, you'd have to take me more seriously then. The only way to stop me would be to cut me down."

The blonde frowned, staring at her sister with a strange gaze.

"...You'd truly go that far? Just for this?"

The redhead's answer was a simple smile. "Anything to accomplish a mission, sister. I am, of course, nothing but a professional." Then, the glowing of the fin funnels intensified. "Now, what is it going to be? Will you stop me? Or will you let me destroy what you hold 'dear'?"

Once more, the blonde hesitated. "I…"

The redhead's smile turned into a ferocious grin.

"The clock is ticking." the fins locked onto a random direction. "Let's see… is the house you're protecting here? Bam."

The blonde's eyes widened, and she quickly dashed between the particle beam that shot out of the redhead's fin funnels. Her hair formed a protective shield around her, making the beam strike it…

—Boom!

Before it ended in a final explosion. A cloud of smoke, dust and debris was kicked up - and right in the middle of it was the blonde, looking slightly singed.

"Oh? Guess, that's not the place then. You're not that desperate to protect it." the redhead said with a thoughtful noise before looking somewhere behind the blonde. "Maybe in this direction? Or there? I wonder where…? Oh well."

"Stop it, Mea!" the blonde shouted, looking truly angered now.

"You do it, sister. You stop me. Or else I won't." Her fin funnels then spread out in different directions. "And this time, there will be no third option."

The weapons glowed with energy. And being aimed in different directions - there was no way to block it like earlier. Separate fin funnels also seem to be dedicated to producing a barrier around her, making it not easy to just shoot at the weapons to stop the attack.

The blonde grit her teeth, mind racing.

A moral dilemma. Between two people a person considers important, which of them should a person choose? It was an unfair question, as it would always result in pain to the person who decides the choice, no matter what.

However this was supposed to be a lighthearted setting, even if there is some action mixed in it. And while things have intensified due to strange circumstances… it remains true that things won't devolve into a tragedy, changing the entire genre drastically.

The world saves the sad stuff for the sad stories, and the happy stuff on happy ones. A straightforward line of logic.

So in the end, what would be the narrative's answer to this unfair question? Like an author being forced to address something controversial and couldn't provide any actual solid answer without ruffling some feathers, the answer was very simple.

—It was a rejection of the question entirely.

Five shots echoed through the street, making both alien bioweapons stiffen. Bullets whizzed past somewhere behind the blonde and towards the redhead.

And then, instead of getting blocked by the defensive barrier - the bullets simply passed through it, before finding purchase at the fin funnels, causing them to explode and make her hair unravel.

The two sister's eyes widened, but then there was a final shot. This time it was aimed right at the redhead directly. The girl disengaged, making a completely unnecessary and showy backflip to dodge the bullet aimed right at her forehead.

Then she landed on the ground, staring at the direction where the bullet came from.

"Who's there?" the girl demanded as her hair reformed into a bladed weapon.

There was no answer. However, footsteps echoed somewhere behind the blonde. Both sisters turned their attention to the new arrival, and there, they saw another blonde who carried a gun with her.

She was human. Yet, there was something about her that made the two alien bioweapons pause. The first was the unmistakable aura of danger around her, but the second…

"A-A maid…?"

…It was because of her strange clothing, wearing a maid outfit of all things.

Nevertheless, the woman stepped up right beside her fellow blonde, calmly reloading her gun.

Then, the woman spoke.

"Excuse me," she stated. "But damage to private property is against Earth's laws."

Then, she pointed her gun at the redhead.


Spoiler

"Please respect our planet's customs next time."

Chapter 29

In a certain house within a neighborhood, a strange conflict was unfolding.

"Rito-kun, where are you going!? It's dangerous!"

"P-Please let me go, Momo-san! Yami-san is… she is…!"

Right in front of the house were two people who were in the middle of a 'struggle'. It was a bit too one-sided to be labeled a fight. In fact, it looked more like a subdual, with one of them pinning down the other to the ground to prevent them from moving.

Said person being pinned down was a boy. With brown hair and a slightly short stature - he was someone who has the appearance of someone that, while looking kinda attractive, would become utterly unremarkable if put in a crowd of people.

That said despite his lack of uniqueness, this boy currently wants nothing more than to risk his own life just to save someone. He may not look like anything special - but it was clear that his courage, bravery, and heart of gold shines brighter than anything else.

In short, he was a person deserving the title of the average harem protagonist.


Spoiler

"We need to help her!" the protagonist shouted. "I saw her getting attacked and—"

"And what? If you get there you'll just be on the way! So just stay here and sit still!"

"—Owowow, Momo-san, that hurts!"

However, despite his great attitude, the fact remains that he was a completely mundane human. He was much weaker than a normal human in fact, because being a person living in a first world country meant that he didn't really experience much hardship or had to do much physical things aside from the occasional sports, and as such he couldn't really do anything when it comes to a fight.

And it was also that reason why he was completely subdued by a girl his age despite the fact that he could, in theory, throw her off quite easily if she tried to pin him into a hold.

…That said, even if he was a bit more on the physical side it still wouldn't result in anything. Because the girl was also anything normal.

After all, she was an alien.


Spoiler

"Oh, sorry." the pink-haired girl said, removing her hold on him. "Anyway, you can't go there Rito-kun! I want to help as well, but those two are super dangerous alien mercenaries. We can't just go there all willy-nilly! You could get killed!"

The boy looked hesitant. "B-But… we can't just leave Yami-san alone."

"I know. That's why I called Lala-onee-sama earlier. She just finished dealing with those weird Serpo aliens that caused some trouble downtown, so she's going to help Yami-san once she arrives!" the girl reassured him. "Though, she did lose quite a lot of energy dealing with them and had to take the bus. She's hurrying as fast as she can though."

"—Momo-san, it takes at least thirty minutes to get here from downtown! By the time Lala-san arrives everything would already be over!"

The girl blinked.

"Naniii!?" the pink-haired girl shouted, instantly losing her cool. "W-W-What should we do!? That means it's completely up to us, isn't it!? Does that mean we should go there right now!?"

"That's exactly what I've been saying, Momo-san!"

"No, wait. Let's calm down!" the pink-haired girl shouted again, making the boy stop. "As I said, we can't just go there all willy-nilly. We need a plan or else we'll just be dragging Yami down as she fights! That's right, with my Devilukean strength and ability to summon plants, along with Rito-kun's smarts, we should be able to beat those guys known to assassinate the galaxy's strongest…!"

The girl trailed off.

There was a poignant pause that followed.

"…Rito-kun. I don't think we can help here." the girl concluded.

"—You gave up way too fast!" the boy retorted instantly as he stood up. "I thought you Devilukeans are like the Yasain aliens in Dragon's Ball? Don't you guys like to fight and all that!?"

"—What the heck!? So we've been doing your jobs!?" the alien cried out, making the tension disappear completely. "Do your work properly! Why do we have to be the ones who do that!?"

With that strange detail sidestepped through comedy, V then gave a much more serious answer that would convincingly address the question and make the narrative move on.

"To be more specific, you all did your jobs greatly enough for us not to think that there's anything wrong." V quickly followed, making the alien pause. "We didn't pay much attention in this place until recently. In fact, we didn't know that there were aliens like you staying in here."

"What? How? Sure, some are putting up closed space technology to prevent collateral damage, but there's still quite a lot of them around here…"

V noted the strange term. "If they truly are using such 'closed spaces', then they wouldn't be our priority." she immediately said. "As I said, the goal of our group is to deal with external threats and keep the knowledge of such things in the eyes of the public. Who we go after… it would be like the alien from earlier."

Realization appeared in the girl's eyes. "Oh. So you're going after the more destructive ones."

V nodded. Then she turned to Aoki, who cleared her throat to speak once more.

"In any case, I don't think V's organization is concerned about your legality in staying here. In fact, they welcome all of your help." the woman stated. "With that said Momo-san, I'd like you to continue answering the question I asked you earlier… Do you mind telling us your experience in dealing with the other aliens in this place? And if there are some irregularities happening lately?"

"Irregularities? Well…"

—And with that, the pink-haired alien started telling them the things that they had been up to lately.

Like what they had inferred from their setting, it appears that it really is just some light-hearted harem anime with a couple battles here and there, usually involving some wacky alien that they will deal with in the end.

In fact, based on her words, this recent battle appears to be an outlier since the stakes are higher than usual. There was a genuine threat that caused actual destruction around the neighborhood and even came close to hurting them. As far as everything in their plot goes, this would likely be the fight they were in most danger.

And also one that carries the most emotional weight, considering the state the blonde alien was left in.

V glanced outside where the alien named Yami was standing on lookout for potential enemies. With her sister working alone this whole time, there was little reason to do it - but it was clear to anyone that it wasn't the true reason why she was outside.

After all, one look at her expression betrayed her inner deep and conflicting thoughts.The girl clearly wanted to be alone right now.

…In any case, the fact that it was an outlier must have meant something. Perhaps it was the effect caused by the world-affecting scenario, although they'd have to investigate that more thoroughly. However, hearing what the pink-haired alien had to say - it seems that they already gained what they needed here already.

"—You have a device that can repair the damages?" V asked.

"Yes. Onee-sama's inventions can easily repair what that girl has destroyed earlier. Pika-Pika Raygun-kun is very convenient! So there's no need to worry or trouble yourselves for everything!" the pink-haired alien proudly informed.

Indeed, that certainly simplifies things. "I see. Then I'll leave you to that."

"Please do!"

As the girl answered cheerily, V met the eyes of Aoki, who simply nodded slightly in a way no one present noticed. They were about to end the discussion… but it seems that there was no need for them to interrupt things.

Because suddenly a scream had interjected as they talked, making them stop.

"—Ahh! I'm sorry!"

"Rito-kun!?"

The protagonist suddenly sat straight when he woke up. There was a short moment as he looked around in a panic - but then, realizing that everything was fine when he looked around the house, he relaxed slightly.

"M-Momo-san? What's going on?" he asked, confused. "Is everything fine now…?"

"Yes, everything is fine, so calm down. That girl left in fluster earlier after you kissed her. It was honestly surprising." Momo replied. "For now we're talking with these guys here. Apparently they're a secret organization that deals with destructive aliens like the girl earlier."

"S-Secret organization!?" the boy said in surprise, before immediately sitting on the table, eyes sparkling. "So something like that exists!? I knew there was something fishy when we didn't find anyone, but there really are people who know about aliens!"

Aoki and V blink in surprise at the passion in the boy's voice.

"I-Is your organization something like from that overseas movie? Like in 'Men in Suits'!? May I ask what sort of things you do on a day-to-day basis!? What sort of aliens do you deal with!? Do you document other strange phenomena that appear on Earth, like—!"

Aoki coughed, making the boy stop.

"My, that's quite a lot of questions." Aoki stated with a smile. "I can see how you'd be very curious, but if V-chan answers all of it then we'd probably be here all day… So if all of you don't mind, then we'd like to take our leave now. Everything seems to be taken care of, after all."

"E-Eh? You're leaving already, Aoki-san?" Run asked in surprise.

The woman nodded to her while both her and V stood up.

"Yes. We still have a lot to do after this, actually. As I said earlier, V-chan is actually conducting an investigation right now." she answered. "Anyway it's nice meeting all of you! It was brief, but it was very helpful!"

"U-Um…" the pink-haired alien spoke up. "T-Thank you for helping us again. And for being so lenient to us."

V shook her head. "So long as you don't cause real trouble, there is no need for concern."

"Yep! Just be good kids and you'll be fine!" Aoki smiled again. "And Run, I'll see you tomorrow okay? Good luck on your tests!"

The idol returned it. "Thank you, Aoki-san! I'll see you tomorrow as well!"

With their farewells said, V and Aoki then went outside the house using the large hole on the wall. As they did so, even without looking, V could see the three of them were staring as they left. And when they left the three's direct sight the pink-haired alien and the protagonist immediately turned to the idol, definitely intending to grill her with questions.

"Run-san, do you know those guys?"

"Tell us more about them!"

"I-I don't know! I didn't even know that Aoki-san has connections to—!"

At that point, V stopped focusing her attention on them and instead turned it to the other person outside, who glanced at them when they left the house. Her fellow blonde met her gaze and turned to face them.

Then she bowed deeply, making Aoki and V stop.

"…Thank you." the alien said, voice soft yet filled with gratefulness. "If it weren't for all of you being here, I…"

She trailed off, voice pained. Her meaning was clear even if it wasn't said out loud.

"..."

V stared at her fellow blonde.

Looking at her, she was instantly reminded of what her enemy had earlier observed when they fought. V and this girl, Yami, certainly have enough physical similarities for the two of them to be mistaken as related - or in the redhead's own words, a clone. Even if V was older than she was and was even a different species at that.

But the similarities don't just end on their physicality. There were some things that she could recognize being displayed by this girl in front of her. Things that V had noticed on herself, making it look like she was looking at a twisted mirror.

—From the way the girl held herself, always tense and cautious of any attack that could arise, which spoke of a life mainly on the battlefield.

—From the way she looked at everything around her like it was unfamiliar and fragile, as if she didn't understand the environment she was in.

—And from the way she held her feelings back, unable to comprehend what her true wishes are, after burying it for all her life.

Perhaps V was just projecting. She was new to being true to her emotions after all. And even now, she was still having difficulty trying to read or understand others, much less her own. Yet despite it all, she couldn't quite shake off a particular feeling.

A feeling as if V was staring at her past self. One that still hasn't realized her true wishes even after her own war had already ended, and even after she had met her own 'Basa' in the form of the harem protagonist.

"…You're hesitating."

Her fellow blonde stiffened at V's sudden words, then looked up at her with a puzzled look. But before she could question what V had meant - the blonde alien's weary eyes met her own, making her stop once more.

Kindred.

She was told that the eyes were the windows of the soul, and you could tell what sort of person is just by looking at their gaze. It was a trope, especially proliferent in the more idealized genres out there. One such as this girl belongs in.

Which was why when V spoke, the blonde listened closely.

"All these feelings are unfamiliar and you don't know what to do." V told her. "You've lived life following orders… but now that you've tasted what life is beyond it, you find yourself hesitating."

Yami stared at her wide-eyed as her feelings were easily vocalized out loud. V, meanwhile, just leaned towards her closely and continued speaking her words.

"Find what makes you hesitate. Explore them, and don't shy away from the unfamiliar. You've survived far worse than that." she stated. "And once you finally find your answer from your search… don't let go of it. Act on it, and make it a reality."


Spoiler

"Because that is what it means to live by your own orders. To live your own life."

Her words were vague as she had a hard time expressing her own feelings on the subject. However, it conveyed her message well enough, even if the girl was unable to comprehend her words. She hadn't reached the point that she could understand it yet, but so long as she can do all those things… she can arrive in the same realization as V did.

That said, with her story's genre, it was already decided that she would realize what she truly wanted. V's actions right here are ultimately meaningless since it will all arrive at the same result… Still, V felt nice helping a person she could relate to.

And so, leaving the girl to stew in her words, V turned around and followed Aoki who was waiting for her outside.

The woman sent her a smile. "That was nice of you, giving her advice like that."

She nodded wordlessly. With everything taken care of, the two of them went to the parked car that they had procured for this particular situation. Aoki went to the driver seat, while V sat on the passenger side, and they quickly started the car and drove off.

And as their distance from the house quickly grew…

"Haahhh…" Aoki let out a sigh as she relaxed slightly. "Finally alone… You're amazing, V-chan. You acted like an actual government agent despite that maid outfit you're wearing. I was really sweating on the inside when they asked questions on who we are, you know?"

V glanced at her. "Were you nervous?"

"Very! I felt like I was some conman! Even though I'm just supposed to be an idol manager you approached, which I technically am!" Aoki stated. "Acting is surprisingly hard. I have an idea how difficult it is from the girls I take care of, but experiencing it for yourself really is a different beast."

She could understand. "I suppose so. I remember not knowing what to do when I was acting as the leader of Golden Dawn." Thinking about it, she was probably feeling nervous that time, even if she wasn't aware of it. "That might be the reason why I performed better. I simply had more experience. And in due time, you will too."

"I guess so." Aoki replied sheepishly. "Honestly, I'm still kinda new to all of this. The responsibility of being a person who turned meta… it's quite daunting. And I have the feeling that they're going to approach us now in case something serious happens."

V nodded seriously. "Yes. Interacting directly like this would definitely make us side characters to their plot."

In fact, strictly speaking, Aoki was already a 'side character' due to the fact she was managing the two alien idols. However what happened today definitely made them directly involved in their story. Aoki and her, with her striking maid uniform that will likely be interpreted as her 'side character quirk', have definitely bumped up their importance in the story that it would definitely require them to be involved from time to time.

That said, it wasn't a bad result. After all, Basa himself had said that it wasn't a bad idea since involving themselves meant that they'd have a way to gain information on other similar settings. He might have a lot of information regarding a variety of mundane, supernatural, and sci-fi settings - but with Basa-kun limiting himself to Earth, his knowledge on aliens is surprisingly sparse.

There was a reason why their first choice on investigating the 'alien' venue in the world-affecting scenario was approaching an idol from Aoki's idol workplace. If they had a much better option, then they would've chosen it.

Still, it looks like she'd have to act as a government agent now. But it was no problem. She's also acting as a revolutionary leader now, after all.

"That'll definitely be worrying. I'm getting kinda nervous hearing that people will depend on us." Aoki stated honestly. Then, she let out a soft smile. But you know what? It's also exciting! Saving the world kinda makes us superheroes, doesn't it?"

"Yes, it really is." she stated, before turning thoughtful. "Saving the world… Yes, I suppose we should get on doing that."

With her words, V went on to take out a certain thing that she brought with her from the car's compartment. It was a crystal ball that, to her, was completely unforgettable. Mostly because she recalled Basa holding it in his hand the first time they met.

She had learned that its purpose was to essentially act as a device that allows a person to peer into someone's fate. A 'clairvoyant retro-precognitive device', as Basa called it. And he used it to determine her as a meta person due to the simple fact that V didn't follow it.

However, that wasn't its only use. It was also an incredible device that weaves various divination magic and powerful computations, one where limiting the number of variables allowed it to simulate certain specific scenarios. Things like, for example, viewing how a certain setting's events would play out without the influence of other neighboring settings.

In short, it allowed them to peer how the harem setting's events would go free of the world-affecting scenario's events. It wasn't perfect of course, but for general comparisons it was very convenient.

It was the very reason how they identified that the redhead alien was a 'change'. And also, with the memories that she obtained via hypnosis from the alien earlier… V could easily pinpoint where the source of this 'change' comes from.

V closed her eyes and the car turned quiet as Aoki let her focus.

For a moment she could only hear the hum of the car's engine, before it too disappeared when she completely shut herself from the world. She went on to parse every memory that she obtained from the alien redhead, ignoring all the unnecessary details, and then focusing more on the recent events on Earth.

It took a few moments. Then after that, V opened her eyes and activated the crystal ball. She grabbed the locks of hair which she cut off from the redhead earlier and put her hand on the device. It activated, and V perused the various simulated events that were displayed.

And then, at some point on her search…

"Found it." she informed.

Aoki turned to her slightly before looking forward again to drive. "You did? What did you find?"

"Around ten o'clock at night three days ago, that alien arrived on Earth via her space ship. And while she was on her way finding her sister, Yami, she encountered a 'closed space' barrier." V explained. "She shouldn't have encountered any other aliens at that point. Yet she was able to witness something that left her stunned because of the sheer power involved."

"S-Sheer power? She found something dangerous?" Aoki asked, surprised.

"Yes. That was also the time she took her mission quite seriously." V answered. "That alien she found also looked like a human girl, but it's mostly a shell. A biological avatar of some sort. The limited impressions I have from her memories say that those types of aliens are purely out of data and are incredibly dangerous. I have no other information to provide context as to what that meant."

Aoki looked incredibly curious but also disturbed by her words… and then she sighed.

"I see. That's a shame, but at least we were able to identify what started the change here." Aoki muttered in thought. "Do you have her face? We can research the identity of this girl if that's the case."

"I do have it, but it's not necessary."

She took a moment to confirm it again, and then nodded.

"—Her uniform points to her as someone who attends Hakoniwa Academy." she revealed.

Aoki's eyes widened. "Hanokiwa Academy… that's the source of the world-affecting scenario, correct? The one setting that Basa-kun told us to not directly involve ourselves in."

V nodded. "Yes, it is."

It seems that they have finally determined the cause for the changes in the neighboring settings. They've dealt with one of them earlier, but it doesn't mean that it's the end of it.

There's still a likely chance that people from other settings would have seen the same thing that the redhead alien did, also causing some sort of change. After all, there was also the matter about the espers. Yuki had told them of a nearby shrine that might relate to it, and it might prove helpful to check it out as well. It was a famous shrine, one that was said to be owned by a renowned spirit medium named… Santa Dodoria.

A strange name. Was this person related to Santa, perhaps? It piqued her interest.

Nevertheless, V also told Aoki the location where the alien had been last time. Coincidentally, or perhaps by design, it was also quite near the location of the shrine that Yuki mentioned, meaning that the relation might not be as far-fetched as initially assumed.

And with that, the both of them went to continue their investigation. As they did - V increased her vigilance, carefully thinking about their next steps so they do not interact with said alien. This wasn't only because of the reality warper present in their setting, but also due to what she saw in the redhead's memories which caused her instincts to go off.


Spoiler

That alien was dangerous. Whatever it was, she doubted that she could take it head on. Because from what she was seeing… they might as well be dealing with another reality warper as well.

V let out an exhale.

She can only hope that the others are faring better than her and Aoki currently.

…

…

Ah, seems like she made a mistake.

That was the so-called flag, wasn't it?


At the same time, in a different place.

In a relatively near distance away from a certain school, one that was inexplicably linked with demons, the House of God can be found. It was the rare church in a Japanese society which has biases towards western religion - which means that currently the church was an abandoned and debilitated place, seemingly forgotten in time by the people in the place.

However, that was only on the surface.

To those who are perceptive, they would notice that damage done to the church doesn't seem to be caused by time but rather… something more purposeful.

From the way the crosses are damaged to make an inverted 't', the little sigils etched on holy icons in places that one may not look, and to a subtle, yet pervading foul-smelling scent of sulfur that clings underneath the smell of wood rot.

And perhaps the most obvious, one only available to those aware of the supernatural - there was an incredible amount of unholy energy that seemed to saturate the place, enough that it might cause feelings of deep fear and anxiety to those who lack the aptitude to feel it.

It was an insidious site. The Church of God was desecrated and turned into a terrible place that only unholy beings may dwell. No ordinary person would enter this place, lest they want to be struck by maladies or curses that seem to almost protect it.

And inside such a location, a certain ritual was occurring.


Spoiler

Right in the middle of the church, a blonde girl was tied upon a strange crucifix. Her clothes were in tatters and barely seemed to cover her while she was held up by chains, but the girl was in no shape to even consider her humiliating state, considering that she is currently unconscious.

And of course, present in the place were also the people responsible for putting the girl in such a position.

"Finally… I finally got her!"

—It was a familiar bunch.

Beautiful faces and bodies, one that gave the impression of impossible grace and perfection. And with the avian wings on their back - it was clear to anyone that these people were designed to be the messengers who represent the splendor of heaven. And they would have done so perfectly… if it weren't for one thing.

Their wings, which were supposed to stay pure-white, are instead stained a deep dark black.

What stood in front of the girl weren't the messengers of God: they were fallen angels, plotting to bring her demise.

"A divine gift… To think that we can finally extract it from this human. With this power, we can use the miracles that were once lost to us!"

The female angel had said those words in front of the girl while having a power-hungry expression on her face. The others around her had different expressions however, varying between boredom, excitement, and curiosity - but not a single one cared to stop what was happening.

"Finally, after waiting to get it for so many years…! Azazel-sama will truly be happy about this…!"

It was clear that they were planning to do something. There had been plenty of instances where a fallen angel was present in the city that was meant to be demonic territory. It spoke of a plot brewing in the background, where the development will lead to another action-filled arc for the cast.

However none of that matters right now. For the stage was set.

On a surface level, it appears that this was nothing but the death of an unfortunate person. But combined with elements such as the fact that the girl being sacrificed was a very beautiful one with a very unique power, along with the almost cliché lines that the fallen angel was saying, a certain standard was being met.

After all… one shouldn't forget the fact that the genre of this setting prevents such tragedies being shown in the first place.

And so, seemingly out of nowhere, the fallen angels stiffened as a burst of demonic energy appeared - a startlingly incredible amount, one that made even immortal beings like them pause. And one that was also rapidly heading to their direction.

Their female leader turned around. "What—!?"

They didn't finish.

—BOOM!!!

Because without any warning - a sudden explosion rocked the church they were in, destroying the incredible defenses present like it was glass, blasting a hole within the building and rocking the entire structure's foundations. The explosion was also enough to knock the fallen angels into the ground from surprise, not expecting the sheer strength of it.

But being immortal beings with an inordinate amount of fighting experience however, they quickly recovered and flared out their wings to face this intruder. Tainted angelic powers were brought forth, ready to destroy those who had attacked them.

And yet, after seeing who it was - the fallen angels immediately paused.

There had been many expectations in their mind when anticipating an attack. Being fallen angels in demonic territory, they had come to understand that they were in a dangerous place. As such, they had thought of the scenarios that might happen when they are discovered.

They could be assaulted by a group of demons, or perhaps a single powerful veteran. The former was more easily dealt with than the latter, and a general outline of a plan was also made.

But what they encountered was none of that. Instead, what faced them was a single young demon who floated upon the destruction she made. A greenhorn that hadn't even reached a hundred years, much less proper adulthood.

Yet despite that, they could feel her power.

A star. It was as if they were staring at a star, burning brightly and lighting everything up for them to see. A roaring light that was compressed into a single point, shining brightly and blinding everyone who started at it directly.

And that same star suddenly spoke to them with a ferocious grin.

"Hey, get away from her, you pigeons!"


Spoiler

"—That girl right there is going to be my future clubmate!"
