Chapter 30

From the very beginning of her life, the girl was abandoned.

She didn't know her mother nor father. Instead, she was simply found left in front of a church as an infant. She grew up to be an orphan along with a few other kids in her small town, not knowing what it means to grow up with a family.

…But she was fine with that.

The church had raised her. Even if they were not related by blood, she had grown to love the priests, nuns and other orphans as her own family. She grew up eating three times a day and with a place to sleep. She was lucky, luckier than others - which is why she is thankful.

She did not know the circumstances of why she was abandoned. Perhaps her parents knew they couldn't take care of her, so they sent her to people who could. In a way, they had shown to care about her.

So she forgave them. In her heart of hearts - she didn't blame or hate her parents for abandoning her. In fact, she had always hoped that wherever they are right now, they are safe and prospering. She hoped for the sake of her parents, who left her in hopes of wanting to live a better life.

After all - if it wasn't for them, then she wouldn't have met the Lord.

Living in a church, she had discovered her true calling. She had learned through His teachings and His word as a child. While the other orphans simply took the Bible studies as lessons, she regarded it differently as she listened to each and every verse that spoke to her heart. From there she learned other things, and she started her journey as a nun.

Her life was filled with devotion and simply doing good deeds to others. She continued doing her utmost best to live a life the Lord expected her to - praying, reflecting, and helping - and trying to be the best that she could possibly be.

But unexpectedly, at some point the Lord decided to bestow upon her a blessing.

Despite simply living out her life and not doing anything extraordinary, she was given the power to bestow miracles. She was able to find out that she can heal the sick and injured, allowing her to help more people. And it was also due to it that she was called a 'Holy Maiden' by many of the people around her.

She knew she didn't deserve such high praise. She was just a normal person like anyone else. But if the Lord saw fit to give her such an ability… then she would use it to the best of her abilities.

By that point, it appeared that the church had noticed her. They called her a girl with a divine gift and a 'Saint'. She was honored to be called as such, especially since she was given a chance to go even to the Vatican after. The priests, nuns and her brothers and sisters - they all supported her and told her to take the chance. And so she accepted, very thankful in her heart to be given such an opportunity.

However… the day before she could set off, everything in her life had come crashing down.

It came in the form of an incredibly wounded person asking for help in the church. She had thought to heal them like the many others she had helped - but the moment that she did, her divine gift seemingly didn't work.

She thought she had failed. So she prayed and prayed… until it finally did, healing the injured person.

But as it turns out, she was tricked.


Spoiler

"Wow! You managed to heal me, a demon, with your divine powers? I wonder if what you wield really is from God?"

Who she healed was apparently a demon. Her faith made her know that they existed, but she hadn't expected them to appear before her as a human, leading her to be tricked by one of them. But even if that was the case, what matters is that she wasn't supposed to be able to heal them in the first place.

The Lord's light heals all and drives back evil. That was how it was meant to be. Yet she somehow managed to heal the manifestation of evil itself - and seconds after she had done it, the church was stormed by exorcists who injured the demon in the first place. And as such, they have witnessed the impossible.

There was only one conclusion to this impossibility. She wasn't a Holy Maiden or a Saint that people thought of her as. What she had was not a divine gift, but rather something else.

She was nothing but a witch.

And on that day, the girl was abandoned a second time.

She was excommunicated and thrown out of the church. She had been doing miracles in the name of the church using witchcraft, acting as a fraud. She was separated from her family, stripped of her belongings, and was cast away from her town so that she would be forgotten.

She had spent her life in poverty and homeless. There were many nights that she was cold and hungry, but she didn't hate the others that caused it. Instead, she directed those feelings to herself. She thought that this was a punishment that she deserved for being a witch. She thought that her ability to grant miracles must've gone to her head, and that this must be a test that the Lord had sent her way to keep her humble.

And so she prayed, reflected, and forgave. And even despite her homelessness and poverty, she still tried to do acts of good and live a life in accord to His teachings. It was hard, and everyday was filled with temptations and doubt - but she had persevered and managed to do so.

Perhaps because of that, she was given an opportunity. At some point, people willing to help her had approached her. While she may be a witch to the church, her ability to heal others was invaluable, and she was taken to an eastern country called Japan where their main organization had stayed.

By that point, she was happy. Helping others was something that she was happy to do. And she thought that maybe, she would find people she would think of as family in this new organization that she had joined.

…She had thought wrong.

Once more, she was tricked. But this time, it wasn't due to demons, but rather fallen angels who had defied the Lord's will. They didn't want her for her healing - they simply wanted to take her ability to heal and use it for themselves, throwing away her body after.

She was going to be killed.

And now, she had wondered if she was going to be abandoned for a third time - abandoned by the very God that she had devotedly worshipped for so long.

—What did she do to deserve this?

—Why was she going to be killed?

—What had she done wrong?

Doubt had filled her heart. She had wondered if the Lord truly did care for her if this was what she received after her devotion. Despite her very best, those thoughts had appeared in her mind. She was only human after all.

But still… in the end, even as much as she wanted to hate and curse the world…

She found herself unable to.

O Lord… if it is possible, let this cup pass from me… yet not as I will, but as you will…

She wanted to live.

She wanted to be saved.

She wanted to be free from the suffering.

Yet, she yielded to the Lord's will, only hoping that his plan and her desires align.

And so, as she had remained there barely conscious, crucified in front of the fallen angels - she waited for His judgement: praying, reflecting, forgiving, and accepting whatever that may come to her way. She had fully thought that the end of her life has come, and she prepared herself for the pain that would come her way—

"Hey, you alright? Don't worry about everything now! I've got you!"


Spoiler

—But the next thing she knew, she was right in the arms of a demon girl. The girl stared down at her with a smile, one that reassured her that everything was going to be fine. And despite the fact that she was a demon… she found herself relaxing in her arms, having lost all her strength after enduring for so long and trusting her fully.

It seems that the Lord really does work in mysterious ways.

Right now, these two are currently between a battle of wills. A test between two parties, where the one who yields first will lose. The circumstances are different and a bit more nuanced than a straightforward fight, but the overall situation can be summarized as that.

Whether Rias gives in to the pain or she reaches the fallen angel, and whether the fallen angel can't stop Rias' fist or she manages to muster the strength to do so despite her strain; the one who has the greater resolve will be the one on the top.

Any of them could be the winners… Or was that really the case?

After all, this was a story. A shounen story at that. And between the fight between a protagonist and their current villain, there was only one outcome to such a scenario.

Therefore, to Rias who had arranged such a situation to occur… it was already decided.

But then, despite all the effort she was currently giving - the narrative decided to give her another curveball.

"—Gah! That's right!" the fallen angel suddenly gasped out in realization as she was leaning away from Rias' fist. "I don't have to face you alone! What am I doing, fighting you like some sort of fool!?"

Rias' eyes widened as the fallen angel suddenly casted a spell that allowed someone to talk from a distance. Then, with a panicked yet victorious look - the fallen angel began talking to the person she was calling.

"Lord En! Please, give us your assistance! There is a high-class demon here!" she shouted in a pathetic, faux-flattering voice. "Please come here as fast as possible! I have her trapped, but she's escaping as we speak!"

There was no verbal answer, but the call suddenly cut. And that was enough for the fallen angel.

"Kekeke! Too bad, girl! You've done your best, but I'm the one who'll be victorious!" she shouted triumphantly. "Now all I have to delay you until Lord En gets here! Then he'll be the one to deal with you personally!"

Rias grit her teeth in frustration.

Damn it, what was happening? She thought about the outcome because of the situation, but did she mess up? Did her thoughts about things being certain somehow trigger some sort of flag? That was probably the case, wasn't it!?

But if she's going to lose because of that… then what the hell is she going to do now?! She can't think of any other maneuver to deal with another opponent! She's actually really trapped this time!

"—There he is!" The fallen angel's shout just made her more panicked. And turning her eyes down to the direction the woman was looking - indeed, there was someone flying towards their position. "Lord En! Right here! Please deal with this hellspawn at once!"

Rias' mind raced as the figure started getting closer and closer. She tried to think of anything… but her mind was blank. She can't think of anything.

And so, she watched helplessly as the fallen angel cackled as her victory was assured. There was no mistaking that the person approaching them was a demon, so it wasn't some sort of miraculous rescue by some other person either.

She had messed up. Big time. She had thought that her greatest sin was laziness and inaction… but it seems like it was pride, for thinking that she could do this alone without any help from the others.

Sorry, everyone.

—And so Rias closed her eyes and waited.

…

…

Wait a minute, doesn't this seem like a survival flag?

Rias opened her eyes slightly. And there, she saw that despite the person was heading towards them - they don't seem like they have the intention to slow down. In fact, they seem to be headed straight to the fallen angel like a missile that was about to crash.

And they did. They crashed into the fallen angel hard.

"—Gak!" the fallen angel let out an ugly noise of surprise unbefitting of her beautiful face, and she turned to the body that crashed into her and was now holding on to her. "W-What? Lord En, what are you—!?"

She paused.

Because what they saw wasn't the demon that would finish Rias, but rather something else.


Spoiler

It was a beat-up demon whose entire facial structure was messed up. He looked barely conscious, only holding on the fallen angel's body out of sheer reflex. There was no trace of a powerful demon scion or anything like that - only a pathetic snivelling loser moaning in pain.

"L-Lord En!?" the fallen angel cried out. "What the hell happened!? Who did this!?"

Rias had an idea.

She looked down towards the direction the demon came from and reinforced her eyesight. It was blurry, but she couldn't mistake the tanned person with a shock of blonde hair looking up towards them for anyone else.

Then the man disappeared further into the building, deciding that his help was enough for her to deal with everything.

…That person, really.

"Hey, wake up! You're supposed to help me here!" the fallen angel shouted desperately as she tried to shake away the demon clinging to her. "Do something, damn it! Don't just keep moaning brainlessly you—!"

"—Hey."

The fallen angel stopped, before turning to her. "W-What…"

Rias stared straight to her eyes. "It doesn't hurt as much anymore."

The fallen angel's expression turned confused, but before she could say anything - Rias' fists crossed over the portal's threshold and punched her right in the face.

The power of destruction that coated her fists were not as potent as before, so it didn't erase her head when she did it. Still, it was incredibly damaging for the fallen angel, and she screamed in pain as a simple punch like that made her nose bleed profusely.

Rias immediately crossed the portal, letting her escape from the barrier. And as the pain and resistance disappeared as she went out of the barrier… she found herself feeling the most free she's ever felt in her entire life.

And also, the most pissed off she's ever been.

"I've decided." she said, cracking her knuckles. "I wanted to wait and see if there was an inch of redeemability between you guys when we fought, but you… you are definitely not friend material. And that you deserve none of my mercy."

"—So I'm going to beat you up, plain and simple."

The fallen angel stared at her with uncomprehending eyes.

"What the hell are you—!?"

She wasn't able to finish.

Because what came after next…

"—ORAORAORAORA!!!"

"—GYYYAAAAAAAGH!!!"

…Was something that can only be described as a beatdown of a lifetime.

Up in the sky, uncaring of the pain in her body - Rias unleashed the most devastating combo of attacks that she could with her fists covered in destructive energy. She used whatever martial technique and knowledge that she learned, whilst also using magecraft to deliver precise strikes and blows to intensify the damage as much as she could.

It was brutal.

It was merciless.

It was incredibly cathartic.

She delivered as much pain as she could, trying to let the fallen angel hold a candle to what she just felt inside her barrier. And as she felt the fallen angel's bones break and insides rupture at each hit - it felt like she did a pretty good job.

"A-Ahh…"

And by the time she was done… the fallen angel was bloody all over, looking more like a wet noodle than a fallen messenger of heavens. She had long since turned unconscious, only moaning occasionally out of reflex more than anything.

In short, kinda like the demon that crashed to her earlier. I guess Basa-kun gave that demon the same treatment.

And with that, Rias brought down her arms and let the fallen angel fall down to the ground, where she was joined by her brothers and sisters.

…The fight was over.

"Finally—! Ow."

Rias suddenly winced, feeling the incredible ache in her body and the echoes of the pain in the barrier. She was also in a terrible shape, bleeding all over with parts of her skin melted with her flesh - and while not as bad as the state she left the fallen angel in, it was honestly still pretty bad.

"I look like a potato… That said, it's nothing that a good healing potion could fix!" she said, bringing out from her subspace and drinking it. "Mm! I like the taste of trivialized stakes! I should probably keep hurting myself while attacking if it means having an absurd power boost!"

She'd have to be careful of surprises like earlier the next time she does it though. But then again, maybe if it wasn't for Basa-kun beating that En guy, then maybe it wouldn't happen. That whole calling for him felt like a set up to show something cool like that.

At any rate - it was probably going to take a while to fix her wounds. She's going to need to take a moment to nap or eat somewhere, because she's definitely going to be tired after healing. And preferably somewhere private… where she could shout freely just to deal with this pain.

"Owie… This hurts so much…" she grumbled, before letting out a sigh. "I hope that the others are doing better than me, at least."

…

…

H-Hold on, she didn't just plant a flag, did she?

Uh oh. Let's hope she just didn't.


—Yuki suddenly looked up.

"The sky is getting dark… looks like it's about to rain."

She muttered those words in thought, before pausing when she realized what she just did. That action of looking up as if she just felt something wrong… That definitely means that something happened that must have concerned her in some way.

Does it have something to do with the flag she possibly planted earlier? She truly hoped that's not the case.

Nevertheless, she'd have to keep her eyes peeled now - especially when she just about reached the place she'd investigate as well. After separating with Basa-kun and Rias earlier, Yuki went ahead to the places in the city known for being popular hangouts for delinquents.

And, as much as she wanted to be when doing so - she wasn't alone.

"…"

Her sister followed shortly behind her as she walked in the streets, observing Yuki quietly. She had long since recovered from her shock when she saw Rias take flight earlier. And during the course of Yuki's investigation, Haru had been intensely questioning her about the supernatural and processing everything that she learned.

It was quite strange, seeing her sister react this way. The Haru that she had known always seemed to be in control and never showed her weakness to anyone. So to see her so unsure about everything almost seemed wrong.

But it was also familiar. The face she made was something she recognized, since Yuki also had it when she had turned meta and met Basa-kun. Judging by the expression she was making, she was at the stage when Yuki researched all about the various strange things happening in the city and went to confront Basa-kun about it.

She doubted that her sister would have the same reaction as she did… but she'll surely express the same level of concern about what she learned.

"Yuki-chan… so you're friends with a demon, huh?"

Speak of the devil. And quite literally, at that.

"I am, nee-san." she replied easily. "But don't let the fact that Rias is a demon color your views about her. Just like humans, they're people. Even if they're more predisposed to sin."

"That doesn't really make me any less worried Yuki-chan." her sister retorted. "You've mentioned that Christianity is real, along with every other religion. I'm not quite sure what to make of that - but as far as I know, demons are generally considered evil. Are you saying that's not the case?"

"Yes, because there are always exceptions. Rias is one of them." she glanced at her sister. "And I know you consider yourself a good judge of character to know that I'm telling the truth. You've observed us a few days ago, haven't you? You should've had a good grasp of Rias already."

"That might be the case - but I'm merely human, dear sister. If there are things out there that could fool me, I'm pretty sure that it would be demons from hell." Haru replied, before letting out an exhale. "Especially that woman, Leviathan-san… I can't fully read her. She's a demon as well, isn't she?"

"She is. But I doubt anyone could compare themselves to her. She's one of the most powerful demons in hell, nee-san. That you can contend with someone like that is impressive in itself."

Haru raised a brow towards her. "No need to lie to make your sister feel better, Yuki-chan. Why would someone like that be acting as a school's director? That seems like a waste of time."

"I'm not joking. I've heard she can destroy a country in seconds."

That made her sister chuckle and shake her head.

"Is that so? I…" she trailed off when she saw her serious look. "…Really?"

Yuki nodded. Then, once more, her sister went quiet.

"...I will process that later." Haru eventually stated, gaze thoughtful. "So, what about Basa-kun? What did you call him again? A magus, was it?"

"Yes. He dabbles in magecraft. You can think of it as a scientist or an engineer. Magic has its own sets of rules just like physics, after all." she answered.

"And he… introduced you to this world."

"No. I stumbled on it and he saved me." Yuki corrected, and her sister's eyes turned to her with focus. "I was unfortunate enough to encounter a mad demon. It was about to eat me, but he was in the area and he saved me. And just like how you are right now after discovering the existence of the supernatural I also confronted him about it. A lot of things happened after that, but I'm helping him now."

Well, there's also the fact that she turned meta, but she can't really explain that to her sister. Because despite the fact that she was now able to see the supernatural - she wasn't actually the same as them. She was just able to cross one type of genre and not the others.

Or perhaps, what she did wasn't crossing genres at all. Likely, something about the plot had changed. One that caused her to discover the supernatural only. She doesn't know what is the catalyst but it very likely happened between today and a few days before when they had met.

That said, she was investigating something different now. That would probably come later.

"…I see. Then it seems that I owe him some gratitude."

Her sister muttered after considering what she said, before letting out a frown.

"But I hope that you're not sticking to him because of all of this, Yuki-chan."

Yuki paused from her sister's words.

"Pardon?" she asked.

"I've wondered why you would suddenly hang out with a person you've never met before. It's why I approached you guys in the first place. But knowing what I know now, I suppose it's understandable." Haru continued. "That said, it also makes me concerned."

Her sister looked her straight in the eyes.

"Yuki." she stated coldly. "When I visited your apartment last time - you said you liked him, didn't you? Was that the truth, or did you just like the fact that you can explore this strange world with him? And this investigation that you're doing now… You're not just loving the fact that you feel like a hero who will save others, are you?"

Yuki turned silent.

It was a very probing question, one that was very in-character with her sister. She never did like the fact that she could say these things directly, while also adding a silent, yet more hurtful implication underneath it all.

—You're not ready for this.

Upon finding that her sister had set foot in the world of the supernatural, that was her first reaction. She examined her actions and formed such a judgement. And that judgement betrayed just how little her sister had thought of her.

To be honest, it needled her for a bit. But her sister's words had a point to it. Those words demanded necessary introspection. And if she couldn't answer those questions that her sister asked… then the implication really was true. She wouldn't be ready for this.

But she did have an answer. And it was because of it that she was able to smile in reply.

"You sure are saying your worries directly this time, nee-san." Yuki commented with slight mirth. "And here I thought you'd keep your tsundere act like usual."

Her sister's eyes narrowed. "Don't avoid this, Yuki. Answer me."

"I am. And I do like Basa-kun." Yuki answered easily. "That said, it has nothing to do with being able to explore this supernatural world. I might enjoy learning from him, but this and that are different. I like him for who he is and not what he offers. Surely you should know that your own sister isn't that shallow of a person, no?"

"And as for the last question… Well, I can't deny that I want to help others, nee-san. You know why I made the Service club." Yuki continued. "I also initially approached Basa-kun after learning that there are people that are in need of help. That said, it's not like I'm throwing myself into every problem out there. I only help when it is necessary, and believe me when I say it is required. We're the only people who can do this."

"What, there's no other magus out here who can deal with problems you're dealing with?" her sister asked skeptically. "What about the demons? Heck, what about angels?"

"Rias is helping us since she's in the same position as I am. As for the other demons and angels… Well, they're stuck in their own places and circumstances. And so are the other supernatural organizations."

"You're being awfully vague, little sister."

Yuki smiled apologetically at her. "Sorry, nee-san. But I can't really explain it fully. Just know that the things we're dealing with are uniquely tailored to us and that not dealing with it is a bad option to take."

Because they're the only ones who are meta. She doubted there are other people who can deal with the world-affecting events that's happening right now. That said, it wouldn't really fully convince her sister because she wouldn't believe it at all. Along with any other answer, actually.

Because the truth is - Haru still thinks of her as the vulnerable and dependent sister who had plenty of self-esteem issues. That was how she acted the majority of her life, following Haru's footsteps, and it was only now that she was starting to change. So unless she managed to change that, her sister wouldn't condone the idea of her doing all this.

So what if she changed that now?

Her sister opened her mouth, likely about to tell her denial and skepticism on Yuki's responsibilities - but then she paused when another voice interrupted her, coming from somewhere across the street they were walking on.

"Oya oya, what's this? Some missies walking alone in these parts?"

The both of them turned, and there they saw a group of shady-looking delinquents heading their way.


Spoiler

Perfect timing.

"Hey, you two!" the person that looked like their leader walked up to them with a leery look. "Are you two lost or something? The both of you aren't from here, aren't you?"

"Want us to help? We know lots'a good places here!"

"Yeah, we could show you a good time! Bwahahaha!"

The delinquents laughed from what they likely thought as a very subtle insinuation. Haru tensed after seeing them and was about to bring out her phone to call for her guards - but then she immediately stiffened when Yuki went on to approach the group.

"Y-Yuki, what are you—?"

Yuki raised a hand, stopping her. Meanwhile the delinquent group stared at her in confusion, perhaps wondering why she was approaching them so confidently.

"Huh? What's your deal?" their leader asked, before making a lecherous grin. "What, so you want to come with us—"

He wasn't able to say the rest of his sentence.

Because with the same hand that Yuki raised, she immediately turned it into a simple closed hand chop which struck the delinquent leader's chin. The man's lower jaw shifted to the side from the hit, moving the skull in such a way that caused a concussion which made the man's eyes roll up.

He dropped on the ground instantly. And before his gang could react - Yuki moved on to efficiently deal with them with simple kicks and punches. She didn't even need to use reinforcement to do it, just simple martial arts and she was able to deal with them all.

"—Eeek! Wait, spare me!"

Well, all except one, that is. She needed this one for questioning. Yuki grabbed him by his collar, lifting him up easily despite their difference in muscle mass and height. He struggled pathetically for a moment but a cold glare made him freeze and dangle uselessly in her grip.

"You're going to answer my questions, got it?" Yuki asked.

He nodded desperately. And from the side she could see that her sister was looking at her with wide eyes and completely surprised at what she was seeing, much like how she had witnessed Rias fly before.

If words wouldn't convince her sister… then perhaps her actions will.

And her sister is definitely going to see a lot of it as Yuki goes to investigate.

At any rate, Yuki turned back to the fearful delinquent and went on to ask her questions, resigning herself to doing the tricky task of identifying a person who has the power that many people wish for, but spends it on pursuing delinquency for some reason.

—It was time for her to find a time traveler.

#3,369
Apologies for the delay. Had an emergency and writing slowed because of it. But you're not here for excuses.

Here's the newest chapter, everyone. And here we finally have a true look at this arc's big bad. I hope you guys enjoy reading!


Chapter 31

People are naturally deceitful creatures.

They live life constantly wearing masks upon their faces. They lie to themselves and to others, acting the role they require in order to achieve a goal that they seek. The mask changes every moment, every situation, and every person they talk to.

When asked to describe someone - their superior, underling, close friend, or a stranger to them will all say different answers. Which of these answers are correct? The answer is none. Because no one can fully know the truth about someone, even themselves.

She had grasped that truth very early in her life. As the eldest daughter of a powerful politician, she had seen time and time again what it means to be human and how they lie all the time. She saw how it turned into a complicated web of relationships where the truth becomes muddled, and she saw how people used it to their ends, much to their detriment or advantage.

And from that, she had learned.

Those who have the clearest idea of the social fabric will be the one who has the greatest power. And if one knows the mask to wear when talking to said person, then they'd be able to do what they want. A small lie there, a simple comment here - simple actions lead to drastic results.

To be successful is to utilize the behavior of people. Because of it, she had amassed the power that she had now, becoming an influential politician a short while after finishing college. She found herself in a very comfortable position, and her only goal now was to keep it going. Or perhaps even grow her own power as well.

Call her a psychopath, manipulator or whatever - she was someone who did what she could to improve her life. And it's not like she went out of her way to hurt other people. She just found it easy to let them do what she wants, that's all.

That was how she, Haru Yanai, had always lived her life.

—However, in comparison to her, her sister was different.

Being the younger one between them, she was shielded from learning the truth of people. Her precious sister was as naive as she was innocent. And she had only learned that the world is not as kind as she thought it was when she was bullied from a very young age… due to being cute of all things.

And at that time, her sister had discovered what it means to be disappointed and betrayed by people you thought you could trust. A certain childhood friend of hers, the people-pleaser Haya-kun, decided that it was much better to prioritize his reputation than protecting his childhood friend.

It took Haru's intervention to stop the bullying. And during it, she had thought that her sister would come to the same conclusion as she did, that she'd learn and mature much like her.

However, she didn't. What her sister settled into was that Haru was someone to be imitated. A shallow conclusion to make, and one that caused her to make constant comparisons to Haru and herself.

It was a long time ago. But such a simple thing influenced her sister's life dearly from then on. The Yuki that she knew formed her own mask to prevent being bullied once more, before striving to embody idealized childish concepts such as being reliable and dependable to others.

But the facade was clear to her as her elder sister - the girl's actions always betrayed her inner lack of self-esteem, along with her cowardice and desire to simply depend on another person just like how Haru saved her before.

Unless her sister stops striving for impossible goals like trying to be like her, nothing would change. She needs to think for herself. Because blindly emulating others is not improving, it's just the refusal to examine oneself and what you need to change to better your life.

Thankfully, the opportunity came in the form of the Service Club that she made. Without Haru around, her sister stuck to a different person - an interesting young man by the name of Makoto. He was dependable enough for her sister to think that he was a person worth striving for but has an amusing enough personality to not warrant her blind emulation.

—But then high school romance came into play and things turned complicated. She should've expected it, really.

She'd seen what was going on in that club of hers. Haru herself had never experienced what love is, but she was sure that what her sister felt wasn't love. There was some attraction, sure, but what Yuki mostly felt was admiration and respect. In comparison to the other girl in the club who also held an attraction to the boy, Haru was sure on what the ending would be.

And when Yuki faced the eventual rejection, she had thought that the growth she was waiting for would finally happen… But that wasn't what happened at all.

Instead, Yuki stuck to another person. And this time it was to a delinquent.

She thought that there must be something definitely wrong at that point. She thought that her sister was being manipulated, or maybe there really was something wrong in the head of her sister after all. But as it turns out, it wasn't any of those things - and that the truth would be much more shocking than what she initially thought.


Spoiler

The Supernatural. Demons, angels, religion and magic - something she doesn't have much belief in for the most part in her life, apparently does exist and had always existed in the background.

How was she meant to react to such a thing? She lived her life with reality already set in her mind. But now she found herself realizing that it was all a lie, and that her sister was now apparently involved with such a thing.

She knew that her sister had her own masks to wear, but since when was she able to wield a katana like that? And since when was she able to fight like she was like in some sort of anime? When did she even gain the strength to act like a superhuman?

Was she even the same sister Haru had in the first place? She looked so different from the girl she knew, the one that looked so vulnerable and lacking in self-esteem.

At some point, her sister had changed it seems.

However, whether that was for the better or not was still to be decided.

And so, even as Haru found herself utterly blindsided by everything in this new world she set foot on - she still went on to do her task to observe and steer her to what she thinks is her right path.

Because… that was her duty as the elder sister, after all.


How does one find a time traveler?

Yuki had seen many types of media which involve time travel, and with her turning meta, the need to study different stories made her much more familiar with such things.

First of all, there are different types of time travel, each with their own effects to consider. The first kind would be the time travel coming from the very far from the future. An example of this would be the witches which Rias had dealt with before. They come from the far future - or in other words, a different setting entirely.

In stories, that type of time travel is just part of the setting. The mere act of time travel is not the main focus - rather, it's the future itself, in the form of its wonder technology and things to explore. In effect, that makes time travel just a medium to explore other parts of the setting. It's no different to a portal transporting a person to a different and fantastical world in terms of use.

However, there is also a second type of time travel. One where the protagonist that has the ability to go back in time regrets something in the past.

This type explores time traveling more as a story. Instead of being used as a way to explore 'the future', it shows the effects of the actions that the protagonist takes to fix a problem that happens in the past. Of course, things don't go the way people expect after doing so, and it becomes an interesting story in its own right. Perhaps it would be a power fantasy. Or perhaps it would be grim and serious. The possibilities are endless.

Basa-kun theorized that it might be the latter, involving some of the other settings included in the world-affecting scenario. More specifically, he mentioned that it would likely be a hypothetical time traveling delinquent.

She'd like to have some more solid confirmation about that… but then again, that was the very reason why she was here investigating. And she couldn't dismiss the fact that the others had already found the 'sources' for the change in the other settings.

V and Aoki-san had already determined that an alien from Hakoniwa Academy caused a destructive fight in another alien setting. The last she'd heard from them, they were checking out the shrine she had told them of and found out that they were hosting a group which apparently deals with yokai and aliens - with one of the characters, the heroine, clearly being an esper.

A strange setting, but not one of the strangest that she'd heard of.

Rias was also the same. Minutes earlier, she received a text notifying that she just finished rescuing the person captured by the fallen angels near Akumano Academy. She also determined that the chaotic gang war happening here shouldn't be at the level that it occurred, and that the one responsible for it all - a demon called 'En Belzeebub' - was supposed to be playing video games in his room instead of joining the fight himself.

Basa-kun apparently quickly put a stop to that though. He quickly defeated the demon and went on his way to look for possible easier-to-miss changes outside the main source of the world-affecting scenario. The ones that they currently aren't doing.

That said, with the rest crossed out, the only possible settings left are the delinquents, the time travelers and the super-powered students. The latter of the three also likely belonged in the main source of the scenario itself… which pretty much leaves her with delinquents and time travelers.

So if that were the case, what type of time travel would it be? If it were to involve a delinquent, then it would likely be the second type. One where they would fix a previous regret.

If that was the case, then the signs are easy to look for - it was to find the most successful gang around. And it's especially good if said gang came out of nowhere like a dark horse.

However, there was one small problem.

"—Bring it on, you bastards!!!"

It was that such gangs are dime a dozen.

Yuki watched from far away as a gang she was observing fought off a much larger group that surrounded them. But despite their enemy's overwhelming number advantage, the gang was somehow holding them off much to their shock. And with the gang fighting while covering each other's backs, standing tall despite their bruised and bloody faces - it made for a very inspiring scene.

"I-Impossible, just who are these people…!?"

"What's with these kids…!?"

"They're really laying their life for this… did they go insane?"

And as their enemies shouted those words - the one in front of the group, someone who Yuki assumed to be their leader, smiled ferociously while bleeding heavily from his head. Then after bringing down someone who attempted to punch him, he looked around and shouted at their enemies.

"This place is under our protection!" he cried out. "I already made the mistake of running away from a fight with you bastards a few years ago - and I'm not going to do it again! So if you want to mess with this town, then you'll have to go through my dead body!"

It was a very passionate declaration.

And it also proved that this wasn't the time traveler that Yuki was looking for.

She turned away from the group upon hearing that and left. The 'gang war' happening currently spans plenty of schools as seen in the challenge letters her sister had given them along with the information she received from the delinquents she interrogated. And so, after crossing out this recent one, she moved on to the next group that she'd heard of.

The next one would be… at Mizo High School, it seems. And it's relatively close to where they were.

Yuki was about to move, but she paused when she noticed something from the side. A group of delinquents seemed to have spotted her and were heading in her direction.

"Hey, looks like we missed one!"

"Her uniform is different. Which gang is she from?"

"That doesn't matter. Look, she's got a katana! Take care of her quickly!"

Not hesitating from what they treat as an active warzone, they rushed at her with bats, brass knuckles, and pipes. Yuki put her hand on her spirit weapon's pommel and consecutively dodged their hits - before quickly drawing her sword and swinging it to them with a flash.

—Schwing!

The thugs stopped in their tracks. And Yuki, having dashed through them, brought back her sword back to its sheathe. And the very moment her sword's pommel clicked against the head of the sheath itself…

"Kuh…!"

"Grrk—!"

…The thugs dropped on the ground, completely unconscious with their eyes rolled up. Yuki glanced at them, and then the area around her to check if there were anymore of their gang who was around. But that doesn't seem to be the case.

With that, she turned to the other person following her. Yuki glanced at her sister, who had been standing there with wide eyes ever since… Well, the past hour, give or take.

"Nee-san. It's time to move." she told her.

Her sister was still staring at unconscious thugs, stunned. For a moment there was silence… then when Yuki was thinking of calling her again to gain her attention, she finally spoke.

"Yuki-chan, did you just kill these people?" she asked.

Yuki blinked at her sudden question.

"Ah, no." she replied. "I used the flat of my blade. They're fine nee-san, just unconscious."

"F-Flat of your blade…?" her sister's face looked like she was having difficulty comprehending the situation. "Something so chuunibyou… No, I-I suppose something like that can actually occur, huh? My sister is actually using a katana now…"

Yuki found her face heating up a bit after her sister's comment, even if she didn't try to show it. She was right, it does seem a bit chuuni to say. But the embarrassment was curtailed by the fact that it was the truth.

So she shook her head and focused. "Anyway, nee-san, I'm moving on to my next destination." she told her. "Unless you want to leave and process everything away from this? You don't need to come. I can freely answer everything later after everything is done."

"…Very well." Yuki said with a nod, before turning around to walk beside her. "Then, please hold that handkerchief that I gave you. I'm sure you've surmised it by now, but that handkerchief hides people in a certain range. It should keep you from being noticed by some of the more mundane fighters here."

She paused for a moment, before continuing to speak.

"But if I encounter someone who's also aware of the supernatural then it might not work. So please hide away if that's the case. I can't guarantee that you'll be safe if you stay around." she told her.

"Will there be someone like that here?" her sister asked, unsure.

"I can't say anything solidly." Yuki said, avoiding any flags that she might say after already messing up earlier. "There might be some people in the area who are aware and practice magic, but I have reasons to believe that the chances of us encountering them are low."

"Just about anything if you're clever enough. As I said earlier, it's like science." Yuki answered.

"I don't think science can let a handkerchief hide people while they're in plain sight, sister."

"You'd be surprised." she commented. "But I said that it's only like science. There's a system to it all that you have to follow, but it's hard. And quite varying at times. I can say that it's definitely much harder to understand than science."

Magic systems are one of the strangest things to learn. Due to the sheer number of supernatural settings around with each of them trying to be unique, the magic learned in one story is different in the other. However, there's a great degree of overlap happening in the magical genre, so that can only be attributed to magic itself being generally flexible. The extremely difficult ones to learn are the isolated systems, because they work on a different logic entirely.

If she could compare it to something, it would be like learning different dialects or languages. With the dialects being the magic systems that overlap while the different languages would be the isolated ones.

However, the latter needed one to be meta first. That meant that her sister would likely be learning the former. Not to say that it'd still be easy for her - because even with a talented teacher like Basa-kun and Rias, Yuki still had a hard time to get to the point that she was in now.

If she had an interest in studying it, that is.

"I see…" her sister muttered, staring at the handkerchief in her hand. "…Can I keep this? This seems useful."

Yuki gave her a flat look. "You can't. It's a treasured possession of mine. In fact, please be careful with it."

—What was she saying? Of course her sister would be interested. Now she can only hope that interest isn't due to her thinking of new ways to manipulate people.

In any case, her sister doesn't seem bothered by her refusal. Instead, she actually looked curious.

"Oh? A treasured possession, you say?" she asked, before looking over the handkerchief once more. "Hmm, now that I think about it, this design doesn't look like your style… this is from a boy, isn't it? Don't tell me it's from Basa-kun?"

Her brow twitched.

"H-How did you even get to that conclusion?" she asked incredulously.

"You just stuttered Yuki-chan. So I am right, aren't I?"

Yuki let out a breath, looking away from her sister and trying to ignore the heat in her face.

"…So what if you are?" she muttered. As expected, her sister just seems to know how to push her buttons. "That doesn't really matter much, does it?"

Even without looking, she could feel Haru's gaze at her.

"You really are smitten with that guy, huh." her sister observed. "I've never seen you make a face like that before. It looks like I've been seeing new sides of you today, Yuki-chan."

That strangely reflective statement made Yuki glance at her once more. "…The same goes for you, nee-san. I don't think I've ever seen half the expressions you've been making since earlier." she answered. "The both of us are learning a lot of new things between one another, it seems."

"You're right about that. Honestly, this is the most proper we've communicated for years, haven't we?"

Yuki paused at her sister's words, and she glanced at her.

Her sister was staring up in the sky with an expression she couldn't quite identify. Her eyes weren't really looking at the clouds up above, but rather at something else. A faraway that only her sister could see, whatever it was.

And it was with that look that Haru continued.

"I can see that you've changed Yuki. It took me seeing you fight in a way that's straight out of an anime, but it really does look like it." her sister spoke. "This was the reason why you allowed me to be with you, right? You could've left me alone and I wouldn't be able to do anything about it. But you didn't, just to show me this."

"…Yes." Yuki replied after a moment, before looking away. "I told you a few days ago. I wanted to prove to you that you don't have to worry anymore, and this is me honoring that promise."

—People are naturally deceitful creatures.

That was a lesson that she had learned in her life.

They can never understand each other short of actual mind-reading magic or devices. People lie to each other and to themselves all the time, and relationships can get entangled in the process. She had naively thought at some point that she could improve herself to the point that she suffered no consequences from that, but all it ended up was her getting caught in drama that had overwhelmed her.

However, as accurate as that statement is - it doesn't mean that's always the case.

It just seemed that way because that was what all it was for them. Drama characters like her are fated to be caught in a strange web of relationships for the sake of the narrative. Misunderstandings, trickery, denial - those are the things that will always follow them for each attempt to form a bond.

But with her turning meta, Yuki was free of that. She was able to see beyond what her previous life offered, and she was finally able to witness the beauty of simplicity and everything else that came with it.

People are naturally deceitful, yes. They can be terrible, hypocritical, and hard to trust.

But so what?

It shouldn't stop people from trying to understand. No one is born perfect, which is why people will always try to make sense of themselves and others. They will try to make sense of everything, trying to uncover and fathom something even if they cannot.

So there was no point in overthinking about it. You just have to live with the fact that people are hard to understand and trust, and then try to understand and trust people despite all that. Because the mere act of striving to make sense of everything around you, thinking that it will result in some sort of happiness or peace of mind…

Well, that's just life, isn't it?

"—Let's be genuine to each other, nee-san."

Her sister paused at Yuki's sudden words.

"That's a bit out of nowhere." Haru commented. "What do you mean by that, Yuki-chan?"

She let out a breath. "You know what I mean. No more talking in circles, no more approaching the other with complicated schemes. Let's talk to each other properly." Yuki told her. "I realize that I've not been truthful about many things in the past and… well, so are you, really. But I realize that it's mostly because of me as well."

Yuki admitted that with a frown, before continuing to speak.

"I looked up to you. And I wanted to be like you. But I wasn't going about it right, and I realized that you were just guiding me in your own strange way." she reflected. "There are times that I hated you. But I suppose you liked it that I wasn't comfortable in your presence… because it meant finally stepping out of your shadow, or something like that."

She remembered it. She remembered the disapproval in her face when she wanted to follow her sister's footsteps. Except, it wasn't really following - since in the end, she always had to depend on her sister or someone else because her methods don't achieve results.

But now…

"But now, there's really no point in doing that anymore, nee-san." she told her. "You've said it yourself: I've changed. So please, just tell me things straight if you have something to say - I'm sure that I've earned a little bit of your trust to have that, right?"

Haru turned silent.

For a very long moment as they walked, there was only silence between the two of them. Yuki quietly waited for her sister's judgement, wondering whether she would agree with her request to reconcile their strange relationship.

And then finally, after a long while of waiting, she spoke.

"…You've matured, Yuki." Haru stated solemnly. "It's ironic that my sister would finally stop chasing after unrealistic things after being part of the supernatural but… I suppose that's what happens when someone gets actual magical powers. They get one hell of a confidence boost."

Then she sighed, before looking forward once more.

"I suppose that's another thing to thank Basa-kun for, after the whole deal of him apparently saving you. It seems that you've changed because of whatever happened while you're with him."

Yuki didn't deny that. That was exactly the case, after all.

"That said… despite everything you've said…" her sister suddenly muttered darkly. "It doesn't mean I'll approve of your relationship yet!"

She blinked. "…Huh?"

Her sister wagged a finger. "Tsk tsk tsk. Just because he helped you mature doesn't mean that he's automatically approved, Yuki-chan! There are more things I need to know about him before I could do that, especially after knowing what I know now!"

Yuki paused.

Why exactly was she talking about this? This was definitely an attempt to steer the conversation away from their current topic. An unnaturally obvious and sloppy attempt even, considering that it's her sister who was doing it.

So why? Why did she say that? Was this a rejection of her request? She turned to look at her sister and—


Spoiler

—Ah.

It seems that there was no need for her sister to answer anything, with a face like that.

And so, looking away from her sister's embarrassed expression, Yuki smiled. "But I don't really need your approval, you know that right, nee-san?" she said, playing along. "And I doubt that you can stop us. Your political power doesn't mean anything in the supernatural world."

"How mean! And this is after you said that we're going to be genuine to each other? Does having a genuine relationship mean trampling over my opinions, dear sister?"

That made Yuki close her eyes and sigh.

"Now that's just unfair." she stated, before opening one eye and glancing towards her sister. "…But aren't you a bit unqualified to judge something like that, nee-san? As far as I know, you haven't had any relationships yet, right?"

"Huh? That's just a low blow right there. You're the one being unfair now, Yuki!"

"You started it."

"Hmph! It's my right as an elder sister." she said, crossing her arms. "And I really am not sure about that Basa-kun, you know? I can't make heads or tails of that guy, so you don't know what he's thinking! Why, just the other day, he mentioned that he was in a harem! Can you believe that?"

Yuki stiffened.

Her sister didn't miss it. "…Yuki?"

"A-Ahem. Well." she stuttered, floundering how to explain this, before spotting something in the distance. "Ah, it looks like we've arrived at our destination, nee-san… Let's just discuss this later, alright?" she told her.

Haru stared at her, the playful expression she held earlier disappearing in exchange for an expression that seemed like a mix of disbelief and incredulity. Then that same expression hardened, and the woman opened her mouth to speak—

"Bastard! Dieeee!!!"

Looks like her talk with her sister would really have to be delayed later.

Yuki put her hand on the pommel of her sword as she looked over the chaotic fight that was currently occurring right in front of the school. It was a familiar scene, similar to the previous groups she had checked out before: A single gang was surrounded but was somehow managing to fight them off, displaying an inspiring scene of man versus many.

That said, this group was more noticeable compared to the other ones Yuki had seen before.


Spoiler

For one, their emblem was the manji character. It was a symbol that meant well-being and good fortune, but it was unfortunately frequently misunderstood by many foreigners due to it being similar to the Nazi swastika. However, the right-facing clockwise direction of the symbol clearly made it different from the left-facing counterclockwise direction of swastika, so unless it was a major misprint, Yuki likely wasn't looking at some neo-nazi delinquent group.

And seeing the symbol on what she associates more with temples than a gang - she also immediately recognized who they are. She had heard the names of the powerhouse gangs from the people she interrogated, and this was one of them.

The To-man Gang. She didn't know what the 'To' means, but the 'man' part definitely means manji in this case.

It was as if he was just a mundane person from her drama plot. The level of brutality is eerily realistic, one that was disturbing enough to make Yuki think if she'd have to step in and stop a murder happening in front of her.

Spoiler

It was a passionate declaration, similar to the group she observed before.

However his words held a silent implication, and a drama character like Yuki managed to pick out the hidden meaning in his words almost instantly. He said that the pain was nothing compared to losing your loved ones, and that implied that he's lost his loved ones before for him to feel that way.

Perhaps something did happen in the past for this to happen. A traumatic experience which made him act desperate enough to shrug off such a beating… But realistically, the odds of something like that happening in a developed country like Japan and in a relatively middle class neighborhood like this are, evidently, somewhat low.

Sure, some people in her country had it hard, but she was sure their problems weren't as bad in comparison to a wartorn country like Westalis. So either this person must have a really colorful backstory to have something like that… or perhaps, the said 'past' hasn't happened yet, and he was fighting to stop the possibility of a tragedy happening.

Yuki might have just found the time traveler she was looking for.

But that was still conjecture. She'd have to prove it, and acting upon what she determined before about the genre - she went with the most convenient and quickest way to do it.

Another pseudo-flash step. The world sped by her as she disappeared from the rooftops and went down to where the delinquents were fighting. To them, they might have blinked only to see that a girl appeared out of nowhere - and judging by their reaction it might have been just that.

Yuki snapped her fingers and a bounded field spread around her.

It looked as if they froze in time, but the bounded field didn't do anything as fancy as that. All it did was produce a simple hypnotic effect that made them stop thinking for a bit, similar to a person getting lost in a daze.

And with that, Yuki was free to gather information.

Saying apologies that definitely went unheard, she then began reading the memories from the delinquent.

His name was Takemichi. A student of Mizo High, founding member of the To-man Gang, and… a time traveler in the future. Ah, it seems that she was correct in her conjecture. From the looks of it, this Takemichi has somehow stumbled upon the power to travel back in time for exactly twelve years, as long as he completes certain stringent requirements.

Currently, he doesn't know how exactly he gained the power. And there are also no clear outliers in his memories which took her attention. Still, while those might help, she didn't really need his memories to determine whatever the world-affecting scenario had changed in this person's narrative.

She brought out the simulating orb device from her subspace pocket and held it up to the dazed delinquent. Then it activated, simulating with great accuracy what the current narrative would be if it wasn't for outlier effects.

And there, she was able to see…

Her eyes narrowed.

And there might be a possibility of character death as well… I should probably heal these people to prevent that from happening."

She wasn't skilled with healing, but giving him a single sip from a health potion in her subspace might be enough to make a difference. She did just that, returning the simulation device and exchanging it with glass phial, before giving him little drops of the healing potion in his mouth.

And that wouldn't be something the people around can do with the combination of them being dazed from the bounded field, the tendency to ignore small details in the fight, and the most important fact that the genre divide wouldn't allow them to notice it.

This should be enough.

With that, she turned around and walked away from the frozen people, heading to the direction where her sister was waiting. She's going to have to observe some more in order to determine if there would be any additional changes, as well as to see the cause of the change itself.

Time travelers should be involved in a way… but the memories don't really give anything specific. She should try to inspect it again to see if there was something that the delinquent missed.

Spoiler

Hakoniwa Academy. The very source of the problem they were dealing with now.

However, Yuki's senses were feeling something completely different.
