Yuki wondered about that as well. The main reason why they wanted to avoid direct contact with that setting is because of the overpowered characters, especially the reality warper that Basa-kun was concerned about.

But despite their efforts, it seems that things still ended up this way. They were safe for now in this apartment considering the amount of defenses present - however, what would be their next move? How would this contact affect the direction of the world-affecting scenario?

As she wondered that, the phone in her began to ring as she received a call. Yuki and everyone else blinked before looking at her, and Yuki stared at the phone's screen to see who the caller was.

It was Basa-kun. She immediately picked it up.

"Basa-kun." she greeted.

"I've seen what happened." he immediately stated, his voice echoing in the living room and making Yuki nod. Right, of course he would be aware of what's happening in the city. "For now you all should just stay put in the apartment. I assume that you all dealt with the changes in the nearby settings?"

Yuki looked around, and the others nodded.

"We did." she answered. "But those people…"

"Yeah, you guys were definitely set up by this shitty world. The plan hinges on us avoiding the source and dealing with it once things are done, but this definitely raises the stakes." he let out a sigh. "That said, it's not like we didn't prepare for this in the past few days. I'll go ahead and do the next part."

"Will all of us interacting with them matter? The possibility of someone failing was raised, but with all of us experiencing this simultaneously…"

"It's fine." he waved off. "You already accomplished the main objective. The point is to contain the effects in the original setting, which means it won't cause an uncontrolled domino effect. That's what's important here, so good job on doing that."

"But didn't you say that we shouldn't make contact with those people?" Rias asked in concern. "After all, you said that reality warper is aware of everything happening within her setting since she's super OP! Should we expect an attack from her if that was the case?"

"Not really. You don't worry about that reality warper, either."

"Why is that?" Yuki asked.

"Because if she really wanted us gone, then we'd be dead already."

—His reply was like a sudden douse of freezing cold water.

As she and the others stiffened, Yuki furrowed her brows and spoke. "What do you mean by that, Basa-kun?"

There was a moment of silence.

"...I didn't want to say this. Hoped not to, really. Since it'll just serve as a distraction." he admitted. "But as I said, that person is dangerous. She is the very definition of unfairness, and out of everything in this shitty world I am very confident that she is one of the possible characters who could destroy the universe. Not the world or galaxy - the entire universe. That's how powerful she is."

"The flimsy defenses in my apartment don't matter in the face of someone like her because, well, there's no beating that person in the eyes of the story. Not without a significant amount of plot armor, that is… That said, she probably still doesn't know where all of you are. Nor is she interested in doing that. From what I know of her, she's essentially just a bored god that lets interesting things develop before involving herself."

There was a poignant silence in the living room after Basa-kun revealed that to them.

He had told them plenty of times that the reality warper is powerful. However, she didn't think that it would be at that level. A person who could potentially destroy the entire universe? Just how ridiculously powerful would someone like that be?

Yuki couldn't even comprehend it. She couldn't even visualize the scale of destruction that would result in, or how someone could defeat a person like that. She couldn't even think of a way that the story could make up a plot to beat such a person, considering she's apparently the main antagonist.

And more importantly, she couldn't even imagine how Basa-kun could face off with them and be so calm about it. Because she doubted that even Basa-kun, who was the most powerful person that she knew, could defeat a being such as that.

Which is why Yuki - with her mind a mess of worry, anxiety, and the slightest bit of frustration due to only knowing this now - muttered her next words to the phone.

"…I would've preferred it if you told us about this earlier." she said to him. "Why didn't you tell us this, Basa-kun?"

He let out a breath.

"Exactly because of your current state. You're pretty worried, right?" he answered her. "No amount of saying 'it'll be fine' from me would satisfy you since, well, that reality warper can destroy the universe. I don't want you jumping at shadows and worrying about something that you don't need to; It's counterproductive. You were all focusing on avoiding contact with characters from the original setting, and I don't need you second guessing yourself worrying about the reality warper after that."

Perhaps that was the case. Despite Basa-kun suspecting otherwise, even now she wonders if the reality warper is aware of them, watching their every move and simply not acting.

That said, despite knowing all that…

Aoki-san frowned as she stared down at her phone. "That's not good, Basa-kun. You should've told us." she scolded, speaking what they all thought. "It doesn't matter if it's counterproductive. We still have the right to worry about it, considering you're going to face them off."

Another silence on the other end of the call. And somehow, Yuki could imagine Basa-kun on the other side, looking away guiltily while scratching the back of his head.

"…Right, sorry. I'll try to be better next time." he apologized.

"Yeah, you better say sorry! We expect that you will make it up to us after this!" Rias said with an emphatic nod.

"Uh huh." Basa-kun's voice was decidedly unimpressed this time, but in the end he seemed to accept that. "But alright. Guess I'll make it up to you guys. Maybe by bringing souvenirs or something…"

Souvenirs? What exactly did he mean by that? Did he plan to go somewhere?

Well, she supposed that doesn't really matter right now. Thinking about that can come later.

In any case, the tension upon learning new facts about the reality warper lessened a bit from Rias' antics. Still it was clear that their minds were still trying to digest that. But out of all of them, it was V who, being the pragmatic person that she was, quickly recovered and asked the important question.

"So how can she be dealt with?" she asked.

"Leave that to me." Basa-kun replied vaguely. "As I said, I'm going to go to Hakoniwa Academy after this."

Rias frowned. "And what about you? Are you sure that you're going to be okay, Basa-kun?"

"I know what to do - I already dealt with this before. Just keep an eye on everything, especially those guys that saw you. This would take a lot of focus that I can't afford to monitor others." he answered, before adding something after a momentary pause. "…By the way, there's also another thing I need to apologize for. There's a good chance I might disappear for a few days, so don't freak out if that happens, yeah?"

Yuki and the others blinked.

"H-Huh? Why?" she asked.

"Sorry, can't say why. Just trust me on that." he answered, and she could imagine him looking away again. "Anyway, time is running out. I'll see you. And I swear I'll make it up to you guys after this, seriously."

"What are you—" the call cut off. "—saying…?"

Yuki gaped at her phone.

"…What the heck!? Did he suddenly end the call after saying that!?" Rias fumed, thinking the same thing as she did. "We need an explanation! He can't just say that without elaborating!"

Yuki closed her eyes and massaged the bridge of her nose, letting out a frustrated breath as she did so.

That person… what was he doing, not elaborating about what he said? There's a chance he'll disappear for a few days? What does that even mean? And how can they not freak out if that's the case?

What could possibly be the reason why he would do all this without explanation?

"…Perhaps he can't explain." V offered, making Yuki and Rias pause. The woman's brows were furrowed in thought as she spoke. "That man might be vague at times, but he never withholds vital information unless he has a reason to do so. He could be practicing operational security. You can never be too careful with a reality warper that powerful, after all."

"Y-Yes, so let's all calm down, alright?" Aoki-san also said, trying to put them at ease, before gaining a frown herself. "…And like what Basa-kun said, we still need to keep an eye on those people we encountered earlier. We should work on that for now."

Yuki let out a sigh.

"Yes… I suppose that makes sense." she muttered, before looking away. "…I still don't like it though."

Aoki-san smiled at her. "Believe me Yuki-chan, I'm worried as well. But talking about that can come later."

Rias also nodded, but then she looked thoughtful. "Right… But going back on monitoring them, how exactly can we do that? Do we even know where to find those people?"

"If there was any place that they'd be, then it would likely be in their school." Yuki inferred. "We're not sure though, so it's better to check if that was the case. And if they are, then we can leave them to Basa-kun while we focus more on double-checking the changes in the nearby settings."

If they really are in their school, then Basa-kun might have already dealt with them already. And while the setting of the place is… gripping, in a way that existential horror would fascinate someone due to its implications, the only real threat to Basa-kun there is actually the reality warper.

That said… "Regarding how we can see them, I think I have a solution for that."

Yuki then brought out the strands of hair she cut off from the time traveler.

"This should be enough for us to scry the time traveler's location." Yuki stated. "She escaped when I went after her, so chances are she should be where her allies are staying. This way, we can observe what they're doing remotely and we wouldn't leave the safety of this apartment in case those people attack us."

"Ohh! That's great! Let's get to doing that, then!" Rias said excitedly.

She nodded. "Yes, we should."

With that, they moved to prepare a scrying ritual. It usually involved a crystal ball or perhaps a basin filled with clear liquid of some sort, but having learned and adapted the spell for modern conveniences - they prepared it by using the TV in Basa-kun's living room.

Finishing the final incantation and channeling prana inside, Yuki placed the strands on hair in a small glowing magic circle near the TV. Simultaneously, the TV turned on and displayed a static signal as the spell searched for the time traveler.

As Aoki helped V fix up her arm, the two were left alone together on the sofa. Rias meanwhile helped her, using her vast magical energy to fuel the scrying in case the distance was farther than expected. The girl had her hand outstretched while also feeding prana to the TV, and as she did that, she spoke.

"This is such a pain… I guess even as people who turned meta, there's just some people out there who we can't take on." the redhead muttered, still digesting what she learned earlier. "A person who can destroy the universe? I know that statement is easily thrown around in anime, but just what the hell is that? Even my brother isn't that powerful."

She then sighed.

"And who knows what those people making a mess of things are capable of. They're only relatively strong compared to that reality warper, but that doesn't really mean anything, does it?" she frowned. "Especially after hearing from Basa-kun how certain characters in those settings act…"

Yuki nodded. She feels the same as well.

It was a cautionary tale for them. Being meta, you can be tempted to do whatever you want in different settings thinking that the genre divide can cover for you. That your actions wouldn't result in bad consequences, especially so when you don't give the world an 'out' to explain things from outside their genre.

That setting was entirely the result of Basa-kun's actions in the past. It was the world's way of coping from his thoughtlessness, turning it into a strange mirror of himself because it couldn't explain anything about his actions.

The main subject of it would be the reality warper, but as for the other characters… Well, they're all terrifying in their own way. Like the time traveler she met as an enemy - that girl seemed weak, but her ability more than makes up for it.

She doesn't know the exact mechanics of her ability but she could easily find her existence erased, and the only saving grace was the fact that her identity is unknown to them.

But who knows how long that'll apply.

"If only we didn't encounter those guys… and all of us as well…" Rias muttered contritely.

Hearing that, Yuki looked down while feeling ashamed, as she remembered something that happened just a couple of hours ago. A stupid quip said in her mind, but might end up just being the one that resulted in all this.

"…I believe I am at fault for that." she confessed, making Rias blink. "A while back, I raised a flag while thinking about something. I'm pretty sure that it's what caused all of this. I'm very sorry for my mistake."

She recalled thinking that the others would fare better than her… and judging by the state of affairs, it definitely didn't go the way she hoped.

However, her bitter self-rumination was interrupted when Rias also said something.

"E-Eh? No way, you did that as well?" Rias suddenly said in surprise. "I actually did the same earlier! I was feeling guilty since I thought I messed everything up!"

—What?

Staring at Rias with wide-eyes, along with the understanding of basic pattern recognition - Yuki then immediately turned to Aoki-san and V, who also looked similarly shocked as they listened from the sofa.

"Could it be, the both of you…?" she asked.

Aoki-san and V nodded, before glancing at one another in surprise as well. That definitely confirms what she suspected. It was exactly like earlier, where all of them experienced the same thing.

What was happening? There's no way this is a coincidence, isn't it?

This was definitely due to the narrative. It was clearly brewing something up for them, especially with the unnatural timings of Basa-kun's alert and the tasks Serafall-san and her sister gave him - but here they are now again, getting caught in its flow without them even knowing.

But what exactly does it have in store, if it made them raise flags? One flag statement definitely results in a bad situation, so what does that mean if all of them did it?

What exactly was waiting for them right now?

—The answer to that question arrived surprisingly fast.

Yuki and the rest stiffened when suddenly, the TV started to become clearer as the scrying ritual finally found its mark. The static gave way to a more identifiable picture, and there they saw the people they were looking for.

It was the time traveler. She was in a place that looked like a student council room - a place that she was inside in just a few hours earlier with her club. And with her were likely the same people that Rias, V, and Aoki-san encountered, judging by the surprise and recognition in their faces.

However, what was strange about them was that they were all in a daze. And the reason for it was Basa-kun who was in the same place. It was clear that he had already done what he needed to do, like what they planned to do days prior to this.

But that wasn't what had surprised them. They didn't even care about the powerful reality warper, which was seated at the head of the table giving Basa-kun a mysterious smile.

Instead, they all stared at the other person in the room with them.

Blonde hair. Tanned skin.

And a mysterious demeanour that knows more than they let on.

"Another Basa-kun…?"

…The narrative, it seems, really gave them a nasty surprise this time.


…

…

Before everything, here's a question to ponder upon.

What does it truly mean to be special?

Well, to be 'special' means to be above a baseline. Being special is a relative property after all. What defines someone as special is defined by what is normal. But that doesn't really answer much.

After all, someone might say everyone is special… However, a closer look would reveal that this is a contradiction. If everyone is special, then the baseline increases and it becomes the new average. So if everyone is special, then no one is.

In that case, 'special' was a synonym for 'inherent human dignity'. It's a social white lie to affirm self-worth, but in reality it's not actually true. As while everyone has equal worth as a human being, not everyone is special in terms of talent, contribution, or rarity.

Being 'special' is also used as a synonym for 'unique' as well, despite being fundamentally different. Everyone is inherently unique at birth. However, being unique doesn't mean you are special - to be special means that there is something in you that is different that is 'better' and 'noteworthy' compared to others. Uniqueness is an objective difference between people, while specialness requires a subjective judgement.

And that makes the special person rare, and the unique person abundant.

Therefore, putting those two together- being special is to be a statistical outlier. Someone who had differentiated themselves from the masses, and a person with great skill, talent and impact that existence or actions deviate from the norm so much that they force the baseline to recalibrate.

Now that's all very deep and all, but how does that relate to the current situation? Well, consider this - I am currently in a shitty anime world, where the wackiest shit happens all for the sake of hooking an audience.

So let's look at those things and spin them into something more entertaining, shall we?

Like for example, take those concepts of what it means to be special that has been discussed. Now, turn them into literal superpowers. Make it so that 'talent', that which separates someone special from a baseline, at some point becomes so extreme that the laws of reality don't apply.

Or in other words - turn someone into a 'main character with a special power'.

Now, make it so that they're gathered in a single school, along with a bunch of normal people here and there.

—And that's how you get this place.


Spoiler

Hakoniwa Academy.

That's what this place essentially is. A setting where all the main characters are gathered. How ridiculous is that? Just how much of a mess will be made in such a place? Perhaps that's the appeal of it.

A place filled with superpowered students who are seen as special, having 'skills' that can either be talent, magic, or any other superpower. Such skills are also quite general, from having abilities that simply make a person good at a certain thing, up to having abilities so strange, obscure and overpowered that the setting with punch ghosts will go green with envy.

Then… There's also the one thing that separates it from the other narratives out there in this shitty world. One that is displayed in a flashy, yet unimportant fight currently happening within the school grounds.

"Useless! You can't beat me. You're just a side character in this world!"

"I don't care! Even a side character like me… I can be special! I can prove it!"

"Hm!? Those words…!"

Some of the characters here are aware of the narrative and the tropes that come with it.

They are aware of their position as a character in the story and are even actively using it for their own ends. Perhaps it's due to the nature of the story of 'main characters gathering and fighting' that the narrative becomes an actual thing they use.

But wait a minute, one might think, does that mean that these people are meta like I and the others are?

Fascinatingly enough, no. That is actually not the case.

Some stories just turn more meta than others. For example, there are gag animes out there that actively make meta jokes that touch on the knowledge that I use. Except, this story is much closer to what I am in the way they treat the narrative as an actual force. I even see people use it in a way that I would.

From determining flag-like statements, using expected narrative events only to backtrack and land cheap shots, not messing with the main characters because of plot armor… that sort of stuff.

Except the thing is, it's just limited to that. They're contained in this setting. They can never venture out to other stories and use that knowledge to do whatever they want. The genre divide works on them as much as the other characters out there.

Furthermore, they don't have a complete understanding of the logic of the world itself. There are many moments that tropes or meta statements are said despite the fact that they can have no way to see it in-character. Things like measuring screen time to measure strength, or maybe changing 'genres' despite the fact that a setting's genre is already set the moment a story is told.

It was as if the world was only humoring them. In the end, while they display meta characteristics, it looks like they're as ignorant as everyone else.

They're still people trapped in the cage. They're more aware than most people, but still trapped nonetheless.

Still, this setting was entirely unique in that regard. No other story around the world was like this, and one might wonder how something like this even came to be… Well, the answer to that is quite simple, actually.

—Me.

This place is my greatest mistake. A direct consequence of a time where I was reckless with my actions when I mistook freedom as the lack of responsibility. The world didn't know how to cope with a person acting like I am, who was truly free from its influence.

So it made a setting like this. A place where pseudo-meta people are present. And at the head of it was the person who was the very first person who was affected by it all. One who you could call a major 'victim' of all my recklessness.

After all - in her perspective she was the one who created all of this.

It was because of that why I monitored this place heavily. It was hard, because a single mistake could mean gaining the attention of that reality warper, but I managed to do so and stayed far away from the setting because that was my only real protection against her. Everything was under control, at least for a while.

Then the reality warper cooked up an insane plan to turn all the people in the world into main characters for some reason. A plan that would undoubtedly affect the world as a whole.

Don't ask me how it works, I don't really get it myself. Perhaps it's just a limited understanding of how this world's logic works. The only thing to remember about it was that it was the classic 'make a utopia with sacrifices' that utilitarian antagonists make.

And what's important is that the world finally threw the problem back in my face. Perhaps with all of my love interests all gathered, it decided that it can finally give me a real problem to tackle instead of something I could just easily deal with.

A story has to have stakes after all, and what better way to make it than making the enemy a much overpowered character?

This stupid world has it out for me, seriously.

…

But I digress. I didn't come here to complain. I've come here to solve problems.

There's a reason why I was going to this school alone. It was partly because I was responsible for this place and kinda feel ashamed of showing it to others, but most of it was because of safety. The reality warper was very dangerous and I didn't want any of the others gaining her attention.

—So, how can I deal with this? Let's consider the situation.

Due to the logical impossibility of the reality warper's plan and the genre being shounen, it was definitely going to be foiled by the main character. However, doing so would undoubtedly result in definite casualties along with a serious effect on the settings on the world itself. So, how can a problem like that be solved in such a way that the narrative will be satisfied?

Well, Yuki and the rest already did the first part. They dealt with the changes outside this setting before it could affect other settings as well. The second domino after the first was removed, causing the others to remain standing when it fell. That means the effects are isolated in this setting only.

But unlike normal dominoes, there's nothing stopping anyone from just doing it all again, causing another set of dominos to fall. Not unless the whole source is dealt with, we'd just repeat everything until the main character deals with them and the plan fails… which was the actual requirement to satisfy the narrative.

It should be the main character who should fix things. Because what sort of main antagonist in an action shounen anime wouldn't be defeated by the main character? In the eyes of the story, I can't be the one that stops them. It has to be the main character or else nothing would change.

But the problem is that they're still actually in the middle of a different arc right now. It would take too much time for us to wait. So how can I make it so that the main character can defeat the reality warper if that was the case?

Well… the answer is to speed things up. Not by timey-wimey stuff because that would be too complicated.

Instead, let's get back to the requirement mentioned - in the eyes of the story, I stated that what matters is that the main character defeats the main antagonist… but technically, it doesn't even need to happen.

—All that matters is that the characters think they experienced it.

And so by planting them with false memories through hypnosis - I can literally speed things up by making every character involved experience an entire anime arc in their head, and then making it feel like some time had passed despite the fact that it didn't.

What's important is that the characters thought it happened after all, not whether or not it really did. You could say that the entire arc happened in a dream world without the characters and even the viewers of the story itself not knowing.

It was my 'destructive arc' special. Used on drastic situations where I had no choice to let bad shit happen just so the narrative can be satisfied.

And so, the plan to deal with this setting was simple.

A quick in and out, because I didn't want to deal with anything troublesome by staying too long. My presence would be absolutely minimal and I'd be literally there for a short time. So the moment that Yuki called me and I hung up - I went ahead and teleported to their school, working as fast as I could.

And I was very, very brief.

—At 0.001 seconds, I arrived at a forgotten corner within the large campus of Hakoniwa Academy.

—At 0.002 seconds, I formed an entire magical circle that enveloped the whole place.

—At 0.003 seconds, I casted an area-wide hypnosis, putting all people present in a daze, and then planting all the prepped memories I meticulously crafted for the past few days and letting them experience the entire arc in their heads.

—At 0.004 seconds, I was done. And now I was free to leave.

Just like that, I finished dealing with the entire setting faster than the speed of a literal thought.

However, the moment I teleported away…

"Leaving so soon?"

…I arrived not at my destination, but rather at a different place. It looked similar to the place I was in just a few hours ago, working on the paperwork regarding the inter-school event.

It was a student council room. I spotted people around the place who were caught by my hypnosis and are currently in a dazed state - the same people that Yuki and the others had encountered earlier, when they went on to deal with the changes on the other settings.

However, seated at the head of the table was the person who wasn't in a daze. Someone who, in response to the hypnosis which I perfected and prepared for a few days, wasn't even affected by the slightest.


Spoiler

"Hello there." she greeted me with a smile. "You and your friends must be the ones who're interfering with us."

I stayed quiet, simply staring at her blankly.

On the outside, it doesn't look like anything was happening.

However, the very moment that she fully acknowledged my existence, I was actually being heavily assaulted mentally and spiritually. I could feel the vast pressure of her skills trying to smash itself through my defenses, trying to obtain whatever secrets that I have in my mind.

But it's not gonna budge. I brought my A-game. It's gonna take much further than that to break me, you know.

Her eyes then turned intrigued. "Oh…?"

Then she glanced her eyes slightly to the side.

—Simultaneously, I brought up an arm to stop a kick right onto my torso. I felt an incredibly powerful attack that would have destroyed an entire building, displacing air and making a thundercrack-like noise when it connected, but all it managed was to make me slide a few feet away from the attacker.

I glanced at them.

They glanced at me.

And there, I was met with a sight that was like looking at a mirror.


Spoiler

The man, who looked like me but wore a stupidly chuuni military coat that I won't get caught dead wearing, furrowed his brows slightly when he stared at me. I can see the confusion in his eyes, probably thinking of something along the lines of 'who the hell is this guy and why is he stealing my look?'

Well, I probably would think the same, honestly.

In any case, he wasn't the only one that seemed surprised about it. The reality warper noted our similarities with a bit of surprise - and then I watched in real time as that surprise turned her initial intrigue into outright curiosity.

"Well, well. Now this is quite interesting." she said, smile growing into a grin. "I wonder who our guest could be?"

…Great. Now I got her attention.

As expected, it looks like the narrative wants entertaining fights, after all.

And now, here's the fight that we're waiting for... Or is it?


Chapter 32

Dear reader, let me tell you a story.

Once upon a time, during the early years of a certain person's forays in the world - there was once a completely ordinary girl living a normal life.

She was someone born without special ability nor was fated to do anything momentous. In fact, she was a normal human through and through. Born in a standard family, having attended school where she has a group of friends to talk to, and along with a hobby which she enjoys: she lived a life that can be described only as 'mundane'.

It was a very standard life with its ups and downs. A blessed life, if described by those in worse circumstances. A boring life, if described by those who lived in a much better position than her.

If she were to be in a story, she would be the side character that barely gets a single scene of screen time. But this sort of thing wasn't entirely unique to her. The truth is, that same story was repeated amongst countless other people - boy, girl, young or old.

But strangely at some point… the girl became aware of this mundanity herself.

A completely uneventful trip with her family in a baseball stadium somehow ended up her realizing just how small people were. To her immature mind, she was able to see that all the people's faces blurred together, as tiny as a grain of rice lost within a sea of everything.

And with that, the girl realized she was simply nothing in the world, and much less in the grand scale of the universe. She was forced to face the fact that her choice meant nothing in the utter vastness in the cosmos, and amidst that large crowd, she would be unnoticeable if she were to disappear.

She wasn't special.

And the young girl couldn't accept that.

Like a child who couldn't accept the idea that they weren't the center of the world and threw a tantrum, the young girl tried to be 'special' as if it would cure the feelings of existential dread. She deviated from the norm, came to hate normal things, and tried to become 'special'.

That effort had led her to be labeled as an oddball. 'Common sense' was something she had thrown away in her endeavors. Yet it also made her excel and she, in a way, became smarter and performed better than the rest of her peers.

But despite the changes she made to herself, she knew that it was simply nothing. Even if she was a step above the average, that didn't make her special at all. There was always someone much better out there in the world. And if she were to chase that route, then there would be no end to it.

And even then, the girl knew her limits. Hard work can only get someone so far. Without the proper talent, opportunities, and various other factors - trying to become someone special that way would be unrealistic.

So, she chose to be logical. Instead of being special by doing something no one has ever done before, what if she discovered it instead? What if she found something that no one had ever seen before, finding the extraordinary out there?

"Still, what beautiful scenery this is… May I ask where you've brought me? I might visit this place again sometime. If this place survives, that is."

Then, he seemingly decided that there was no harm in answering truthfully.

"Avalon."

That made the girl's head tilt curiously. "The mythical island in the Arthurian legends? Fascinating. It seems separated from the world itself along with having strange properties… I notice that there is not a single fairy around here though."

"It's not the whole thing. I stole part of it." he said with a shrug.

"You're making it hard for me to not act interested here, you know." the girl said with a smile. "Can you tell me your true identity already? You're not Basa-kun, that much is clear. And yet… you're very much like him. In the ways that matter."

"I'll tell it to you if you allow yourself to be hypnotized."

"And miss out on the fun? No thanks." the girl said, sticking out a tongue.

"Then we are at an impasse."

"Yes, indeed." she smiled again. "I feel so excited right now. You're quite strong, and the mysteries that you and your companions hold - it fascinates me to no end. So knowing that our goals differ… there should be only one conclusion this will end in, no?"

"…It does seem like it."

Another moment of silence. However, unlike earlier, there was an undercurrent of anticipation under it.

The world of paradise they were in was said to be the safest and most everlasting place in existence, repelling all damage and interference due to housing the soul of the world. And while it may just be a stolen part of it, the same properties should still apply.

Yet faced with what these two beings were about to do… the world of paradise itself had trembled, as if sensing what they're about to do and fearing it.

—Power surged.

The ground quaked, and the air thrummed from an invisible pressure.

"So, mister." Haruhi Ajimu started, releasing an incredible amount of pressure that would have flattened a small country in seconds. "Shall we have a dance for a bit? The audience requires a good preview of what is to come, after all."

Basa stood under that pressure, unbothered.

"Do whatever you want." he answered easily. "Though, I'd just like to ask you to keep meta statements to a minimum. It doesn't sound clever at all when you keep repeating it. Especially when you have no idea what you're even talking about."

That made Haruhi giggle. "Is that so? And that is as opposed to you?" she replied, before shrugging. "I guess I'll trust the expert, then. But as for now… hmm, let's see, what would be a good thing to start things with… Ah, I know!"

The girl's smile widened into a grin.

"—Why don't I try to end this world? That should be a good enough stress test, shouldn't it?"

It was an ominous statement.

On any other occasion, her words would've been taken as a joke. After all - this place belonged to a setting which easily dabbled with the conceptual. But if it was said by this person, a reality warper which the universe listens to… then those words easily become all too real.

To which she quickly proved it true when the girl activated just a single ability out of her twelve quadrillion skills. One that appears to be an homage, or even parody, of another ability in a different setting.

And thus, the Haruhi Ajimu spoke:



"Made in Heaven."
​


—It was then that a fundamental change was made.

The world turned into night. Then, it turned into day, and then night again. Night, day, night, day, night, day; the large flaming ball in the sky began to rise and fall at an accelerated rate as time itself sped up, until its fast movement eventually converged into a single ring in the sky.

Ethereal flowers died, spread themselves, and multiplied. Rocks weathered and broke down, exposing new ones in its wake. Water dried up, caused rain, and eventually seeped back down to the ground.

The everlasting paradise was subjected to infinity.

And in response to it… it somehow held.

Temporarily, at least.

"My, oh my. It seems that this place really is the real deal." the girl said with a curious tone, looking around as time continued to accelerate at ridiculous speeds. "However, in the face of the end of the universe, even something everlasting due to being connected to the planet is nothing. I wonder how long this can last? And more importantly…"

She stared straight at the man in the eyes..

"I wonder how long you can last against me, mister?" she asked, sounding amused. "After all, is there even any way that you can beat someone like me in a fight? I'm not a person who brags, but even Basa-kun wasn't able to beat me, you know?"

The man said nothing, his face not betraying any emotion he felt.

Then, he stepped forward, flexing his fingers to form into a fist—


Spoiler

—Before moving in a burst of speed right to the girl and striking her with enough force to destroy everything behind her and flatten it. It shook the entire world that they were in, testing the boundaries of a place where everything 'cannot be damaged'.

That said, the same girl just easily blocked the incredibly destructive attack with just a hand while wearing a cheery smile. After the dust settled, they were left with the sight of the man's fist pushing against her palm, which remained uninjured despite the fact that it met the attack directly.

But seemingly undeterred by the sight, the man simply used their lessened distance to answer her earlier question.

"You'll just have to see it." Basa stated simply.

In response to that, the reality warper let out a grin.

"Definitely right." she agreed. "Then, I look forward to it. Show me your prowess."

The man didn't reply after that. There was no more need for words, after all.

With that, as the two disappeared as they went on to move faster than the eye could even register, sudden quakes and explosions occurred within the span of seconds followed by countless amounts of projectiles, spells and effects being thrown around.

It was a ruinous fight, one that would've likely drastically altered or even destroyed the planet if it were done not in some isolated parallel dimension, and surpassing the power of many of the shounen action genres out there in terms of destruction.

A fight of epic proportions that exceeded far more than anything before.

—And with that, the meta character finally fought the reality warper.

Chapter 33

How does someone beat the unbeatable?

It's an impossible question to answer.

After all, 'unbeatable' by definition means that you cannot defeat them. To beat an unbeatable person would mean going against the premise of the scenario. And if the premise is challenged, then the question loses its meaning.

Logically, the answer doesn't exist. There's no beating the unbeatable.

And in theory, that should extend to my opponent right now.

Huh? Does that mean it's game over? Am I actually screwed? Should I turn off my phone, close my eyes, and sleep since I have work tomorrow? Well, not really. Reality is weird in a way that logical things like that don't always apply. Yes, even in this fuckass world where fiction is actually reality - it still doesn't work that way.

In theory, concepts and scenarios are reduced so that our feeble minds can comprehend it. But reality is far more complicated. And fiction, being a simpler and more digestible form of reality that is put in a medium, is still not a place where 'things completely work in theory'.

And in this case, it's the simple case of asking this particular question.

What exactly does 'beating someone' mean in this case?

This girl I'm facing is someone that I cannot defeat. Her powers are so stupidly bullshit that it eclipses my own bullshit by several orders of magnitude. I do not know the extent of her powers since I maintain minimal contact with this setting, but I know that she has me beat in raw power and variety.

That said, while I cannot defeat her - I don't really care if I defeat her in battle or not. After all, that's not my goal.

My goal is to deal with the world-affecting scenario. It just so happens that this person is an obstacle to it. If I can manage to achieve my goal without defeating her, then I'd still consider that as a victory.

And in that way, I managed to 'beat' her.

That is how you beat the unbeatable. It's the simple requirement of fulfilling your imposed victory conditions… as long as said conditions aren't outright defeating the unbeatable character, that is. But then again, I say 'imposed' because most of the time the conditions are a matter of perspective.

Victory is achieving goals you set out to do, not removing the obstacles blocking you from it. From that simple understanding, titles such as 'unbeatable' lose their meaning. And from that, the possibilities become endless.

…Although, even considering all that, it's quite tricky to do it with an opponent like this.

—Gargantuan explosions, world-shaking tremors, and other sounds caused by unknown phenomena and the mundane universe' laws being broken. And around us, the everlasting paradise strained itself to remain unaltered in the face of everything accelerating exponentially until the end of time, along with the constant destruction and reformation of the terrain by our incredibly destructive attacks.

Above us, night and day had mixed and turned into dusk. And the fake sun, along with the stars that dotted everything up above, all turned into blurred lines that streaked the sky.

And what's more, like when a Samurai-themed or a Yamato Nadeshiko character appears, the flowers being brought back and destroyed in quick succession caused us to be bathed with an obnoxious amount of ethereal petals like blossoms in the wind.


Spoiler

It was an alien, yet beautiful sight.

That said, I couldn't really appreciate it with my attention focused on the person I was fighting.

"Dead Lock, Life Zero, Standing Ovation, Mirror Juvenile, Five Focus, Door To Door, Give Up-Down, Count Up, Lady Guitarist, Sword Look, Leg Walker, Trick Sword, Dead Or I Love You, Limited Foot, Amateur Armor, Hi-Fi Speed, No Motion, Dynamite Smile, Ad Hoc Attack, Remote Light, Child Control, Life Scars, Head Edge, Ghost Cutter, Sword With Red Ice Cream, Atomic Number—"

I watched closely right in front of me as my opponent began yapping up a storm. In accordance to the standard anime battle protocol, she was saying out loud the names of her skills and abilities. And she truly has a lot of them, which made it look ridiculous since it sounded like she was saying a bunch of nonsense.

However, it would be deadly to underestimate her.

After all, this girl has the power to do virtually everything with the quadrillion skills under her disposal, and has the ability to manipulate reality itself into whatever she wants it to be. Incredibly powerful to the point that one would wonder how this person can even be beaten as an antagonist, or how they can even contribute to the story without making everything else trivial.

That is the person that I was currently fighting.

"—Paradox Engine, Glass Ceiling, Reality Bypass, Terminal Velocity, System Shock, Ghost Protocol, Logic Bomb, Zero Hour, Vector Shift, Absolute Zero, Phase Lock, Structure Collapse, Ego Death, Mirror Breach, Void Step, Chain Reaction, Rule Breaker, False Flag, Event Horizon, Kinetic Drain, Static Pulse, Frame Perfect, Hit Box, Nerve Pinch, Soul Tether—"

"—Karma Return."

An incomprehensible chaos followed.

The light show that I was subjected to wasn't something that would make a Victorian child go into a seizure, but rather straight up burn their corneas and make them blind or possibly go insane. If it weren't for the hundreds of parallel thought processes I have right now, along with a hundred other spells running in the background that improves my reaction times and foresight - I wouldn't have been able to make sense of it.

A variety of skills and abilities from spatial, temporal, elemental, kinetic, mental, and conceptual attacks. All with complicated interactions, which would likely boost its destructiveness even further.

—And I managed to avoid it all.

I ducked, weaved, and teleported around. As I dodged the hits - literal stars, voids and incomprehensible projectiles made of bullshit powers appeared all around me, along with various cuts stretching beyond kilometers carved itself on the realm. The more conceptual attacks simply splashed on the barrier that I surrounded myself with, before dissipating once I no longer needed it.

All of that done by Movement skills, Causality-nullifying spells, and then Physical, Mental and Conceptual barriers. It's not quite as many abilities utilized in comparison to whatever that girl just did, but it got the job done.

After all, while a complicated amount of abilities sounds intimidating and powerful - simple always worked best.

In any case, after doing all that in a matter of milliseconds and crossing the distance between us - I summoned my spirit weapon, twirled it open and went on to stab the girl. The butterfly knife's blade sliced through the air as it seeked the girl's heart, but before it could manage to even make contact with her clothes, something intercepted it.

A folding paper fan. The girl brought it out of her pocket and caught the blades between it.

I stared at her and the girl smiled.

…How graceful.

"Nice moves." she said cheerily. "I don't recognize any of the things you just did, but I recognize that they're actual power systems with history behind them. Where did you learn it?"

I pulled back my knife and she brought up an arm. Then, instead of dodging the arm that she extended - I slashed my knife to the left, imbuing it with various cutting spells, abilities and skills which amped up the range and damage significantly.

It resulted with the entire mountain range that was on my left being obliterated into pieces from a hundred thousand cuts. The girl in front of me faded away, and the real one appeared on my left a slight distance away with a cracked bubble around her.

I glanced at her direction.

"Learned it in Lala land." I answered her question.

"Pfft." The girl looked amused. "Is that so? I know pretty much all the places in the world, but I'm pretty positive that place doesn't exist… Unless you're saying that you're not from this world?"

As she said that, the girl didn't let up one bit and shot me a bunch of unstable energy projectiles. I batted them away, and they exploded far away to the horizon behind me, each one having the strength comparable to a hundred megaton warhead explosion.

"Not really. Maybe you just missed them." I replied, ignoring the heat behind me. "They're pretty hidden, after all."

A sharp laugh came out of her. "Haha. If any other person said that, I'd just laugh them off." she chuckled. "I have eyes everywhere, you know? I thought that I knew everything about this world already… and yet here you are, standing as a direct opposition to that. You're really a mystery."

Then, she tilted her head.

"I'm supposed to be the antagonist in our story, so I wonder what exactly your role here is? A side character to measure up against my power? Or a Deus Ex Machina, perhaps? I am pretty strong, after all. I even sometimes question how the main character could even beat me…"

I stayed silent, and she pouted.

"Not even a hint?" she sighed. "Whatever. I'll eventually find the answer myself."

Then the girl snapped her fingers.

—And the next moment, the sky lit up as stars suddenly appeared up high. Or to be more specific, it was due to the appearance of millions of projectiles that were similar to the ones that I batted away earlier, each one carrying the power to level a large city.

She grinned. "Try not to die, alright?"

And with that, the projectiles all fell towards me like a world-ending meteor shower. And looking up, I simply stared at it blankly, my incredibly boosted perception allowing me to watch the whole thing in very slow motion.

What a pain, this girl. Is she just trying to wreck the place?

The vast majority of them weren't even aimed at me.

I brought up an arm and pointed a finger towards it, before shooting a simple curse spell. That thing was enough to prematurely destroy one of the projectiles which caused a chain reaction of it detonating those around it, and this realm we were in became brighter in that single moment.

Not all of it exploded, but those that were aimed at my general direction did. That said, it was all just something that was meant to distract me, it seems.

Since the very next moment I did that - the reality warper in front of me and started to fight me in close combat.

I dodged, blocked and countered a countless amount of strikes from the girl as she suddenly displayed the greatest display of martial skill I have ever encountered. In a span of a single second, I was subjected to feints, techniques and various other martial arts bullshit that almost overwhelmed me with the strength and sheer amount of strikes she let out.

Keyword being almost, however. I matched it to the best of my ability… but even then it was only barely. She moved faster than I could and caught me in hits that I didn't expect, due to a significant difference in our martial skill.

It was something that I hadn't experienced in a very long time, being so outmatched like this.

"You can keep up with me, but it's clear that you have your limits." the reality warper observed with her usual smile, her breath and words steady despite our intense close combat. "Let's see… These aren't skills like the ones in our school. I think these are real martial art styles?"

I furrowed my brows before delivering a counter to her recent kick that obliterated the land behind me. The girl brought up her forearm to block the hit, but I activated a phasing ability in a split second which made me go through her. The reinforced strike connected to her face, making her pause for a bit.

"…Various fatal spells targeting to stun and destroy the internal organs, as well as to exponentially amplify strength. Is there a hint of sunlight there as well?" she muttered in thought. "Hmm, the thaumaturgical foundation is like a normal magus', but it's also muddled with things I do not know."

The girl then started to fight me in close combat again, this time in a much more intense manner and seemingly adapted to the styles I was using earlier. I frowned, and then prepared something at the back of my head.

"But considering everything… your abilities aren't the same innate skills that we have. You learned them the hard way. That's very impressive." She deduced, before looking curious. "Which means that whatever you are, you're beyond our setting—"

I caught her in a grab, and suddenly a portal opened underneath us which sucked us inside. The girl blinked as we suddenly found ourselves absurdly high above Avalon, right where space is. Or at least, a very good facsimile of it.

"—…"

Absolute silence surrounded us as sound was unable to travel. Her yapping finally stopped, and the flyswatting-like vibe that she was setting herself up for was terminated for a moment.

And simultaneously, the various amounts of prepared spells and tech that I set up while she was distracted by me finally activated. I teleported away as something resembling a singularity suddenly appeared in her spot, before readying my spirit weapon.

She clearly got caught by the attack, but I already know what's coming next. I quickly struck behind me, stabbing the reality warper that suddenly appeared out of nowhere. It was a direct hit to her chest.

—But above me, an identical girl struck me with a spinning axe kick. I grit my teeth as she managed to hit me directly, passing through the protections I weaved on myself and sending my flying down while breaking the sound barrier.

The reality warper suddenly teleported herself right to my face a moment after. She smiled.

"You're aware of how the world runs like a story too. You just tried to silence my monologue just now, didn't you?" she continued her deduction as we finally entered the realm's atmosphere. "You grasp its logic far better than the others in our school. Enough to manipulate it more delicately. And as far as I know, that's only limited to me and Basa-kun."

I didn't reply.

Instead, I stabbed my arm with my knife, activating a ritual curse that connected to the girl and the rest of her clones present. The girl blinked once more when a wound appeared in her arm, before she turned wide-eyed as her teeth started falling off and everything in her mouth started to rot. She grasped her jaw, before her eyes turned back to me.

I met it. I stared at her straight with a hand closed over my own mouth, utilizing the blood I spilled to unleash a biblical-level pestilence on myself. I ignored the intense pain of my entire body rotting from my mouth to my insides, watching her as she also felt the same pain as I did across all her bodies.

It was a horrifying thing to watch, having an impact that was more visceral and disturbing in comparison to the awesome displays of power we had unleashed earlier. It was also whiplash-inducing, since a sense of realism suddenly appeared in what looked like a typical destructive shounen fight.

—Then, the world cracked, and everything wasn't like that anymore.

Somehow I found myself falling again, completely whole. There was no trace of my self-inflicted attack as if the very existence of it happening was erased, and the girl in front of me was also undamaged because of it.

Said girl was also staring at me with puzzlement, as if she wondered why I just did that.

"…You are acting differently to us, however." she muttered, continuing her earlier talk. "You conduct yourself under a different set of logic. Is it because you're not at our level of understanding in the world? No, that can't be it. You were following what I was talking about. And there's also the stunts you did earlier."

She then frowned, her brows furrowing as she considered the implications of such.

"Or is it us who are not at your level…?" she muttered.

Again, I was silent.

With my attempt to make a seinen-like atmosphere failing thus preventing me from sneaking in an attack - I finally opted for a brute force strike which I saved to deal with this reality warper.

In an instant I gathered spiritual energy on my foot and distanced myself away from the reality warper using the air as footing. And as I did that, I formed hundreds of clones which I controlled with parallel thought processes, surrounding the girl before she could react.

Each one did separate spells, techniques to even artifacts and techs. It was much like the trap earlier, utilizing her unfamiliarity with the many settings that she hadn't encountered - except this time in a much greater variety since I pretty much used all the every single thing tucked into my brain and subspace.

I bound her so she can't move. I turned space inward in case she tried tricks like portaling out or teleporting. I stopped every single supernatural phenomenon around her. I erased the concept, result, and possibility of her ever leaving that place. And I set this event in the timeline, making it something that would undoubtedly occur, stopping causality bullshit from interfering.

There was no escaping this attack. Only one thing would result from this - and it's the reality warper getting hurt.

—Then, I struck.

Another incomprehensible light show, similar to the one that I subjected the reality warper earlier into. I kept an eye on my surroundings this time to prevent anything like before from happening again, but as far as I know, the reality warper hadn't been able to move a single inch.

And so, I watched as the light show settled… and there, floating in the middle of it was the reality warper. Her uniform was ruffled and scorched, and for the very first time it truly looked like I finally reached her with that attack.

The girl blinked.

"Huh." she muttered, looking at herself. "You actually made me bleed. That hasn't happened for a long time."

Then, she looked up at me.

"…You're not going to repeat that again though." she declared.

What followed was a blur. Literally.

Somehow, all my clones were instantly vaporized as the girl moved. I managed to bring up my defenses by dilating time the greatest that I could to the point that time itself had stopped, but even then I was barely able to react to the girl moving in to engage in close combat again. I dodged the fist headed to my face by tilting my face to the side, barely avoiding my head from being atomized.

Somehow she managed to break through the restraints that I put on her. How did she do it? Conceptual manipulation? No, it's likely that she just overpowered it, somehow. Likely with some ability which she pulled out of her ass.

"You really are like Basa-kun in the ways that matter." she stated, somehow managing to speak normally despite incredibly dilated time. "He was the only one that accomplished that after I got this strong. He wasn't as creative as you are though - but then again, you're not using innate skills like we are."

Having no choice after using everything I could on that attack, I went on to simply brawl with the girl once more.

It was a fight that I was clearly losing. Blood seeped out of my wounds as the girl slowly tore me apart bit by bit each strike, having managed to outbullshit my own bullshit martial arts. An impressive bullshit feat only reserved by bullshit characters like her.

"Is that the reason why you look like him? Are you perhaps a clone of Basa-kun?" the girl continued to speak idly, trying to divine my identity. "It's a plausible development. If someone wants to defeat me, then they're greatest chance of doing that is either to somehow clone me or him."

The reality warper then shook her head, letting out an exasperated sigh.

"Unfortunately, I can only be defeated by the main character so there's no way for me to get defeated. All the efforts of you and the people who made you are wasted. Although, I do wonder what method you used to somehow clone Basa-kun…"

The girl suddenly trailed off.

Despite the violence I was being subjected to, I just stared at her, not saying a thing.

"…What's with that look in your eye?" she asked with a strange tone.

For the most part, I haven't been replying to her constant yapping. I didn't see the point of talking after all, and admittedly, this girl was powerful enough that I couldn't afford being distracted by having a conversation with her.

That said, I had been listening to the words that had been coming out of her mouth. So while I couldn't really speak out what I thought and didn't particularly feel like doing it, it must have still shown itself through my expression. And for a reality warper like her who surely had an ability about reading faces or something - it was enough for her to determine what I was feeling transparently.

And seeing myself right now…

"Why are you looking at me in pity?"

Somehow, despite the fact that she was winning our battle - a clear expression of frustration appeared on the girl's face. Out of all the attacks which I sent to her, this was seemingly the one that had affected her the most. The expression was wiped away a moment later however, replaced entirely with a frown.

"I don't like it. You staring at me like that with that face." the girl muttered, before letting out a sigh. "…I can't figure you out at all. Why do you fight? What is the point of all this? To what end is your entire character even meant to serve?"

Then, she furrowed her brows.

"And why do I feel this familiarity around you…? It's just so odd…"

"…"

Once again, I didn't answer.

Throughout our fight, I could see the way her mind raced as she tried to make sense of everything. A reality warper like her who carries so many abilities definitely carries an intellect that is way beyond the normal genius. A twelfth level of intellect, able to understand many phenomena in the universe as if they were solving simple addition.

Narratives usually don't show such a thing in actuality. Rather, stories display it by somehow being able to conclude the right things from limited evidence, along with being able to manipulate events by slapping a 'just as planned' after the story headed to whatever it wanted to be in. Then it would just be a matter of not breaking the suspension of disbelief after that.

Which was why this girl can definitely figure out the truth of what was happening, despite the fact that I hadn't spoken much or the fact that she wasn't meta like I am. And the truth is, she was already approaching it. She already deduced things about me earlier, and it would only be a matter of time she'll be able to determine who I am as well.

And yet, as I watched her try to do just that… the girl looked like she stopped herself from continuing her thoughts. She closed her eyes, and like a person turning a blind eye from a terrible truth - she chose to remain ignorant.

"…I suppose it doesn't really matter." she stated, tone blank for a moment, before turning her attention to me. "Say, you're barely even trying to fight me anymore. You're just getting beat up. What happened to the tricks you kept showing earlier? Did you give up?"

I was barely holding on now, fatally wounded from our constant exchange that I could barely keep up on. It was only through the constant healing and regeneration spells, artifacts and tech that I was using made me hold on. But it was still clear that I was being defeated.

And yet, I just stared at her.

And seeing that made the girl turn frustrated once more.

"…I'm growing tired of this."

With those words, the girl teleported away. I looked around before spotting her a bit far away. Around us, the still-occuring nuclear explosions from her earlier meteor shower attack traveled in slow motion from my time dilation. But almost in conflict with that, the realm was still in constant time acceleration from whatever this girl just did earlier, giving a truly alien scenery.

And right in the focus of it was the reality warper.

"I was hoping that you would show me more interesting things, but if this is how it will be, then there's no point in sandbagging anymore." the reality warper declared. "I'll defeat you, and then claim whatever secrets you're keeping in that pretty little head of yours."

Then, she extended her hand.

By this point, Avalon's fabric was tearing apart. It may be boasted as the ever-distant utopia which remains eternal no matter what, but even the thaumaturgical phenomenon caused by the world even has its limits. And in the face of everything that we've thrown to each other, it was vastly approaching said limit.

—But whatever this girl was doing pretty much broke beyond that.


Spoiler

I don't think I can even describe what I was looking at. In fact, staring at it instantly made my eyes blind. I healed it an instant later and applied my strongest barriers to myself, but even then I knew that whatever the reality warper was about to throw at me - my meager defenses definitely wouldn't be enough.

I'm not going to survive an attack like this. Not a single thing in my repertoire could even deal with it. Hell, I don't even understand what the hell I'm looking at in the first place.

So this is what it means to face a bullshit character, huh…? Seems like I was finally tasting my own medicine.

Nevertheless, through that incomprehensible chaos, I somehow heard the girl's voice.

"You're probably going to die, but it's fine. I can just bring you back. I'll kill you again and again and again - until you finally spill all your secrets." she declared, her threat of violence said with such casualness as if she was talking about the weather. "Unless you want to speed things up and just give up now?"

There was no point in answering such an obvious question.

I brought up my knife and pointed it at the girl.

"Very well." the girl simply stated.

"Then, I hope you don't regret this."

And with those words, the girl unleashed her attack. Avalon, the everlasting paradise, finally broke - and I was enveloped by the absurd nonsense that the reality warper made. I felt the absolute defenses I had developed my entire life get destroyed in an instant, and I got swallowed whole.

In the face of something that can shape the universe as they wished - I was simply nothing.


…And with that I, Basa-kun, had finally died.


























—Or not, actually.

I stood right in front of the student council room in Hakoniwa Academy, very much alive, inside a bubble which can be essentially described as the greatest gaslighting device in existence. A perfected mix of magic and tech from various disciplines, essentially combined to make the perfect dreaming device that was indistinguishable to reality.

And right in the middle of it was the reality warper, just standing there this whole time.

At some point when we were talking, I ensnared the girl and made her think that she was fighting me and put her in a hypnotic state. That's right, all of the things that just happened… It was nothing but a dream.

It's the shittiest conclusion to many stories. But for this case, it was an absolutely necessary move to make.

Why? Because I'm actually not stupid enough to fight someone that can destroy the universe. At no point could I possibly defeat this person in these conditions, no matter how many tricks I pull. So the best that I can do is to distract her and make her waste time while I fulfill my own objectives.
