The street was rife with people, all of which had stopped in their tracks to stare at the scene. Some looked at it wide-eyed, searing the sight straight in their minds. While others looked away, unable to stomach it. And as for a strange or just a confused few, they had taken out their phones to take pictures or record it.

All are uniquely human ways to respond to tragedy. However, out of all of these people around - a single girl stared at the accident not with shock or horror, but rather something different.

Sadness, disappointment.

Along with a heavy and familiar weight of melancholy.

It wasn't the right feeling in such a situation. However, that was what the girl truly felt right now.

She stared at the bloody scenery right in front of her. The image of the person she had met long ago was slowly leaving her mind as the narrative itself worked to remove it. The sense of incongruence in her memories increased, and no matter what she did with her mind-boggingly many skills, she couldn't do anything to stop it.

It was over. Her opponent lay dying in front of her.

And yet, she felt like she was the one who lost.

The girl stood there for a long while… until at some point she was joined by someone else. A person with the same face with the one she had fought just now, but oh so different.

The man stood right beside her as always. She knew that his mind also suffered the same thing as she did - in just a few seconds, they'd find their memories wiped of this encounter, and they'd likely be back in the Hakoniwa Academy doing whatever they were going to do after their 'arc'.

There was no point in staying. And yet, they remained. Choosing to use these scant few seconds to simply stare at the person who had changed their life so much, yet knew so little of.

And finally, the silence broke.

"How unfair." Haruhi muttered. "I just wanted to see what else the world can offer. Is that so bad?"

For a moment, Basa-kun said nothing.

"Perhaps." he then stated. "You were getting too addicted to our adventures for your own good. The others were worried, especially when you wanted that plan of yours enacted."

The girl considered his words for a moment after hearing that.

"…Maybe I am." the girl replied, before turning to the man beside her with an amused smile. "Is that why you didn't take your fight seriously, along with hypnotizing yourself and the others? Just to teach a lesson for little 'ol me?"

A simple nod was her answer. "Someone has to take care of your spoiled ass, after all."

The girl chuckled at that. "I see."

Seconds ticked by, and she could feel the majority of her memories disappear and become replaced by unfamiliar ones. As another bout of silence between them fell once more, the girl found herself asking a question in a strangely vulnerable tone.

"Hey." Haruhi muttered. "What do you think will happen after this? With our roles in the story finished… What are we going to do? Will our adventures finally be over?"

Another pause.

"…Who knows. Maybe we'll find ourselves in a new story, with new roles and such. Or maybe we'll get none of that at all, and just become side characters to the current one. I'm not as versed on the mechanics as the other guy."

The man answered her question with that, tone neutral. As expected, his answer wasn't as reassuring in the slightest, choosing a much more honest approach than lying about the situation.

But his next words changed that outlook entirely.

"—Although, that doesn't really matter, does it?" he muttered, looking at the direction of Hakoniwa Academy. "As long as we're with the others… adventure or not, I'm happy with it."

Haruhi paused, remembering her opponent's words earlier.

…Then, she smiled softly.

"You're right." she agreed. "That's the only thing that really matters, it seems."

Silence had fallen between them once more. Yet unlike earlier, the heavy sense of melancholy had disappeared, replaced with something more of comforting acceptance.

As that happened, the girl went on to close her eyes and rest her head on the man's arm, simply enjoying his presence beside her and resigning herself on what was to come.

And finally… the clock struck twelve.

The moment their memories were replaced, the two disappeared from where they stood as if they were ghosts. Where they went was unknown, and who knew what the narrative had in store for them.

But despite it all, there was one thing that was for sure - the entire world-affecting scenario was finally over. Things went back into stability once more, and no one knew how it came close for everyone involved. Aside from a select few, that is.

With that, the curtain finally came into a close.

And the world kept turning as it always did.


































—Sometime after that.

"…Everything seems to be in order."

Yuki muttered those words as she stood up, removing her hand on the delinquent girl's head that was sprawled unconscious in front of her. She appeared as a textbook sukeban member, complete with a modified uniform and a face mask.

Except, the girl had a real katana with her. She was also skilled with it, judging from the memories she just scanned in her mind. The standard action anime, except with a delinquent setting.

And in those same memories, Yuki determined that the large-scale gang war that happened around the place seems to be wrapping up already. The girl quickly brought out her phone to tell everyone about the state of this particular genre.

…They've finally finished it.

Every single concern and loose end for the whole world-affecting scenario had been dealt with.

After that stressful battle with Basa-kun's expy, they monitored and checked everything that needed fixing right after, knowing that their job still might not be done. Everything that was involved in the world-affecting scenario had experienced their story climax in the form of various large scale fights, either in terms of destruction or just the amount of people involved.

Thankfully aside from the few adjustments they did right now, there wasn't much to take care of. Their initial changes helped a lot it seems, stopping a potential cascade from ever happening.

That said, there's still the concern of Basa-kun facing that reality warper alone…

"I hope he's doing okay, at least." she muttered, worriedly.

Even now, she struggles to think how he could even beat someone like her. The only reason they were able to 'defeat' Basa-kun's expy was because he wasn't trying to fight them seriously in the first place. She doubted that it would be the same for the reality warper he was facing.

However, Basa-kun mentioned that he had a plan to deal with it, even if she didn't really know the details. So she was forced to wait, hoping that the man would be fine even while facing someone like that.

"…Stupid Basa-kun."

Yuki grumbled those words, feeling an uncharacteristic frustration bubbling in her chest. Can't he at least try telling them what he plans to do? She understood that it's to prevent his plans from reaching the reality warper in case of mind reading, but surely they could at least have a hint that things would be fine…

She sighed. No, she was being unreasonable.

"I should probably return back to school now." Yuki mumbled to herself.

She opened a portal in front of her and stepped in, arriving directly right into a vacant and tucked away storage room within her school. The lights were turned off, and since the sun had finally set - the only source of illumination was the faint glow of moonlight.

However, Yuki wasn't alone in this dark storage room. Someone was waiting for her.

Her copy smiled as she arrived. "Good evening. I trust that everything has been taken care of?"

Yuki nodded. "Yes, things went… relatively smoothly." she answered, before giving her copy a curious look. "I hope that everything went the same on your end."

For some reason, her copy reddened a bit at that. Yuki blinked, wondering what caused her such a reaction, but instead of saying anything else her copy gave her a smile as she approached.

"I enjoyed the day quite a lot. But you should find out what happened yourself."

With a nod, Yuki then extended her hand and put her palm on her copy's forehead. She closed her eyes, and the copy slowly turned into wisps as she slowly got absorbed into her being. As that happened, the memories of what happened the entire day appeared before her.

Enjoying the interschool event with her club.

Having an exciting adventure with Rias and the others.

Finally getting her first kiss with Basa-kun—

…

Wait, w-w-what…?

Yuki instantly blushed as she recalled what happened, the memories of the past day fresh on her mind from what her soul copy had just shared. She envisioned the specific scene which was, coincidentally, the exact same place she was in right now.

And from there, she recalled in her mind's eye—

It was a sudden thing.

It was after the sports event, following a lively basketball match between Sobu and Kuoh Academy's teams. One that proved entertaining due to a strange set of circumstances that led to some of Sobu's players being unable to play, and forcing the club to look for other players.

And out of all of them, the people who were chosen were Haya-kun, Makato-kun and… Basa-kun. It was a very exciting watch, mostly due to how funny it was for her to see Basa-kun struggling to act normal in the basketball match. And more than that - there were also interesting developments, such as when the two boys in Rias' club ended up joining Kuoh's team as well.

It was fun. But after that, there was a brief period of rest. And at that point, Basa-kun asked her to come with him and they arrived in this very room.

There, he spoke to her.

"I have a feeling that you might be pissed considering you don't know the details of how I'd deal with the reality warper, so I'm going to tell you right now what I'm planning to do."

As the man launched into an explanation - her soul copy blinked, not having any idea of what he was saying. However, for the current her, she had understood the idea. Hypnotize every single person in the setting, make the narrative alter the reality warper's memories, and then escape into a different genre that the reality warper cannot access.

It was a clean plan. She understood the logic. And he even told her all the things that he'd be doing to return to them. Learning all about it was fascinating for her.

However, to her soul copy that had no idea of what was going on - she locked into a particular detail that, in her current state of mind, felt that she was most concerned for.

"Y-You'll be gone for a while…? Why?"

"Because while I could easily go Isekai myself from here, it's a completely different thing to find a method to return to Earth from there. It's going to be much harder to find." he answered her. "I'm sorry to bring it up to you now, but it's the only way for me to escape her."

"T-That's…" she felt confusion, but determination also welled up from within her. "Then let's make use of the time we have now before you'll be gone. Let's go ahead and—"

"That… might not be possible either. The reality warper just broke out of containment. I can't escape her by teleportation, and she's finding out where my other clones are." Basa told her, tone clipped while looking somewhere only he can see. "…I might need to dispel all instances of my clones right now. Sorry."

Yuki felt herself slump in place.

"But… the event, it's still not yet done." she mumbled. "It's just a shame, there's still many things that we can do…"

"I know. But I'll only be gone for a few days." Basa-kun consoled her. "Plus, this isn't the only interschool event, you know? We'll be doing this again but in Rias' school. I'll make it up with you guys during that time, alright?"

"…"

Basa-kun scratched his head after seeing her expression.

"What's with the long face? Is it really that big of a deal…?"

Perhaps it was because her soul copy was just meant to emulate her mundane self. However, Yuki did feel really genuinely sad about the situation that she couldn't understand. It was genuine enough that after muttering those words, for a short moment, Basa-kun turned silent.

And then he let out a resigned sigh.

"…Hey, Yuki. Look at me." he suddenly told her.

Confused, she looked up at him.

Then, Yuki's eyes widened as she felt her chin being guided by Basa-kun's hand, along with the sight of him leaning down towards her. She felt her heart skip when she felt his lips touch his - and for a short and sweet moment, one that almost seemed to last forever in her perspective, they remained just like that.

Basa-kun had given her a kiss.


Spoiler

It was chaste.

Almost childishly pure, even. At least in comparison to what he usually gave to Rias or Aoki-san.

And yet… being on the receiving end of such a thing… It was different.

Then, that short magical moment ended, and Yuki was with an incredibly bright blush on her face. Her heart raced, and she was breathless. And for the life of her, she couldn't find the strength to speak or even form a coherent thought right after.

Yuki watched, wide-eyed, as Basa-kun leaned away from her. Then in a manner that he always seemed to do whenever he expresses affection… he turned his eyes to the side, unable to meet her eyes.

And on his cheeks, a slight dust of red could be seen.

"There. Something you can look forward to next time, so cheer up." he muttered, before turning around and walking away. "…Anyway, I'll get rid of my clones now. I'll leave everything to you guys."

The next moment after that, he disappeared out of nowhere.

Yuki wasn't able to say anything, simply staring at the place he was gone, putting a hand on her lips in shock—

—Yuki opened her eyes, before bringing down her hand from her lips when she realized that she unconsciously did the same motion. And similar to that memory - her blush was intense, her heart beats almost a hundred times a minute, and she was breathless.

T-This is… He… T-They…!

Her mind was thrown for a loop.

But before she could digest everything that happened - she found herself almost jumping in shock when the storage room's door opened with a 'bang!', revealing a familiar person on the other side.

"—Yuki-chan! You're here! I just got done with my own thing as well, there's no problems!" Rias beamed. "I can't wait to go and see what we've done today! We probably had so much fun!"

Then, she paused and looked around.

"…By the way, is Basa-kun around? I tried to find him but I didn't see him in the school. Did he already disappear from wherever he'd go like he said he would?"

"Yes. Yes, he did."

Rias blinked at her answer, and then the redhead seemingly took another and more closer look at her.

"Yuki-chan? What's wrong?"

"N-Nothing." Yuki stuttered, before clearing her throat. "I just found out where Basa-kun had gone, that's all."

"R-Really!? You did!?" Rias cried out, eyes brightening. "Then let's go pick him up! Where is he!?"

"That might be a bit tricky, Rias. After all, that man… he decided to isekai himself to escape. Somehow."

Rias stiffened. "E-Eh? Isekai?" she asked. "…You mean he can just decide to do that?"

"Apparently. And he also explained that the reason why he won't be back for a few days is because it might take a while for him to return home." Yuki paused. "And considering how isekai stories rarely have a person returning back to the modern world, I suppose it's already impressive."

"What the heck!? So the reason why he's gone is because he went on an isekai adventure!?" Rias shouted indignantly. "I thought that he'd be hurt! And that he'd need to recover in a bio-tank or something!"

Yuki sweatdropped. "What is he, a yasai-jin?"

"That guy… seriously, give me back my worry! Or better yet, bring me with you!" Rias continued to grump, before a glint appeared in her eyes. "…You know what? I hope that nothing bad happens to him. I mean there's no way that he could get hurt, is there? He'll probably be—Gweh!"

Yuki sighed, bringing down her hand after chopping Rias' head. "Don't do that. You might delay things by doing that, you know. And in the end it's only you who's losing. Because we're going to do our work without him."

"Mrrmm…! Fine." Rias rubbed the place she hit her, before glancing at her with an unreadable. "…By the way, did you and Basa-kun have sex here or something?"

"W-Wha—!?" Yuki subconsciously raised her hand towards her mouth before stopping midway. "W-We didn't! Where did that even come from!?" she shouted, feeling the heat rush into her face.

"I have a sixth sense for this. I am a demon, after all."

"—What is that supposed to mean!?"

Rias ignored her reasonable question and pointed a finger at her. "I will eventually know what you're keeping from me! Something definitely happened in this storage room based on your reaction, and I will uncover it!"

Yuki's face twitched, before she let out a sigh.

A few days without Basa-kun… This was definitely going to be a stressful thing. They have very big shoes to fill, and if it wasn't for the confidence boost that they had in dealing with his own expy, then Yuki might not have thought that they were ready for this.

Hopefully the flag Rias had raised wouldn't really— Oh, who was she kidding, it probably already went into effect.

"Best of luck to you, Basa-kun…" Yuki muttered under her breath. "You'll probably need it."

Then, a moment later, she found her face heating up a bit as she quietly confessed something. One that was a reply to what he had last stated to her before disappearing entirely.

Yuki smiled, softly.

"…I look forward to continuing things once you get back."





…

…

I, Basa-kun, am in a bit of a pickle.

I have managed to escape Haruhi after a great amount of effort and in the process had dealt with that tricky world-affecting scenario. In theory, things are supposed to be easier after that. But you know how it is with theories and realities.

They mix as well as migraines and brain cancer. Which is to say, not pretty good. Still part of the same system though, with one being a small part of the other.

Anyway, poor simile aside, the moment I managed to escape Haruhi I did some stuff that involved some trickery that might have angered some gods and made myself whole once again. It was as if I hadn't died, and what's more, I went through the gate without being asked for some grand quest or something.

And now, I'm here.

—The Reverse Side of the World.

It is a place that is known to many settings that have magi or spellcasters in them. In academic circles, it is generally agreed upon that it was the place that phantasmal species and the gods retreated to after humanity dominated the Earth.

The reason for it is due to various circumstances, such as the being unable to compete with major religions or the human world not being a sufficiently magical place to live anymore. Science has grown, and the laws of physics have become a major discipline which weakened magic's influence as a whole. And in general, the human world's capacity for magic as humanity transitioned into the modern era.

The place is also a bit different from other realms within the world's texture. It's different from afterlives like heaven or hell, since it's still actually Earth in a sense. It can be more accurately described as a parallel world which mimics humanity when it was still young - when there was no technology and people relied on swords, bows, and armor, and when the belief of magic for everything unexplained was at its peak.

Or in other words, it's literally the generic fantasy setting.

And I had isekai'd myself into one.

Let it be known that Isekais are a pain. If one were to ignore the fact that it's pure slop in anime form, the amount of bullshit that is headed my way now that I'm in one is definitely something that I don't want to deal with.

So, after arriving in the world itself, I went ahead and tried to stay low profile while finding a way back home as quickly as possible. But even then, that didn't seem to work.

Because, as I said, isekais are a pain to deal with.

—Green eyes stared at me.

—I stared back, face blank.

—Elven ears flicked.


Spoiler

"…You're quite interesting." the elf said those words blankly, after approaching me specifically out of every single person in this tavern. "You don't have a single trace of mana around you. Are you hiding it?"

I kept staring at her.

The elf didn't take the hint. "…Do you mind teaching it to me? I'll give you a cool ancient artifact I found."

There was a very short moment that I considered that question.

And it took an even shorter moment to vocalize my answer.

"No."

With that, I looked away and began to eat the food that I ordered, ignoring the pair of eyes that bored intensely at my side as I went on to take my first taste of the local fantasy cuisine. I might as well enjoy it at least, since I know that the peace is not going to last anytime soon.

And what do you know? As it turns out, I was completely right.

Because the next thing I knew I was forced by this elf to join me in their journey.

—Anyway, that was how I met my temporary fantasy party.


The extended focus on other characters seems to have caused some frustration. I guess it's my fault for not making it interesting enough. But at least this arc is finally over, and we'll move onto the next one instead.

Before we focus on how Basa meets Frieren, first we see how he actually got there first.


Chapter 34

—Let's roll things back a bit.

Immediately after my soul left my body after I got run over by the Almighty and Iconic Truck-kun, I became conscious.

Perceiving things as a soul was strange. No longer being bound to a physical realm, there was nothing to see, hear or feel. It's like a blind and deaf person who was paralyzed and completely numb to everything - a quadruple handicap that would likely turn people insane.

Because of that, people normally don't 'wake up' while in this form. If they do, they'd probably immediately dissipate, unable to cope with what was happening.

Unless, of course, you're proficient with soul magic like yours truly.

In some settings, the soul is what is used to perceive spiritual/soul energy that fuel most of their attacks and techniques, and in this case I can use it to find out what was happening around me. Due to it, I was able to 'see' things as a soul in a way normal people can't.

And right now, I can tell that I was in the boundary between the Modern World and the Reverse Side of the World.

The Great Veil, or as others would call it - the Textures of the World.

The best way I could describe this place is a film separating mediums. A non-permeable film made of dense ether which nothing can normally go through, except for certain situations where something that could dissolve in it (i.e. souls) can adsorb, diffuse itself through the film, and desorb on the other side.

And right now, we're in the diffusing stage. Normally, souls lose form over time and return to the Root due to inherent conservation laws present in many magic systems, but it doesn't seem to be the case here. It wasn't outright Third Magic where our souls were unable to lose form, but rather the ether surrounding us fueling our existence.

That said, this stage usually takes a long time. In many cases, the soul can actually get trapped in here. Without something to guide it from the other side, it will continue to simply be guided by the waves of dense ether aimlessly, never leaving the barrier separating the two worlds.

And that's where summoning magic comes in. Rather than pierce through the veil which would take astronomical amounts of magical energy, it's more of a guiding current that would make the soul arrive to the other side. Then, once the soul pops out, they'll be given a physical body based on the information recorded in the soul itself and, boom, you got through.

On the modern side of the world, it's one of the many ways to summon a strong creature from the Age of the Gods as a familiar. On the reverse side, it's essentially how the isekai-through-magic thing works.

And right now, I'm riding on a 'current' that was supposed to be targeting another soul. It was the soul of the blonde white knight that died with me. If I let things be, then I'd probably show up in the same summoning circle he was in after being summoned by some random royal family or whatever.

Honestly, I'd rather not let that happen.

—Which is why moments after I woke up, I didn't waste any time and 'propelled' myself out of the current and into the untamed sea of ether. There I was subjected to the turbulent and uncontrolled flows, heading to no direction in particular, for a moment, before heading towards any other current that I can sense.

As I've said before, this place is the texture of the world. I've described it as a film but the truth is that it's far more complicated than that - It's more of a realm on its own, one that's acting as a barrier between many realms. Many, because while it also mainly separates the Modern World and the Reverse Side of the World, it also holds pockets in it that would count as separate realms instead.

As for those separate realms… think of Kur, the Underworld, Valhalla, Hell, Heaven, and all that stuff. In other words - it holds many of the afterlifes found in many of the pantheons. As well as some other realms used in various mythologies as well.

Each of those has their own current guiding them. If a soul passes, then their faith would guide them to their destination. And if I manage to get to any of those realms, then I could probably find a way back to the modern world if that was the case.

Unfortunately, it would take some luck to do that. But it's a chance I'm willing to risk to save myself from the effort of finding a way back home from the Reverse Side of the World.

And what do you know? I just found a different current headed towards another place. I quickly joined the other souls in it and went along with the ride.

My soul traveled across the vast sea of ether, until finally, I found myself arriving into a new realm and—

"Tanaka Takashi-san, welcome to the afterlife." A woman's peaceful voice greeted me. "Unfortunately, you've died. It might have been short, but your life's now… Eh?"

I opened my eyes.


Spoiler

I was seated in a chair, and right in front of me was a being that was definitely divine. I don't really think that they're a god in a capital 'G' sense, but rather the type of divinity that screams 'Minor God' or 'God that's probably forgotten in the modern world'. Powerful, but not really that much in comparison to the known pantheons.

That said - I quickly looked around, and saw that I was in a mystical-looking room. It's nothing special either, just a decorative bounded field probably meant to impress the normal souls that end up here. And right in front of me was… were those flyers?

Yes, they were. They were flyers of what looked like magical items. There's swords, bows, shields, staffs, armor, trinkets - all that stuff and equipment you'd expect from traditional role-playing games. And written below are the descriptions of said magical items which, in layman's terms, are absolutely OP.

I stared at it.

I'm definitely in a realm meant to isekai people, aren't I.

"Who are you supposed to be?" the goddess muttered to herself after seeing me, before taking out what looked like a file beside her. "I don't think the next soul is some yankee. Actually, doesn't the system exclusively target no-life losers in Japan who'd jump at a chance on our isekai racket? What's a person like this doing here…"

What's with this goddess? She sure is blunt.

"—Nope, you're definitely not Takanashi Takana-san." the goddess declared after taking a look at her files. Then, she stood up and pointed at me. "And it looks like you're not in any of the other lists either! Who are you supposed to be? And how did you get here!?"

I didn't answer. Instead, I stood up from my chair and walked forward.

That made the goddess immediately squared her shoulders.

"W-What is this? Why do my godly instincts warn me that I'm facing something dangerous…!" She went into a fighting stance for some reason. "I-I don't know what your deal is, but you better stop or you'll face the wrath of the gods!"

I didn't stop.

"Ooh, you asked for it! Take this, my Divine Create Water!"

High-pressure water hit me directly. It was pretty strong - but after blocking the attack by applying the proper defenses, I was still standing there unharmed. I was completely wet like usual though. Somehow. Despite the fact that I'm still technically a soul right now.

Anyway, the goddess freaked out when she saw me still standing.

"E-Eh!? No damage!? How!?" she shouted in complete shock. "T-That was my strongest divine spell! It would've been enough to kill a demon lord twice over!"

"…"

I stretched out my hand.

"—Eeeek! Forgive me! I'm sorry, I'm just a minor god who knows nothing!" the goddess squealed, quickly backing away from me. "W-What do you want? Do you want divine gifts? I could give you that! I-If you would just let me contact my superiors for it, I—!"

She wasn't able to finish.

And that was because the very next moment, my hand touched a specific wet flyer on the soaked floor, before I dragged something out of thin air as I accessed the magical artifact within. As for what artifact it was - what I chose was probably the most normal and uncreative out of all of them.

The magic sword, Excalibur.

Or one of them at least. And this one is definitely one of the weakest out of every version that I had encountered. It might be useful though, so I kept it in my subspace for now.

"—Eh?"

In any case, the goddess reacted with shock when she realized that I wasn't actually going to hurt her. Then, she blinked when what followed after was a magical circle appearing out of thin air. I stared at it, analyzing the structure in seconds.

Hm… the coding is unfamiliar, but I can recognize enough of the inscriptions to know that this will transport me to the Reverse Side of the World. It was also programmed to appear after I got an artifact. And it seems that it'll reform my physical body as well based on what was recorded on my soul.

Guess there's really no choice but to go there at this point. Although, let me modify where I'll go, since I'd rather not go to their equivalent to a noob town or whatever. Let's see… a scratch here and some writings there, and… Voila. Done.

I turned back to the goddess.

She stared at me from behind her throne.

"…You didn't see me here." I told her.

I could see the gears in this goddess' mind turn when I said that.

Then, when she got what I was saying - she immediately sent me a thumbs up.

"Yes! I definitely didn't see anything!" she shouted, in an agreeable tone that you'd make on unreasonable bosses giving you shit. "Please don't mind me - this minor goddess hadn't witnessed anything out of the ordinary! I'm just waiting for Katakana Tanashi-san after all! Ahaha!"

…Somehow, this goddess lacked any sort of grace compared to the few ones that I've encountered. At least try to remember the dead guy's name properly. It'd be way too pitiful if you didn't.

Well, I guess that's how it is with comedy types. I'm thinking she's going to be an idiot character in whatever story she's involved with.

Wishing my luck to whoever will have to deal with this goddess, I let myself get completely swallowed by the light and get my soul transported to the Reverse Side of the World. The modifications to the magical circle made my destination being the most mana-rich continent, since that's where definitely the good stuff was.

And soon enough, instead of arriving in a small town or whatever - I opened my eyes to the sight of a thick and dense forest. Then I glanced around, taking it all in for a moment.

"You heard him, Frieren-sama. The shady man doesn't want anything to do with you." Oi, did she just call me shady again? "Let's go back to our table and order some food. Come on, we can order some dessert for today—"

"No. Don't you see it, Fern? Look at his mana."

The girl stopped at the elf's interjection. "What do you…?" she frowned, before turning to me. I could see her eyes analyzing me intensely, and then… "H-Huh? But that is…!"

I frowned as her eyes widened, seemingly discovering something strange about me. What is it? What the hell do they find so shocking about me? I'm not doing anything particularly special, I'm pretty sure.

Hold on a second, that elf mentioned having not a single trace of mana around me. What the hell is that supposed to mean? Is she saying that it's normal for people to let out mana or something? Actually - wait, maybe that really is the case.

Compared to all of the people here in the Reverse Side, the internal mana my body generates is actually pretty miniscule. I cheat using other systems and use magical energy from other sources to conduct my spells. And perhaps what was the most important detail of all - I actually suppress my mana into nothingness since that's pretty much needed to blend in with mundane people back home.

But that's not the same here. Since it's still the Age of the Gods, a mundane person with no talent for magic still generates plenty of mana inside them. That makes me an outlier, so if I want to match what the normal mana level was…

I glanced at some of the people on the side, before adjusting my mana suppression to the normal level.

The girl stiffened while the elf blinked.

"Ah. He changed it." the elf muttered.

"I didn't." I instantly denied. "You're just imagining things. I mean, are you sure that it's not just your senses failing you or something, old hag?"

"There's no way I imagined that, especially considering both me and my student saw what happened. You somehow have expert control of your mana. One that surpasses me, even." she stated, before frowning. "…Also, old hag? How rude."

"What's rude is that you keep trying to bother me when I clearly stated that I don't want to be bothered. So try not to be a hypocrite, will you? Just leave me and my succulent meal alone."

"Unfortunately, I'll have to pass on that. After all, I'm an old hag that's as stubborn as a mule and can't hear your words. That's what you claimed I am, right?"

"—I don't remember adding the rest of those things."

"—Is that so? I apologize then."

A moment of intense silence followed.

I stared at her, and she met it head on.

This elf… she definitely isn't going to back down no matter what words I say to her. I don't know what sort of story she's involved in, but I actually really can't be bothered to deal with it now. Which means there's only one option that will allow me to deal with this nuisance.

I turned to my plate and started eating, ignoring her existence entirely.

"Frieren-sama…" I heard the girl beside her mutter.

A pause, followed by a sigh. "There's no choice. Buckle up, Fern. I didn't really want to do this, but…"

I heard the chair right next to me scrape on the floorboards. Unable to hold the urge, I glanced to the side to see that the elf had sat down right next to me at the counter top. As her clearly hesitant apprentice followed beside her, she then called out to the barkeep.

"Excuse me, we'd like to have what he's having." she said, pointing at me. "Oh, and two glasses of milk as well. If you have some."

"—Coming right up! Just wait for a bit."

I frowned at her as the barkeep moved to prepare their orders. "The hell are you doing?"

"And here I thought that you're going to ignore me?" the elf asked, before shaking her head. "Well, since you're clearly acting stubborn - I just decided to take a page from someone I've been in a party with in the past. He's really good when it comes to convincing people, you see."

"Uh huh." I said blankly. "And surely that doesn't involve harassing me while I eat, does it?"

The elf smirked at that. "Hmph. Of course not. Something like that won't work."

It's good that she knew that. However, I was familiar enough with this development to know the comedic shenanigans coming my way, one that will definitely involve my misfortune in one way or another.

And I was proven right the next moment she opened her mouth.

"—I just need to bother you every single moment of the day, that's all."

…

…

I stared at the elf with a deadpan gaze.

Yeah, this is definitely gonna be a pain.



I have now graduated, so that's cool. Also - I have a patreon which offers 10 advanced chapters. If you somehow like my stories enough to pay for it, I hope you check it out.
