Chapter 35

"—Potatoes! Tomatoes! We've got a new batch of fresh produce here!"

"—Hey, mister, are you interested in some medicinal herbs?"

"—That's a hundred copper coins! Pleasure doing business with you."

I was in a very busy place.

Countless footsteps hitting cobblestone, the trotting of horses and the creaking of their wagons, the constant voices of people calling out and haggling with one another. It was very noisy, but the reason why is understandable once one realizes where exactly I was.

I was exploring the city's equivalent of a local market district.


Spoiler

Being the main place of commerce in the city, all I could see around are shops, stalls and tents that offer goods and services. Wagons and caravans pulled horses or other creatures were also a common sight. And there were also plenty of people around, comparable to a busy side walk during the rush hour in a city downtown.

It was a sight I've seen a hundred times at least, both personally and in isekai slop shown on TV. That said, for the personal part, this place was definitely bigger than the ones I encountered the last time I visited the Reverse Side of the World. It's likely due to the fact that the city was bigger overall than those that I saw previously, or perhaps it's because of the passage of time or something.

Lots of progress can be made in years after all, especially in a world where humanity is known for its innovations.

This place was really nice though. I could see a bunch of objects and trinkets that caught my eyes ever since I came here. Not to mention materials so incredibly rare in the Modern World that seem to be in abundance in this world that they're commonly sold in markets.

I'm definitely making use of this trip to check everything out and get all the rare stuff I could find.

That said, I couldn't really fully appreciate everything right now… and that was because of certain unwelcome presences who seemingly decided to join me on my venture here.

"You're looking to buy something?"

The elf walking beside me asked that casually, as if we were friends and not a harasser and their harassee. And trailing slightly behind her, thankfully staying quiet throughout it all, was the purple-haired girl who was clearly this elf's apprentice.

They've been following me ever since I left the tavern and some parts of the city. For the most part, I've thought about ignoring them and losing them since I don't really want to get involved in a story's plot right now. However, no matter how much stealth or magic I used to escape, they were somehow able to find me somewhere in the city.

It's clear that the plot treated my escape attempts as a comedy routine or something. Although, this elf probably has some sort of way of identifying where I am as well. I'm pretty sure I could feel the traces of nature magic in her staff there.

"You're quite slippery to find. I wonder what spell you're using to prevent yourself from being tracked." the elf commented, before turning to the side. "Anyway, as you can see Fern, tracking spells aren't foolproof. Sometimes people find ways to counteract it, and you have to be creative in finding them instead."

Her apprentice nodded. "I understand."

…Was this elf using me as a way to conduct lessons? Seriously?

Whatever. At this point no matter how much I try to escape these two, they'd still be finding me. Anything short of leaving the city itself would probably result in that conclusion. And I don't really want to leave the city now, considering I want to find clues on how to get back home and this is the biggest city in this part of the continent.

Also, I have no idea where the other cities are. That old man from before provided me with a mental map, but it's just that. A map. I'm going to have to actually explore and locate a city since I don't have the coordinates to go there.

No choice then… Looks like I just have to get myself involved with these two. What a pain.

"So, what are you going to buy here?" the elf asked curiously. "Are you looking for something specific?"

I glanced at her, before looking forward again.

"Nunya." I answered.

The elf tilted her head. "Nunya…? I'm not familiar with something like that. Is that a new thing?" she turned to her apprentice. "Fern, are you familiar with something like that?"

Said apprentice was looking at me like trash. "Frieren-sama. Don't fall for it. He's just messing around with you with stupid playground jokes—"

"Nunya business."

The elf blinked. "Nunya business…? Oh, I understand it now. A play of words on 'none of your business'." she nodded with a slight smile. "I see, that's a pretty clever one. I'll make sure to use that sometime."

What's with that reaction.

"And you said that it's a playground joke, Fern? It's amazing that human kids can think of something like that. You have to teach me those things some time."

"Frieren-sama…" her apprentice muttered in exasperation, before letting out a sigh. "I'm not teaching you those things. Only childish people get to find some use for it."

"—Hey, you calling me childish?" I asked.

"I said nothing of the sort. Perhaps you just didn't hear it properly?" the girl denied, blank-faced much like the elf.

This girl… she's really jabbing at me indirectly, completely opposite to her mentor's straightforward harassment. Seriously, what the hell is this? What are they even trying to accomplish by doing this?

You know what, they can do whatever they want. I'll just humor them and focus on finding things that are interesting in this market. With that, I approached one of the stalls that caught my eye to check out their inventory, with the two following me as I did so.

"Welcome, welcome! Have a look!" the shopkeeper greeted.

"An herb shop?" the elf commented as she looked around. "Interesting. Are you planning to make a potion?"

I picked out most of the mana-rich herbs I could find. I could probably farm all of this with the right conditions and use it as alchemical material. The potions that I actually use also involve the use of similar plants, but from what I could tell, these ones would improve them more.

In any case, I chose the good quality ones. Then I went to pay the shopkeeper.

"That'll be ten silver, sir."

That seems like a fair price. I put a hand in my pocket and discreetly glanced at his drawer on the side, where I knew where he kept his money. Let's see… structural analysis, take out silver inside my subspace, and transmutation magic. There, silver coins ready to go.

I took out the coins in my pocket and gave it to the shopkeeper. This many coins shouldn't crash the economy. Or other coins that I'll make from now on, for that matter.

As I turned around and left the tent, the elf spoke while she and her apprentice followed once more.

"You just did something, though I don't know what." the elf commented casually, before tilting her head. "…By the way, are you sure you don't need that in a bag? You still plan on shopping some more, right?"

"It's fine." I answered, before 'folding' the herbs and 'putting' them in my pocket.

The elf blinked. So did her apprentice.

"…Frieren-sama, what did he just do?" the purple-haired girl asked, surprised. "Did he just fold those herbs to put them in his pocket? That shouldn't be possible."

The elf nodded. "You did. And I doubt he really did fold it. It's impossible for that amount of herbs to fit in his pocket… He must have used some sort of spatial magic. I've never seen it applied like that, though. And with so little mana being used."

No, I actually didn't even use mana. I was using subspace technology. But it's not like they'll ever know that.

In any case, I continued shopping, not really paying attention to them at this point.

Being a big city, this market has surprisingly a lot of things being sold. I've checked stalls and stores that sell unique trinkets, some of which have interesting effects and properties. A passing merchant caravan who were from the Northern lands apparently offered a bunch of unique materials such as dragon scales and phoenix feathers. All of which I've obtained, considering their potential to be used for material or catalysts.

I also brought some stuff as souvenirs. Like a book that covers the entire magical history of the continent, a ring that makes you sparkle when you put magical energy in it, and a preserved beautiful glowing flower in a jar. That, and many more.

There's even fantasy animals being sold here. One of them caught my attention for looking kinda cute. It looks like a chick that'd grow up to be a chicken, but it's apparently one of the two-legged birds being used to pull wagons like a domesticated ostrich. As of now though, it's more of a big ball of feathers that the others would likely find cute.


Spoiler

I bought the thing and folded it.

"Wha—!?" the elf's apprentice and the merchant I was talking to shouted in shock.

As I left the store after doing that, the elf explained what was going on to her apprentice and the merchant. She was right, but the actual explanation was very different due to the genre divide. Afterwards, the two went on to follow me again.

The purple-haired girl won't stop giving me peeved looks though. The hell is this girl upset about? It's your fault for assuming things, you nincompoop.

Moving on - while souvenirs are pretty nice, it's not the only reason why I was here. The reason why I'm mainly in this market was to look for things that I could potentially use to go on. Finding that was tricky though, but I had the help of some surface mind-reading and questioning techniques.

And also, the wisdom of an experienced adventurer apparently.

"If you're looking for the good stuff, then you're better off heading deeper into the city rather than checking the stores out in the open."

The elf said those words after I questioned a merchant that I purchased some knickknacks from. She then pointed to the road at the side, one that seems to head away from the market itself.

"I actually found a good place earlier when I was out exploring. It's a shop full of magical artifacts owned by a mage." she added, before tilting her head. "So? Are you interested?"

I stared at her. It's clear that she's gonna use this as an 'in' to my cold and edgy heart.

…I suppose it wouldn't hurt.

"Fine." I sighed out. "Lead the way."

The elf smiled slightly.

"I promise to you that it won't disappoint."

Well, we'll see about that.




It took less than a few minutes of us walking for her to use the opportunity to make me talk.

"By the way, we never did introduce ourselves. It was a bit hard to do it with you constantly ignoring us." the elf commented, before glancing back at me. "As you may have heard, I'm Frieren. Just your usual elf mage. And this is my apprentice, Fern. It's nice to meet you."

Said apprentice bowed slightly even if she was still giving me a cautious look. I ignored it.

"There's no way an elf mage who lived hundreds of years could be called the 'usual'." I instead replied.

"Perhaps. But in comparison to you, I might as well be." she said easily. "So, who are you? Are you a hero?"

I raised a brow at the term again. "What makes you say that?"

She glanced at my waist. "Well, you have a magic sword. I do not know if you use it well, but you must be strong since your skills in magic exceeds mine. As far as I know I only met one person who's like that, and they're known as a hero in the southern lands."

Then she tilted her head, looking thoughtful.

"Although, considering how you seem unfamiliar with many of the things you bought in the market, despite the fact that they can be found in the wild… Are you perhaps a hero from a different place? That would at least explain the unfamiliarity."

Hm. That's a reasonable assumption. This elf really thought it through.

That said, it's still wrong.

"I'm not a hero. I'm just your usual adventurer who picked up some tricks." I told them. "As for my name, I…"

I paused for a moment, before settling into the cool name I chose earlier because of my sword.

"They call me Arthur. Arthur Pendragon."

The elf and her apprentice blinked at my answer.

"…I see." the elf eventually replied, before looking forward once more. "Arthur Pendragon, huh."

"—Frieren-sama, there's no way that is this man's name. That's a person who only exists in fairy tales." her apprentice instantly replied.

"No, that one I gathered. I also heard of that story too, you know?" the elf replied, although she looked lost in her memories. "That said, it's been a long time since I've heard that name… that tale is very old. I believe the last time I heard it was when I was still a child. So it's still being told to humans to this day, huh?"

"When you were still a child… how long ago would that be?"

"I wouldn't know. But if there is a real King Arthur, then they'd probably have lived more than five thousand years ago. Even my parents know him as nothing but a fairy tale, as far as I know."

"T-That's… a very long time."

As the purple-haired girl wrapped her head around that amount of time, I instead noted that information.

So they also have 'his' story in here, huh. Makes sense, with Rhongomyniad being the one to connect the Reverse Side and the Modern World and with King Arthur's legend interconnected with the fae and all. Elves here have a connection to the fae, but it seems like the gap has grown enough in time.

That said, it was an interesting factoid knowing that a person from our side of the world was known here. Although, to a person who comes from the Modern World like I do, there is one thing about what she said was strange. She had mentioned that King Arthur was a person who preceded her thousand year-old life, possibly living five thousand years prior to her or so.

However, those with common sense would realize that King Arthur had lived in the middle ages. Five thousand years ago was way before that time, since at that age humanity was still stuck using bronze instead of iron. So unless there's time fuckery involved, there's no way that was true.

And there is, actually. Time fuckery, I mean.

The truth is, a day in the Modern World lasts like five days here in the Reverse Side.

Time dilation occurs much like the parabolic time chamber back home, except at a smaller rate. So when I said to Yuki and the others that I'll be back in a few days, I actually meant quite several, which would probably be around a month or somewhat less.

It's honestly something to be thankful about in this case. I don't think it'd be possible for me to find a way out of here without a foundation to work on. The last time I was here, it took me a couple of months. I also wasn't powerful and rich with resources like I do currently, so I wasn't able to establish a support base like I have back home.

I have the opportunity to do it right now though. It might be good to establish a support base here, along with constructing a way to make travel between the two worlds easier. Then there's also the fact that travelling between said worlds disrupts my connection between clones on the other side, causing them to dispel. If I want to maintain a constant presence everywhere like I usually do, then I'd need to find a way to circumvent that.

But I digress. For now, I need to find a way to get back home first. My last method was one-time only, so I'd need to find a different one. And hopefully, it's repeatable.

In any case, the elf spoke to me again.

"If you want your name kept private, that's fine by me." she stated idly. "But I'd like to ask: how did you get here? The way you're acting in the market reminds me of people who arrived here on this continent through ships. But there are no coastal towns near this city though."

Was this elf calling me a tourist?

…Well, I suppose it's not inaccurate.

"I came here because I'm from a different world." I answered her question straightforwardly. "It's because a goddess sent me or whatever. It's also where I got this neat magic sword. When I got here, I was in the forest right next to this city."

Once more the elf blinked.

"…I see." she replied again. "A different world, huh."

"—Frieren-sama, this guy is clearly just messing with us." her apprentice instantly interjected. "All that he's been saying so far is lies. And I don't think he's planning to answer honestly anytime soon."

It's actually the truth this time, though.

"Well, we have been harassing him the entire time, after all. It makes sense he wouldn't trust us." Such impressive self-awareness. Now if only they'd act on it. "Oh well, we'll get you eventually… Ah, there it is. The shop that I'm talking about is just past that place, by the way."

She pointed much further down the winding road that we were walking in. At some point, as we were traveling further and further into the city's less trodden paths, we arrived in what looks like a pretty sketchy part of the neighborhood.

I could visibly see the gloom in the atmosphere. The mana here is slightly tainted too, although it's just a miniscule amount. The place we're in is undoubtedly the underbelly of the city, the one place where most of the downtrodden and the more illicit individuals reside.

In short, it's the city slums.


Spoiler

"Frieren-sama, is this really the place we're headed in?" the elf's apprentice asked, her face slightly concerned. "I don't think there's any shops in a shady area like this. This place…"

She looked to the side, and there, you could see some hoodlums lurking about. They actually look the part, with them having mohawks, earrings, tattoos and… Hm, these guys just look like band members or something. Only with a fantasy outfit. Maybe they're not bad guys?

Oh, no wait. They have knives. One guy just licked it. Yeah, these guys are definitely fantasy criminals.

In any case, the apprentice looked at them with a revolted expression. "This place is clearly filled with unsavory people, Frieren-sama. These people look like they're delusional enough to think that they're from a different world. They definitely won't hesitate to rob us."

"Hey, did you really just compare me to those guys?" I asked.

"I did no such thing. That said, please look in the mirror the next time you have an opportunity."

"You really just did, huh." I deadpanned. "For the record, I'm not shady. Rather it's your mentor. May I remind you of the fact that she's the one who's harassing me and who brought us to this place. And the one who also apparently offered her body in our very first meeting, for some godforsaken reason. I think that part should be specifically emphasized."

The elf tilted her head. "…I can understand the first two, but is there something particularly shady about the last one? It's meant as payment for you teaching a very valuable skill. Shouldn't lending you my services as a capable mage be an equivalent exchange?"

I stared at the elf.

This feeling of denseness that rivals a neutron star… What's with this elf, is she a harem protagonist?

Her apprentice coughed, her face looking slightly red. "Frieren-sama. I know you didn't mean it that way, but the way you said it was like…"

The girl leaned into the elf's long ears which twitched. Then, as the girl whispered her explanation to her mentor - she blinked in surprise.

"O-Oh. Is that what I said?" The elf muttered, wide-eyed. Then she turned to me. "Sorry about that. That's… that's not what I meant. At all."

I waved it away. "It's fine."

"…Right."

The elf turned around again, resuming her walk. It looked a great deal more stiff than earlier though, and I could partially hear the elf's voice as she whispered to herself.

"I can't believe that's what I actually said… Uu…"


Spoiler

So she actually has the capacity to be embarrassed. Also, what's with that weird expression?

Anyway, despite the apprentice's earlier protests, we made our way through the slums to get to the shop that the elf was talking about. Some hoodlums eyed us but clearly valued their lives enough, not wanting to mess with two obvious mages who were accompanied by a really cool third guy with a similarly cool-looking sword.

And eventually, after passing through a few alleys and going down some stairs - it seems we've finally arrived at what looks more like a door to a basement than an actual building. And one that was guarded by a hooded man with a partially disfigured face.

He turned to us when he noticed our presence, then he spoke gruffly.

"The elven mage of the party that defeated the Demon King? What are you doing here?"

The guy suddenly dropped a major detail out of nowhere. Defeated the demon King? Seriously, what the hell is this plot I got involved into?

"We're interested in your wares." the elf answered casually. "Your place was recommended to me by some acquaintances. I want to check if they're really telling the truth."

For a moment the man just stared at her.

Then, he grinned. "Then you'll find them correct, elf. Come right inside."

We did. As we entered, the torches lit themselves up on their own and illuminated the place inside. And there I was subjected to a sight that made me realize that this place was definitely the real deal.

This place was chock-full of things that a mage would consider as treasure. Historical items full of mystery, pieces and fragments of divine constructs, cursed objects and many more. There's also a bunch of other things like spellbooks and grimoires, ones that contain pretty powerful spells that likely cost a pretty penny or are perhaps considered as forbidden research.

Seeing all this… yeah, I'll probably find some way I could get home here. Looks like going along with the elf's plot paid off. I mean, I could probably find this place if I looked hard enough, but objectives accomplished for a quarter of the required effort is worth celebrating.

In any case, the elf immediately went to the spellbooks and grimoires in the shelves, and her apprentice followed behind her. Meanwhile I checked out the artifacts displayed on the cabinets. Let's see what might help me here…

The historical items contain an incredible amount of mystery that can be used for some truly powerful magecraft, although it lacks any sort of use to achieve my objectives. The same goes for the divine construct fragments and the cursed objects. Ideally, what I wanted was something that could make me establish a connection to the modern world, where… Wait, hold on.

Is that a v8 engine there at the bottom? What the hell is that doing here? Ahh, no, I get it. It probably came from one of those isekai's that try to use their modern knowledge to their advantage.

That's a shame. Yeah, casting a structural analysis spell at it, I can see that its history is entirely contained in this world. I probably would've been able to establish a connection using it if it actually came from the other side, but what are the chances that a car was isekai'd along with someone?

…Maybe there's a plotline out there where someone gets in a car accident with the Almighty Truck-kun? With how uninspired the genre is, I wouldn't put it past them.

Before I could consider it some more however, a voice interrupted my thoughts.

"You've got quite a good eye there, sir." I glanced to the side to see that it was the disfigured man, who approached me with a shady smile. "What you're looking at there is the future of transportation. That one there is called—"

"—An engine, right? Yeah, I know." I interrupted, making him pause.

"You do? Hm." the man looked at me consideringly. "You don't seem to be from here… Are these things perhaps more common from where you are?"

What's with people assuming that I'm a tourist? Not that I wasn't, but I would've thought people wouldn't notice it that much. I suppose mages have a better eye for detail than anyone though.

"You could say that. I know how it works." I saw his eyes sharpen. Oh? Looks like he's hungry for knowledge. He reminds me more of a modern magus than a normal fantasy mage. "Tell you what - if you could give me an artifact that has a connection to other realms, then I'll teach you the way you can use this. Considering you have it stored here, you have no idea how to operate it, do you?"

The disfigured man considered that. "A connection with other realms, you say…? You're looking for something specific? Holy? Pagan?"

"Just show me anything, really."

"…Very well. Follow me."

The man then led me to a different room. The elf and her apprentice glanced at me as we passed by them, before going back to checking the spellbooks and grimoires. When I got to the room itself, I was subjected to a storage room that reminded me of a magus' workshop back home.

The disfigured man then started taking out some things from crates and stuff while muttering underneath his breath. Then, after taking out all the necessary things, he put them on a nearby table.

"Here are all of the things you're looking for." he stated, gesturing at the artifacts. "So? Does this satisfy you?"

I glanced at all of them and casted a structural analysis spell, viewing their structural makeup and history. Most of these things are from pantheons that originate in the Reverse Side, which I immediately ignored. If I accessed those realms I wouldn't be able to connect to the Modern World.

That leaves things that both worlds have in common. And here, I see exactly three things that fit the bill: a holy object, a demonic weapon, and an enchanted item by the fae.

The holy object produces a wavelength almost identical to the holy energy produced by the Abrahamic Heaven back home. It's probably just from a similar pantheon, but a few adjustments would probably make me able to use it as a catalyst to establish a connection to Heaven.

But that would also mean invading the place, and I'd really rather not make an enemy of the angels. What's more, it'd also be a one-time passageway if I do it like that. I want to establish an easier pathway so that I can travel here back home easily given the opportunity.

As for the demonic weapon - this one is definitely a gamble. There are hundreds of hell realms, and all of them are pretty similar. I could do it by trial and error and try to connect to the Abrahamic Hell in the Modern World, but considering we're dealing with the turbulent sea of ether dividing the two worlds… it's definitely going to require some truly powerful, intense, and complicated engineering to make it work.

This one is more of a problem with sensitivity. If there is a change caused by various factors separating the Modern World to the Reverse Side, I could easily end up in a different destination from what I planned. Hence, complicated engineering is required.

Which leaves the fae item. A crown of thorns.

It's just a minor enchanted item with a stupid gimmick, but a bit of work and it can definitely lead me to where Rhongomyniad is located. The lance has a connection to both the Reverse Side and the Modern World, anchoring it along with the other textures of the planet. If there was one place that would allow me a direct connection, it was in there.

And also… I glanced at my sword.

Hm. Thematic connection.

Yeah, I'm definitely not going to be involved in the Arthurian Legend with the way things are going.

"I'll take this one." I said, taking the fae item.

"The Iron-Bane Thorns?" the disfigured man asked, confused. "Just so you know, that item makes your skin as hard as iron, but actually touching iron would make you extremely weak. It's a useless battle item made by the pranks of the cruel fae."

Well isn't he surprisingly nice, letting me know all that.

"I'm not using it. As I said, I'm interested in the way it's connected with realms." I told him. Then I produced a paper booklet/manual from subspace, one that detailed the v8 engine's assembly, operation, and maintenance. "Can you read this language?"

The man took it, and his eyes widened when he saw the contents. "T-This is…! Yes, I've definitely seen this script before." he then hid it within his robes and chuckled. "Hehe, this is a worthwhile trade. I'll have some fun deciphering this. You have my thanks, sir."

Getting rid of a stupid enchanted item in exchange for valuable knowledge? Yeah, I'd be definitely thanking myself too. I put the fae item in the subspace, ignoring the disfigured man watching my magic as I did so.

Anyway, we went ahead and left the room after that. And when we did, I found that the elf and her apprentice were waiting for us, with the elf having chosen a few spell books from the shelves.

"I'll be taking this." the elf said, before throwing a pouch.

The man caught it and opened it, revealing a bunch of gold coins. "Hehe, pleasure doing business with you."

We left the store together right after. The elf glanced at me as we got past the door and closed it.

"So, did you find what you need?" she asked.

"Yeah."

She nodded. "Good. That means you owe me one. Feeling much more talkative now?"

I glanced at her. "That part was meant to be unspoken, you know."

"I prefer it to be spoken out loud. I was never that good at the unspoken stuff." Evidently. "I'll be cashing in on that favor, by the way. I expect you to follow your word, or else you'll gain the wrath of the mage who was a member of the party who defeated the Demon King."

I raised a brow. "Wasn't the entire purpose of this harassment about you wanting to learn how to fully suppress your mana? Why wait when I can teach you right now?"

"No, I figured that out already." What. "You have a lower mana pool than we do so it makes it relatively easier to suppress your mana into nothingness. That said, your mana control is still superb. You probably trained a lot for it."

I mean, I did, but I'm actually just cheating you know? The difficulty of mana suppression is the fact that you have to focus to suppress it and just live life like that constantly. It's the magical equivalent of constantly holding in your gut. If you have parallel thought processes though, that problem just goes away on its own.

But whatever. It's her choice.

"So if it's not that, what is the repayment for the favor gonna be?"

The elf stopped walking. Her apprentice and I did the same. Then, she fully turned to me.

"Join our party, Arthur." she stated.

…

It was a very unreasonable request that she just said there, and in response to it I simply raised a brow. However, her apprentice didn't react to that nearly as quietly as I did.

"F-Frieren-sama!?" the purple-haired girl shouted in shock. "You want him to join us on our journey!? I-I apologize, but where did this come from!? Why would you invite a stranger with us out of—!"

"Fern, we're two mages. If we want to fight monsters then we need a frontline fighter with us. Although, I suppose that he's not exactly a frontline fighter with him being more skilled in mana control than I am. But it's definitely going to be a great deal safer if we go together."

The apprentice still looked doubtful. "B-But still, asking him to go with us is still asking a lot… He can't very well just leave whatever businesses he needs to do just for our sake, especially considering we're travelling far off the mountain region…"

Huh, so this girl actually does care a bit. How considerate.

That said, her mentor holds the opposite sentiment.

"It's fine, Fern. After all…" she looked back at me. "…You're searching for something, aren't you? Especially with the artifact that you bought. Something with connection to other realms, was it?"

"It's rude to eavesdrop." I pointed out blankly.

"It's not really eavesdropping. Us elves just have naturally good hearing, these long ears aren't just for show." Then she tilted her head. "So, what do you think? If you're looking for a particular place, then we could team up together until you find what you're looking for or we go our separate ways. Not a bad arrangement, right?"

I stared at her. As I did so, it might have looked like I was a potential party member considering the offer on the outside, but the truth is that I'm considering the entire situation I've found myself in.

My goal is to establish a connection between the Reverse Side and the Modern World while also building a support base here for future operations. I can easily accomplish both of those with lots of clones. If I reject this elf's offer, then I can probably focus on my goals and do it much faster.

However, right now, the character known as 'Arthur' is actually now considered a side character to this elf's story. One that was judged as a potential member of their little party. I could easily leave the city now that I've gained what I needed, and being meta, the story can't do anything but adjust to my actions.

However, is that really the right choice?

That exact adjustment resulting from that is hard to pin down. What sort of changes would happen to the story if a potential party member just up and left without repaying a favor? Will I gain an enemy? Will I be branded as an antagonist? Will I be talked about as a hated character in social media or discussed in video essays by people with too much time in their lives?

Whatever it is, in a story like this where the mood seems to be chill or good vibes thus far - a person acting like an asshole is definitely a highlight. And since said asshole was also going to be me, I'd rather not risk it. All that trouble is not worth adding a single body in my clone workforce.

And also, I'd rather not act like an asshole. These two seem like nice people, so they don't really deserve getting done dirty like that. You know, despite the fact that they stalked me, talked shit about me, and essentially manipulated me.

…Actually, maybe I should consider leaving in the end.

That said, I suppose it's not like it matters at all. Because considering this development and my personality thus far, Arthur was still someone who clearly doesn't trust the elf enough. The answer is a clear resounding 'no', since saying anything otherwise would break the suspension of disbelief.

So what does the story do to prevent that?

"Help! S-Someone, help—!"

Well, it throws conflict in our faces to help everyone bond, of course.

The elf and her apprentice stiffened at the shout. Meanwhile, I turned to its direction. That woman's shout echoed in just a second before quieting down immediately after, perhaps being muffled by the people taking her.

In any case, we exploded into action an instant after. The two mages flew up in the air with their staffs, while I simply jumped up the buildings and ran across the rooftops. It took just a moment for us to arrive where the shout came from.

And there we saw the hoodlums from earlier. With them are a couple of women that they've definitely kidnapped.

"Hyahaha! No one's gonna hear you here, missy!" the hoodlum laughed, putting a knife on the woman's throat. "Just stay still… You don't want to get stabbed, do you? It'd be a shame if merchandise would be damaged—

"Zoltraak."

"—Gack!"

The hoodlum was sent flying when he was hit by a beam in the gut. His other friends immediately stiffened when they saw him go down, before quickly turning to the source of the attack.

The apprentice brought down her staff as she floated above the ground. She glared at the men, expression dark.

"Let those women go, or else you're next." she threatened.

Fear clearly entered their expressions at the sight of mages, but one of them seemingly had a good head on his shoulders and didn't let the pressure get to him. He grit his teeth and grabbed one of the women, pointing his knife at her neck.

"S-Screw you! You leave us alone!" he shouted. "I-If you make a single move, I'm going to kill this woman!"

The apprentice grit her teeth. But when she opened her mouth - she was interrupted.

"—Bind."

The hoodlums were barely able to react when the rings of light suddenly appeared around them and bound their arms to their bodies. The woman held hostage dropped when the man no longer was able to grab her, and she quickly made distance.

The elf and her apprentice floated down and touched the cobblestone ground. They quickly went to the two women and attended to them, who were still in a state of panic after everything.

They probably won't react well if I approach them. So instead, I went to the struggling hoodlums and knocked out everyone with well placed blows to the skull. With the last one being the smart one, that is.

"Oi. You." I called out to him, making him stiffen after seeing me knock out his comrades. "You said that those women are merchandise, right? Are you selling them somewhere?"

"I-I ain't telling you shit—Grgkh!"

"Just wanted confirmation." I replied after knocking him out as well with a kick in the face.

Then I touched his head and skimmed his memories. And there I saw… Hm, so it's a slave ring. Yeah, something like this is definitely prevalent in many isekai fantasies.

I stood up. Then as I was about to head towards the location of the place, someone called out to me.

"I've heard. I'll be searching with you." the elf stated, grabbing her staff. "Fern will be putting those two girls to safety and will be joining us right after. Let's split up and search the area—"

"No need, I already got the location." I replied, making her pause.

"…I see. Lead the way, then."

She didn't need to tell me. The moment she floated above ground - I reinforced myself, dashing through the road with the elf following after me.

The story wants me to do all this? Well, I don't really mind. In fact, I kinda welcome it.

—And with that, we went ahead and enacted some good ol' adventurer justice.




Wind blew past her as she soared through the skies.

She went the fastest that her flight allowed, while also readying her offensive magic for what was to come.

After helping the women get to safety and quickly alerting the city guards of the problem, she immediately returned as fast as she could to help out her mentor and the unknown man they had followed to deal with a particular problem.

A slave ring. It was a revolting concept.

She was a victim of a demon attack, with her village being wiped out by the remnants of the Demon King's army. There was nothing that she truly hated aside from those creatures. However, she has also come to learn that evil comes in many forms - and there are times that humans have shown to be just as evil as the demons they're fighting.

Slavery was something that was abolished many years ago between all the human kingdoms. However, there are still remnants of it to be found in places the authority hadn't thought to look. One such case was present in this city currently, and if it weren't for their presence, it might have remained undiscovered.

She wanted to get rid of it. She wanted to eradicate it completely, just like the demons she had been fighting. Such evil is reprehensible enough to be compared to demons.

So when she saw the sight of her mentor floating in the air in the distance, she immediately sped up and prepared herself for a fight.

—Or at least, that was what Fern thought until she realized that her mentor was simply just floating there, doing nothing and simply looking down on the ground.

"Frieren-sama?" she asked, slowing down her flight.

"Oh, Fern. You're here." the elf replied, turning to her.

Fern frowned at how casual she was acting before dismissing it. She'd let out her grievances later. "Frieren-sama, have you found the slave ring yet?" she asked instead, before looking around. "I've already called the city guards, if we could locate it, then—"

"It's fine. Just stay put for now."

Her mentor's words made Fern blink and turn to her once more. "What are you…?"

She trailed off when her mentor pointed down.

Fern followed it and… There, she saw something that made her eyes widen.

Within the slums, a place that looked like a collection of houses was completely wrecked. It looked as if a hurricane had gone through it, and with those houses destroyed, it revealed what was definitely the base of operations of the slave ring out to the world.

Armed men had gathered around, numbering about a hundred or so. It was an army of people who all wore armor and had steel swords. And what's more, with her magical senses, she could see that some of those people have the capacity for magic. It was definitely a band of mercenaries, likely meant to act as security for the slave ring.

A terrifying force. She wasn't sure that the city guards would be enough to beat them. And if it wasn't for the presence of her mentor, Fern probably wouldn't be confident in beating them either.

And yet here they were, seemingly all fighting one man.

The unknown man who had introduced himself as 'Arthur Pendragon'.


Spoiler

She watched with wide eyes as he demolished every single person that had attacked him. She saw the way he used his sword with finesse that even a person like her who is untrained with a sword would find impressive. She witnessed as the man coated himself with mana in a manner she was unfamiliar with, boosting his movement significantly in a way that exceeds physical limits would allow.

It was mesmerizing to watch. Despite the fact that they outnumbered him significantly, he was somehow coming out on top… No, that wasn't accurate. He was simply the one on top, being somehow better than all of a hundred people combined.

He was strong. Much like her mentor right beside her.

"So? What do you think about him?" Fern blinked when she heard her mentor speak, and she turned to the elf. "Do you think he's a good fit for the party now, Fern?"

Good fit…? In the first place, she had never expected that they'd be joined by another person.

That said, they don't really know who he was. The name and background he told them was clearly fake. Everything about him was a complete mystery.

She had thought that he looked shady the first moment she saw him in that tavern, and yet somehow Frieren-sama had taken interest in him. The fact that he has plenty of skills that surprised even her mentor, who had lived very long, made it clear that they weren't dealing with a normal person. And what she was seeing below only served to prove that.

Any normal person would be right to think that they don't really trust him. However, considering that he was fighting for the sake of destroying that slave ring…

"I believe that he can be trusted if he were to join us." Fern answered. "He's a good person. If he wasn't, then he wouldn't have bothered to fight right now. He'd be essentially helping strangers for no good reason, after all."

Frieren-sama hummed at that.

"That's a good observation." the elf commented. "But you know, Fern, just because it's easy to help someone in need if you're powerful. Who knows if a person would react the same way if what they're facing is much more powerful than them?"

Fern blinked. "Are you saying that he isn't a good person, then?" Why would she invite him if that was the case?

"Oh, I think he is a good person. I'm just giving you a lesson on not judging things too rashly, Fern. You were quite rude to him with your snide comments earlier, you know?"

She sweatdropped. "Frieren-sama… between my comments and your constant harassment, you're definitely the one that's more rude. I don't think you can lecture me about it."

"Well, I guess you have a point there. Let's both apologize later."

That was something she could get by. That said… there was something she was curious about.

"Frieren-sama." she called out, making her mentor's ears twitch. "If fighting to save others was not enough reason to prove he's a good person, then what made you think that he was?"

"Oh, that?"

Her mentor let out a soft smile. It was a familiar smile, one that was tinged with happiness and nostalgia. And one that she knew the elf always let out whenever she was reminiscing in her memories.

And it was with that smile that she answered her question

"—He just reminded me of a heroine that travelled with me in the past."

Fern blinked.

Heroine…? Could she perhaps be talking about…?

Before she could finish her thoughts however, her mentor looked down again. That made Fern mirror her, and there she saw that the last of the men fighting were defeated, leaving only one man standing amidst the wreckage.

That's… that was only a few minutes. He'd dealt with all of those people in that little span of time?

"Ah, seems like he's done." Frieren-sama turned to her. "Let's go, Fern."

She nodded, stunned at how fast he defeated them all. Then she followed her mentor as they floated down to the ground to meet with the man that they had followed the entire day.

Arthur-sama glanced at them as they approached. "You guys done sunbathing?" he asked, sheathing his sword. It looked like he didn't even break a sweat. "Sure must've been difficult doing a whole load of nothing."

"You had it in the bag, so I left you alone." Frieren-sama easily replied. Then she looked around. "Hm… you really didn't kill anyone. That's honestly amazing, considering I saw you slash a lot of them. There isn't even a drop of blood in sight. How'd you do it?"

"I hit them with the blunt edge of my sword."

Blunt edge? But isn't a sword sharp on both sides?

"Hm, I don't know what that really means, but I'm not a warrior so I doubt I'd understand it anyway. That said, I'm more interested in the answer to my other question… the one that I asked you much earlier."

Frieren-sama tilted her head.

"So, what do you think? Do you want to join our party, Arthur?"

There was a moment of silence as Arthur-sama stared at her.

…Then, he let out a sigh.

"You're seriously annoying, aren't you? If I refuse now, you'd probably keep bothering me." he grumbled.

"I would." her mentor shamelessly agreed. "It won't be forever though, since we have things to do… so I'd probably stick around for five or six days, perhaps?"

"That doesn't really make it better, you know."

"You should see the priest at our party. He harassed someone for thirty days straight, you know?" Fern blinked. Was she talking about Heiter-sama? "It was impressive to see, really. We wouldn't have defeated the Demon King without that dedication."

"—What's that supposed to mean? Are you saying that I should be thankful you weren't that stubborn? Is that what you're saying?"

"You can take it as whatever you'd like." Frieren-sama replied easily.

Another exasperated sigh from the man. Then, after considering it for a few seconds or so, he looked away and scratched the back of his head. Ah, it seems like he wouldn't be joining them after all. She supposed it's understandable, considering the way Frieren-sama approached him—

"Fine. Do whatever you want."

Fern blinked.

…Did she just hear that right?

Frieren-sama smiled. "I knew you'd come around. Then I look forward to travelling with you." then her mentor turned to look at her. "Alright, let's bind all these unconscious people and free the captured slaves. Help me out with this, Fern."

She nodded, still a bit surprised. "Y-Yes."

As she went on to follow the elf, she took a moment to glance back to the person who accepted her mentor's offer to join their journey. With seemingly nothing else to do, the man decided to sit down on a still intact crate and decided to look over the many unconscious bodies that littered the ground, keeping a close eye on them in case one of them stood back up again.

He was someone that they don't know. Perhaps he was a hero like her mentor had assumed. Perhaps he really was Arthur Pendragon like he claimed he was. Or perhaps all of that were lies, and he was something else entirely instead.

However, his strength and conduct were undeniable. And for Frieren-sama, that was enough.

…Perhaps, she should also act the same way.

"Arthur-sama." she called out.

The man glanced at her with furrowed brows. "Did you just call me Arthur-sama…?" he asked incredulously, before shaking his head. "Whatever. What is it?"

She bowed at him.

"I apologize for my earlier remarks." Fern stated, before looking back up. And there she saw the man's stunned face for the very first time. "I was rude towards you. You don't deserve it, especially since you saved all these people. Thank you."

As he digested her apology, his stunned expression then slowly disappeared, and it returned once more to his usual blank one.

"…It's fine." Then he glanced to the side, where Frieren-sama was discreetly watching them. "If anything, it's your mentor who's supposed to apologize. You only got dragged in unwillingly."

The elf stiffened. Fern also glanced at her.

"That's true. She was the one who suggested saying sorry, and yet she immediately forgot about it." she agreed.

"I-I'm sorry…"

A weak apology reached their ears. The man ignored it.

And so, as Frieren-sama awkwardly said her apologies to the man right after, Fern couldn't help but let out an amused smile as she went on to help her mentor bind the unconscious mercenaries.

She didn't really know what fate had in store for them with a new member joining their party… but there is something that she definitely knew now that things ended up this way.

—Their journey had become a lot more interesting.

Chapter 36

After that little episode of me getting accosted into a temporary party, a day had passed.

We hadn't left the city yet. That was mostly because the whole slave ring thing was actually a pretty big deal for everyone - so right after I dealt with them and the city guards arrived, we were brought for questioning. It's all standard procedure considering the circumstances.

There was some curiosity about me when they realized I was the one who defeated all those people. However, when the elf introduced herself and said that I was a member of her party, the questions stopped coming and we were let go.

It really does look like she's a big deal. I suppose that makes sense, considering she was one of the people who defeated the Demon King. And it's easy for people to assume that she's surrounded by pretty strong fighters as well.

That said, since I was the one who dismantled the entire slave ring - it appears I am entitled to a reward for my good deeds. Apparently the mercenary band I defeated had people with bounties, which meant that I got to claim them.

—Which is why I was currently in the Adventurer's Guild early in the morning, standing right in front of the receptionist's desk with a blank look on my face.

"Hey, is that him? The one that destroyed that slave ring?"

"I've heard some nasty stuff happening in the slums, but to think there's something like that…"

"How strong do you think he is?"

"Look at his waist, that's definitely a magic sword. And beating that mercenary band by himself… that guy is definitely strong."

It looks like news travelled fast, since the very moment I entered the building it looked like everyone's attention turned to me. They weren't being obvious about it, but I can hear their whispered mutterings and easily notice their discreet peeking as I stand here waiting for my reward.

This place was definitely a unique location. After all, it reminds me of the idol agency which Aoki works at.


Spoiler

It was a genre melting pot.

Lots of people in different appearances, clothing, and internal mana reserves. The first two are more apparent for the women around - I can see some people have more pragmatic gear, which probably means they're from a more serious setting, while there are some who show so much skin or curves which likely point to them being part of the standard isekai slop genre.

As for the last one, the ones with lower mana belong to a setting where realism is a big part, while those with a bigger mana pool have those where magic happens commonly. It sets the divide between hard magic and soft magic systems, and the difference is clear to me since they group together.

Adventurer Guilds are pretty useful. This place, along with taverns, are the best places to gain information based on my experience in the Reverse Side before. However, that also applies in relation to my line of work now, especially now that I'm building a support base for myself here in the Reverse Side.

I should probably work on putting some clones in every Adventurer's guild out there. Clones that are overlooked and treated as mobs.

Which was exactly the opposite of what's happening right now, considering the amount of people staring at me.

I thankfully didn't have to wait long under all that. Because after a few seconds or so, the receptionist I was waiting for came back, along with a guy who looked like an higher up here.

"Here you go, sir!" the receptionist said to me with a bright smile on her as she put down a tray with coins stacked on them. "Fifty gold coins exactly, the combined reward for the bounties."

Fifty gold coins… that's five hundred thousand copper. Easily a year's amount of work for a high paying job here in fantasy world. That's a lot of money.

I guess the people I defeated are actually a pretty big deal, huh.

I took it and put it all in my pouch, before subspacing it as I put it in my pocket. And as I did that, the guy with the receptionist cleared his throat.

"Ahem! Arthur-dono." he started, making me glance at him. "On behalf of everyone who lives here in this city and the people who can return to their families once more - please accept our commendations and the accompanying sum. Thank you for doing us this great service."

Then, he straightened himself.

"It has also come to our attention that you are not a registered adventurer here. Frieren-sama had mentioned that you are an adventurer in someplace else, and normally these sorts of deeds result in promotions. As such, we're also giving you the opportunity for you to join our guild with a rank of Gold—"

"No."

"—Eh? A-Ahh, as you wish."

I waited for a moment to see if they were going to say something else, before turning around and walking away once it was clear there's none. As I did, I could hear the hushed whispers of people muttering behind me as I left, undoubtedly talking about this mysterious aura farmer who just ignored such a big opportunity. Or maybe they're just cursing me in jealousy and calling me stupid for doing that.

The elf, who had been waiting by the entrance, must have heard the latter with her sharp ears. She walked beside me as I passed by her, with her apprentice accompanying us as well.

"You're fine with throwing away an opportunity like that?" she commented. "I've never really bothered with the guild ranking stuff. But from what I heard, a Gold rank is supposedly a big deal."

"I don't really mind." I answered.

Like her, that stuff didn't matter to me at all. As I said earlier, what I wanted is to make the foundation of how I do things back home. And that didn't necessarily mean I'd need to get a higher rank.

What I want is a bunch of side character identities that I could use to gather information. And to do that, two clones would walk through this door: one to join the staff, and the other to also act as an adventurer. Maybe at some point that adventurer would be a gold one, or perhaps in a different place where I can retain that rank without raising much interest in any narratives I involve myself in.

And also…

"I did say I was going to be travelling with you guys." I answered. "I doubt I'll be able to do my adventurer responsibilities if that was the case."

"That's a good point. And you are looking for other realms, like you've said. I doubt you'd be easily available while doing that." Frieren paused. "…Speaking off, does the fact that you're looking for another realm have something to do with how you're from another world? Are you trying to find a way back home?"

I paused.

She believed that…? Normally people wouldn't, dismissing it as nonsense. It's the reason why I always say some bullshit stuff in front of other people despite it being the truth - the fact that it's not part of their genre means that they won't believe it. So unless this elf's story has actual isekai in it, which I doubt is the case…

I glanced at her with a frown. But before I could say or do anything about it, someone else spoke up.

"—Frieren-sama, do you seriously still believe what he said yesterday? It was clear he wasn't being honest because of your constant harassment." her disciple chided.

The elf crossed her arms. "You never know, Fern. What if he was telling the truth? A mage needs to be open-minded to succeed, especially in this fascinating world of ours."

Her apprentice stared at her with blank eyes.

"I know that you're trying to act wise, but please don't make a fool of yourself more than what you're doing. It's embarrassing."

"E-Embarassing? How mean…"

…Hm, what a delightful comedy combo, these two.

In any case, the genre divide clearly worked that time and they have no idea of my circumstances still. For a moment there I thought it didn't work with this elf - but as her apprentice showed, it was just probably used for that particular gag.

That said, the possibility of someone turning meta… I've already had four heroines in the Modern World based on different genres. The only remaining one would be someone from a fantasy genre. From a story standpoint, it'd be weird to introduce one this late, but the possibility is still there.

Hm, maybe I should check it for sure. And considering the genre this elf belongs to…

"Hey, Frieren." I called out, making her turn to me. "Have you seen that elf dressed in skimpy armor earlier?"

The elf blinked. "…There was? I didn't see anyone."

I see. False alarm, then.

Nevertheless, with the beneficial information that I gained, there must also be an equivalent sacrifice. Almost immediately as I said that - arms suddenly enveloped the elf which pulled her further away from me. I glanced to the side, and there I was met with a very cold and harsh sight.


Spoiler

"Excuse me, but what exactly was that?" the apprentice said coldly, looking at me with suspicion. "Why ask such an inappropriate question out of nowhere? Is this sexual harassment? Are you trying to pick up Frieren-sama?"

What's with this girl.

"Sorry but I prefer them big, so no worries on that. I was just confirming something." I replied.

The elf and apprentice looked down on themselves. The former looked kinda blank as she stared, like she was pondering the existence of the universe, while the latter immediately looked up to me with a disturbed expression.

"—Are you including me too!?"

No seriously, what's with this girl.

"Give it a few years, maybe." I replied blankly, before looking forward and resumed walking. "Also, good for you, having so much confidence in yourself. That'll bring you far."

The elf also did the same. "Yeah, good for you, Fern."

"…Mnn." the apprentice slumped and followed us as well. "…I might have overreacted. I apologize."

"It's fine." I easily replied.

I guess she has the right to be suspicious. I am a guy accompanying them after all, and my identity is still a mystery to them. Combine that with my sketchy NTR guy aura, I'm definitely someone that has the label 'suspicious' slapped to them a lot of times.

Anyway after that little comedy skit, we went our way out of the city. That detour to the Adventurer's Guild was the only thing stopping us from leaving, and we already prepared the stuff before we left.

The two fairies and the fake one blinked as the corruption stopped.

"What? Like hide and seek, but for items?" the first fairy asked.

"But you need it to be people! Or else you can just bury it or put it under a rock or something!" the other fairy also piped up.

"Sure. Which is why I can only hide this thing here without moving." they blinked again. "Are you ready? If we play the game and you don't find it after a minute, then you'd have to do what I say."

The fake fairy frowned. "That sounds really boring—" I subspaced the item with flair. "—Woah! It disappeared!"

"I-It's gone…!"

"How!? I didn't feel any magic…!"

The two fairies and the fake one all fluttered around me as they started searching for the item. And they won't be able to detect it in any way - after all, it wasn't magic, but rather through the use of technology. The genre divide actively prohibits them from actually accessing it since it meant interacting with advanced technology.

It's nothing like putting a phone in front of them. They might just interpret it as a magical artifact. No - this was as if they're putting an actual mech right in their eyes. The incompatibility between the genres is too big.

In any case, they didn't find it.

"Time's up. You guys didn't find it." I stated, before letting out of the subspace again with flair. "Looks like I win."

The first fairy tried imitating my movements, while the fake one stared at me with childlike wonder. Hm, seems like it's not all succubus for that thing.

The third fairy, however, pointed at me. "How!? How did you do that!?"

I smirked. "That's a secret." I replied. "Anyway, since you lost you're gonna have to tell me who made this thing."

That made the fairy stare at me with a frown. "They're pretty important." she answered. "…Why would you want to meet with them anyway? And who even are you?"

"I want to have a chat. As for my name…" I paused. "Yeah, I'm not giving you that. You can just call me a traveler."

"Huh? What's that supposed to mean? Why won't you give us your name?"

I raised a brow. "Because you're going to steal it."

"What? We're not gonna do that." the fairy looked vaguely offended. "Nobody even does that kind of thing anymore. That stuff has been outlawed thousands of years ago!"

"Yeah! Also, it's really mean!" the other fairy agreed.

Hm. Outlawed, they say? Looks like there might be some difference between the fae here and the fae back home. Or perhaps I just stumbled upon a setting where they don't actually do that. Or, you know, they're just lying.

"Well, I value my privacy quite a lot, so I'm still going to have to not give it." I replied. "So? I beat you fair and square. Still not going to let me meet with them?"

"Of course not! Like I said, they're pretty important! They have better things to do than meet humans like you!"

I frowned, considering that. So they're still not that convinced, huh… Then, how about I show them something that would definitely get their attention. This should make them at least intrigued a bit.

"What if I show you this cool-looking sword, then?"

"Huh? How's that gonna help—" I drew Excalibur from its scabbard. "—Woah! What is that!?"

"Pretty…!"

"Ahh! It kinda burns a bit!"

The two fairies looked very intrigued at my sword, while the fake one was driven away by the holy aspect of it. Clearly, the latter happened due to their conceptual connection with the weapon. This was one of the many swords that bore the name 'Excalibur' after all, and while it was unquestionably divine by nature due to being made by gods, it was also different.

And it was definitely enough to garner the fairies' interest. "What's with that sword? It's weird…" the same fairy muttered. "Are you some sorta big shot, mister? One of those Hero guys that roams around beating monsters?"

Seriously, there's so many settings that have heroes in them, huh.

"I guess you could say that." I answered, before sheathing the sword back. "So, does that make me important enough to meet with whoever they are?"

The two fairies looked at each other.

"Probably! Okay, mister, you can come with us!" the first fairy from earlier stated, before flying back to the ring of mushrooms. "Step inside here and we'll guide you to her!"

Finally, I can get to the fairy realm. Now, let me just ready this current clone to make sure that I'll get the information that I need if ever it gets trapped inside… There. That should be enough.

With that, I stepped forward and went inside the mushroom ring. And as I did so, I felt the world shift beyond the ring around me, and I found myself entering a realm that was clearly different from the Reverse Side. Although, it was a place that was clearly just as magical.

That said - looking around it was also strangely familiar. Because I'm pretty sure I've been in this place before.


Spoiler

The place looked kind of like the piece of Avalon that I stole back home, one that Haruhi had wrecked even through her dream-like state with her bullshit powers.

It seems to only have a superficial similarity to it though. The place lacks the everlastingness present in that realm. And it seems fairly small, so it probably means it's just one of the many fairy realms around present here in the Reverse Side.

And stepping inside here… Hm, there's a slight difference in time between this place and the outside, with the time here going much faster. It shouldn't be much of a problem though.

"Your highness! We have a gueeeest!"

Anyway, the first fairy called that out the moment we crossed the border, flying across the field with her two companions. Almost immediately, I saw that I gained the attention of fairies present in the realm. There appears to be different kinds around, and they also come in different forms and sizes. Although, something else did catch my attention.

The fake fairy - it seems that there's more of her kind in here. They blended in with the other fairies, and I can see the traces of their corruption which had spread around the place. And similar to the one I met earlier, they also immediately started eyeing me like I was a piece of meat.

Looks like I'd need to be careful lest I get assaulted.

Anyway, I ignored their stares for now and followed the two fairies and the fake one. They flew right to the very heart of the realm, and with what they shouted and their earlier statements about them being important - it was already clear on what type of fairy I was going to be talking to.

Although, it's not like I didn't expect it. I did read the fae item's history, after all. I already had suspicions with what exactly I'm going to be dealing with, and that suspicion was outright confirmed when I saw the three approach a being gracefully seated on a table while having tea.

It was a fairy bigger than the rest. One that looked more like an elf. Of course, they couldn't be more different - and that was because of the large ethereal wings on her back and the incredible power coming from her that rivals divine spirits.

—A Fairy Queen.


Spoiler

The blonde woman brought down her tea and gave me a curious look as I approached.

"Oh, a guest? It's been a long time since we've had someone brought here." she stated, before giving me a refined smile. "To whom do I owe the pleasure of speaking?"

"He doesn't want to say!" the fairy earlier tattletaled. "He said that he didn't want his name stolen, so he's keeping it a secret from us! He just wants to be called a traveler!"

The fairy queen blinked. "Oh my. That's quite an outdated view you have of us. None of us do that anymore."

"…Forgive me for saying this, but I don't quite believe that." I replied, making her blink. "I have my own previous encounters with the fae and all of them are malicious. So I'm going to have to err to the side of caution for now."

That made the Fairy Queen frown. "Well… I suppose I can't speak for others of my kind. I know that some of them can get pretty bad." she admitted, before giving me a reassuring look. "But rest assured that most of us don't act like them. I treat my subjects and guests fairly."

"Is that so? Then I'll take your word for it."

She gave me a smile again. "Thank you. Now, please have a seat." I did so, and the woman stood up and walked towards me, holding her teapot. "…Would you care to have some tea? Oh, and this isn't a trap by the way. I'll make sure to not claim you once you drink this."

Hm, I guess it's fine to believe her. And in the event she's lying, I can easily dismiss this clone anyway.

I shrugged. "Sure."

The woman brightened. Then, she started to pour tea right into my cup.

And as she did so, I immediately noticed something strange. It wasn't anything malicious - however, when she poured the tea, the Fairy Queen leaned down in an almost inappropriately close distance from me.

The instant that she did so, I was blasted with this woman's otherworldly beauty, along with an addictingly pleasant floral scent that reminded me of flower beds. She also moved a lock of blonde hair behind her ear - a movement which, coincidentally, made one focus on her large bosom that lightly touched the table due to how big they were.

It was honestly just simple movements. It looks as if they were done accidentally… until I finally took a look upon the Fairy Queen's face.


Spoiler

It was a lewd look. My hentai senses, sharpened from my experience with Aoki, made it clear that this fairy wanted to tease me and had her eyes on me. And immediately, I was also reminded by the fact that the fake fairies had populated this realm, spreading their corruption everywhere.

It looks like this place was in a more dire situation than I thought.

"Here you go."

The expression disappeared in an instant the moment I glanced at her. She finished pouring the tea, before straightening herself up and giving me an innocent-looking smile. There was no trace of the lewdness anywhere around her, replaced with this mother-like aura as she sat back down on her chair.

I took a sip of the tea. It was tasty, but more importantly it seems like she was telling the truth about not ensnaring me to this realm. Not like she was planning to ensnare me in a totally different way though. No sir.

"This is very delicious." I complimented her.

"Thank you! Brewing tea is a hobby of mine." she stated, before tilting her head. "In any case, may I ask what your business is here? And I'm quite curious how you've managed to convince my little ones here to let you come in here. They're very shy."

"He wants to talk to you! That man has something you enchanted a really long time ago, your highness!" the fairy informed her. "Also, we let him in because he has a cool sword! It's very pretty!"

That made the Fairy Queen blink in surprise.

"Something I enchanted…? It's been a long time since I did that. Centuries, maybe? I wasn't the Queen of this realm the last I did that." she muttered in curiosity. "And what do you mean by cool sword?"

"It's a very weird sword. I like it as well though." the other fairy stated. "I think he's one of those human heroes in the stories that everyone mostly talks about!"

The queen's curiosity turned into outright intrigue. "Really…? Do you mind showing me your sword, traveler?"

I did so, drawing the sword from its sheath once more and offering it to her. The Fairy Queen's eyes immediately widened at the sight, before she gingerly took the blade from me.

"T-This is…! It's definitely a sword of divine origin. I cannot be mistaken." she muttered, touching the hilt of the sword. Then she looked at me again. "…And considering you have this with you, you really must be like the heroes in the stories…!"

Not really. I got it from threatening a dumb goddess. Not very heroic, if you ask me.

Nevertheless, with the Fairy Queen thinking that I'm an important person - she quickly recovered her composure and cleared her throat, trying to make herself look proper once more. Though there was no denying there was an excitement underneath her graceful facade.

"Ahem! Anyway, I suppose someone like you came here for a quest of some sorts." she said, elegantly bringing up her tea cup once more. "May I ask again what your name is, hero? I assure you, I'll help you to the best of my ability. I simply want to know who you are."

Again, I suppose I have no reason to deny that. Even if she had tried to seduce me, she hadn't actually done anything outright malicious like the fae back home. I could probably give her my name without consequence.

Although - why the hell would I do that? I have a perfectly cool fake name I could use. I am, after all, currently acting as a different character.

So, thinking that, I gave the Fairy Queen a simple answer.

"Arthur Pendragon."

"—Pffff!"

I was immediately drenched in liquid after answering her. The Fairy Queen coughed after spitting out the tea she had been drinking, and any sort of gracefulness and elegance she tried to display before had been completely erased from what she did.

However, it looked like she didn't really care a single lick about that. Because right now, the queen was now staring at me with wide eyed surprise. That, along with something else that no one else displayed when I had started introducing myself with the name since I set foot in this world.

Recognition.

"Cough cough! W-What…!?"

Hm.

Seems like I found a clue to my goal now.
